# Canon

> Component library for internal tools (tables, forms, records) in accessible plain HTML. The markup is the contract: elements and attributes say what each thing is, a theme decides how it looks, and an optional script (canon.js) adds behavior. Two files from a CDN, no build step, no client framework.

Use Canon for back-office screens, admin panels, dashboards and record pages whose HTML a server or framework writes: Django, Rails, Laravel or Go templates, htmx, or a React app that renders the same elements. It suits teams with a back end and no front-end team, several stacks that should share components, a brand or several to follow, and tools that must last years. 67 of its 68 components work without JavaScript.

Canon is not a JavaScript component library (there is nothing to import or call), not an app framework (no routing, data loading or state) and not for marketing sites (no hero sections or pricing tables).

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/canon-ui@0.2.0/css/canon/canon.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/canon-ui@0.2.0/js/canon.js" defer></script>
```

Every document below is also at https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/ under its path. Links between them are relative to docs/.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/markup-rules.md

# Writing Canon markup

The rules every page that uses Canon follows. They are short on purpose: for people and for AI assistants writing Canon's HTML. Each component's specification (`docs/components/<component>.md`) gives its exact elements and attributes; the [decisions](decisions.md) explain why.

## Setup

Two lines in the page, no build step:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/canon-ui@0.2.0/css/canon/canon.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/canon-ui@0.2.0/js/canon.js" defer></script>
```

Any server or framework that writes HTML can use it. There is nothing to import or call.

## Copy the specification

- **Write each component as its specification shows**, with every required element, in order. Don't invent elements, classes or wrappers.
- **Start from the reference page's markup** (`reference/<component>.html`, the HTML under each example and in the Playground) and change the text and values.

## Say what it is, never how it looks

- **`class` is what a thing is:** `canon-button`, `canon-field`, `canon-label-text`. Only `canon-` classes, never variant or state classes.
- **`data-*` is what it means:** `data-emphasis="high | medium | low | minimal"` (how strongly it asks for attention; `medium` is the default), `data-intent="info | success | warning | danger"` (or `neutral` where a component has it). Each component lists the values it takes.
- **Never write a look in the markup:** no `outline`, `ghost`, `primary`, `rounded`, `blue`, `large`, no `style`. A theme decides how every meaning looks.
- **One `high` emphasis per view**, for what the view is for (Save, Create). Cancel, Back, Close and buttons that open menus or dialogs are `neutral`.
- **Never pick colors.** Where a color means something, it is `data-intent`; where it tells things apart (an avatar, a tag), it is `data-seed`, a stable number from the app.
- **Hints are optional:** `data-size`, `data-density`, `data-display="icon"` and the like say what only the author knows. Put them on a container and they apply to everything in it. Leave them out and the theme decides.

## State is native or ARIA

- Use the platform's attributes: `disabled`, `checked`, `required`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-busy`, `aria-pressed`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-current`, `aria-selected`.
- Never state classes (`active`, `is-open`). `data-state` is canon.js's, not yours.

## Indicators come from attributes

- Don't write chevrons, spinners or external-link icons. The theme draws them from the attribute that declares the behavior: `aria-haspopup="menu"` gives a chevron, `aria-busy="true"` a spinner, `target="_blank"` the external mark.
- **Icons are named, not drawn:** `<span class="canon-icon" data-icon="trash" aria-hidden="true"></span>`. Use the names in Canon's stylesheet; directional ones are logical (`arrow-forward`, `arrow-back`), so right-to-left pages mirror them.

## Accessibility is part of the markup

- **Every control has a name:** a `<label for>` (in a Field), or `aria-label` where a component's specification says so.
- **Icon-only buttons keep their text:** `data-display="icon"` on the button or a container, and the `canon-button-label` stays, as the button's name.
- **Write the roles and ARIA the specification lists**, every one. Canon's styles hang on them, so markup without them looks wrong as well as being inaccessible.
- **Real elements:** `<button>` for actions, `<a href>` for navigation, `<table>` for tables, `<dialog>`, `popover`, `<details>`, `<select>`, `<input type="…">` for what they are.

## Behavior is declared

- **Use invoker commands, not `onclick`:** `commandfor="<id>"` with `command="show-modal"`, `"close"`, `"toggle-popover"`, or Canon's own (`"--canon-copy"`, `"--canon-clear"`, …) as the specification gives them. canon.js fills them in where the browser lacks them.
- **Tooltips use interest invokers:** `interestfor="<id>"` on the trigger and `popover="hint"` on the tooltip.
- **Pages work without canon.js.** Forms submit, links go, dialogs open. Don't make anything depend on the script that a native element can do.
- **Canon has no data or state:** saving, fetching and routing are the app's. Swapping HTML in (htmx, Turbo, a framework) is fine; canon.js picks up new markup.

## Layout belongs to containers

- Components never set the space around themselves. Put them in a [Stack, Cluster or Grid](components/stack.md) with `data-gap` (in the theme's steps, never lengths), or in an App Shell, Section, Card or Form Layout.
- Don't add margins, widths or flex rules to `canon-` elements. Write layout CSS for your own containers, and app CSS without layers, which beats Canon's without specificity fights.

## Text is the author's

- Every word people see (labels, "(optional)", empty states, button text) is written in the markup. Canon writes none, except its own announcements ("Copied"), which `i18n/<lang>.css` translates.

## Check it

- In development, load `css/canon.debug.css` and `js/canon.debug.js` from the repository. They outline any markup that breaks a component's contract (a missing name, a part in the wrong place, a second primary action) and say why. Never load them in production.

## What Canon isn't for

Marketing sites (hero sections, pricing tables, mega menus) and anything that needs a client-side framework's components. Use Canon for internal tools: tables, forms, records, dashboards and the shell around them.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/decisions.md

# Decisions

The rules behind Canon: what it is for, how its markup speaks, how its CSS and JavaScript are built, and what it leaves out. Each component's own rules are in its specification (`docs/components/<component>.md`).

## Vision

**The most complete, accessible plain-HTML kit for internal tools.** Canon's HTML is the only source of structure, semantics and state. Its look is one stylesheet, its behavior one optional script, and neither asks anything of the markup beyond what each component's specification documents. Because the look lives apart from the markup, a team can restyle Canon, or replace its look entirely, without touching a page.

- Scope: what internal tools need (tables, forms, records, dashboards, the shell around them). Depth over breadth: each component covers its real cases (every state and size, keyboard, right-to-left, no JavaScript) before the next one is added.
- HTML is the core product and gets the most attention. Changes to it are deliberate and versioned.
- Canon ships raw HTML only. No template helpers: any server or framework that writes HTML can use it.
- The platform first: native elements and features do the work, and canon.js fills only the gaps.

## Naming

The system is called **Canon**: the body of work accepted as authoritative within a story's universe.

- Classes: `canon-` prefix (`canon-button`, `canon-label-text`).
- CSS custom properties: `--canon-` prefix.
- Data attributes are unprefixed (`data-emphasis`); they are always scoped by a `canon-` class.

## Markup channels

| Channel | Job | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `class` | What it is (identity, slots) | `canon-button`, `canon-label-text` |
| `data-*` (enumerated) | What it means (variant axes) | `data-emphasis="high"`, `data-intent="danger"` |
| ARIA / native attributes | Semantic state | `disabled`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-busy`, `aria-pressed` |
| `data-state` | JS-only state (rare) | `data-state="open"` |

- Default emphasis is `medium`. `high` must be chosen deliberately.
- `data-size` is **optional**. Without it, the theme decides size (by default and by context).
- `data-seed` (avatars, tags) is **identity, not appearance**: a stable number from the app that a theme turns into one of its colors, the same hue on every component. Authors never pick colors. Where a color means something, it is `data-intent`; a tag takes one or the other.

## Cross-cutting conventions

- **Precedence: the author always beats the theme, but the author never has to say anything.** For optional presentation hints (`data-size`, `data-density`, `data-display`, `data-orientation`, `data-placement`): own attribute → nearest ancestor attribute → theme context → theme default. `data-gap` is the exception that isn't inherited: a Stack, Cluster or Grid takes only its own.
- **Inherited hints:** `data-size="xs|sm|md|lg|xl|2xl"`, `data-density="compact|comfortable|spacious"` and `data-display="icon"` work on containers and apply to descendants. Components with fewer sizes use their nearest (controls: xs → sm, xl and 2xl → lg).
- **Emphasis** (`high | medium | low | minimal`): how strongly an element asks for attention relative to its neighbors.
- **Intent vocabulary** (system-wide): `info | success | warning | danger`, with neutral as the default. Each component supports the subset that makes sense.
- **Icons:** HTML names the icon (`<span class="canon-icon" data-icon="trash" aria-hidden="true">`). How it's drawn (mask, background image, font) is up to the theme. The icon names Canon uses are listed in its stylesheet.
- **Indicator rule:** visuals that indicate behavior are derived from the attribute that declares the behavior (menu chevron from `aria-haspopup`, loading from `aria-busy`, external link from `target="_blank"`). They are never written in HTML.
- **Accessory position:** after the trailing icon, accepts a `canon-kbd` or a `canon-count`. Shared by buttons, nav items, tabs, menu items.
- **Theme obligations** are part of the contract (e.g. never hide a label with `display: none`).
- **Layout belongs to containers**, not components (e.g. full-width buttons). Components never set the space around themselves; [Stack, Cluster and Grid](components/stack.md) do.
- **A size hint maps to a size, never to a role.** If a theme's bigger variant means something specific (a start button, say), it is not a size and needs its own contract or container context. A theme with one size ignores the hint.
- **Sizes belong to each component.** The same `data-size` does not guarantee the same height across components (Canon's fields and buttons match; another theme's may not). Side-by-side alignment is a container's job: baseline alignment (`align-items: last baseline`) by default, and toolbar / filter bar themes may match heights inside them.
- **Hover is for pointers that hover.** A hover look (a background, a border, a color) is themed under `@media (hover: hover)`, so a tap on a touch screen doesn't leave it stuck. What hover reveals or opens (a row's actions, a toast stack, an avatar's spotlight) stays ungated: a tap is the only way to it there. A look shared with `:focus-visible` keeps its focus half outside the gate.
- **Motion by how often it's seen.** What opens from the keyboard many times a day (the Command Palette) opens at once. State changes settle without overshoot. Skeletons show only after a short wait, so quick loads never flash them.
- **Direction:** themes must use logical properties (`inline-start`, not `left`) so RTL works. Directional icon names are logical too (`arrow-forward`, `arrow-back`, not `arrow-right`), so themes can mirror them in RTL.


## CSS architecture

- Cascade layers: `@layer canon.core, canon.theme, canon.hints;`. Themes declare this order, then `@import url("canon.core.css");` (no `layer()`: core places its own rules). Unlayered app CSS beats all three, so apps can override Canon without specificity fights.
  - `canon.core`: mechanics and defaults; themes override them freely.
  - `canon.theme`: the theme.
  - `canon.hints`: author attributes (`data-size`, `data-density` (resolved to `--canon-density`: -1 / 0 / 1), `data-display`, `data-max-lines`, `data-resize`, `data-orientation` on fieldsets and sliders, `data-placement` on tooltips, `data-layout` on forms, `data-sticky` on form actions, `data-gap` on stacks, clusters and grids, `data-columns` and `data-align` on grids and clusters). Above the theme, so **"the author beats the theme" is enforced by the cascade**, not by theme discipline.
- `css/canon/canon.core.css` (optional for themes): contract mechanics with zero visual identity: size inheritance, the icon box, RTL mirroring of directional icons, button reset, visually-hidden labels and `canon-visually-hidden` (text for assistive tech only), the avatar's one-cell stack and the avatar group's row, the field grid (default: label above), the chromeless native element inside `canon-control`, textarea line math, the choice grid and the fieldset's flex layout. Every selector is wrapped in `:where()` (zero specificity).
- `attr()` reads the element the rule applies to, never a child. Prefer native sizing where it exists (an input's `size` attribute sizes it once its box shrinks to fit).
- Core's size mechanism: `data-size` (xs and sm, md, lg to 2xl) resolves theme-provided `--canon-control-*-{sm,md,lg}` tokens into `--canon-control-block-size`, `--canon-control-padding-inline`, `--canon-control-font-size`, `--canon-control-gap` and `--canon-icon-size`. Custom-property inheritance makes the nearest `data-size` win.
- `js/canon.js` (optional, `defer`): T2 behavior. **Behavior is declared with invoker commands** (`commandfor` + `command="--canon-…"`), not `onclick` or data hooks; canon.js listens for the `command` event and polyfills custom commands where invoker commands are missing. JS-driven visual state goes in `data-state`. Command buttons are hidden under `@media (scripting: none)`. Avatars whose photo fails get `data-state="error"` so the fallback shows; avatars also get their count's width (`--canon-count-inline-size`) and their seed's slot (`data-seed-slot`, from the theme's `--canon-seed-colors`; tags too) for browsers without typed `attr()` and `if()`. Tooltips use the platform's interest invokers (`interestfor` + `popover="hint"`); canon.js polyfills them where missing (hover/focus delays, hoverable tooltip, Escape, one at a time, anchoring by name), and, in every browser, names the trigger when a tooltip opens (`--canon-tooltip-anchor`) so theme arrows can aim at it: CSS can't generate unique anchor names yet. Fields with an empty message show the browser's validation there, as a danger message, instead of its bubble. Field counters (`canon-field-counter`) show how much of the control's `maxlength` is used and make it a soft limit (moved to `data-maxlength`; past it the control is invalid at once and the excess is marked), with `data-state="near"` / `"over"` and a delayed announcement. Comboboxes (`canon-combobox` around a `<select>`) get a trigger (or a text field, `data-search="inline"`), a popover list (`role="listbox"`, `aria-activedescendant`; type-ahead, or a search field with `data-search="list"`: matches marked, results announced), tags with remove buttons for `multiple`, "Add …" (`data-creatable`), `canon-search` events for app-supplied options (`data-filter="none"`, `aria-busy` while loading), `data-max` and one-row tags (`data-tags="collapse"`); the select keeps the value, validation and labels. `--canon-clear` also clears selects. Password boxes get rule checks (`data-rule`, blocking submit through `setCustomValidity`), a rules-based score (`data-score="rules"`), revealed rules (`data-reveal`), Caps Lock (`data-state="caps-lock"`), a confirmation (`data-match`) and `--canon-generate-password`. canon.js also enhances native elements that need live values CSS can't read, without markup of their own: sliders get `--canon-slider-percent` (or `-start` / `-end`), synced `<output>`s, placed marks and `aria-valuetext`.
- **Customizable select** (`appearance: base-select`) is a theme opt-in, for `pointer: fine` only. Named anchors on pseudo-elements: `anchor-scope` does not reach `::picker(select)`, so core names only the box whose select is `:open` (one at a time, so the name is unique).
- **Strings.** Text Canon produces itself (theme CSS like a link's "(opens in new tab)", canon.js announcements like "Copied") is a CSS custom property `--canon-text-<key>`. English defaults live in core; **translation files** are `i18n/<lang>.css`, switching with `:lang()`, so they follow the `lang` attribute of each element (an Arabic section inside an English page gets Arabic strings). CSS uses them with `content: var(...)`; canon.js reads them from the element it works on. One file per language (`:lang(de)` covers de-DE, de-AT, de-CH); a regional file (`de-CH.css`) loads after its base and overrides only what differs. Files coexist, so multilingual apps load several. Author-visible words (labels, "(optional)") are always the author's, never generated.
- `css/canon.debug.css` (development only, unlayered, loaded after the theme): outlines markup that breaks the contract. The reference pages turn it on with "Contract check" (`?debug`). Every new contract rule that CSS can detect gets a check here.
- **Light/dark:** the native `color-scheme` property is the switch; there is no Canon attribute. A theme declares support with `color-scheme: light dark` on `:root` and writes colors with `light-dark()`, the only CSS mechanism that follows the `color-scheme` property (a `.dark` class or `prefers-color-scheme` media query can't). `light-dark()` only accepts colors, so per-scheme values like alpha percentages must be written as two full colors.
- **Sources and builds:** the stylesheets and the script are built, not edited. Each module's code lives in `src/css/core/<module>.css`, `src/css/theme/<module>.css` and `src/js/<module>.js`; `src/css/order.json` and `src/js/order.json` keep every part in order (the cascade's; the script's single closure), and `src/manifest.json` says what each module needs. `node tools/build.mjs` writes `css/canon/canon.css`, `css/canon/canon.core.css` and `js/canon.js` with everything; `--only data-table,select --out dist` writes the three with just those components and what they need, behaving exactly as the full build; `--list` shows the bundles and the components. Bundles (`src/manifest.json`'s `bundles`) group modules as apps use them: Core, always in on the Build page, then App shell and navigation, Data Table, Date picker, Combobox, Rich Text, Color picker, Avatars, More form controls and Code Block; `--only` takes bundles and modules alike. The rules are `tools/bundle.mjs`, shared with the reference's Build page, which builds the same files in the browser (choose bundles, download the three; single components are the command line's). Build tools: Node, nothing to install. Pages always link one `canon.css` and one `canon.js`, whichever build it is.
  - In the script, a component's set-up is in the build's list only when the component is (`typeof` on a name never declared is safe), and its commands (`commands["--canon-…"]`) are registered by its own module; helpers more than one module uses live in `base`.
- **A theme is a folder:** `css/<theme>/<theme>.css`, with whatever else it needs (icons, fonts) beside it. Canon's own is `css/canon/`, which also holds the core its stylesheet imports; `css/canon.debug.css` stays outside, for any theme.
- **Canon's look:** `css/canon/canon.css`. Lucide icons at stroke 1.5, Inter (with ss01, cv02, cv03, cv04 and cv11), JetBrains Mono for code; light and dark. It declares the layers and imports the core, so it is the one stylesheet a page links.
- **Lines and depth (Canon's look):** lines inside a component (table rows, a dialog's header line, separators, the shell's edges) are hairlines: one device pixel on sharp screens (`--canon-theme-hairline`, 0.5px at 2x and up, else 1px) in see-through colors (`--canon-theme-rule`, black or white at 10%; `--canon-theme-rule-faint` for the shell, 7–8%), so they read the same on white, tints and stripes. Frames that tell people "this is a control" (text fields, checkboxes, chips) stay 1px. What floats has no frame: a hairline edge (`--canon-theme-edge`, 12%) and one of three shadows, `--canon-theme-shadow-raised` (a tooltip), `-floating` (menus, popovers, lists, popup calendars and color pickers, toasts, the bulk bar) or `-overlay` (dialogs, drawers, the command palette, the narrow sidebar). Surfaces resting on the page (Card, Table, Code Block, Alert, Menubar) have the same hairline edge instead of a frame, a Card also the raised shadow. Framed controls you click or type in (low Buttons, Button Groups, text fields) have a faint lift (`--canon-theme-shadow-control`), gone while pressed or disabled. A transparent 1px border stays under every edge, so sizes don't change and forced colors still draw a frame.
- **Supported color schemes** are declared by the theme's `color-scheme` on `:root` and read from computed style.
- **Decoration budget:** a component has more visual layers than its two pseudo-elements (on an `appearance: none` checkbox or radio too, which is how choices draw their indicators without extra markup): `background-color`, stacked `background-image` layers, `border`, `outline`, `box-shadow`. A state layer can be a `background-image` gradient over the container color, so both pseudo-elements stay free for indicators.
- **When a theme's habits conflict with the contract, the contract wins** (e.g. `pointer-events: none` belongs on `disabled` only, never on `aria-disabled`, which must stay reachable).
- Themes keep variant rules at equal specificity (`.canon-button:where(...)` that only sets local `--_*` properties), so rule order decides and disabled can simply come last.

## Contract rules

1. **No per-instance presentation options in HTML**, with these exceptions, all optional **hints**: facts only the author knows about a thing's place or content, which the theme turns into a look. A hint never names a look ("outline", "rounded", "blue"); the theme decides what each one looks like, and a theme may ignore one.
   - **Size and density:** `data-size`; `data-density` (how tightly things sit, independent of size: an avatar group's overlap); `data-width` on a Dialog or Drawer (only the author knows whether it asks a question, holds a form or shows a table); `data-display="icon"` (only the author knows the icons say enough on their own: a toolbar, a rail).
   - **Arrangement:** `data-orientation` on a fieldset (only the author knows whether the labels are short enough to share a row) or a slider (a vertical slider belongs to its layout, like a mixer); `data-placement` on a tooltip (only the author knows what it must not cover; it still flips to fit); on a form, `data-layout="aside"` (only the author knows it is a settings page, read section by section) and `data-sticky` on its actions (only the author knows the form is long); `data-gap` on a Stack, Cluster or Grid (only the author knows how closely the things in it are related), in steps of the theme's spacing, never lengths; `data-columns` on a Grid (only the author knows how many of its things read well side by side); `data-align="end"` on a cluster's child, a card's footer item, a filter bar's item or a table cell (only the author knows what belongs at the far end, and that a column holds numbers); `data-fill` on a Segmented Control or Tabs (only the author knows its options should share their place, as in a narrow panel).
   - **Text:** `data-wrap` on a table cell (only the author knows whether it holds a name to keep on one line, a note to wrap, or a path whose middle can go); `data-max-lines` and `data-resize` on a textarea (only the author knows how long the answers run).
   - **Tables and lists:** `data-frame="none"` on a Table (only the author knows it already sits in something framed: a card, a dialog); `data-lines` on a Table, Description List or Stat row (only the author knows whether the items need separating); `data-striped` and `data-hover` on a Table (only the author knows the rows are long or wide enough that the eye needs help following one).
   - **Open in the page:** `data-inline` on a Color Picker or Date and `data-strip` on a Date (only the author knows the choice is the page's main task, worth showing open); `data-header="select"` on a Date (only the author knows the dates are far apart: a birthday, years away).
   - **Loading:** `data-shape` on a Skeleton (only the author knows what it stands in for: a line of text, a block, an avatar's circle, an icon's square); `data-motion="sweep"` (only the author knows the wait may be long enough to need showing it is still loading).

   Label placement, icon position and similar choices belong to the theme; density does too unless the author gives `data-density`. The markup must be structured so CSS can place things as freely as possible.
2. **Variants describe meaning, not appearance** (e.g. emphasis × intent, never "outline" or "ghost").
3. **State:** native pseudo-classes and ARIA first. When JS-driven state is unavoidable, use `data-state="…"`, never classes.
4. **System icons belong to the theme**, not the HTML.
5. **JS fallbacks are polyfills** of web standards, not custom behavior.
6. Components vital to internal tools are in; components for other kinds of sites are out (see Out of scope).
7. **The contract check** (`css/canon.debug.css`, development only) outlines breaches in a dashed amber line (the warning accent). Each check is its own rule naming its contract and its reason (`--canon-contract`, `--canon-contract-reason`), so the stylesheet is also the list of rules; one unsupported selector disables only its own check. `js/canon.debug.js` reads those rules and shows a warning for each outlined element: the contract, the reason, the exact condition it fails (and, for an unknown value, the values that are known), a floating one dismissible until the breach changes (a block has no close button: it stays while the breach does). It looks like a warning toast, with its own values so it reads the same in any theme. Where it goes: a container marked `data-canon-debug="after"` (in the docs, the playground's preview and every example frame) takes the warnings about everything inside it as blocks right after it, each naming its element (pointing at one marks the element); elsewhere a warning floats under its element in the top layer. Never inserted next to the element itself: a `<div>` there would break structures being checked (a Split Button, a list, a table). A container marked `data-canon-debug="off"` is left out entirely, outlines and warnings alike: for markup that is only decoration (in the docs, the Introduction's frame of components).

## Out of scope

- Ripple effects (pointer-position effects in general).
- Marketing-site patterns: Canon is for internal tools and apps, so there is no Navigation Menu (top navigation with dropdown panels, mega menus), hero section or pricing table.

## Tiers

- **T0**: pure HTML/CSS
- **T1**: native platform features (popover, dialog, invoker commands, anchor positioning), polyfilled where needed
- **T2**: works without JS, enhanced with JS
- **T3**: requires JS

Without canon.js a component shows nothing that only canon.js can work: core hides such controls under `@media (scripting: none)` (command buttons, the Data Table's search, panel buttons, export and select-all, the Split Pane's resize cursor), so a page whose script doesn't load has no dead controls. Where a T2 component keeps only its plain base without canon.js (the Data Table: a Table), its tier line says so.

## Components

Each links to its specification; the reference pages (`reference/<component>.html`) show them working.

**Layout:** [App Shell](components/app-shell.md) T0/T2 · [Page Header](components/page-header.md) T0/T2 · [Section](components/section.md) T0 · [Separator](components/separator.md) T0 · [Sidebar](components/sidebar.md) T0/T2 · [Split Pane](components/split-pane.md) T0/T2 · [Stack, Cluster and Grid](components/stack.md) T0 · [Toolbar](components/toolbar.md) T0 · [Top Bar](components/top-bar.md) T0/T2

**Actions:** [Button](components/button.md) T0 (toggle and copy T2) · [Button Group](components/button-group.md) T0 · [Link](components/link.md) T0 · [Segmented Control](components/segmented-control.md) T0 · [Split Button](components/split-button.md) T1 · [Toggle Chip](components/toggle-chip.md) T0

**Forms:** [Checkbox](components/checkbox.md), [Radio](components/radio.md) and [Switch](components/switch.md) T0 (sharing [the choice anatomy](components/choice.md)) · [Color Picker](components/color-picker.md) T2 · [Combobox](components/combobox.md) T2 · [Date](components/date.md) T2 (a date, a range, a week, a day strip) · [Field](components/field.md) T0 · [Fieldset](components/fieldset.md) T0 · [Form Layout](components/form-layout.md) T0 · [Form Repeater](components/form-repeater.md) T2 · [Input OTP](components/input-otp.md) T2 · [Label](components/label.md) T0 · [Number Input](components/number-input.md) T2 · [Password](components/password.md) T0/T2 · [Range Slider](components/range-slider.md) T0/T2 · [Rich Text](components/rich-text.md) T2 · [Save Bar](components/save-bar.md) T0/T2 · [Select](components/select.md) T0/T1 · [Slider](components/slider.md) T0 · [Swatches](components/swatches.md) T0 · [Text Input](components/text-input.md) T0 · [Textarea](components/textarea.md) T0 · [Time](components/time.md) T2

**Data display:** [Accordion](components/accordion.md) T0 · [Avatar](components/avatar.md) T0 · [Avatar Group](components/avatar-group.md) T0 · [Card](components/card.md) T0 · [Code Block](components/code-block.md) T0/T2 · [Data Table](components/data-table.md) T2 (with its bulk action bar) · [Description List](components/description-list.md) T0 · [Empty State](components/empty-state.md) T0 · [Filter Bar](components/filter-bar.md) T2 · [Kbd](components/kbd.md) T0 · [Stat](components/stat.md) T0 · [Status Indicator](components/status.md) T0 · [Table](components/table.md) T0 · [Tag](components/tag.md) T0

**Overlays:** [Dialog](components/dialog.md) T1 · [Drawer](components/drawer.md) T1 · [Menu](components/menu.md) T1 (context menus included) · [Popover](components/popover.md) T1 · [Tooltip](components/tooltip.md) T1

**Feedback:** [Alert](components/alert.md) T0/T2 · [Banner](components/banner.md) T0/T2 · [Skeleton](components/skeleton.md) T0 · [Spinner](components/spinner.md) T0 · [Toast](components/toast.md) T2

**Parts other components hold** (not counted among the 68): [Count](components/count.md) T0 (in Avatars, Nav Lists, Tabs and Buttons) · [the choice anatomy](components/choice.md) (Checkbox, Radio, Switch) · [Data Table editing](components/data-table-editing.md) T2.

**Patterns:** List → Detail → Edit (`reference/list-detail-edit.html`) · Master–Detail (`reference/master-detail.html`) · Settings Page (`reference/settings-page.html`) · Sign-in Page (`reference/sign-in-page.html`)

**Planned:** File upload and dropzone · Meter and Progress · Tree View · Timeline · Rating · Steps · Status pages (403, 404, 500, maintenance) · A wizard pattern. Later: calendar, kanban, Gantt, charts, JSON and log viewers, diff viewer, query builder, notification center, a bridge for third-party rich text editors.

## Working on the docs

- `reference/<component>.html` holds the canonical markup for every variant, state and stress case: each page is a fixture a theme must render. Page chrome uses `ref-` classes and never styles `canon-` classes or sets inherited typography. Shared chrome lives in `reference/ref.js` (the top bar, navigation, example frames and playground) and `reference/ref.css`.
- Each component page has two tabs: "Reference" (the fixture) and "Playground". The Playground is a workbench: on windows wider than 56rem it fills the page under the top bar, the preview over the HTML (a divider between them drags, the arrow keys move it, a double click resets it), the controls at the end and the navigation at the start, always there to jump to another page. Wide, the Reference / Playground switch sits in the top bar after the page's name, in the same place for both views. Going to another page keeps the view: from a Playground, the next component opens on its Playground. The preview takes a width, in the URL: a ruler over the preview shows the width in its middle, a button that opens presets (full width, mobile 360, tablet portrait 720, tablet landscape 1024, desktop 1280; those wider than the preview are off), and a side at each end of the frame drags it from its middle, from 360px up to the full width, holding at a preset as it passes (the arrow keys move it too; a double click goes back to full width). Narrower than the preview, the area beyond the frame is hatched with faint diagonals. A width chosen wider than the preview shows at full width until there's room again; the divider's place is remembered in the browser. Narrower, it stacks. Each parameter gets the control that suits its options, worked out from them unless the playground names one (`widget`): meanings as colored tiles with their icons, emphasis as tiles drawing each level, icons as a field showing the chosen one that opens a grid of them, an ordered scale (sm, md, lg; compact … spacious) as a slider with a stop each, a few short options as a segmented control, numbers as a field with − and + whose label scrubs, the rest as menus, fields and switches. A changed parameter's label is in the text color; Reset puts everything back.
- **Playground:** `reference/playground/<component>.js` exports `controls` (name, label, type, options, default, group, `when`) and `render(state)` → HTML. The engine in `ref.js` renders the preview and shows the exact HTML, ready to copy. A label's note in parentheses becomes the control's tooltip and description (or, for "empty: …", its placeholder). Pattern pages have no playground.
- **Everything is in the URL** (`scheme=light|dark`, `debug`, `long-text`, `rtl`, `view`, `p.<control>`), so any configuration is a shareable link.
- **Stress modes** (from the search, or the URL): `long-text` makes every component's text on the reference about 40% longer and accented, between ⟦ and ⟧ so a clipped end shows, as translated and real-world text can be; `rtl` mirrors the fixtures. The notes, code and keys stay as they are. Empty, single-item and very long states belong to each page's own sections.
- **Navigation** lists every planned page; pages not written yet show a "Soon" Tag and are left out of Search. On narrow screens it's a drawer whose sections (Introduction, Components, Patterns) are tabs that switch its list in place.
- **Resizable demos:** a demo people drag narrower is marked `.ref-resizable` (a box around components, its start width inline or `-narrow` / `-wide`) or `.ref-resize` (on a page-like frame, its start width inline). Alone in its frame, ref.js makes the frame itself the thing you drag, with its padding: no box in a box. Give it a note of its own before it, so other demos go in other frames.
- **Static popovers:** a fixture can show popovers open (`popover="manual"` next to a `.ref-anchor[data-ref-opens="<id>"]`). ref.js opens each against its anchor when it scrolls into view and again after each scroll or resize, because anchor positioning keeps the last placement that fit.
- Built in Canon's own spirit: plain HTML, CSS and a little vanilla JavaScript.
- **Local preview:** serve the project folder over HTTP (for example `python3 -m http.server`) and open `reference/introduction.html`. Turn caching off while you work, or the browser keeps stale CSS.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/app-shell.md

# App Shell

Tier: **T0** · the sidebar's toggle and the narrow drawer are **T2** (canon.js)

The frame of an app's pages: a [Sidebar](sidebar.md) the full height at the start, a [Top Bar](top-bar.md) over the content, and the page's `<main>`. Both stay put while the page scrolls.

## Elements

```html
<body>
  <div class="canon-app-shell">
    <div class="canon-sidebar" id="sidebar">
      <div class="canon-sidebar-header">
        <a class="canon-sidebar-brand" href="/">…</a>
      </div>
      <div class="canon-sidebar-body">
        <nav class="canon-nav-list" aria-label="Main">…</nav>
      </div>
    </div>
    <header class="canon-top-bar">
      <div class="canon-top-bar-start">
        <button … commandfor="sidebar" command="--canon-toggle-sidebar" aria-controls="sidebar" aria-expanded="true">…Sidebar…</button>
        <button … commandfor="palette" command="show-modal" aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K Control+K">…Search…</button>
      </div>
      <div class="canon-top-bar-end">…</div>
    </header>
    <main>…</main>
    <dialog class="canon-command-palette" id="palette" aria-label="Command palette">…</dialog>
  </div>
</body>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-app-shell` | yes | Usually the body's only child. |
| [Sidebar](sidebar.md) | no | One. |
| [Top Bar](top-bar.md) | no | One. |
| `<main>` | yes | The page. |
| Dialogs and popovers | no | Take no place (a Command Palette, the account Menu). |

- **The toggle**: one, at the bar's start, in the same place whether the sidebar is open or a rail (without a bar, in the sidebar's header).
- **[Banners](banner.md)** go before the shell, not in it: first in what holds it (the `<body>`).

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--canon-app-shell-height` | the shell (a style) | a length | `100dvh` | yes (CSS) |
| `--canon-sticky-offset` | the shell (a style) | a length: where sticky things in the page (a sticky [Page Header](page-header.md)) start | the theme sets it to the Top Bar's height when there is one (plus the Banners') | yes (CSS) |
| `--canon-banners-height` | the shell's parent (canon.js) | the height of the [Banners](banner.md) before it | `0px` | yes (CSS) |

## Core

- A grid: the sidebar the full height at the start; the bar over the content; `<main>` under it.
- The sidebar is the window's height (`--canon-app-shell-height`) and stays put (sticky), its body scrolling on its own; the bar stays at the top. So the shell needs the window, or a frame that height, to scroll in: in something taller that doesn't scroll, the sidebar stops at that height.
- The shell is at least the window's height (`--canon-app-shell-height`, for a shell inside something else).
- Under Banners (`--canon-banners-height`), the sidebar and the bar stick under them, and the sidebar and the shell take the height they leave; `--canon-sticky-offset` includes them.
- The shell is a size container named `canon-app-shell`: its own width, not the window's, decides when it is narrow (so a shell inside something else behaves too).

## Behavior (T2, canon.js)

- **Narrow: the sidebar becomes a drawer.** Below the width the theme sets (`--canon-sidebar-drawer: 1` on the sidebar, from a container query on the shell), canon.js makes the sidebar a drawer (`data-drawer="closed"` or `"open"`): it takes no room, so the page has the full width, and the toggle (still at the bar's start) opens it over the page, at the shell's start, inside the shell (a shell inside something else keeps it inside too).
  - Open, it is the whole sidebar, labels and all (a rail is one again when the shell widens; `data-display` is put back).
  - Escape closes it (focus back to the toggle when it was inside), and so do a click or focus elsewhere and choosing a page. Opened from the keyboard, focus goes to the current page's link (or the first).
  - The toggle's `aria-expanded` says whether the drawer is open.
  - Only with the toggle outside the sidebar (in the Top Bar): a toggle in the sidebar's header would go with it, so that sidebar stays in place.
- Without JavaScript the sidebar stays in place at every width.

## Accessibility

- Landmarks: the sidebar's navigation, the bar's banner, the main, in the page's order (the grid places them; the order stays the reading order).
- The toggle never moves, so focus stays on it when the sidebar collapses or opens.
- The drawer is not modal: the page stays reachable, and leaving it (Escape, a click, choosing a page) closes it. A task that must block the page is a [Drawer](drawer.md), not this.

## Theme obligations

- The sidebar and the bar meet cleanly (one line between them, not two).
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the sidebar is on the right.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A medium width turning the sidebar into a rail by itself | Not planned: it would override what people chose; the bar's folding handles a cramped middle width |
| A skip link to the main | The app (before the shell) |
| A second sidebar at the end (details of a selection) | Split Pane, or a Drawer |

## Look

The page zinc-50 (dark zinc-950) behind white panels (dark zinc-900); the Sidebar and Top Bar's fills and their lighter lines (hairlines in the faint rule: black at 7%, dark white at 8%), one line where they meet. Narrow under 640px of its own width (a phone, or a small window): the sidebar a drawer.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/page-header.md

# Page Header

Tier: **T0** · folding when narrow and renaming in place are **T2** (canon.js)

The top of a page: what it is, what state it's in, and what you can do here. It sits at the top of the page's `<main>`, under the [Top Bar](top-bar.md). What stays the same on every page goes in the bar; what belongs to this page goes here.

## Elements

```html
<main>
  <header class="canon-page-header">
    <a class="canon-page-header-back" href="/invoices">
      <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="chevron-left" aria-hidden="true"></span>Invoices
    </a>
    <div class="canon-page-header-title">
      <h1 id="title">INV-2041</h1>
      <span class="canon-tag" data-intent="warning"><span class="canon-tag-label">Overdue</span></span>
      <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-intent="neutral" data-display="icon"
              commandfor="title" command="--canon-edit">
        <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="pencil" aria-hidden="true"></span>
        <span class="canon-button-label">Rename</span>
      </button>
    </div>
    <p class="canon-page-header-description">Globex Corporation · Due 3 October · €12,400</p>
    <div class="canon-page-header-actions">
      <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-intent="neutral">…Download…</button>
      <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="high">…Send reminder…</button>
    </div>
  </header>
  …
</main>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `header.canon-page-header` | yes | A `<header>` inside `<main>` (so not a banner landmark). |
| `a.canon-page-header-back` | no | First: one step up ("Invoices"), its icon decorative. |
| [Breadcrumb](breadcrumb.md) | no | First, instead of the back link, when the trail is deeper. Where people are is the page's: a Breadcrumb goes here, not in the Top Bar. |
| `.canon-page-header-title` | no | One heading (`<h1>` on a page; another level where the header heads a part of one), then optional status ([Tag](tag.md)s) and a rename Button. |
| `p.canon-page-header-description` | no | One line of facts: who, when, how much. More facts go in a [Description List](description-list.md) under the header. |
| `.canon-page-header-actions` | no | [Buttons](button.md) (also Split Buttons, Button Groups, and the Menus they open): what you can do to this page or record. Neutral by default; at most one primary (`data-emphasis="high"`), last, and only when one action is what the page is for. A view only to read (a log, a report) has none, or no actions at all. |

- **Two pages, one header.** A collection's page has the collection as its title ("Invoices"), a line of facts, and its actions ("New invoice"; a list only to read, like an audit log, may have just "Export", or nothing). A record's page has the record as its title ("INV-2041"), a back link or a trail, its status, and what you can do to it. Same parts, different choices.
- **The title is optional.** Some pages need no visible title, like a dashboard named by its sidebar link. Keep one for screen readers anyway: a visually hidden `<h1 class="canon-visually-hidden">` in the title, so people can still find where the page starts.
- **Tabs** for the page's parts go right under the header, in the page, not in the header.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-sticky` | the header | present | absent | no |
| `data-size` | the header or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |
| `--canon-sticky-offset` | a container (a style) | a length: where sticky things in the page start | `0`; an App Shell's theme sets it to its Top Bar's height | yes (CSS) |
| `--canon-page-inset` | a container (a style) | a length: the page's side padding | `0` | yes (CSS) |

## Core

- A grid: the back link or trail over the title, the actions beside the title, the description under both. Under 24rem of its own width (a container query), the actions go under it all.
- The title's parts wrap; a long title wraps too, and is never cut.
- **Sticky** (`data-sticky`): it sticks under `--canon-sticky-offset`, with the back link or trail tucked away above it, so only the title, the description and the actions stay in sight. It reaches across the page's side padding (`--canon-page-inset`), so the page doesn't show beside it as it scrolls.

## Behavior (T2, canon.js)

- **Folding**, each part on its own, undone as room comes back:
  - `actions`: when the actions leave the title less room than it needs (its own width, up to 20rem), they go into one **More** menu where the first of them was, the primary action staying. Shared with the [Top Bar](top-bar.md#behavior-t2-canonjs): a toggle as a check, a Button opening a Menu as a submenu, and only when two or more would fold.
  - `breadcrumb`: a trail that doesn't fit its row keeps its last page, after a "more" button whose Menu lists the rest in order.
  - `data-fold` on the header lists the steps taken; folded things get `data-folded`.
- **Sticky:** canon.js measures how far the title starts below the trail and sets `--canon-page-header-tuck`, so exactly the trail tucks away. Without it the whole header sticks.
- **Rename in place:** a Button with `command="--canon-edit"`, `commandfor` the heading, edits the heading's text where it is.
  - A text field takes its place, named by the button ("Rename"), the text selected.
  - Enter or leaving the field keeps the change; Escape drops it. Enter and Escape bring focus back to the button.
  - `canon-edit` fires on the heading first (`detail.value`, `detail.previous`, cancelable). Cancel it to keep the old name, for example when saving fails. An empty or unchanged value changes nothing.
  - The heading and its button are `data-editing` (hidden) meanwhile.
- Without JavaScript nothing folds (the actions go under the title when narrow), the whole header sticks, and the rename button is hidden, like every Canon command button.

## Accessibility

- The heading is where the page starts, and the title's `<h1>` the page's name, heard first. Keep one even when it isn't shown.
- The back link's name is where it goes ("Invoices"); its chevron is decorative.
- A status is a Tag's text, read with the title: "INV-2041, Overdue".
- Folded, every action keeps its name, as an item of the More menu ("More", `--canon-text-more`).
- Renaming: the field is named by its button and holds the old name selected; the new name is the heading's text, so it is what screen readers hear next.

## Theme obligations

- The title clearly the most prominent text on the page; the back link and the description quieter.
- A primary action, when there is one, visibly primary; the rest quieter.
- Sticky, a background that hides the page scrolling under it.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the back link's chevron points right and the actions sit on the left.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Tabs under the header | Tabs, next |
| An avatar or icon beside a record's title | If it comes up |
| Editing other text in place (a description, a table cell) | `--canon-edit` works on any text; a contract for it when it comes up |

## Look

**Sizes:** sm / md / lg: the title 20 / 24 / 30px on 28 / 32 / 36px lines; the trail and description in the control's type (12 / 14 / 16px); the shell's inset above and below, and between the trail and the title (8 / 12 / 16); 6 / 8 / 10 between the title and the description; 16px between the title and the actions; 8px between actions and between the title's parts.

Canon's own type and the shell's measures. The title semibold zinc-900 (dark white); the back link and description zinc-500 (dark zinc-400), the back link darkening on hover. Sticky: the page's color behind it, and the shell's line under it once stuck (a scroll-state query; browsers without one show no line). Renaming: the field in the title's type, on a zinc-100 fill (dark zinc-800), inside the focus ring.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/section.md

# Section

Tier: **T0**

A titled part of a page: billing details, payment terms, a settings group. The same anatomy as a [Card](card.md), without the frame; in a Card, Sections are its parts.

## Elements

```html
<section class="canon-section">
  <header class="canon-section-header">
    <h2 class="canon-section-title">Billing details</h2>
    <p class="canon-section-description">Where invoices go, and when they're due</p>
    <div class="canon-section-actions">
      <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-intent="neutral">…Edit…</button>
    </div>
  </header>
  <dl class="canon-description-list">…</dl>
</section>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-section` | yes | A `<section>` (a `<div>` or `<fieldset>`'s content also fits). |
| `.canon-section-header` | no | First. The title, then an optional description and actions. |
| `.canon-section-title` | with a header | A heading (`<h2>`–`<h6>`): under the page's `<h1>`, an `<h2>`; in a Card, one level under the card's title. |
| `.canon-section-description` | no | A `<p>`: one line about the section. |
| `.canon-section-actions` | no | [Buttons](button.md) about the section. |
| Content | — | Anything after the header. |

- **Section or Card?** A Section when the page's own spacing is enough to tell parts apart; a [Card](card.md) when a part needs setting apart (on a tinted page, among other things, or as one of many).
- **In a Card:** Sections directly in a card are its padded parts, a line between them.
- **Landmarks:** a `<section>` is not a landmark unless named; its heading already puts it in the page's outline.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-size` | the section or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |

## Core

- The header: the title and the actions in a row, the description under both; narrow (under 20rem, a container query), the actions go under it all.

## Accessibility

- The title is a real heading: people move through the page by its sections.

## Theme obligations

- The header clearly above its content; the title more prominent than the description.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the actions sit on the left.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Space between sections on a page | [Stack](stack.md) (`data-gap="xl"`) |
| A collapsible section | Accordion |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** The header 12 / 16 / 20 above the content; titles 14 / 16 / 18px on 20 / 24 / 28px lines; text in the control's type (12 / 14 / 16px).

A Card's header and type, without the frame: titles semibold, descriptions zinc-500 (dark zinc-400). In a Card, padded like its body with a hairline rule between (black at 10%, dark white at 10%).

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/separator.md

# Separator

Tier: **T0**

A line between things, optionally with a word or two in it ("or").

## Elements

```html
<hr class="canon-separator">

<div class="canon-separator">or</div>

<hr class="canon-separator" aria-orientation="vertical">
```

| Element | When | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `<hr class="canon-separator">` | A line | A thematic break: screen readers hear a separator. As wide as its container, with space above and below. |
| `<div class="canon-separator">` | A line with words | The words are its only content, read as ordinary text; the two lines are the theme's. Not `role="separator"`: a separator's content is hidden from screen readers. |
| `aria-orientation="vertical"` | A vertical line | On the `<hr>`, in a row (a flex container): as tall as the row, with space beside it. No words. |

- Separators inside other components are this one too: between a [Menu](menu.md)'s items, a [Select](select.md)'s or [Combobox](combobox.md)'s options (in the `<select>`; canon.js copies them into a combobox's list), and before the [Color Picker](color-picker.md)'s swatches.
- The words say what comes on each side in a sentence's terms ("or", "Older messages"), not a heading's.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-orientation` | the `<hr>` | `vertical` · `horizontal` | `horizontal` | — |
| `data-size` | the separator or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |

## Core

- The `<hr>`: no browser border or margin, its own block. Vertical: stretches in its row.
- The `<div>`: a flex row, the words between `::before` and `::after` that share the rest of the width; one line of words.

## Accessibility

- An `<hr>` is a separator for assistive technology; a vertical one says so with `aria-orientation`.
- Words in a `<div>` are read in reading order, like the text around them.

## Theme obligations

- The line visible against its background, the words quieter than body text.

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** A 12 / 16 / 20px row (the line in its middle); words 12 / 14 / 16px on 16 / 20 / 24px lines, 4 / 6 / 8px from the lines.

A hairline rule (black at 10%, dark white at 10%; 1px on screens under 2x), its space growing by what the line gives up so nothing moves; words zinc-500. Vertical, the same line with the same space beside it.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/sidebar.md

# Sidebar

Tier: **T0** (a column of Nav Lists) · collapsing to a rail, and a drawer on a narrow App Shell, are **T2** (canon.js)

The column beside an app's pages: the app's name, its main links, and what belongs at the bottom (help, settings). It collapses to a rail of icons. The links themselves are a [Nav List](nav-list.md); the sidebar is the column around them. Usually inside an [App Shell](app-shell.md).

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-sidebar" id="sidebar">
  <div class="canon-sidebar-header">
    <a class="canon-sidebar-brand" href="/">
      <svg aria-hidden="true">…</svg>
      <span class="canon-sidebar-brand-name">Globex Corporation</span>
    </a>
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-intent="neutral" data-display="icon"
            commandfor="sidebar" command="--canon-toggle-sidebar" aria-controls="sidebar" aria-expanded="true">
      <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="panel-left-close" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="canon-button-label">Sidebar</span>
    </button>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-sidebar-body">
    <nav class="canon-nav-list" aria-label="Main">…</nav>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-sidebar-footer">
    <nav class="canon-nav-list" aria-label="Help and settings">…</nav>
  </div>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-sidebar` | yes | The column: a `<div>` (its Nav Lists are the landmarks). An `id` when a toggle names it. |
| `.canon-sidebar-header` | no | First. A brand (or a workspace switcher), then the toggle when there is no Top Bar to hold it. |
| `.canon-sidebar-brand` | no | The app's or workspace's mark (an `<img>` or `<svg>`, decorative) and a `.canon-sidebar-brand-name`; a link home, or a button opening a workspace Menu. |
| `.canon-sidebar-body` | yes | After the header: the Nav Lists (one or more; a [Separator](separator.md) may go between them). The part that scrolls, so the header and the footer stay. |
| `.canon-sidebar-footer` | no | Last, at the bottom: a Nav List (help, settings), or the account. Where the account goes (here, or a Top Bar) is the app's choice. |
| Toggle | no | One [Button](button.md) with `command="--canon-toggle-sidebar"`, `commandfor` and `aria-controls` the sidebar, `aria-expanded`, icon only, named "Sidebar". In the same place in both states: a [Top Bar](top-bar.md)'s start, or the sidebar's header when there is no bar. |

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-display` | the sidebar | `icon`: the rail. Icons only, the brand's mark only; names stay for screen readers. | open | yes (to its Nav Lists and Buttons) |
| `data-size` | the sidebar or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg`: its Nav Lists' rows | theme decides | yes |
| `--canon-sidebar-width` | the sidebar or a container (a style) | a length | theme decides (Canon: 16.5rem) | yes (CSS) |

## Core

- A column: the header, the body, the footer at the bottom. When the links don't fit, only the body scrolls (on its own, not the page): the brand and the footer stay in place, and the scrollbar runs beside the links only.
- Open, it is `--canon-sidebar-width` wide; a rail is as wide as its icons (a theme may give it an explicit width, to animate between the two).
- A long brand name is cut (…).

## Behavior (T2, canon.js)

- **Collapsing:** `--canon-toggle-sidebar` sets or removes `data-display="icon"` on the sidebar and the toggle's `aria-expanded`. The toggle stays where it is, so focus does too.
- **The rail's links:** names show in each link's [Tooltip](tooltip.md) (`interestfor`), beside it (`data-placement="inline-end"`); a section's sub-pages open beside it (see [Nav List](nav-list.md#rail)).
- **A drawer:** on a narrow [App Shell](app-shell.md#behavior-t2-canonjs) the sidebar leaves the page and the toggle opens it over it (see there).
- Without JavaScript the sidebar stays as written (open, or a rail), in place at every width.

## Accessibility

- Its Nav Lists are named navigation landmarks; the sidebar adds none of its own.
- The toggle says whether the sidebar is open ("Sidebar, expanded") and which element it controls; it never moves, so focus stays on it.
- In a rail, every name is still there for screen readers; tooltips show them on hover and focus.

## Theme obligations

- Set apart from the page (a line, a fill).
- A rail's icons and their current page as clear as the open sidebar's.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the sidebar is on the right.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Remembering open or rail between visits | The app (it writes `data-display`) |
| Resizing by dragging | Split Pane |
| A workspace switcher's menu | [Menu](menu.md) from the brand button |

## Look

**Sizes:** sm / md / lg (the size scale, through one inset of 8 / 12 / 16): 264px open at every size; a rail 48 / 64 / 80 (with its line), as wide as the Top Bar is tall; inside, the inset above and below and 4px more at the sides (8 12 / 12 16 / 16 20; a rail the inset all round); 24 / 32 / 40 between header and links; the header a row tall (32 / 40 / 48), lined up with the bar.

White (dark zinc-900), a hairline at its end in the shell's faint rule (black at 7%, dark white at 8%). The brand a 24 / 32 / 40 mark 10 / 12 / 16 before its name (Button's type, semibold: 12 / 14 / 16; zinc-900, dark white). Collapsing and opening animate the width (0.2s; none with reduced motion); in the rail, items fill its one-square column, so their fills narrow with it and the icons glide the 4px between the two paddings. The toggle a minimal neutral icon Button: a panel and a chevron drawn apart, the chevron turning 180° (in to close, out to open); mirrored in right-to-left. A rail's header stacks the mark and the toggle when it is there. Canon keeps one toggle in one place. A drawer: from the shell's start over a 30% black scrim on the shell, with a shadow, sliding in (0.2s; none with reduced motion). The side padding is the header's, body's and footer's, so the body's scrollbar sits at the sidebar's edge. Thin scrollbars; none in a rail (it still scrolls by wheel, touch and focus), where one would narrow the one-square column.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/split-pane.md

# Split Pane

Tier: **T0** (two panes at a set size) · resizing is **T2** (canon.js)

Two panes side by side (a list and its record), or one over the other (a query and its results), and a handle that shares the room between them.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-split-pane">
  <div id="invoices">…the list…</div>
  <div class="canon-split-pane-handle" role="separator" tabindex="0"
       aria-label="Resize the list" aria-controls="invoices" aria-orientation="vertical"
       aria-valuenow="35" aria-valuemin="20" aria-valuemax="60"></div>
  <section>…the record…</section>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-split-pane` | yes | Exactly three children: a pane, the handle, a pane. As tall as its place gives it (the window under a Top Bar, a frame). |
| The first pane | yes | Any element, with an `id` the handle points at. Its size is the handle's value. |
| `.canon-split-pane-handle` | yes | An empty `<div>`: `role="separator"`, `tabindex="0"`, named by what it resizes ("Resize the list"), `aria-controls` the first pane. |
| The second pane | yes | Any element; it takes the rest. |

- **Side by side or stacked:** the handle's `aria-orientation` says how it lies. `vertical` (a line between two columns): side by side. `horizontal` (a line between two rows): stacked.
- **The size** is the first pane's share, in percent: `aria-valuenow`, between `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`. Set limits that keep both panes usable.
- **Nesting:** a pane can be a Split Pane itself (a list beside a record with its activity under it).
- **Not a [Sidebar](sidebar.md):** the app's navigation collapses to a rail; a Split Pane shares one page between two parts of it.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-orientation` | the handle | `vertical` (side by side) · `horizontal` (stacked) | — (required) | — |
| `aria-valuenow` | the handle | the first pane's share, 0–100 | 50 | — |
| `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` | the handle | its limits, 0–100 | 0, 100 | — |
| `--canon-split-size` | the box (canon.js) | the first pane's share, a percentage | from `aria-valuenow` | — |
| `data-state` | the box (canon.js) | `resizing` while dragging | — | — |

## Core

- A grid: the first pane `--canon-split-size` of the box, the handle, the second pane the rest. Without canon.js, half each, and the handle is only the line between them: no resize cursor, nothing to drag (`@media (scripting: none)`).
- Each pane scrolls on its own; neither grows past the box.
- While dragging, nothing in the panes is selected or catches the pointer.

## Behavior (T2, canon.js)

- **Dragging** the handle (mouse, touch, pen) resizes the first pane within its limits; in right-to-left the first pane is on the right.
- **Keyboard** on the handle: the arrows along its direction (Left and Right side by side, mirrored in right-to-left; Up and Down stacked) by 2%, with Shift by 10%; Home and End to the limits; Enter folds the first pane to its minimum, and again brings it back.
- **Double click** the handle: back to the size it started with.
- canon.js keeps `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext` (the share as a percentage, in the page's language) and writes `--canon-split-size`.
- **`canon-resize`** fires on the box when a resize ends (`detail.size`): the app remembers it (and writes it back as `aria-valuenow` next time).

## Accessibility

- The handle is a focusable separator, heard with its name and value: "Resize the list, separator, 35%".
- Everything dragging does, the keyboard does too.
- The panes are in reading order; each pane's own landmarks and headings say what it is.

## Theme obligations

- The handle visible as a line between the panes with a grip on it, so it reads as something to drag; easy to grab (wider than it looks), and clearly marked on hover, focus and while dragging.
- In forced colors, the line and its focus still show.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the first pane is on the right.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| One pane at a time on narrow screens | The Master–Detail pattern |
| Limits in rem or px | If it comes up (a pane's own `min-inline-size` works meanwhile) |
| More than two panes in one box | Nest them |

## Look

**Sizes:** A 1px line, 8px to grab; a 4 × 24px grip on its middle (across it when stacked), 32px long while active.

The line zinc-200 (dark zinc-800), the grip zinc-300 (dark zinc-600); hover (after a short pause), focus and dragging color the line and the grip blue-500 (dark blue-400), the grip 32px long. Forced colors: the line and grip in the text's color, focus in Highlight.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/stack.md

# Stack, Cluster and Grid

Tier: **T0**

The space between components. Canon's components never set the space around themselves: what sits next to what, and how far apart, is a container's job. These three are those containers, and an app writes no spacing CSS of its own.

- **Stack:** things one under another, a steady gap apart: a page's sections, cards in a column, a form above a table.
- **Cluster:** things in a row that wrap when they run out of room: tags, a few buttons, a page's facts ("Draft · Edited 2 hours ago · Ada").
- **Grid:** equal columns, as many as fit: cards in a gallery, settings tiles, a dashboard's panels.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-stack" data-gap="xl">
  <section class="canon-section">…</section>

  <div class="canon-grid" data-columns="3">
    <section class="canon-card">…</section>
    <section class="canon-card">…</section>
    <section class="canon-card">…</section>
  </div>

  <div class="canon-cluster">
    <span class="canon-tag">…Design…</span>
    <span class="canon-tag">…Research…</span>
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-align="end">…Edit tags…</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-stack` | — | A `<div>` (or the element the content needs: a `<section>`, a `<ul>`). Its children one under another, each as wide as the stack. |
| `.canon-cluster` | — | A row of its children at their own widths, wrapping onto more lines, centered on each other. A child with `data-align="end"` goes to the row's end, and what follows it with it. |
| `.canon-grid` | — | Columns of equal width, at least `--canon-grid-min` each (16rem), as many as fit, up to `data-columns`; its children fill them in order. |

- **No roles, no names.** They are layout: they add nothing for assistive technology and change no reading order. A list of things is still a `<ul>` (`<ul class="canon-cluster">`), a group still a named group.
- **They nest:** a page is usually a Stack of Sections, whose content holds a Grid or a Cluster.
- **Buttons and other inline things go in a Cluster.** In a Stack every child is as wide as the stack, a Button too.
- **Not a [Toolbar](toolbar.md):** a Toolbar is one control (one Tab stop, arrow keys between); a Cluster is only space. **Not a [Form Layout](form-layout.md):** a form's fields, rows and sections have their own spacing; put the form in a Stack, not its fields.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-gap` | a stack, cluster or grid | `none` · `sm` · `md` · `lg` · `xl` | theme decides (Canon: `md`) | no: each one's own |
| `data-columns` | a grid | `2` · `3` · `4` · `5` · `6`: at most that many columns | as many as fit | no |
| `--canon-grid-min` | a grid (a style) | the narrowest a column may be | 16rem | — |
| `data-align` | a cluster's child | `end`: it, and what follows it, at the row's end | — | no |
| `data-size` | the container or one above | `sm` · `md` · `lg`: the gaps scale with it | theme decides | yes |

- **`data-gap` is the author's because only the author knows how related the things are.** Tags that belong together sit close (`sm`); a page's sections sit far apart (`xl`). Each step is a step of Canon's spacing at the current size, never a length.
- **It isn't inherited:** a stack inside a `data-gap="xl"` stack has its own gap (the theme's, unless it says).
- **`data-columns`** caps the count; the columns still narrow to one when there isn't room for two at `--canon-grid-min`. No breakpoints: the grid fits the room it has, wherever it is (a page, a Card, a Drawer).

## Core

- **Stack:** a flex column; children stretch to its width; their own block margins are dropped (the gap is the space).
- **Cluster:** a flex row that wraps, children centered on each other's middles; the gap both across and between lines. `data-align="end"` takes the free space before that child.
- **Grid:** `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(…, 1fr))`: a column is at least `--canon-grid-min` (never more than the grid's width), and, with `data-columns`, at least the share of `data-columns` columns, so no more than that many fit. Children can shrink below their content's width (`min-inline-size: 0`), so long words wrap instead of widening a column.
- `data-gap` and `data-columns` are hints (the `canon.hints` layer): they win over the theme. The gap's lengths are the theme's (`--canon-gap-sm` … `--canon-gap-xl`, at each size).

## Accessibility

- Nothing is announced: they are presentation only, and reading order is the markup's. A Cluster's `data-align="end"` moves a child visually only within its row, never before what precedes it.
- Right to left, rows and columns run from the right.

## Theme obligations

- Four gaps that read as clearly different steps, at every size, and a default.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left a Cluster starts at the right, and `end` is the left.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Two parts side by side that stack when narrow (a list and its detail) | [Split Pane](split-pane.md), or Form Layout's aside layout |
| Lines between children | [Separator](separator.md) between them; a row of stats has its own lines ([Stat](stat.md)) |
| Items spanning several columns, a masonry | If it comes up |
| Centering a page's content to a measure | The app's page CSS (an [App Shell](app-shell.md) holds the page) |

## Look

**Gaps (sm / md / lg sizes):** `sm` 4 / 8 / 12; `md` 12 / 16 / 20 (Fieldset's step between fields, the default); `lg` 16 / 24 / 32; `xl` 24 / 32 / 40 (Form Layout's step between sections); `none` 0. A grid's columns at least 16rem.

No look of their own: no lines, fills or padding.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/toolbar.md

# Toolbar

Tier: **T0** (the arrow keys between controls are T2, canon.js)

A row of controls that act on one thing, such as a text editor's formatting: Buttons, Button Groups, Selects, menu buttons and vertical Separators. One stop for Tab; the arrow keys move inside.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-toolbar" role="toolbar" aria-label="Formatting" data-size="sm">
  <div class="canon-button-group" role="group" aria-label="History" data-display="icon">
    <button type="button" class="canon-button">…Undo…</button>
    <button type="button" class="canon-button">…Redo…</button>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-select">
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="text-cursor" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <select aria-label="Text style">…</select>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-button-group" role="group" aria-label="Alignment" data-display="icon" data-select="one">
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" aria-pressed="true">…Align left…</button>
    …
  </div>
  <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral" data-display="icon">…Link…</button>
  <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral" popovertarget="insert-menu" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">…Insert…</button>
  <div class="canon-menu" id="insert-menu" popover role="menu" aria-label="Insert">…</div>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-toolbar` | yes | `role="toolbar"`, named by `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` ("Formatting"). |
| Controls | yes | [Buttons](button.md) (on their own: low and neutral, `data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral"`; icon only with `data-display="icon"`, toggles with `aria-pressed`), [Button Groups](button-group.md), [Selects](select.md), menu buttons ([Menu](menu.md)), vertical [Separators](separator.md). Menus and popovers they open can sit inside; they aren't part of the row. |

- **Order** is the DOM's: the arrow keys follow it, and so does wrapping.
- **Grouping:** related buttons go in a Button Group (named, joined); controls stand 8px apart otherwise. A vertical Separator marks a stronger break.
- A toolbar is for controls that act on something (the text, a selection). Navigation is a nav list or Menubar.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-orientation` | the toolbar | `vertical`: a column; Up and Down move | horizontal | — |
| `data-size` | the toolbar or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |
| `data-display` | a group, a button or a container | `icon` | theme decides | yes |

## Behavior

**T0:** a wrapping row of controls, each its own Tab stop.

**canon.js (T2), the toolbar pattern:**

- **One Tab stop:** the control last used (the first, to start). Tab leaves the toolbar; coming back lands on the same control.
- **Left and Right** (Up and Down when vertical; mirrored in right-to-left) move to the previous or next control, through groups too, wrapping at the ends; **Home** and **End** go to the ends.
- In a text field inside the toolbar, the arrows stay the field's. A Select keeps Up and Down; a menu button opens its menu with Down.
- A [Select](select.md) in a toolbar keeps the width of its longest choice (Select's own behavior), so the controls after it don't move.
- Disabled and hidden controls are skipped; controls added or removed later are followed.

## Core

- A wrapping flex row (a column when vertical), its controls their own size.

## Accessibility

- `role="toolbar"` with a name: screen readers announce it and its controls; one Tab stop keeps the page's tab order short.
- Every control keeps its own name (icon-only buttons through their label), and toggles their pressed state.

## Theme obligations

- Controls visibly grouped (groups joined, standalone controls apart); a single low neutral button looks like the toolbar's grouped buttons.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| An overflow menu for controls that don't fit | If it comes up (today the toolbar wraps) |
| Typing a letter to jump to a control | If it comes up |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Controls the given size (a text editor's: sm, 32px); 8px apart and 8px between rows.

Selects as they are; Button Groups as they are (one zinc-200 frame, dark zinc-600, a 1px line between buttons; pressed zinc-100, pressed in, with the icon in the label's color); a single button a low neutral Button, held while its menu is open. The Select's arrow is Select's chevron; Insert is a menu button with Button's menu chevron.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/top-bar.md

# Top Bar

Tier: **T0** · folding when narrow is **T2** (canon.js)

The bar over an app's pages: the sidebar's toggle and search at the start; the app's own actions and the account at the end. Usually inside an [App Shell](app-shell.md), beside a [Sidebar](sidebar.md).

## Elements

```html
<header class="canon-top-bar">
  <div class="canon-top-bar-start">
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral"
            commandfor="palette" command="show-modal" aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K Control+K">
      <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="search" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="canon-button-label">Search</span>
      <kbd class="canon-kbd" aria-hidden="true">⌘K</kbd>
    </button>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-top-bar-end">
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="medium" data-intent="neutral" data-display="icon" aria-pressed="false">…Dark mode…</button>
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="medium" data-intent="neutral" data-display="icon">
      <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="bell" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="canon-button-label">Notifications</span>
      <span class="canon-count">3<span class="canon-visually-hidden"> unread</span></span>
    </button>
    <button type="button" class="canon-avatar" id="account" popovertarget="account-menu" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">…</button>
    <div class="canon-menu" id="account-menu" popover role="menu" aria-labelledby="account">…</div>
  </div>
</header>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `header.canon-top-bar` | yes | A `<header>`: the page's banner when it isn't inside another landmark. |
| `.canon-top-bar-start` | no | The [Sidebar](sidebar.md)'s toggle, then search (a [Command Palette](command-palette.md)'s button). Where people are (a [Breadcrumb](breadcrumb.md), a back link) is the page's: it goes in its [Page Header](page-header.md). |
| `.canon-top-bar-end` | no | At the end: the app's own [Buttons](button.md) (icon only, neutral), then the account: an [Avatar](avatar.md) button opening a [Menu](menu.md). |

- **Search** is a Command Palette's button, not a field: it opens the palette (also with its shortcut from anywhere). A field that searches in place is a [Combobox](combobox.md).
- **A toggle** (dark mode) is a Button with `aria-pressed`; **notifications** a Button with a [Count](count.md), which an icon-only button carries in its top-end corner.
- **What belongs here:** what stays the same on every page (search, creating things, help, notifications, the account, the workspace or environment, the language). What changes with the page (its title, its actions, a dashboard's date range, who else is viewing, "Saved") goes in its Page Header, under the bar.

## Core
