- A row: the start, then the end at the far end. The start gives up room first: what doesn't fit is cut at its end, never drawn under the end.

## Behavior (T2, canon.js)

- **Folding:** when its things don't fit, the bar folds, a step at a time, and unfolds as room comes back. The steps, each only where it applies:
  1. `kbd`: the search drops its shortcut.
  2. `search`: then its label (the Button becomes icon only, keeping its name).
  3. `end`: the end's Buttons go into one **More** menu (an icon Button, where the first of them was, with their emphasis): a toggle (`aria-pressed`) as a check, a Button opening a [Menu](menu.md) as a submenu; choosing an item clicks the Button it stands for. Only when two or more would fold.
- **Never folds:** the sidebar's toggle, a Button carrying a [Count](count.md) (notifications: live state stays in sight), and the account.
- `data-fold` on the bar lists the steps taken (`"kbd search end"`), for themes; folded things get `data-folded`. Fixed steps rather than one item at a time, so the bar looks the same at the same width and each step can be shown.
- Without JavaScript nothing folds; the start is cut instead.

## Accessibility

- A banner landmark (its `<header>`), so people can jump to it; the account and notifications are named buttons.
- The search button's shortcut is in `aria-keyshortcuts`; its Kbd is hidden from screen readers.
- Folded, every Button keeps its name: the search as an icon Button, the end's as items of the More menu (named "More", `--canon-text-more`).

## Theme obligations

- Set apart from the page (a line, a fill); readable in both schemes.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the start is on the right.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A notifications panel | A [Popover](popover.md) or a Drawer from the button |
| Tabs across the top | Tabs |

## Look

**Sizes:** sm / md / lg (the size scale): 48 / 64 / 80 tall (a row and the shell's inset of 8 / 12 / 16 above and below); 16 / 20 / 24 at the sides; 12 / 16 / 20 between things. Folded: the More button the end's emphasis (medium neutral), Lucide's `more` dots.

White (dark zinc-900), a hairline under it in the shell's faint rule (black at 7%, dark white at 8%); search the Command Palette's button as it is (a low neutral Button with its Kbd); dark mode and notifications medium neutral icon Buttons; the Count a rose pill 4px past the button's corner; the account an Avatar button a row's size.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/button.md

# Button

Tier: **T0** (toggle behavior is T2, or T0 via a form round trip; copy is T2)

## Elements

| Element | When |
|---|---|
| `<button type="…">` | It **does** something: submit, open, delete, toggle |
| `<a href="…">` | It **goes** somewhere |

- `type` is **required** on every `<button>` (`button`, `submit` or `reset`).
- Not allowed: `<input type="submit">`, `<div role="button">`, `<a>` for actions.

## Anatomy

```
canon-button
├── canon-icon            optional · leading
├── canon-button-label    required, always (also on icon-only buttons)
├── canon-icon            optional · trailing
└── accessory             optional · canon-kbd (canon-count reserved)
```

```html
<button type="button" class="canon-button">
  <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="plus" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="canon-button-label">New user</span>
</button>
```

- At most one icon on each side of the label.
- Icon position is DOM order. Themes detect leading/trailing structurally and may override it.
- The trailing icon is for icons that carry meaning ("Next →", "Export ⬇"). Indicator icons are never written (see "Drawn by the theme").
- A keyboard shortcut is a `canon-kbd` accessory with `aria-hidden="true"`; the button gets `aria-keyshortcuts` (e.g. `"Meta+K"`) so assistive tech announces it once, and only where the shortcut really works. See [kbd.md](kbd.md).

```html
<button type="button" class="canon-button" aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K">
  <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="search" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="canon-button-label">Search</span>
  <kbd class="canon-kbd" aria-hidden="true">⌘K</kbd>
</button>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data-emphasis` | `high` · `medium` · `low` · `minimal` | `medium` | no |
| `data-intent` | `neutral` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` | none (the accent) | no |
| `data-size` | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |
| `data-display` | `icon` | theme decides | yes |

### Emphasis: how strongly the action asks for attention relative to its neighbors

| Value | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| `high` | **The** action of this view (one per view, by convention) | Save, Create user |
| `medium` | An alternative action | Export, Duplicate |
| `low` | Available, not encouraged | Cancel, Back |
| `minimal` | Repeated or ambient actions | Row actions, toolbars, dialog close |

### Intent: what kind of consequence the action has (independent of emphasis)

| Value | Consequence | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| none | Ordinary, in the theme's accent | Save, Export, Create |
| `neutral` | Ordinary, without an accent: actions that shouldn't draw the eye | Cancel, a toolbar's buttons, a data table's Filter and Columns, a search trigger, Close |

**Accent or neutral?** The accent is for what the view is for (Save, Create, Apply, Publish, Invite people, an empty state's way forward). Everything that serves it is neutral: Cancel, Back, Discard; buttons that open a menu, a popover, a dialog or a drawer ("Options", "Filters", "Link"); toolbar and row actions, "…" menus; Close; Clear all, Load more, Add another, Change. Danger, warning and success keep their intents.
| `danger` | Destructive or irreversible | Delete user, Revoke access |
| `warning` | Risky, bypasses a safeguard | Force deploy, Override lock, Proceed anyway |
| `success` | Gives a positive verdict | Approve, Accept request, Mark resolved |

Themes design **4 emphasis × 5 intents = 20 variants**.

### `data-display="icon"`

Hides the label visually; the label stays in the DOM as the accessible name. It can come from the author (on the button or a container) or from the theme (context, container queries).

```html
<button type="button" class="canon-button" data-display="icon">
  <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="trash" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="canon-button-label">Delete</span>
</button>
```

## States

| State | Hook | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Hover / active / focus | `:hover` · `:active` · `:focus-visible` | |
| Disabled | `disabled` or `aria-disabled="true"` | Styled the same. `aria-disabled` keeps focus (for tooltips) and is the only option for `<a>`. It does not block clicks; the author handles that. |
| Loading | `aria-busy="true"` | The theme draws the indicator ([Spinner](spinner.md)'s ring, in place of the leading icon). The author may change the label ("Saving…") and should add `aria-disabled="true"`. |
| Pressed (toggle) | `aria-pressed="true\|false"` | A toggle button is a Button. canon.js (T2) flips it on click, like a checkbox: before the click's listeners, and back if one calls `preventDefault()` (an app that keeps the state itself). Not command or submit buttons. In a [Button Group](button-group.md), `data-select="one"` keeps one pressed. |
| Expanded | `aria-expanded="true\|false"` | Set by JS or a polyfill. |
| Current | `aria-current="page"` | For button-styled links to the current page. |
| Copied | `data-state="copied"` | Set by canon.js for 2 seconds after `--canon-copy`. See "Copy". |

### Toggle button without JS (form round trip)

```html
<form method="post" action="/tickets/42/pin">
  <button type="submit" class="canon-button" aria-pressed="true" name="pinned" value="false">
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="pin" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="canon-button-label">Pinned</span>
  </button>
</form>
```

## Copy (T2, canon.js)

A copy button is a Button with the `--canon-copy` command ([invoker commands](field.md#box-actions-t2-canonjs)), not a component of its own. `commandfor` names what it copies: an input's or textarea's value, otherwise the element's text.

```html
<span id="invite-link">https://example.com/invite/7Fq2</span>
<button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" commandfor="invite-link" command="--canon-copy">
  <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="copy" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="canon-button-label">Copy link</span>
</button>
```

- **The confirmation:** the button gets `data-state="copied"` for 2 seconds and canon.js announces "Copied" (the string `--canon-text-copied`). The label stays; the theme shows the state (Canon: the `copy` icon becomes a check, popping in).
- **Say what it copies** when there are several ("Copy link", "Copy API key"), also on an icon-only button, whose label is its name.
- **In a field's box** (an API key, a token): a trailing button, see Field's [box actions](field.md#box-actions-t2-canonjs).
- Without scripting the button is hidden, like every Canon command button. Where the browser refuses the clipboard (an insecure page, a denied permission), nothing is copied and no confirmation shows.

## Drawn by the theme, never written in HTML

| Visual | Trigger |
|---|---|
| Menu indicator (chevron, triangle, …) | `[aria-haspopup]` |
| Loading indicator | `[aria-busy="true"]` |
| External-link indicator | `a[target="_blank"]`, heard as "(opens in new tab)" (`--canon-text-opens-in-new-tab`) |
| Focus ring | `:focus-visible` |

## Theme obligations

- Style `disabled` and `aria-disabled="true"` identically.
- Hide labels with the visually-hidden technique (clipping), **never** `display: none`.
- Render all 20 emphasis × intent variants. Variants **may look identical** when the theme's language calls for it (a theme whose main button is green may draw success + high as its default button).
- Draw the indicators listed above.
- Confirm `data-state="copied"` visibly (an icon change, a color), without changing the button's size.
- **Icons on labeled buttons may be hidden** (they are `aria-hidden`, i.e. decorative). Icons on icon-only buttons must always be shown.
- When the source system conflicts with the contract, the contract wins (e.g. `pointer-events: none` only on `disabled`, never on `aria-disabled`).

## Not in the contract

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Shape (pill, square, circle) | Theme |
| Full width | Container layout |
| Link-styled button | [Link](link.md) on a `<button>`: `class="canon-link"` |
| Inverse / on-dark | Theme, from context |
| Split button, button group | Separate components |
| Checkbox styled as a button | [Toggle Chip](toggle-chip.md) |
| Ripple | Out of scope |

**Lift:** a low button (the framed one) has a faint lift under it (0 1px 2px, black at 5%; dark 30%), gone while pressed and when disabled, like Text Input's; a Button Group has it under its frame.

**Motion:** pressed, a button with words gives a little (98%, 0.1s); icon buttons and the joined halves of a Button Group or a Split Button don't. Copied, the check pops in from 50% and fades in (0.2s). Neither with reduced motion.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/button-group.md

# Button Group

Tier: **T0** (toggling is T2: canon.js flips `aria-pressed`)

Related buttons joined in one row: text styles, alignment, actions on one thing. The buttons are ordinary [Buttons](button.md) in a named group; the theme draws them as one piece.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-button-group" role="group" aria-label="Text style">
  <button type="button" class="canon-button" aria-pressed="true">
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="bold" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="canon-button-label">Bold</span>
  </button>
  <button type="button" class="canon-button" aria-pressed="false">
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="italic" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="canon-button-label">Italic</span>
  </button>
  …
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-button-group` | yes | `role="group"`, named by `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` ("Text style", "Alignment"). |
| `.canon-button` | yes | Two or more, `<button>` or `<a>`, each a complete Button (its own label, also when only the icon shows). |
| `.canon-tooltip` | no | A button's tooltip, right after it ([Tooltip](tooltip.md)); it takes no place in the row. |

- **Each button does its own thing.** Tab moves through them one by one, as through any buttons. (A toolbar's single tab stop with arrow keys is Toolbar's job.)
- **Toggles:** buttons that switch something on and off carry `aria-pressed` ([Button](button.md)); canon.js flips it on click. Any number can be on (bold, italic, underline), or one at a time with `data-select="one"` (alignment). A choice that is a form value (one of several, submitted with the form) is a [Segmented Control](segmented-control.md), a radio group.
- Buttons stay in one row; a group never wraps. Groups next to each other (a toolbar) wrap as wholes.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-select` | the group | `one`: pressing a toggle releases the others; the pressed one stays pressed · `any` | `any` | no |
| `data-size` | the group or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` (xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes |
| `data-display` | the group or a container | `icon`: every label hidden, square buttons | theme decides | yes |
| `data-intent` | a button | `neutral` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` | none | no |

- `data-emphasis` on buttons in a group: a group is one piece, so themes may draw every emphasis alike (Canon does). `data-intent` still shows (a Delete in a group stays red).

## Behavior (canon.js)

- **A click flips `aria-pressed`, like a checkbox:** before the click's listeners run, so they read the new state, and back if one cancels the click (`preventDefault()`). An app that keeps the state itself (a text editor, from the selection) cancels the click and sets `aria-pressed` as it needs.
- **`data-select="one"`:** the clicked toggle is pressed and the group's others released; clicking the pressed one leaves it pressed.
- Not for command buttons (the command sets the state) or submit buttons (the server does). The same applies to a toggle Button outside a group.
- Without canon.js the buttons show their state but don't flip; the app (or a form round trip) does.

## States

Each button's own ([Button](button.md)): hover, focus (its ring shows over the neighbours), pressed (`aria-pressed="true"`, drawn as clearly held), disabled (`disabled` or `aria-disabled="true"`). A group with every button disabled is disabled.

## Core

- An inline flex row (`max-inline-size: 100%`), buttons at their own width. Nothing else: the joining is the theme's.

## Accessibility

- The group's name says what the buttons share; each button's label says what it does. Icon-only buttons keep their label as their name, and can show it in a tooltip.
- Pressed state is `aria-pressed`, heard as "pressed" / "not pressed".

## Theme obligations

- Draw the buttons as one piece (Canon: one frame), the ends rounded as the theme's buttons.
- Keep the focus ring visible over the neighbours.
- A pressed button clearly held, by more than color alone where the system allows (Canon: filled, pressed in by an inner shadow, and a darker icon).
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the group runs from the right.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| One tab stop, arrow keys between buttons | Toolbar |
| A choice that is a form value | [Segmented Control](segmented-control.md) |
| Vertical groups | If it comes up (`data-orientation`) |
| A menu button in a group (split button) | Split Button |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** The group 32 / 40 / 48 tall, its ends rounded 4 / 8 / 12; the buttons its full height, their padding the button's; icon only, square (32 / 40 / 48).

The buttons joined in one frame: a zinc-200 line (dark zinc-600) around them and a 1px line between them that takes no space, like a [Toolbar](toolbar.md)'s single buttons and Selects, with the low button's faint lift under the frame. Labels zinc-900 (dark white), icons zinc-500 (dark zinc-300); disabled labels zinc-400, icons zinc-300 (dark both zinc-500). Hover zinc-50 (dark zinc-800), pressing zinc-100 (dark zinc-700). Pressed (`aria-pressed`): zinc-100 (dark zinc-700), pressed in by an inner shadow (0 1px 2px, black at 8%; dark 40%), the icon in the label's color; pressed and disabled, zinc-50 (dark zinc-800) without the shadow. Forced colors: pressed in Highlight, the lines between buttons borders. Focus: the button's ring (2px white, 1px blue-600; dark zinc-900, blue-400). Every emphasis alike; an intent colors label and icon, and hover and pressing take its tints, the low button's (danger: red-400 at 8% / 15%; dark red-500 at 10% / 20%).

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/link.md

# Link

Tier: **T0**

Text that goes somewhere: in a sentence ("see how payouts work"), or on its own ("View all invoices"). It takes the text's font and size.

## Elements

```html
<p>Payments arrive within two working days. See <a class="canon-link" href="/payouts">how payouts work</a>.</p>

<a class="canon-link" href="/invoices" data-standalone>
  View all invoices
  <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="arrow-forward" aria-hidden="true"></span>
</a>
```

| Element | When |
|---|---|
| `<a class="canon-link" href="…">` | It **goes** somewhere: another page, a place on this one, a file. |
| `<button type="button" class="canon-link">` | It **does** something, from inside text ("Didn't get the code? Send it again."). Elsewhere, an action is a [Button](button.md). |
| `.canon-icon` | Optional, before or after the text, `aria-hidden="true"`: the text names the link. |

- **Its text says where it goes** on its own ("how payouts work", not "click here"): screen reader users often list a page's links.
- **With an icon** the link is one piece (the text still wraps inside it), and the gap between icon and text is the theme's; the markup's spaces don't matter.
- **Not for actions outside text,** and not a Button with a link's look for navigation: an `<a class="canon-button">` goes somewhere and looks like a button ([Button](button.md)).

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-standalone` | the link | (present): on its own, outside a sentence (under a list, in a card, a table cell) | in text | no |
| `data-emphasis` | the link | `low`: the surrounding text's color (a footer, fine print) | the theme's link color | no |
| `target="_blank"` (native) | `<a>` | opens a new tab | | — |
| `disabled` (native) | `<button>` | | | — |
| `aria-disabled="true"` | `<a>` without `href` | a link that can't go anywhere now | | — |

- **In text a link is underlined** (it shows by more than its color). A standalone link's place says it's a link, so the theme may drop the underline until hover or focus. A low link keeps its underline: its color doesn't tell it apart.
- **A new tab** (`target="_blank"`) only when leaving would lose the person's work. The theme draws the indicator, and screen readers hear "(opens in new tab)" (the `--canon-text-opens-in-new-tab` string, translated in `i18n/`). Browsers don't let the new page reach this one (no `rel` needed).
- No size: a link is as big as its text (a heading's, a `<small>`'s).

## States

| State | Hook |
|---|---|
| Hover, active, focus | `:hover`, `:active`, `:focus-visible` |
| Disabled | `disabled` (button), `aria-disabled="true"` (a link without `href`) |
| Visited | `:visited`, the theme's choice (app links usually show none) |

## Core

- Inline, in the text's font; icons are 1em. A `<button class="canon-link">` loses the button's box (no padding, border or background) and flows as text.
- With an icon: an inline flex row, the text setting the baseline, the icon centered, a `--canon-link-gap` (0.25em) between.

## Accessibility

- A link's name is its text; icons are hidden. A new tab is announced through the indicator's alternative text.
- A disabled `<a>` has no `href`: it isn't focusable or announced as a link, so say nearby why it isn't available when it matters.
- The focus ring follows the text across lines.

## Theme obligations

- A link in text tells itself apart from the text by more than color (an underline), in every color scheme.
- Hover and focus visible; focus as a ring around the text, on every line it wraps to.
- Draw the new-tab indicator with the `--canon-text-opens-in-new-tab` alternative text, mirrored where it points.
- Use logical properties: icons and the indicator follow the text's direction.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Plain `<a>` in long-form text (articles, docs) | Prose foundation (the Rich Text area already draws its links this way) |
| A link to the current page | Nav List, Tabs, Breadcrumb (`aria-current`) |
| Intents (a red link) | A [Button](button.md) with `data-intent`, if it comes up |
| Download size and format ("PDF, 2 MB") | The author's words after the link |

## Look

**Sizes:** The text's; icons 1em, 0.25em from the text; the new-tab icon 0.875em, 0.2em after it.

The rich text area's links made a component. Blue-600 (dark blue-400), hover blue-700 (dark blue-300); underlined 1px at 0.2em, the line at 40% of the color, full on hover. Standalone: no line until hover or focus. Low: the text's color, always underlined. Focus: a 1px blue-600 ring 2px out (dark blue-400), 2px corners. Disabled zinc-400 (dark zinc-600). New tab: Lucide's external icon, mirrored right to left. No visited color.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/segmented-control.md

# Segmented Control

Tier: **T0**

One value from a few, as joined segments: a view (Day, Week, Month), a period (Monthly, Yearly), an alignment. It is a radio group: the chosen option is a form value, and the keyboard is the browser's.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-segmented" role="radiogroup" aria-label="Calendar view">
  <label class="canon-segmented-option">
    <input type="radio" name="view" value="day">
    <span class="canon-segmented-label">Day</span>
  </label>
  <label class="canon-segmented-option">
    <input type="radio" name="view" value="week" checked>
    <span class="canon-segmented-label">Week</span>
  </label>
  <label class="canon-segmented-option">
    <input type="radio" name="view" value="month">
    <span class="canon-segmented-label">Month</span>
  </label>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-segmented` | yes | `role="radiogroup"`, named by `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. In a [Field](field.md) it takes the box's place and is named by the field's label (a `<span id>`, as for [Swatches](swatches.md)); a description is linked with `aria-describedby` on the group. As wide as its options. |
| `<label class="canon-segmented-option">` | yes | Two or more, the group's only children. Each wraps its radio, an optional icon and its text. |
| `<input type="radio">` | yes | The option's first child, one per option, the same `name` across the group. `value` is what the form submits. One is `checked`. |
| `.canon-icon` | no | Before the text, `aria-hidden="true"`. |
| `.canon-segmented-label` | yes | The option's text, also when only the icon shows (it stays as the option's name). |

- **One option is always chosen:** `checked` on one radio. A choice with no default, longer labels, descriptions or more than about five options are [Radio](radio.md) buttons.
- **Not Tabs:** [Tabs](tabs.md) switch between panels of content, each its own (General, Billing, Members); a Segmented Control sets a value for the same content (the same calendar by day, week or month). Both are a raised card on a track in Canon; Tabs carry icons and counts and head a page's parts.
- **Not a Button Group:** toggles (`aria-pressed`) change the interface right away and aren't form values (bold, italic); see [Button Group](button-group.md).
- **The keyboard is the radio group's:** Tab reaches the chosen option, the arrow keys choose the next one (skipping disabled ones). Choosing fires the radios' `change`.
- **No intents:** a choice between options has nothing to warn about.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-size` | the group or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` (xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes |
| `data-display` | the group or a container | `icon`: the text hidden, square options | theme decides | yes |
| `data-fill` | the group | present: as wide as its place, the options sharing it equally | absent: as wide as its options | no |
| `checked`, `disabled` (native) | a radio | | | — |

- `disabled` on a radio: that option can't be chosen. On every radio, or a disabled `<fieldset>` around the group, the whole control is disabled and keeps showing its value.

## States

| State | Hook |
|---|---|
| Chosen | `:has(> input:checked)` on the option |
| Hover, pressing | `:hover`, `:active` on the option |
| Focus | `:has(> input:focus-visible)` on the option |
| Disabled | `:has(> input:disabled)` on the option |

## Core

- The group is an inline flex row, as wide as its options (`max-inline-size: 100%`); with `data-fill`, as wide as its place, the options sharing it. Options are centered rows that don't wrap; in too narrow a place they shrink and cut their text (…), keeping their full name.
- Each radio covers its option, invisible (`opacity: 0`, `appearance: none`): clicks, touch, screen readers' exploring and the keyboard reach the real radio.

## Accessibility

- A radio group: the group's name, each option's name (its text), its state (checked) and the arrow keys come from the native radios. Heard as "Week, radio button, checked, 2 of 3".
- Icon-only options keep their text as their name. Tooltips can't attach to radios yet; choose icons that read without one.
- The chosen option is marked by more than color: its raised card, and its darker label.

## Theme obligations

- The chosen option unmistakable at a glance, by more than color; hover clearly weaker than chosen.
- Focus visible on the option, over its neighbours.
- In forced colors, the chosen option still shows (Canon: the system highlight).
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the options run from the right.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Tooltips on icon-only options | When Tooltip supports radios |
| Several values at once | [Toggle Chips](toggle-chip.md) (checkboxes) |
| Switching panels of content | [Tabs](tabs.md) (the same look) |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** The group 32 / 40 / 48 tall with 3px inside and 2px between options, its corners Button's plus 2px (6 / 10 / 14); options 26 / 34 / 42, corners 3px tighter (3 / 7 / 11), so the card's curve follows the track's; padded and set as a button (Button Group's type); icon only, square.

A filled track, no lines: zinc-100 (dark zinc-800). Labels and icons zinc-600 (dark zinc-400); hover darkens the label to zinc-900 (dark white), pressing adds zinc-200 at 60% (dark zinc-700 at 60%). The chosen option is a white card (dark zinc-700) lifted by a ring of black at 6% (dark white at 6%) and a soft shadow (0 1px 2px at 8%, 0 1px 3px at 5%), its label zinc-950 (dark white). Focus: the button's ring (2px white, 1px blue-600; dark zinc-900, blue-400). Disabled labels zinc-400 (dark zinc-600); chosen and disabled, a flat card (the ring, no shadow; a zinc-400 label, dark zinc-500). The chosen card is drawn once by the track and anchored to the chosen option, so it glides to the next one (0.3s, fast then settling; none with reduced motion); without anchor positioning, and in forced colors, each option draws its own. Forced colors: the chosen option in Highlight.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/split-button.md

# Split Button

Tier: **T1** (the arrow opens its menu with the browser's popover) · the menu's keyboard is **T2** ([Menu](menu.md))

A button with a menu beside it: the action people usually want one click away, its variations one more ("Add", or add from a template, import…). Two [Buttons](button.md) joined, the second opening a [Menu](menu.md).

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-split-button">
  <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="high">
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="plus" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="canon-button-label">Add</span>
  </button>
  <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="high" data-display="icon"
          popovertarget="add-menu" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">
    <span class="canon-button-label">More ways to add</span>
  </button>
</div>

<div class="canon-menu" id="add-menu" popover role="menu" aria-label="More ways to add">…</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-split-button` | yes | Exactly two Buttons. |
| The action | yes | A Button: what it does without the menu. |
| The arrow | yes | A Button with `data-display="icon"`, `popovertarget` (its menu) and `aria-haspopup="menu"`. Its label says what the menu holds ("More ways to add", "More save options"): it is the button's name. The arrow itself is the theme's (Button's menu indicator). |
| The menu | yes | A [Menu](menu.md), outside the split button, named like the arrow (`aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` the arrow). |

- **One look:** both buttons carry the same `data-emphasis` and `data-intent` (a Delete with "Delete permanently" in its menu is danger on both).
- **Size:** `data-size` on the split button sizes both; the menu takes it from a container around both, or carries its own.
- **Minimal** suits toolbars ("Text color ▾": the action applies the last choice, the arrow picks another). Themes may draw it as one piece at rest and show the two halves only on hover, focus or while the menu is open.
- Each button keeps its own states: the arrow alone can be `disabled` (nothing else to offer just now); both disabled disable the split button.
- Not a group of equals: buttons that are alternatives side by side are a [Button Group](button-group.md).

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-emphasis` | both buttons | Button's | `medium` | no |
| `data-intent` | both buttons | Button's | neutral | no |
| `data-size` | the split button or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |

## Behavior

Each button is a Button; the arrow opens its menu like any menu button (Menu's behavior: Down or Enter opens it at the first item, a choice closes it and returns to the arrow). canon.js marks the menu `data-split-button`: it opens under the arrow and ends where the split button ends (flipping to fit).

## States

Button's, on each half. Open: `aria-expanded="true"` on the arrow.

## Core

- An inline flex row of the two buttons. The menu (`data-split-button`): `position-area: self-block-end span-self-inline-start`.

## Accessibility

- Two buttons, each with its own name: "Add", "More ways to add, menu, collapsed". Two Tab stops.
- The arrow's name says what is in the menu, not "More" or "Options" alone.

## Theme obligations

- Join the two buttons (one piece, a line or gap between) and show the arrow on the second.
- Keep the focus ring visible over the neighbour.

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Button's sizes (32 / 40 / 48); the arrow square.

The two joined, corners only at the ends; between them a hairline that takes no space, the button's own tint laid over it: white at 15% on high, the medium tint (tone-400 at 15%; dark tone-500 at 20%) on medium, the low border (tone-200; dark tone-300 at 35%) on low; disabled zinc-200 (dark zinc-800). Minimal (a toolbar's "Text color ▾") is one quiet piece at rest, with no line; pointing at either half, focusing it or opening the menu joins them: both take the lightest tint (tone-400 at 8%), the half in use a stronger one (15%, pressed 20%), and the line shows in the low border's color. The arrow is the menu chevron, turning up while open, the arrow held at the pressed look. The menu opens 4px under it, ends level. Minimal, intents, dark mode and states, from Button.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/toggle-chip.md

# Toggle Chip

Tier: **T0**

Options you turn on and off, drawn as chips: quick filters (Remote, Full-time), interests, categories. Each chip is a checkbox, or a radio when only one can be on; its value is sent with the form.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-toggle-chips" role="group" aria-label="Job type">
  <label class="canon-toggle-chip">
    <input type="checkbox" name="job-type" value="remote" checked>
    <span class="canon-toggle-chip-label">Remote</span>
  </label>
  <label class="canon-toggle-chip">
    <input type="checkbox" name="job-type" value="contract">
    <span class="canon-toggle-chip-label">Contract</span>
  </label>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-toggle-chips` | for a set | The set's only container: `role="group"` for checkboxes, `role="radiogroup"` for radios, named by `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. A wrapping row. In a [Field](field.md) it takes the box's place and is named by the field's label (a `<span id>`, as for [Swatches](swatches.md)); a description is linked with `aria-describedby` on the group. A single checkbox chip needs no set. |
| `<label class="canon-toggle-chip">` | yes | Wraps its input, an optional icon and its text. |
| `<input type="checkbox">` or `<input type="radio">` | yes | The chip's first child, named; `value` is what the form submits. Radios share a `name` and live in a set. |
| `.canon-icon` | no | Before the text, `aria-hidden="true"`. While the chip is on, the theme's check takes its place. |
| `.canon-toggle-chip-label` | yes | The chip's text and name. |

- **Checkboxes:** any number on; Tab moves from chip to chip, Space turns one on or off.
- **Radios** (`role="radiogroup"`): one on at a time; Tab reaches the chosen chip, the arrow keys move between them. For a few short options in one row, a [Segmented Control](segmented-control.md) reads better; chips suit a longer set that wraps (sizes, time slots).
- **Not a Tag:** a [Tag](tag.md) shows something and can at most be removed. **Not a Checkbox list:** [Checkbox](checkbox.md) suits longer labels, descriptions, a form read top to bottom. **Not a Button toggle:** `aria-pressed` changes the interface right away and isn't a form value ([Button](button.md)).
- Choosing fires the input's `change`; an app filtering as you click listens there.
- **No intents.**

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-size` | a chip, the set or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` (xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes |
| `checked`, `disabled` (native) | an input | | | — |

## States

| State | Hook |
|---|---|
| On | `:has(> input:checked)` on the chip |
| Hover, pressing | `:hover`, `:active` on the chip |
| Focus | `:has(> input:focus-visible)` on the chip |
| Disabled | `:has(> input:disabled)` on the chip |

## Core

- The set is a wrapping flex row, as wide as its chips (`max-inline-size: 100%`). A chip is an inline row that doesn't wrap; wider than the room, it cuts its text (…) and keeps its full name.
- Each input covers its chip, invisible (`opacity: 0`, `appearance: none`), as in Segmented Control: clicks, touch, screen readers and the keyboard reach the real input.

## Accessibility

- Checkboxes and radios: the set's name, each chip's name (its text), its state and the keys come from the native inputs. Heard as "Remote, checkbox, checked" ("M, radio button, checked, 3 of 6").
- On is marked by more than color: the check.

## Theme obligations

- On unmistakable by more than color; hover clearly weaker than on.
- Turning a chip on or off never changes its width, so the chips after it stay where they are (Canon: a chip without an icon keeps the check's room while off).
- Focus visible on the chip.
- In forced colors, chips that are on still show (Canon: the system highlight).
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the chips run from the right.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A count on a chip ("Remote 12") | A [Count](count.md) accessory, if it comes up |
| A chip that removes itself | [Tag](tag.md) with its remove button |
| A row of filters with facets | [Filter Bar](filter-bar.md) (chips sit in it as quick filters) |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Chips 24 / 32 / 40 tall (a control's height − 8), padded and set as a button, fully rounded, 6 / 8 / 10 apart; icons and the check the icon size.

Button's look as a chip. A zinc-200 line (dark zinc-700), labels zinc-700 (dark zinc-200), icons zinc-500 (dark zinc-400); hover zinc-50 with a zinc-300 line (dark zinc-800, zinc-600), pressing zinc-100 (dark zinc-700). On: a neutral high Button's colors, zinc-900 with a white label (dark: white with zinc-900), hover zinc-800 (dark zinc-200), pressing zinc-700 (dark zinc-300), and a check before the label in place of the icon; a chip without an icon keeps the check's room while off, half on each side, and the check grows into it (0.15s, none with reduced motion), so its width never changes; hover and pressing a step stronger. Focus: the button's ring (2px white, 1px blue-600; dark zinc-900, blue-400). Disabled: zinc-400 labels, a zinc-100 line (dark zinc-600, zinc-800); on and disabled, zinc-100 (dark zinc-800). Forced colors: on in Highlight.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/checkbox.md

# Checkbox

Tier: **T0** (indeterminate needs one line of the author's JS)

Select any number of options; the choice takes effect on submit. For an on/off setting that applies immediately, use Switch.

Anatomy, states and shared obligations: `choice.md`. Groups: `fieldset.md`.

```html
<div class="canon-choice">
  <input type="checkbox" id="terms" name="terms" required
         aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="terms-message">
  <label class="canon-choice-label" for="terms">I accept the terms of service</label>
  <p class="canon-choice-message" id="terms-message" data-intent="danger">Accept the terms to continue.</p>
</div>
```

- Alone (a single yes/no like accepting terms) or in a fieldset (select any of several).
- A single invalid checkbox gets `aria-invalid="true"` and a danger `canon-choice-message`. In a group, the fieldset's message carries the error.

## Indeterminate

HTML has no attribute for it. The author's JS sets the property; themes style `:indeterminate`:

```js
document.getElementById("select-all").indeterminate = true;
```

- **Theme obligation:** scope indeterminate styles to checkboxes (`[type="checkbox"]:indeterminate`). A radio is `:indeterminate` whenever no radio in its group is checked.
- canon.js does nothing with it in v1.

## Size

**sm:** 16px box (control), 12px label

**md / lg:** 20 / 24px, 14 / 16px label

## Look

**Box:** The control is the icon size (16 / 20 / 24), the box 90% of it with corners a quarter of it (4 / 5 / 6px), a 1px zinc-400 line (dark zinc-500); label 12 / 14 / 16px on 16 / 20 / 24px lines, 6 / 8 / 8px away. Hover: a zinc-600 line (dark zinc-300) and a 3px zinc-100 halo (dark zinc-800). Focus: a 1px blue-600 ring (dark blue-300) 2px out, around box and label. Disabled: zinc-200 fill (dark zinc-600), label zinc-400 (dark zinc-500)

**Checked:** a neutral high Button's colors: zinc-900 fill with Lucide square-check's check in white (dark: white with a zinc-900 check), stroke 1 / 1.25 / 1.5px; hover keeps the halo; disabled zinc-300 with a zinc-100 check (dark zinc-600, zinc-400). Indeterminate: the same with a dash

**Invalid:** Text Input's error line (red-400, dark red-500; hover red-600 with a red-100 halo).

**Motion:** a squeeze and a stroke. Pressing squeezes the box (to 82%, 0.08s); let go, it eases back to its size (0.2s), without overshooting. Checking, the fill comes in (0.08s) and the check (or the dash) is drawn along its stroke, the short leg then the long one (0.22s from 0.05s, eased in and out); unchecking, the mark goes at once and the fill fades. None with reduced motion.

## Deferred

- **Select-all helper** in canon.js (a parent checkbox reflecting its children as indeterminate).

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/radio.md

# Radio

Tier: **T0**

Select exactly one option of a group.

Anatomy, states and shared obligations: `choice.md`. Groups: `fieldset.md`.

```html
<fieldset class="canon-fieldset" aria-describedby="plan-message">
  <legend class="canon-fieldset-legend">Plan</legend>
  <div class="canon-choice">
    <input type="radio" id="plan-free" name="plan" value="free" required>
    <label class="canon-choice-label" for="plan-free">Free</label>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-choice">
    <input type="radio" id="plan-team" name="plan" value="team" required>
    <label class="canon-choice-label" for="plan-team">Team</label>
  </div>
  <p class="canon-fieldset-message" id="plan-message" data-intent="danger">Choose a plan.</p>
</fieldset>
```

- **Radios are always inside a fieldset** (the legend is the question). The contract check outlines a radio that isn't.
- `required` on any radio makes the group required.
- The error belongs to the group: a danger `canon-fieldset-message`.
- Orientation is the fieldset's hint (`data-orientation`). Without it, the theme decides (Canon stacks them).

## Size

**sm:** 16px circle (control), 12px label

**md / lg:** 20 / 24px, 14 / 16px label

## Look

**Ring:** Checkbox's, round. The control is the icon size (16 / 20 / 24); the circle 90% of it, a 1px zinc-400 line (dark zinc-500); label 12 / 14 / 16px on 16 / 20 / 24px lines, 6 / 8 / 8px away. Hover: a zinc-600 line (dark zinc-300) and a 3px zinc-100 halo (dark zinc-800). Focus: a 1px blue-600 ring (dark blue-300) 2px out, around circle and label. Disabled: zinc-200 fill (dark zinc-600), label zinc-400 (dark zinc-500)

**Selected:** a neutral high Button's colors: zinc-900 fill with a white dot (dark: white with a zinc-900 dot), a quarter of the control (4 / 5 / 6px); hover keeps the halo; disabled zinc-300 with a zinc-100 dot (dark zinc-600, zinc-400)

**Invalid group:** the danger message (see Fieldset); a radio that is `aria-invalid` or `:user-invalid` takes Text Input's error line (red-400, dark red-500; hover red-600 with a red-100 halo)

**Motion:** Checkbox's squeeze: pressing squeezes the radio (to 82%), let go it eases back to its size (0.2s). Selecting, the fill comes in (0.08s) and the dot grows from the middle (0.2s), without overshooting; it goes at once. None with reduced motion.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/switch.md

# Switch

Tier: **T0**

An on/off setting that **takes effect immediately**, without a submit. For a choice that is submitted with a form, use Checkbox.

Anatomy, states and shared obligations: `choice.md`. Groups (a settings section): `fieldset.md`.

```html
<div class="canon-choice">
  <input type="checkbox" role="switch" id="maintenance" name="maintenance" checked
         aria-describedby="maintenance-hint">
  <label class="canon-choice-label" for="maintenance">Maintenance mode</label>
  <p class="canon-choice-hint" id="maintenance-hint">Visitors see a maintenance page.</p>
</div>
```

- `role="switch"` on a checkbox is the contract. Safari's `switch` attribute is harmless but nothing depends on it.
- No indeterminate state, no `required`.
- **Theme obligation:** a theme without a switch renders it as a checkbox.
- Visible "On" / "Off" text comes from the strings `--canon-text-on` / `--canon-text-off`, written as `content: var(--canon-text-on) / ""` so assistive tech, which already hears the state, doesn't hear it twice.
- The thumb moves to the inline end, so it mirrors in RTL.

## State text (optional)

Words for each state, for when "on" needs saying in the setting's own terms (Private / Public, Paused / Active):

```html
<div class="canon-choice">
  <input type="checkbox" role="switch" id="visibility" name="visibility">
  <label class="canon-choice-label" for="visibility">Profile visibility</label>
  <span class="canon-choice-state" aria-hidden="true">
    <span class="canon-choice-state-off">Private</span>
    <span class="canon-choice-state-on">Public</span>
  </span>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `canon-choice-state` | no | After the label (and hint), `aria-hidden="true"`. Switches only. |
| `canon-choice-state-off`, `canon-choice-state-on` | both, when there is state text | The only children. Core shows the one for the current state (`:checked`), so it works without canon.js. |

- **The label never changes.** It is the switch's name; the words beside it change. A name that swaps with the state reads as a contradiction ("Only visible to you, switch, off"), so the label says what the setting is and the words say its value.
- **The words are hidden from assistive tech**, which already announces on and off. They are not a second `<label>`: a label's text joins the name even when it is hidden.
- Layout: the label moves above the switch (a field's label) and the words take its place beside the switch; the hint stays under the label, the message under the switch.
- canon.js makes a click on the words toggle the switch, as a label would (T2). Without it the words are plain text and the switch itself still works.
- Theme obligation: a theme that writes its own "On" / "Off" shows the author's words instead when they are present.

## Size

**sm:** 28×16 track (16px thumb), 12px label

**md / lg:** 34×20 / 40×24, 14 / 16px label

## Look

**Track:** The control's height, 1.5× it + 4px wide, with a 2px ring of the track's color outside it (so the label is 8 / 10 / 10px away). Off zinc-300 (dark zinc-700), on zinc-900 with a white thumb (dark: white with a zinc-900 thumb), a neutral high Button's colors. Focus: Checkbox's ring around the switch and its label, 2px out from the track's ring. In a group, switches sit 4px further apart than checkboxes, so the space between the rings matches. Disabled in Checkbox's greys (off zinc-200, dark zinc-800; on zinc-300, dark zinc-600); invalid and off, Text Input's error line color. No hover look. State text: the label above in Label's type (12 / 14 / 16px medium), the switch 6px under it or its hint (plus its ring), the words beside it in the usual label type, the focus ring around the switch and the words

**Thumb:** the control's height, white (off in dark: zinc-400), with a 1px 5% black ring and a 1px drop

**Motion:** the thumb springs across, past the end and back (0.3s), squeezed while it moves: flatter and wider mid-way (80% tall, 120% wide), a touch taller as it rebounds. None with reduced motion.

**Label:** beside

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/choice.md

# Choice anatomy

Not a component: the markup that **Checkbox** (`checkbox.md`), **Radio** (`radio.md`) and **Switch** (`switch.md`) share, the way text input, textarea and select share Field's box. Each has its own spec, reference page and playground. They are grouped with **Fieldset** (`fieldset.md`).

[Toggle Chip](toggle-chip.md) and [Segmented Control](segmented-control.md) are also checkboxes and radios, but look like buttons, so they don't use this anatomy.

## Anatomy

```
canon-choice                      grid; every slot is a direct child
├── <input>                       checkbox or radio, no class, first child, has an id
├── canon-choice-label            <label for>, required
├── canon-choice-hint             optional · helper text
├── canon-choice-state            optional, switch only · words for off and on (switch.md)
└── canon-choice-message          optional · data-intent="danger | warning | success"
```

```html
<div class="canon-choice">
  <input type="checkbox" id="updates" name="updates" aria-describedby="updates-hint">
  <label class="canon-choice-label" for="updates">Email me product updates</label>
  <p class="canon-choice-hint" id="updates-hint">About once a month.</p>
</div>
```

- `canon-choice` is a grid (core default: input, label beside it, hint and message under the label). Themes move slots with `grid-template-areas` (a toggle's label above it, say).
- **The input is first, the label follows.** The label never wraps the input.
- **The input draws itself.** Themes set `appearance: none` on the input and draw the box, ring or track on it; the check, dash, dot and thumb come from its state (`:checked`, `:indeterminate`) on its `::before` / `::after`. No extra markup.
- Core centers the input and the label's first line on each other, whichever is taller (themes size the input with `--canon-choice-control-size` and put the label's typography on `canon-choice`, so `1lh` matches).
- The item's own hint and message are wired with `aria-describedby` on its input.

## States

| State | Hook |
|---|---|
| Checked | `:checked` |
| Focus | `:focus-visible` on the input |
| Disabled | `disabled` on the input, or on its fieldset |
| Required | native `required` |
| Invalid (server) | `aria-invalid="true"` + danger `canon-choice-message` |
| Invalid (browser) | `:user-invalid` |

## Size

`data-size` reaches choices (on the choice or any ancestor). Themes map it where their system has sizes and ignore it otherwise. Each component's spec lists its mapping.

## Theme obligations (all three)

- Draw every state from the input itself (`appearance: none`; `::before` / `::after` for indicators). Never require markup.
- Never hide the label with `display: none`.
- Hide an empty message (`:empty`).
- Use logical properties, so RTL mirrors the layout.

## Pending verification

- Pseudo-elements on `appearance: none` checkboxes and radios render in Chromium. To check in Safari and Firefox: open `reference/checkbox.html`, `radio.html` and `switch.html`.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/color-picker.md

# Color Picker

Tier: **T2** (without canon.js it is the browser's color input)

Pick any color: a native `<input type="color">` in a box that shows it. canon.js opens a picker under the box instead of the browser's: a saturation and brightness area, hue, opacity, an eyedropper, the value as HEX, RGB, HSL or HSB, and swatches. For a choice among a few colors, use [Swatches](swatches.md).

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-field">
  <div class="canon-label"><label class="canon-label-text" for="brand">Brand color</label></div>
  <div class="canon-color">
    <input type="color" id="brand" name="brand" value="#3b82f6" list="brand-colors">  <!-- alpha: opacity -->
    <datalist id="brand-colors">                                                       <!-- optional -->
      <option value="#3b82f6" label="Blue"></option>
      <option value="#22c55e" label="Green"></option>
    </datalist>
  </div>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-color` | yes | The box: Text Input's frame, sizes and states, as wide as its swatch and chevron. |
| `<input type="color">` | yes | The value (what the form submits). Named by a `<label for>` (in a Field) or `aria-label`. |
| `<datalist>` | no | Linked with `list`, inside the box. Its options are swatches in the picker, named by their `label`; their values may have opacity (`#18181b80`). The browser's own picker shows them too. |

### What canon.js adds

Themes style these; authors don't write them.

```html
<div class="canon-color">
  <input type="color" … aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="…">  <!-- transparent, over the box -->
  <span class="canon-color-swatch" aria-hidden="true"></span>                          <!-- --canon-color on the box -->
  <div class="canon-color-popup" popover role="dialog" aria-labelledby="…">
    <div class="canon-color-area" role="slider" tabindex="0" aria-label="Saturation and brightness" aria-valuetext="…">
      <span class="canon-color-thumb"></span>
    </div>
    <div class="canon-color-tools">
      <button class="canon-color-eyedropper" aria-label="Pick a color from the screen"></button>   <!-- where the browser has one -->
      <div class="canon-color-sliders">
        <input type="range" class="canon-color-hue" aria-label="Hue">
        <input type="range" class="canon-color-opacity" aria-label="Opacity">                       <!-- alpha -->
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="canon-color-fields">
      <div class="canon-select" data-size="sm"><select aria-label="Format">HEX · RGB · HSL · HSB</select></div>
      <div class="canon-color-values"><div class="canon-text-input" data-size="sm">…</div>…</div>   <!-- one per value -->
      <div class="canon-text-input canon-color-percent" data-size="sm">…%</div>                    <!-- alpha -->
    </div>
    <hr class="canon-separator" data-size="sm">                                                <!-- with a datalist -->
    <div class="canon-color-caption">Swatches</div>
    <div class="canon-swatches" role="radiogroup">…</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value` (native) | input | a color | `#000000` | — |
| `alpha` | input | (present) opacity: the value is an 8-digit hex | opaque | — |
| `data-inline` | `.canon-color` | (present) the picker in the page, always shown, in place of the box | a box that opens it | no |
| `list` (native) | input | the `<datalist>`'s id: swatches | none | — |
| `data-size` | the field, the box or a container | `xs` · `sm` · `md` · `lg` · `xl` · `2xl` (three-size themes: xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes |

Everything else is native: `disabled`, `required`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`.

## Behavior (canon.js)

- **Opening:** a click on the box, Enter, Space or Down on it opens the picker (not the browser's). Escape, a click outside or a second click on the box closes it, and focus goes back to the box. Opened from the keyboard, focus starts on the area with its ring; by the pointer, on the area without one.
- **The area:** drag or click to set saturation (across) and brightness (down); the arrow keys move by 1, with Shift by 10. It mirrors in right-to-left. Screen readers hear "Saturation 76%, brightness 96%".
- **Hue and opacity** are native range inputs (keyboard and screen readers included).
- **Fields:** the format select shows the value as HEX (one field), RGB, HSL or HSB (three joined fields), and the opacity in percent with `alpha`. A value applies on Enter or when the field is left; one that isn't a color is put back.
- **Swatches** (the datalist): picking one sets the color; the one matching the color is chosen.
- **Eyedropper:** where the browser has the EyeDropper API (Chromium), a button picks a color from the screen. Elsewhere there is no button.
- **The value:** the input gets `input` as the color changes and `change` when the picker closes with a new color, as the native one does. Without `alpha` it is the browser's 6-digit hex. With `alpha` it is an 8-digit hex (`#3b82f680`); browsers can't keep opacity in a color input yet, so canon.js turns the input into a read-only text field holding that code (the same name, id and label; the box still shows the swatch). Where a browser supports `alpha` natively, its input is kept.
- **Inline (`data-inline`):** canon.js puts the picker right after the box, as a `role="group"` named like the input, and the box is hidden (its input still holds the value the form submits). A click on the label goes to the area. `change` fires where a native control's would: a drag ends, a key is released, a slider's `change`, a field is applied, a swatch is picked, the eyedropper returns. The input's `disabled` disables every control in the picker; its `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` are copied to the group. Without canon.js it is the usual box.
- **Apps** that set the value in code fire `input` or `change` on the input; canon.js follows. Form resets are followed.

Without canon.js (inline too), the box shows the native swatch and opens the browser's picker, with the datalist's colors; `alpha` has no effect.

## States

| State | Hook | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Open | `.canon-color-popup:popover-open` | Shown like focus; the chevron turns. |
| Focus | the input's `:focus` | |
| Error | `aria-invalid="true"` on the input | With a danger message, in a Field |
| Disabled | `disabled` | Doesn't open. Inline: every control in the picker is disabled. |

## Core

- Without canon.js the input owns the box as a Select does (`--canon-select-start` / `-end`), its swatch where a value would be. With canon.js it covers the box, transparent, over `.canon-color-swatch`.
- The popover is anchored to the box, in the first place it fits in the window: below, then above (starting at the box's start edge, else ending at its end edge), then beside the box at its inline end, then its inline start (centered on the box, shifted to stay in the window). Five fallbacks (`position-try-fallbacks`), the most Chromium tries. `self-` keywords: the field's own direction (in right-to-left, "end" is the left). Themes set the gap with `--canon-popup-offset`.
- The area is the hue under a white-to-clear gradient (from the inline start) and a clear-to-black one (from the top); the thumb sits at `--canon-color-saturation` and `--canon-color-brightness`. The hue track shows every hue, the opacity track the color fading to clear (`--canon-color-track`). Colors for themes: `--canon-color` (with opacity), `--canon-color-opaque`, `--canon-color-hue`.

## Accessibility

- The input keeps its label and is announced as opening a dialog (`aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded`). The picker is a dialog named like the input.
- The area is a slider with a two-part value text; hue and opacity are native sliders; fields are named ("Red", "Hue", "Opacity").
- Swatches are a radio group named "Swatches", each named by its datalist label.
- Strings (`color-area`, `color-area-value`, `hue`, `opacity`, `eyedropper`, `color-format`, `hex`, `red`, `green`, `blue`, `saturation`, `lightness`, `brightness`, `swatches`) are translated in `i18n/` and follow `lang`.

## Theme obligations

- The box looks like a Select at rest, with the color in place of the value; see-through colors over a checkerboard.
- Thumbs visible on any color (area and sliders); focus visible on the area, the sliders and every field.
- The picker reads as part of the box (anchored to it), and fits a narrow screen.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Every format at once (four rows) | Dropped: one row with a format select |
| Wide-gamut colors (`colorspace="display-p3"`) | When browsers support it on color inputs |
| Saving picked colors as new swatches | Not decided |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** The box: a text input's height (32 / 40 / 48), the swatch and chevron the icon size, 8px apart and (height - icon) / 2 from the edges (56 / 68 / 80px wide). The picker: one size, 344px wide.

The box is Text Input's, the swatch a swatch's circle (90%). The picker: 16px padding and gaps, corners 16px, white (dark zinc-900), 4px under the box; as a popup no frame: a hairline edge (black at 12%, dark white at 12%) and the floating shadow, in the page a zinc-300 line (dark zinc-600). The area fills the width (312px), corners 4px, a zinc-200 ring (dark zinc-700); its thumb 24px. The eyedropper: 40px, corners 8px, zinc-100 (dark zinc-700) with a 20px zinc-500 pipette (dark zinc-400). Sliders 16px from it, 4px apart: 12px tracks with round ends and a 20% line, the opacity one over a checkerboard; 16px thumbs. Thumbs: the color with a 3px white ring inside and a 1px zinc-900 line. Fields: sm, the select 72px, hex 80px or three joined into 156px, opacity 60px at the end. A small [Separator](separator.md) (12px), the caption in Select's group caption type, 24px swatches 12px apart, 16px more under them. Focus rings (the choices'), the eyedropper's hover (zinc-200, dark zinc-600). Inline: the same panel, no wider than its container; an error turns its line red-600 (dark red-500); disabled, it fades to 45% like a disabled swatch. The format select keeps Select's chevron.

**Motion:** the picker opens and closes as a Popover does: it fades in from 97% (0.15s) and out where it is (0.1s); with reduced motion it only fades.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/combobox.md

# Combobox

Tier: **T2** (without canon.js it is a [Select](select.md))

Pick one or several options from a list. The author writes a `<select>`, as for a Select; canon.js adds a box that opens a styled list (on touch screens too) and shows several values as tags. Search is optional: a field on top of the list, or typing in the box itself. With a search it can offer to add new values, and let the app supply the options as people type. With no options at all it is a tag input (free values). The select stays the source of truth: its options, its value (submitted with the form), `required`, `disabled` and validation.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-combobox">
  <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="globe" aria-hidden="true"></span>      <!-- optional -->
  <select id="country" name="country" required>                             <!-- multiple: several values -->
    <option value="" hidden>Choose a country</option>                        <!-- placeholder, optional -->
    <optgroup label="Europe">
      <option value="ie">Ireland</option>
      <option value="de">Germany</option>
    </optgroup>
    <hr class="canon-separator">
    <optgroup label="Asia">
      <option value="jp" disabled>Japan</option>
    </optgroup>
  </select>
  <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-display="icon"
          commandfor="country" command="--canon-clear">                     <!-- optional -->
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="close" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="canon-button-label">Clear</span>
  </button>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-combobox` | yes | The box: [Select](select.md)'s box (Text Input's frame, sizes and states, the arrow). |
| `<select>` | yes | One value, or several with `multiple`. No `size`. (One value, no search, nothing else: a [Select](select.md) does the same natively.) Named by a `<label for>` (in a Field), `aria-labelledby` or `aria-label`; canon.js passes the name on. |
| `.canon-icon` | no | Leading, `aria-hidden="true"`. |
| `<option value="">` | no | **Placeholder:** first, with an empty value, `hidden`. Shown in the box while nothing is chosen (with `multiple` too). |
| `<optgroup label>`, `<hr class="canon-separator">` | no | Groups with a caption, [Separators](separator.md): as in a Select. |
| Clear button | no | After the select: a [Button](button.md) with `command="--canon-clear"` and `commandfor` the select (as in [Text Input](text-input.md)). Clears every value, or goes back to the placeholder. Hidden while nothing is chosen (keeping its space); themes may also show it only on hover and focus. The only button a box takes. |

### Options

Select's options: plain text, or `.canon-icon` / `.canon-avatar`, `.canon-option-label`, `.canon-option-description`, with spaces between. `disabled` works the same. No destructive options: picking a value isn't an action (a choice with a destructive result belongs in a Select; actions in a Menu). Then:

| On an option | With | Means |
|---|---|---|
| `data-seed` | `multiple` | Colors its tag, as on a [Tag](tag.md). |
| `data-intent` (`info` · `success` · `warning` · `danger`) | `multiple` | A **status**: shown as a status tag, in the list and in the box (a filter on a table: "Waiting", "Done"). It may start with a `.canon-tag-dot` or an icon. A status has no seed. |

### What canon.js adds

Themes style these; authors don't write them.

```html
<div class="canon-combobox">
  <select … tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true">…</select>                       <!-- out of sight, still in the form -->
  <ul class="canon-combobox-tags">                                            <!-- multiple -->
    <li><span class="canon-tag" data-seed="15"><span class="canon-tag-label">Design</span>
      <button type="button" class="canon-tag-remove" tabindex="-1" aria-label="Remove Design"></button></span></li>
    <li class="canon-combobox-more" aria-hidden="true" hidden>
      <button type="button" class="canon-combobox-more-button" tabindex="-1" interestfor="…"><span class="canon-tag"><span class="canon-tag-label">+2</span></span></button>
      <div class="canon-tooltip" id="…" popover="hint" role="tooltip">Writing, Legal</div></li>
    <li class="canon-combobox-input-item"><input class="canon-combobox-input" role="combobox" …></li>   <!-- inline -->
  </ul>
  <button type="button" class="canon-combobox-trigger" role="combobox" aria-haspopup="listbox" …>   <!-- not inline; "dialog" with a search field -->
    <span class="canon-combobox-value">…</span>                               <!-- the value, or .canon-combobox-placeholder -->
  </button>
  <input class="canon-combobox-input" role="combobox" …>                      <!-- inline, one value -->
  <div class="canon-combobox-popup" popover>
    <div class="canon-combobox-search"><input role="combobox" …></div>        <!-- data-search="list" -->
    <div class="canon-combobox-list" role="listbox">
      <div role="group" aria-labelledby="…">
        <div class="canon-combobox-caption" id="…">Europe</div>
        <div class="canon-combobox-option" role="option" aria-selected="true"><mark class="canon-combobox-match">Ir</mark>eland</div>
      </div>
      <hr class="canon-separator" aria-hidden="true" hidden>
      <div class="canon-combobox-option canon-combobox-create" role="option" hidden>…Add “…”</div>
    </div>
    <div class="canon-combobox-loading" hidden>…Loading…</div>
    <div class="canon-combobox-empty" hidden>…No results for “…”</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

A one-value combobox can also sit in a [Text Input](text-input.md), first or last, like a Select (a searchable country code: `data-search="list"`). It keeps the width of its widest option.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-size` | box or a container | `xs` · `sm` · `md` · `lg` · `xl` · `2xl` (three-size themes: xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes (the list and the tags follow) |
| `data-intent` | box | `warning` · `success` | none | no |
| `data-search` | box | `list`: a search field on top of the list · `inline`: type in the box itself | no search (typing jumps) | no |
| `data-creatable` | box | (present, with `data-search`) offer to add a value no option has | off | no |
| `data-filter` | box | `none` (with `data-search`): the app filters (see below) | canon.js filters | no |
| `data-tags` | box | `collapse`: tags on one row, the rest as "+N" (`multiple`) | tags wrap | no |
| `data-max` | select | a positive number: at most that many values (`multiple`) | no limit | no |
| `data-intent`, `data-seed` | option | see Options | none | no |

## Behavior

- **Opening:** clicking the box, Enter, Space, Up, Down or Alt+Down on it, or typing (with a search, what was typed starts it). The keyboard's place starts on the chosen option.
- **Without search** (the default): focus stays on the box while the list is open. Up, Down, Home and End move; typing jumps to the next option that starts with what was typed in the last half second (the same letter again: the next one with it); Enter or Space picks.
- **Searching** (`data-search`): the list keeps the options whose label or description contains what was typed, ignoring case and accents, and marks the match. Groups with nothing left go, and so do separators with nothing on one side. With nothing left: "No results for “…”". The number of results is announced (polite) after a pause in typing.
- **In the list:** Up and Down move (disabled options are skipped), Enter (or Space, without search) or a click picks. One value: the list closes. Several: the option is added or removed and the list stays open. Escape closes, Tab closes and moves on.
- **Typing in the box** (`data-search="inline"`): the box is a text field. With one value it shows the value's label; typing opens the list, and closing it without picking puts the label back (Escape does too). With several values the field follows the tags; after a pick it empties for the next one, and Backspace in the empty field removes the last value (announced). Leaving the box closes the list. The box shows labels only, not the option's icon or avatar.
- **New values** (`data-creatable`): when what was typed isn't an option's name, the list ends with "Add “…”" (also when nothing else matches). Picking it adds an `<option>` with that text as its value and label, chosen. If an option has that name (ignoring case and accents), it is chosen instead. An added value stays an option only while it is chosen: removing it (or picking another value) takes it out of the select and the list, so there is nothing to delete later. To keep it as an option for next time, the app adds it to its own options (on `change`).
- **Options from the app** (`data-filter="none"`): canon.js doesn't filter. It fires `canon-search` on the select (bubbling; `event.detail.query`) when the list opens and as people type. The app sets `aria-busy="true"` on the select while it loads (the list shows "Loading…"), replaces the options, and removes `aria-busy`. The app keeps the chosen options in the select, or their values are lost. Matches are still marked.
- **Free values** (a tag input): several values (`multiple`), typed in the box (`data-search="inline"`), new values allowed (`data-creatable`), and **no options to pick**: the select holds only a placeholder and the values to start with (chosen). There is no list, and the field is a plain text field, not a combobox. Enter or a comma adds what was typed, and so does leaving the box (nothing typed is lost); an empty field lets Enter submit the form. A paste with commas or line breaks adds each part, keeping the last unfinished part (and any past a limit) in the field. A name already chosen (ignoring case and accents) isn't added twice. Backspace in the empty field removes the last value and Escape clears what was typed, as inline. Every value is an option of the select only while chosen, the starting ones too, so the form submits them under the select's name. If the app adds options later (`data-filter="none"` is not free), it becomes a combobox again and they are suggestions. Without canon.js the empty select can't take values: keep this for forms that need JavaScript, or offer a text field there.
- **A limit** (`data-max`): once that many values are chosen, the other options (and "Add") can't be picked until one is removed.
- **Tags:** each has a remove button (a click removes the value and focus returns to the box). Tags still chosen stay as they are when the value changes; a removed one closes its room sideways (`data-state="closing"`) where it was, and one chosen later opens its room (`"opening"`). When they take more rows or fewer, the box is `data-resizing` (`"opening"` or `"closing"`) while its height follows, from `--canon-motion-from-height` to `--canon-motion-to-height`. The buttons are out of the tab order: keyboard users remove a value from the list (or with Backspace, inline). With `data-tags="collapse"` the tags that don't fit give way to "+N", whose [Tooltip](tooltip.md) lists them; the last tag left is cut short. Clicking "+N" opens the list.
- **Clear:** the clear button empties the select (or picks the placeholder), fires `input` and `change`, and returns focus to the box.
- **The select:** picking sets its options and fires `input` and `change` on it. If the app changes the select in code, it fires `change` (or edits the options or attributes, which canon.js sees). Form resets are followed.
- **Names and states:** the select's label, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `required` and `disabled` are mirrored on the box's control. Focus that reaches the select (its label, a failed submit) goes to that control. In a Field, validation messages work as for a Select.

## States

| State | Hook | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Open | `.canon-combobox-popup:popover-open` | Shown like focus; the arrow turns. |
| Focus | the trigger's or the field's `:focus` | |
| Placeholder | `.canon-combobox-placeholder` in the value, or the field's placeholder | Muted |
| Error | `aria-invalid="true"` on the select, or `:user-invalid` | |
| Warning, success | `data-intent` on the box, or a field's message | |
| Disabled | `disabled` on the select | Tags lose their color and their remove buttons. |
| Loading | `aria-busy="true"` on the select | The "Loading…" row |
| Option chosen | `aria-selected="true"` | Marked by the theme (a check, with several values too) |
| Option highlighted | `data-state="active"` | The keyboard's place, also where the pointer is |
| Option disabled | `aria-disabled="true"` | Also the options a limit blocks |
| Filtered out | `hidden` | |

## Core

- The select is visually hidden once canon.js has run; the trigger takes its place and owns the whole box, as the select does in a Select (`--canon-select-start` / `-end`). Inline, the field owns the box as a text input does.
- With tags, the trigger lies under the whole box (a click anywhere opens the list) and its text, the values, is for screen readers; tags let clicks through except on their remove buttons. Inline, the field follows the tags and is at least 4rem wide.
- `data-tags="collapse"`: the tags row doesn't wrap and clips; canon.js hides the tags that don't fit.
- The clear button sits above the trigger and hides while nothing is chosen.
- The popup is a popover anchored to the box (canon.js names the anchor), at least as wide, below it, flipping above when there's no room. The search field stays; the list scrolls.
- Rows hidden by the search are hidden whatever display the theme gives them.

## Accessibility

- The box is a `role="combobox"` button with `aria-expanded`; its text is the value (several values: all of them, comma-separated). Without search it controls the listbox (`aria-haspopup="listbox"`) and points at the highlighted option with `aria-activedescendant`, keeping focus. Inline, the box's field is the combobox (`aria-autocomplete="list"`), and with several values the values are its description. With free values there is no list, so the field drops the combobox role (a plain text field, named like the select), and the values are still its description.
- With a search field in the list, the button opens a dialog (`aria-haspopup="dialog"`) named like the select; the search field controls the listbox and points at the highlighted option with `aria-activedescendant`, so focus never leaves the field.
- The listbox has `aria-multiselectable` with `multiple`; options say `aria-selected`; groups are named by their captions. "Add “…”" is an option; "Loading…" and "No results" are not, and the result count is announced instead.
- "+N" and its tooltip are hidden from screen readers, and out of the tab order: they get every value from the trigger or the field.
- Strings canon.js uses (`search`, `no-results`, `no-results-for`, `results-*`, `create-option`, `loading`, `remove-value`, `removed-value`, `more-values`) are translated in `i18n/` and follow `lang`. Counts use the language's plural forms.

## Theme obligations

- The box looks like a Select at rest; the list like a Select's, with the search field on top when there is one.
- Chosen options marked by more than color; the keyboard's place visible; the match visible on every row (highlighted, chosen, destructive).
- Tags of the box's size, wrapping inside it; the arrow and the clear button stay reachable.
- "No results", "Loading…" and "Add" read as part of the list; loading moves (gently under reduced motion).
- A list taller than its limit scrolls under the search field.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| The option's icon or avatar in an inline box | Not decided yet |
| Menus of actions | Menu |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Box: Select's (32 / 40 / 48); free values: no arrow, ending as a text input does. Search field: the box's height, padding 8 / 10 / 12, a 16 / 20 / 24 search icon, text 30 / 38 / 44 from the edge. List: Select's; rows below the search field. Several values: tags of the box's size (24 / 32 / 40), 4px from the border, 4 / 8 / 12 apart; the arrow 4 / 4 / 8 past them, on the last row.

Search field: a hairline rule under it (black at 10%, dark white at 10%), icon zinc-400 (dark zinc-500), placeholder zinc-500 (dark zinc-400). Tags: [Tag](tag.md)'s medium emphasis with a remove button; on hued tags the button is a zinc-100 segment (dark zinc-700). **Built from the option row:** "No results for “…”" and "Loading…" are rows with an icon in the icon color (Lucide search-x; loader-circle, turning) and text in the caption's zinc-500 (dark zinc-400); "Add “…”" is an option with a plus, after a separator. Under the search field's line, a list starting with options (and these rows) keeps a separator's space: 5.5 / 5.5 / 9.5px. The list scrolls after 8.5 rows of the box's height (272 / 340 / 408px). The match: a tint of the text color behind it (14%, dark 24%), as Kbd's. Disabled tags: neutral, from the box's disabled text, without remove buttons. The clear button: Text Input's box button, before the arrow, shown while the box is hovered or focused (always on touch screens). Statuses: Tag's status pills, in the list too.

**Motion:** the list opens and closes as Select's: it fades in from 97% (0.15s) and out where it is (0.1s); filtering doesn't replay it. With reduced motion it only fades.

**Tags' motion:** a removed tag fades (0.12s), then narrows away (0.18s) as its neighbours close up; a new one widens (0.18s), then fades in (0.12s). When the tags take more rows or fewer, the box's height follows them (0.18s, as they narrow or widen) instead of jumping. With reduced motion they only fade and the box changes at once.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/date.md

# Date

Tier: **T2** (without canon.js it is the browser's date field)

One date: a native `<input type="date">` in a `.canon-date` box, Text Input's frame. canon.js draws the field itself (day, month and year parts, the same in every browser) and adds a button that opens a calendar, or shows the calendar in the page (`data-inline`). The input stays underneath, hidden: the value (`2025-10-10`), `min`, `max`, `required` and the form value are still the browser's.

A **range** is two date inputs in one box (a start and an end), with a two-month calendar and optional presets. A **week** is an `<input type="week">` in the box, with week numbers in its calendar. The **day strip** (`data-strip`) shows a date as a row of days in the page (a week, or as many as fit).

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-field">
  <div class="canon-label"><label class="canon-label-text" for="start">Start date</label></div>
  <div class="canon-date">
    <input type="date" id="start" name="start" min="2025-01-01" data-weekdays="1-5" placeholder="Select date">
  </div>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-date` | yes | The box: Text Input's frame, sizes and states. |
