| `<input type="date">` | yes | The value (what the form submits). Named by a `<label for>` (in a Field) or `aria-label`. |

### A range

```html
<div class="canon-field" role="group" aria-labelledby="stay-label">
  <div class="canon-label"><span class="canon-label-text" id="stay-label">Stay</span></div>
  <div class="canon-date">
    <input type="date" id="stay-from" name="from" aria-label="Check-in">
    <input type="date" id="stay-to" name="to" aria-label="Check-out">
    <datalist>                                          <!-- optional: presets -->
      <option value="this-week"></option>
      <option value="last-7-days"></option>
      <option value="2025-12-24/2025-12-26" label="Holidays"></option>
    </datalist>
  </div>
</div>
```

- **Two native date inputs**, each with its own `name` (the form submits both) and `aria-label` (the author's words: "Start", "Check-in"). As for a [Range Slider](range-slider.md), the field's label is a `<span id>` naming the pair, with `role="group"` and `aria-labelledby` on the field.
- **min, max and the other rules** can go on either input; the calendar follows them all (a day is out if any input rules it out). An end before the start is invalid ("The end date is before the start date.").
- **Presets** (`<datalist>` in the box): each option's value is a keyword, named in the reader's language — `all` (`min` to `max`, or empty), `today`, `yesterday`, `this-week`, `last-week`, `last-7-days`, `this-month`, `last-month`, `last-30-days`, `this-year`, `last-year` (weeks start on the calendar's first day; "this" is the whole period) — or a start/end range with a `label`. Without canon.js the datalist shows nothing.

### A week

```html
<div class="canon-field">
  <div class="canon-label"><label class="canon-label-text" for="sprint">Sprint</label></div>
  <div class="canon-date">
    <input type="week" id="sprint" name="sprint" value="2025-W42" min="2025-W01">
  </div>
</div>
```

- **The value is an ISO week** (`2025-W42`): weeks start on Monday, and a week belongs to the year of its Thursday, so `2026-W01` starts on 29 December 2025. The calendar starts on Monday whatever the language (`data-week-start` doesn't apply).
- **The field** shows the week and its year in the `week-format` string ("Week {week}, {year}"), drawn like a date's.
- **Browsers without week inputs** (Firefox, Safari) make it a text input; canon.js draws the same field and calendar, keeps the same value, and checks `min` and `max` itself ("This week can't be chosen."). Without canon.js there, it is a plain text field.
- `data-weekdays`, `data-unavailable` and `canonUnavailable` are for dates; a week takes `min` and `max`.

### The day strip

```html
<div class="canon-date" data-strip>
  <input type="date" id="slot" name="slot" value="2025-10-03" min="2025-10-01">
</div>
```

- **A row of days in the page**, in place of the box: each day its weekday, number and month. As many whole days as fit, a week at most; previous and next move by the days shown (a week when all seven show, three when three fit). For picking a day close to now (a delivery slot, a booking), where a month is more than needed. One date input; not with a range, a week or `data-inline`.
- A whole week starts as the calendar's (`data-week-start`, else the language's); fewer days start around the value (it near the middle) and slide from there. `min`, `max` and the other rules grey the days that can't be chosen.

- **Why canon.js draws the field:** browsers draw date fields differently and each adds its own picker (Firefox an icon inside the field that CSS can't hide, Safari a popup on click). Drawn by canon.js, it looks and behaves the same everywhere, and only Canon's calendar opens.
- **The order and separators follow the reader's language** (`10.10.2025`, `10/10/2025`, `2025-10-10`); the value is always ISO (`2025-10-10`).
- **Placeholder:** with `placeholder` on the input, canon.js shows it while the field is empty and not focused (a native date field has none).

### What canon.js adds

Themes style these; authors don't write them.

```html
<div class="canon-date">
  <input type="date" … tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true">               <!-- underneath, invisible -->
  <div class="canon-date-segments" role="group" aria-labelledby="…">    <!-- the field; data-empty: empty, with a placeholder; a range's: data-part="start" / "end" -->
    <span class="canon-date-segment" data-type="month" role="spinbutton" contenteditable aria-label="Month"
          aria-valuemin="1" aria-valuemax="12" aria-valuenow="10" aria-valuetext="October">10</span>   <!-- data-empty: no value yet -->
    <span class="canon-date-literal" aria-hidden="true">/</span>
    …day, year in the language's order…
    <span class="canon-date-placeholder" aria-hidden="true">Select date</span>
  </div>
  <!-- a range: <span class="canon-icon canon-date-arrow" data-icon="arrow-forward" aria-hidden="true">, then the second input and its field -->
  <button class="canon-button canon-date-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-display="icon"
          aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="…">  <!-- the popover's invoker -->
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="calendar" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="canon-button-label">Choose date</span>
  </button>
  <div class="canon-calendar" popover role="dialog" aria-labelledby="…" data-view="days">   <!-- data-inline: after the box, role="group" -->
    <div class="canon-calendar-header">
      <button class="canon-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-display="icon">…Previous month</button>
      <button class="canon-button canon-calendar-title" data-emphasis="low" aria-label="Oct 2025, choose a month">Oct 2025</button>
      <button class="canon-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-display="icon">…Next month</button>
    </div>
    <table class="canon-calendar-grid" role="grid" aria-labelledby="…title">
      <thead><tr><th scope="col" abbr="Sunday">Su</th>…</tr></thead>        <!-- data-unavailable: a weekday that can't be chosen -->
      <tbody><tr><td aria-selected="true">                                  <!-- the value -->
        <button class="canon-calendar-cell" data-date="2025-10-10" aria-label="Friday, 10 October 2025">10</button>
      </td>…</tr></tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</div>
```

A range's calendar has two `.canon-calendar-month`s side by side (each a header and a grid; previous on the first, next on the last, a `.canon-calendar-spacer` in their place elsewhere; plain titles) and, with presets, a `.canon-calendar-presets` group of buttons (`aria-pressed` on the one matching the range). A one-month calendar is one `.canon-calendar-month` too.

The day strip (`data-strip`) follows the box: `.canon-date-strip` (`role="group"`, named like the input) holds previous, `.canon-date-strip-days` (as many days as fit) and next; each day is a `.canon-date-strip-day` button (named by its full date; `aria-pressed="true"` is the value, `aria-disabled` can't be chosen, `aria-current="date"` today) of `.canon-date-strip-weekday`, `.canon-date-strip-number` and `.canon-date-strip-month`.

A week's calendar adds a column of week numbers before the grid (`.canon-calendar-weeks`, a table hidden from assistive technology; its buttons, out of the tab order, carry `data-week`; the chosen one's cell is `[data-selected]`), in a `.canon-calendar-body` with the grid; its title is plain. The chosen week's day cells are `[data-in-week]` and `aria-selected`.

The days view is always six weeks, the days of the months before and after filling it, so the calendar keeps its height from month to month. A day button can be `[data-outside]` (another month), `aria-disabled="true"` (can't be chosen) and `aria-current="date"` (today). In a range, its cell is `[data-in-range]`, with `[data-range-start]` / `[data-range-end]` at the ends, `aria-selected` on every day of the range, and `[data-preview]` on the days a range in the making would take. The months view is a 3 × 4 grid of month buttons (`data-month`), the years view a 4 × 3 grid of a decade with the year before it (`data-year`; the first is `[data-outside]`).

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value`, `min`, `max` (native) | input | ISO dates | — | — |
| `data-weekdays` | input | ISO weekdays that can be chosen, 1 is Monday: `1-5`, `1,3,5`, `1-5 7` | every day | — |
| `data-unavailable` | input | dates and start/end ranges that can't be chosen: `2025-12-25 2025-12-29/2026-01-02` | none | — |
| `placeholder` | input | text shown while empty | none | — |
| `aria-label` | each input of a range | its name ("Start", "End") | — (required) | — |
| `data-inline` | `.canon-date` | (present) the calendar in the page, in place of the box | a box that opens it | no |
| `data-header` | `.canon-date` (not a range) | `select`: the month and the year as two Selects in the calendar's header | a title that zooms out | no |
| `data-strip` | `.canon-date` (one date input) | (present) a row of days in the page (as many as fit, a week at most), in place of the box | a box that opens a calendar | no |
| `data-week-start` | the box or a container | `1`–`7` (1 is Monday, 7 Sunday) | the language's first day | yes |
| `data-size` | the field, the box or a container | `xs` · `sm` · `md` · `lg` · `xl` · `2xl` (three-size themes: xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes |

Everything else is native: `required`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, `name`, `form`.

### The app's function

For rules no attribute can say (booked days, a holiday API), the app sets a function on the input:

```js
input.canonUnavailable = (iso) => bookedDays.has(iso);   // true: can't be chosen
```

canon.js asks it for every day it draws and every value typed. It is read when the calendar draws, so after the rules change, the next open (or the next month shown) follows them.

## Behavior (canon.js)

- **The field** (not inline): a part takes digits and moves on when it can't take more (a month of 2, a day of 4, four year digits); a separator key moves on too. Up and Down step a part (from today when empty, wrapping days and months), Left and Right move between parts (reversed right-to-left), Tab goes through them like a native field's segments, Backspace clears a part, then goes back. Enter submits the form. A pasted date (ISO, or numbers in the field's order) fills every part. Parts are editable (`contenteditable`), so phones show a number keyboard; typing goes through `beforeinput`. A press on the box, or on the label, goes to the first empty part.
- **The value:** a complete date sets the input and fires `input` and `change` (a day past the month's end becomes its last day); clearing a part empties it. Leaving an incomplete date fires `change`, and the input is invalid ("Enter a complete date.").
- **Opening:** the calendar button ("Choose dates" for a range, "Choose week" for a week), or Alt+Down in a field. A second click on the button, Escape or a click outside closes it; focus goes back to the field. It opens at the value (else today, kept within `min` and `max`), with focus on that day: with a focus ring from the keyboard, without one from the pointer.
- **Picking a day** sets the value, fires `input` and `change` (as the browser's picker does), closes, and focus goes back to the field.
- **The day strip:** a click, Enter or Space picks a day (`input` and `change`); one tab stop, the day in hand; Left and Right move a day, past either end on to the next days shown (reversed right-to-left), Home and End go to the first and last shown, Page Up and Page Down by the days shown; previous and next move by the days shown (and say which). How many show follows the space it has (whole days only, 1 to 7), again when it changes. It shows the value (else today) and follows the value. `disabled` makes it inert. A click on the label goes to the strip.
- **Picking a week:** a click on a week number, or on (or Enter on) any of its days, sets the week, fires `input` and `change`, closes, and focus goes back to the field. The keyboard moves by days as in a date's calendar.
- **Picking a range:** the first day picked sets the start (and empties the end); the pointer, or the keyboard, then previews the range to the day under it; the second sets the end (either order: the earlier one starts), closes, and focus goes to the end field. A preset sets both and closes. Each input fires its own `input` and `change`. The two months follow the focused day; previous and next move both. Days of the months before and after can be picked too.
- **Month and year Selects** (`data-header="select"`): the header holds two [Selects](select.md), "Month" and "Year", in place of the zooming title (which stays, hidden, naming the grid). Choosing either shows that month; previous and next update them. Months outside `min`–`max` are off; years run from `min` to `max`, else a century back and ten years ahead (always including the one shown).
- **Zoom:** the title shows the view and goes out a level: days → months → years → days. Picking a month shows its days; picking a year, its months. Previous and next move by a month, a year or ten years; the calendar is `data-turning="next"` or `"previous"` while the theme's animations run (also when the keyboard crosses into another month).
- **Keys** (the grid): arrows move a day (a week up and down); Home and End go to the week's start and end; Page Up and Page Down move a month, with Shift a year. In months, arrows move a month (three up and down) and Page keys a year; in years, a year (four up and down) and Page keys ten. Enter or Space picks. The grid follows the direction (right-to-left reverses Left and Right).
- **Can't be chosen:** before `min` or after `max`, a weekday outside `data-weekdays`, a date in `data-unavailable`, or one the app's function rules out. Such days are greyed, can be reached by the keyboard but not picked; months and years entirely outside `min`–`max` too, and previous / next stop there. A typed date ruled out by the last three makes the input invalid (`setCustomValidity`, "This date can't be chosen."), as `min` and `max` do natively; in a Field it shows like any validation message.
- **Inline (`data-inline`):** the calendar follows the box, in the page (`role="group"`, named like the input); the box is hidden. A click on the label goes to the calendar. `disabled` or `readonly` on the input makes it inert.
- **Disabled and read-only:** disabled parts leave the tab order; read-only parts can be focused but not changed, and the calendar button stays, off (`aria-disabled`).
- **The language** (the nearest `lang`) gives the month and day names (two letters in English, `Su Mo`; the narrow form where short names are long), the digits and the week's first day.
- **Apps** that set the value in code fire `input` or `change` on the input; canon.js follows. Form resets are followed.

Without canon.js: the browser's own date field and picker; `data-weekdays`, `data-unavailable` and the placeholder have no effect (`min` and `max` still do).

## States

| State | Hook | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Open | `.canon-calendar:popover-open` | The box shows focus. |
| A range | `[data-in-range]`, `[data-range-start]`, `[data-range-end]`, `[data-preview]` on day cells | |
| Focus | the input's `:focus` | |
| Error | `aria-invalid="true"` on the input, or `:user-invalid` | With a danger message, in a Field. |
| Disabled, read-only | `disabled`, `readonly` | The calendar button is off; inline, the calendar is inert. |

## Core

- Without canon.js the input fills the box like a Text Input's. With it, the input covers the box, invisible and out of reach (`opacity: 0`, `pointer-events: none`), under `.canon-date-segments`: a flex row taking the input's place, tabular figures. The placeholder lies over it, at the box's padding, while `[data-empty]` and not `:focus-within` (the parts are transparent then).
- The popover is anchored to the box like Color Picker's (below, then above, then beside; `--canon-popup-offset`).
- The grid is a table: seven columns of the control height (`--canon-control-block-size`), months and years sharing that width. Cells are buttons filling them, tabular figures. Previous and next icons mirror in right-to-left.

## Accessibility

- The field is a group named like the input (its label, description, `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` copied) of spinbuttons named "Day", "Month", "Year", each with its value (the month by name) or "Empty". The hidden input is out of the tab order and the accessibility tree; its label still works (it moves focus to the field), and so does its validation (an invalid date on submit moves focus to the field, and a Field shows the message).
- The calendar button is named "Choose date" and says it opens a dialog; the calendar is a dialog (inline, a group) named like the input.
- The grid is `role="grid"` named by the title ("Oct 2025"); previous and next announce the new month, year or decade; weekday headers carry the full name (`abbr`); each day button is named by its full date ("Friday, 10 October 2025"), today is `aria-current="date"`, the value's cell `aria-selected`, days that can't be chosen `aria-disabled` (still reachable, so nothing jumps).
- One tab stop in the grid (roving `tabindex`); the title says what it does ("Oct 2025, choose a month").
- A range's fields are each named by their input ("Check-in"), inside the field's group ("Stay"); the range's end days add ", start" and ", end" to their names; presets are a group named "Presets" of toggle buttons.
- A week's field is spinbuttons named "Week" and "Year"; the week numbers' column is for the pointer only (the days pick the week from the keyboard, and the grid says which days are chosen).
- The day strip is a group named like the input, of toggle buttons named by their full dates ("Friday, 3 October 2025"); previous and next announce the days now shown.
- Strings (`choose-date`, `choose-dates`, `choose-week`, `previous-week`, `next-week`, `week-column`, `week-format`, `date-week`, `date-week-placeholder`, `week-incomplete`, `week-unavailable`, `range-start`, `range-end`, `date-range-order`, `presets`, `preset-all` … `preset-last-year`, `previous-month`, `next-month`, `previous-year`, `next-year`, `previous-years`, `next-years`, `show-months`, `show-years`, `show-days`, `date-unavailable`, `date-incomplete`, `date-day`, `date-month`, `date-year`, `date-day-placeholder`, `date-month-placeholder`, `date-year-placeholder`, `date-empty`) are translated in `i18n/` and follow `lang`.

## Theme obligations

- The box looks like a Text Input with the calendar button at its end; with focus in the field, or the calendar open, it shows focus. The part being typed in is marked; empty parts look like a placeholder.
- The chosen day stands out by more than a hue change (a filled cell); days of other months and days that can't be chosen are told apart from each other and from the rest; focus is visible on every cell and header button; today is marked.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A range calendar that wraps (one month under the other) in a narrow space | If needed: an inline range with presets is about 620px wide at sm |
| Several dates, time, date and time | Later in the family |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** The box: Text Input's (32 / 40 / 48). The calendar: cells 32 / 40 / 48 square, padding and corners 8 / 12 / 16 (240 × 328 / 304 × 396 / 368 × 464, always six weeks), cell corners 4 / 8 / 12, Text Input's type.

White (dark zinc-900); as a popover no frame: a hairline edge (black at 12%, dark white at 12%) and the floating shadow, in the page a zinc-300 line (dark zinc-800); 4px under the box. Header: Button's minimal icon buttons and a low title, zinc-900 (dark white). Weekdays regular zinc-500 (dark zinc-400); days medium; 16 between header, weekdays and days, rows 8 apart. Other months zinc-400 (dark zinc-500); can't be chosen zinc-300 (dark zinc-700), their weekday headers too; hover zinc-100 (dark zinc-800), a step lighter than a range's band; chosen as a neutral high Button: zinc-900 with white text (dark: white with zinc-900). The box: the calendar icon zinc-400 (dark zinc-500), the placeholder in the placeholder color. A range: two months the icon size (16 / 20 / 24) from a hairline rule between them (black at 10%, dark white at 10%), 496 × 328 / 624 × 396 / 752 × 464 with a six-week month, plain titles; its two ends chosen, the days between a zinc-200 band (dark zinc-700) in the text's color, rounded at its ends and each week's; days of other months in it the band at 40% with zinc-400 text (dark zinc-500), so the range reads in its own month's pane; a preview the band with zinc-400 text; presets a column past another line, Button's minimal ones in zinc-500 (dark zinc-400), the matching one on zinc-200 (dark zinc-700); the box: the two dates at its ends, a zinc-400 arrow (Lucide arrow-right) between. Today's dot sits 4 / 6 / 8 above the cell's bottom. `data-header="select"`: two Selects 4 apart, the month 68 / 84 / 100 wide and the year 76 / 92 / 108, centred. The day strip: the calendar's frame (432 × 72 / 576 × 88 / 720 × 104), padding 8 / 12 / 16 across and 4 down and its parts that far apart; days 48 / 64 / 80 wide, 4 above and below, Text Input's corners; weekday zinc-500 and month zinc-400 a step smaller than the medium number (10 / 12 / 14); chosen zinc-900 (dark white), the number white (dark zinc-900), the weekday at 75% and the month at 60% of it; hover zinc-100 (dark zinc-800), focus (the choices' ring), days that can't be chosen zinc-300 (dark zinc-700), no today dot (aria-current only). A week: the week numbers' column the cell width, a hairline rule the icon size from it on each side (304 × 328 at sm), "W" in the weekday type; the chosen week's number chosen (zinc-900, white); its days the band, rounded at the row's ends. The range's calendar button (kept, so both kinds open the same way), the dark range colors, the presets column sizing to its labels, the field's parts (empty ones and separators in the placeholder color, the focused one on zinc-200, dark zinc-700, 2px corners), the focus ring (the choices', blue: focus keeps the focus color), today's dot (4px, under the number), an inline calendar disabled at 45%.

**Motion:** the calendar opens and closes as a Popover does: it fades in from 97% (0.15s) and out where it is (0.1s); with reduced motion it only fades.

**Turning:** to another month (year, decade), the days slide in 12px from the side it turns to and fade in (0.2s); the header and weekdays stay. Mirrored in right-to-left; with reduced motion they only fade.

**Day strip:** picking a day, the chosen fill glides to it from the day before (0.3s, fast then settling; drawn once and anchored to the chosen day, each day drawing its own where anchor positioning is missing and in forced colors). Moving to other days (previous, next, the keys past either end; `data-turning` on the strip, canon.js), the days slide in 12px from the side they come from and fade in (0.2s), the fill moving with them. Mirrored in right-to-left; with reduced motion nothing glides or slides, the new days only fade in.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/field.md

# Field

Tier: **T0** (client-side messages and the counter are T2)

## Scope

Field is the **wrapper anatomy** for every control with a label above/beside a box: text-like inputs (`text-input.md`), textarea (`textarea.md`), select (`select.md`), number (`number-input.md`), password (`password.md`), search, combobox (`combobox.md`), sliders (`slider.md`, `range-slider.md`), the date family (`date.md`: date, range, week, inline calendar, day strip), color (`color-picker.md`), swatches (`swatches.md`) and one-time codes (`input-otp.md`). The Field page of the reference shows each of them in a field.

Around fields: [Fieldset](fieldset.md) groups them under a question, [Form Repeater](form-repeater.md) repeats a row of them, [Form Layout](form-layout.md) arranges a whole form (sections, fields side by side).

Checkbox, radio and switch are **not** Fields: their label follows the control and they come in groups. Each is its own component (`checkbox.md`, `radio.md`, `switch.md`), sharing the choice anatomy (`choice.md`); groups use Fieldset (`fieldset.md`).

## Anatomy

```
canon-field                       grid; every slot is a direct child
├── canon-label                   required · the label block: label, "(optional)", info, description (label.md)
├── canon-field-action            optional · a link or button on the label row
├── canon-text-input              the box, always present: text-input.md, or canon-textarea (textarea.md), canon-select (select.md), canon-combobox (combobox.md), canon-password (password.md), canon-number (number-input.md), canon-date (date.md), canon-color (color-picker.md), canon-swatches (swatches.md), canon-otp (input-otp.md); slider: canon-control for now
│   ├── canon-icon                optional · leading
│   ├── canon-text-input-prefix   optional · text
│   ├── <input> / <textarea> / <select>    the native element, no class
│   ├── canon-text-input-suffix   optional · text
│   ├── canon-icon                optional · trailing
│   └── canon-button              optional · trailing actions (clear, show password, copy)
├── canon-field-message           optional · data-intent="danger | warning | success"
└── canon-field-counter           optional, empty: canon.js shows the count (T2)
```

```html
<div class="canon-field">
  <div class="canon-label">
    <label class="canon-label-text" for="email">Work email</label>
    <p class="canon-label-description" id="email-description">Use your company address.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-text-input">
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="mail" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required
           aria-describedby="email-description email-message" aria-invalid="true">
    <span class="canon-text-input-suffix" aria-hidden="true">@acme.com</span>
  </div>
  <p class="canon-field-message" id="email-message" data-intent="danger">Enter a valid email address.</p>
</div>
```

- `canon-field` is a grid with every slot as a direct child, so themes place the label above, beside, or inside the box (floating) from the same DOM. The label never wraps the input.
- The box: for text-like inputs it is the [Text Input](text-input.md) component (`canon-text-input`), specified there with its anatomy, states and box actions; textareas are [Textarea](textarea.md) (`canon-textarea`), selects [Select](select.md) (`canon-select`) or [Combobox](combobox.md) (`canon-combobox`), and passwords [Password](password.md); sliders still use the shared `canon-control`. It is **always present**, even without affixes: the frame (border, background, focus ring, status icon) belongs to it, not to the native element. It can also be used without a Field (e.g. a toolbar search), with the native element named by `aria-label`.
- The **main control** is the box's direct `<input>`, `<textarea>` or `<select>` child. It has no class. A select box beside it (a country code: a `canon-select` inside the text input, see [text-input.md](text-input.md)) is a second control, not the main one.
- Box content follows Button's pattern: icon, text, native element, text, icon, in DOM order. Themes may reorder.
- DOM order is label (with its description) → action → box → message → counter. Themes reorder visually (to put the description under the box, `.canon-label { display: contents }` makes its parts grid items); only the box and the label's info button are focusable, so focus order is unaffected.
- **One helper text:** the label's description (`canon-label-description`). There is no separate hint under the box; below the box is for messages.
- `canon-field-action` goes on the element itself: `<a class="canon-field-action" href="…">Forgot password?</a>`, or a `canon-button` that also carries `canon-field-action`.

## Rules

1. **Inside a `canon-field`, text-like inputs and textareas carry a `placeholder` attribute.** A bare `placeholder` (empty value) is enough.
   - It is not content: it is the only signal CSS has for "this field is empty" (`:placeholder-shown`). Floating labels can't work without it.
   - Real text is an example value. Themes show it as their system does (floating-label themes only on focus).
   - Exempt: `<select>` and date/time/color/range/file inputs, which never look empty.
   - Standalone `canon-control` (no field, no label): optional.
   - A missing attribute is an authoring error. Themes' safety net keeps the field usable (a floating label stays floated), and `canon.debug.css` flags it.
   - Verified: bare `placeholder` matches `:placeholder-shown` in Chromium. Pending: Safari and Firefox (`reference/checks/placeholder-shown.html`). If either fails, the canonical spelling becomes `placeholder=" "`.
2. **Affix text is `aria-hidden`.** The label and description must carry the meaning ("Price in USD", not "Price" + `$`). Affixes hold text only; a control beside the value (a country code) is a select box in the text input, with its own accessible name.
3. **Description and message are wired with `aria-describedby`** on the native element.
4. **Required is native `required`.** The theme draws any symbol (e.g. an asterisk). **Words are the author's:** "(optional)" is written in the label text (`canon-label-optional`), never generated by CSS. See `label.md`.
5. **Expected length** is expressed with native `size` or `maxlength`. Themes may use them to size the box (the box shrinks to fit and the browser sizes the input from `size`).
6. **`type="search"` has no native clear button** (core removes it; it can't be themed). To offer clearing, add a trailing `canon-button`. Escape still clears natively.
7. **Side by side with a button:** a theme may give fields and buttons different heights. Containers align them; the default is `align-items: last baseline`, which lines up the input's text with the button's label.

## A field that names a group

When the box holds more than one control (a range slider's two thumbs, a date range's two dates) or a set of choices (swatches), the label names the group, not one control:

```html
<div class="canon-field" role="group" aria-labelledby="stay-label">
  <div class="canon-label"><span class="canon-label-text" id="stay-label">Stay</span></div>
  <div class="canon-date">
    <input type="date" name="from" aria-label="Check-in">
    <input type="date" name="to" aria-label="Check-out">
  </div>
</div>
```

- The label is a `<span id>`, not a `<label for>`; the field (or, for swatches, the `role="radiogroup"` box) is labelled by it, and each control has its own short name (`aria-label`).
- Description and message go in each control's `aria-describedby` (swatches: the group's).
- An error is the message; ARIA has no invalid state for a group (as in [Fieldset](fieldset.md)), so the controls that are wrong carry `aria-invalid`.

## Label beside the box (author hint)

```html
<form class="canon-form" data-label="start">
  <div class="canon-field">… Display name …</div>
  <fieldset class="canon-fieldset">… Notifications (radios) …</fieldset>
  <div class="canon-choice">… Show my profile publicly (switch) …</div>
</form>
```

| `data-label` | On | Labels |
|---|---|---|
| absent, `above` | a field or a container | above the box (`above` inside a `start` container puts them back) |
| `start` | a field | beside the box, always |
| `start` | a form or any container | beside the boxes of the fields inside while the container has 32rem of room (a size container; a Form Layout's form already is one); above below that |

- **Beside:** the label at the box's inline start, in a column `--canon-label-width` wide (default 33%), `--canon-label-gap` (1rem) from the box, level with the box's first line (a textarea's first line, not its middle). The label's description stays under it; the message and counter go under the box; a field action under the label.
- **In the same container:** a [Fieldset](fieldset.md)'s legend (and hint) takes the label column, its items beside it (a horizontal fieldset: the legend first on the row); a single checkbox or switch starts where the boxes do.
- **Fields side by side** (a [Form Layout](form-layout.md) row, a [Form Repeater](form-repeater.md) item) keep their labels above.
- **When:** forms people edit and scan (account details, settings, a record's properties, an inspector). A form filled in once, top to bottom, reads faster with labels above, and long or translated labels fit better there.
- A hint in the `canon.hints` layer, like `data-size`: only the author knows the form's purpose.

## Message

| `data-intent` | Meaning | Native element |
|---|---|---|
| `danger` | Error | add `aria-invalid="true"` |
| `warning` | Accepted but questionable | — (ARIA has no warning state; the message is the hook) |
| `success` | Validated | — |

For client-side validation, render the message **empty and present** so it works as a live region; themes hide it while `:empty`:

```html
<p class="canon-field-message" id="email-message" aria-live="polite"></p>
```

**canon.js fills it (T2).** In a field whose message is empty, the browser's own validation (`required`, `type`, `pattern`, `minlength`, and custom checks such as Password's rules or confirmation) shows there instead of the browser's bubble:

- on a failed submit, every invalid field shows its message, and the first gets focus;
- on leaving a changed field that is still invalid;
- as people type, an open message updates, and clears once the value is valid (also when another field fixes it: a confirmation).

It writes the browser's `validationMessage` (localized by the browser, or the custom message), sets `data-intent="danger"` on the message and `aria-invalid="true"` on the control, and marks the message `data-state="validation"`. A message the author wrote is never touched. Forms with `novalidate` are left alone.

## States

| State | Hook | Theme reads it as |
|---|---|---|
| Focus | `:focus-within` on `canon-control` | Focus ring on the box |
| Disabled | `disabled` on the native element | `.canon-field:has(:disabled)` |
| Read-only | `readonly` | `:read-only` |
| Invalid (server) | `aria-invalid="true"` + `danger` message | Error styling |
| Invalid (browser) | `:user-invalid` | Same styling. canon.js (T2) copies `validationMessage` into an empty message, below |
| Warning | `.canon-field:has(.canon-field-message[data-intent="warning"])` | Warning styling |
| Success | `.canon-field:has(.canon-field-message[data-intent="success"])` | Success styling |
| Empty / filled | `:placeholder-shown` (only when `placeholder` is present) | Floating labels |
| Autofilled | `:autofill` | Theme obligation: override browser autofill colors |

## Counter (T2, `canon.js`)

```html
<div class="canon-field">
  <div class="canon-label">
    <label class="canon-label-text" for="bio">Bio</label>
    <p class="canon-label-description" id="bio-description">Up to 160 characters.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-textarea">
    <textarea id="bio" name="bio" rows="3" maxlength="160" placeholder aria-describedby="bio-description bio-message"></textarea>
  </div>
  <p class="canon-field-message" id="bio-message" aria-live="polite"></p>
  <p class="canon-field-counter"></p>
</div>
```

- `canon-field-counter`: empty, after the message. canon.js shows how much of the control's `maxlength` is used ("12 / 160") and, for screen readers, what is left ("148 characters left"). Without canon.js it stays empty and hidden. It sits at the end of the message's row.
- **The limit is `maxlength`** on the control (a text input or textarea), and with a counter it is **soft**. A hard limit fails quietly: typing stops and pasted text is cut without saying what was lost. So canon.js moves `maxlength` to `data-maxlength` (again if an app puts it back), and people can type or paste past it, then shorten. Without canon.js, `maxlength` stays a hard limit. Without a counter, it is native everywhere.
- **Past the limit** the control is invalid with "Use 160 characters or fewer." (`setCustomValidity`). Unlike other validation, which waits until people leave the field, this shows at once (also for a value that starts too long): the box's error state (`aria-invalid="true"`) and the field's message, cleared as soon as the text fits. So a field with a counter needs a message (an empty one is enough).
- **The characters that are too many** are marked in the control itself. A textarea can't color part of its text, so canon.js draws a copy of the text behind the control (`.canon-limit-mirror`, `aria-hidden`: same font, padding, wrapping and scroll position), with the excess in a `<mark class="canon-limit-excess">`, and the control's own text turns transparent (`data-state="over"` on it). The caret, selection, spellcheck and typing stay the control's.
- **The last tenth** of the limit: `data-state="near"` on the counter; past it `data-state="over"`. Screen readers hear what is left (or how many too many) after a second's pause in typing, only once it is near.
- Characters are counted as `maxlength` counts them (a line break is one).
- Say the limit in the description too.
- Strings: `count`, `characters-left-*`, `characters-over-*`, `too-long-*` (plural forms), translated in `i18n/`.

The message's type (10 / 12 / 14px) in its muted zinc-500 (dark zinc-400), tabular figures, at the end of the message's row; near the limit amber-700 (dark amber-300), over it red-700 (dark red-300), both medium weight. The characters past the limit: the danger button's medium colors, red-700 on red-400 at 15% (dark red-300 on red-500 at 20%), corners 2px; the caret keeps the text color, the selection a translucent blue.

## Textarea

Textareas have their own component: [Textarea](textarea.md) (`canon-textarea`), with fixed, growing and resizable heights.

## Select

Selects have their own component: [Select](select.md) (`canon-select`), with the styled list, groups, separators and rich options.

## Box actions (T2, `canon.js`)

Trailing buttons get behavior from the platform's **invoker commands**: `commandfor` names the target, `command` names a Canon custom command. `canon.js` handles the command; browsers without invoker commands get a polyfill for custom commands.

| Command | Does | State the theme can style |
|---|---|---|
| `--canon-clear` | Empties the target, fires `input` and `change`, focuses it | Core hides the button while the field is empty (`:placeholder-shown`) |
| `--canon-toggle-password` | Switches `type` between `password` and `text` | `aria-pressed` (label stays "Show password") |
| `--canon-copy` | Copies the target's value (or text), announces "Copied" ([Button: Copy](button.md#copy-t2-canonjs)) | `data-state="copied"` for 2 seconds |

```html
<div class="canon-text-input">
  <input id="password" name="password" type="password" placeholder>
  <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-display="icon"
          aria-pressed="false" commandfor="password" command="--canon-toggle-password">
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="eye" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="canon-button-label">Show password</span>
  </button>
</div>
```

- Without scripting (`@media (scripting: none)`), core hides command buttons, so there are no dead buttons.
- The "Copied" announcement is the string `--canon-text-copied`, translated by `i18n/<lang>.css` (see decisions: Strings).

## Drawn by the theme, never written in HTML

| Visual | Trigger |
|---|---|
| Required marker | A required control beside the label (`label.md`), on `canon-label-text` |
| Error / warning / success icon in the box | `aria-invalid`, `:user-invalid`, message intent |
| Select chevron | `.canon-select` (select.md) |

## Theme obligations

- Support label placement for the theme's own system from the same DOM; never require markup changes.
- **Space slots with margins, never `row-gap`.** The field grid has a fixed row per slot; absent slots leave empty rows, and grid gaps still apply between empty rows.
- An author hint wins over the theme (`canon.hints` layer). E.g. a `canon-field-action` button with `data-size="sm"` stays that size; a theme that wants a one-line label row uses negative block margins, not a smaller size.
- Hide an empty `canon-field-message` (`:empty`).
- Style `:autofill`.
- Use logical properties (RTL). Affix text keeps its own direction (`unicode-bidi: plaintext` in core).
- **The main control owns its whole box.** Clicking anywhere in the box (padding, icons, affix text, status icon, select arrow) focuses or opens the native element; only trailing buttons and controls inside an affix keep their own clicks. Box icons, affix text and decorations ignore the pointer.
  - **Select:** core extends it exactly to both borders. Themes set `--canon-select-start` (padding, + icon and gap with a leading icon) and `--canon-select-end` (gap + arrow + padding, + the status icon when shown). Exact, because a native popup is as wide as the select.
  - **Input:** affix widths are unknowable, so core extends it 20rem past both edges with matching padding (text doesn't move) and the box clips the overshoot (`overflow: clip`). Paint order keeps trailing buttons on top. No theme values needed.
  - **Textarea:** 20rem overshoot at the start; on the other sides it takes over the box padding exactly, so its scrollbar and resize handle sit at the box's inner edge. Themes set `--canon-textarea-inset-block` and `--canon-textarea-inset-end`. Inputs and textareas measure their content box, so `rows × 1lh` and the 4rem minimum are unaffected.
- A theme may give fields and buttons different heights, and may ignore the size hint where it has one size.

## Look

**Label:** above, description under it; beside with `data-label="start"`, start-aligned

**Description / message:** message below, after an icon in its color (error triangle-alert; warning circle-alert, success circle-check). Filling in (an error after leaving the field or a submit), it slides down 4px and fades in (0.15s) while its room opens, so the form under it moves instead of jumping (where the browser can animate to its height); cleared, it goes at once. With reduced motion it appears at once

**Status icon:** none in the box

**Required:** red `*` 4px after the label

## Deferred

- `data-content="code"` on textarea: monospace, tab width, no wrapping.

## Out of scope (for now)

- Enter-to-submit behavior.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/fieldset.md

# Fieldset

Tier: **T0**

Groups choices (checkboxes, radios, switches) or fields under one question.

```
canon-fieldset                    <fieldset>
├── canon-fieldset-legend         <legend>, first child, required
├── canon-fieldset-hint           optional
├── canon-choice / canon-field …  the items
└── canon-fieldset-message        optional · data-intent="danger | warning | success"
```

```html
<fieldset class="canon-fieldset" aria-describedby="regions-hint regions-message">
  <legend class="canon-fieldset-legend">Regions</legend>
  <p class="canon-fieldset-hint" id="regions-hint">Where the service runs.</p>
  <div class="canon-choice">
    <input type="checkbox" id="regions-eu" name="regions" value="eu">
    <label class="canon-choice-label" for="regions-eu">Europe</label>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-choice">
    <input type="checkbox" id="regions-us" name="regions" value="us">
    <label class="canon-choice-label" for="regions-us">United States</label>
  </div>
  <p class="canon-fieldset-message" id="regions-message" data-intent="danger">Select at least one region.</p>
</fieldset>
```

- DOM order is legend → hint → items → message. Themes reorder visually (a theme may put the error above the items, or the hint and error below them).
- Hint and message are wired with `aria-describedby` **on the fieldset**.
- **Invalid group:** ARIA has no invalid state for a group, so a message with `data-intent="danger"` is the signal (`aria-invalid` on a fieldset is a contract error).
  - Typical case: "select at least one" (roles, notification channels, regions, weekdays). HTML can't express it (`required` on a checkbox means that box must be checked), so the error always comes from the server or the app's JS.
  - Themes decide whether to mark every checkbox in the group or only the group (Canon marks every checkbox).
- For client-side validation, render the message empty and present with `aria-live="polite"`; themes hide it while `:empty`.
- **Disabled group:** native `disabled` on the fieldset disables every control in it (`:disabled` matches them).
- Core lays the fieldset out as a wrapping flex row: legend, hint and message take a line each; items too, unless the group is horizontal. The legend is floated, which turns it from a "rendered legend" (drawn in the border) into an ordinary item, so themes order and space it like any slot.
- Grouping fields (a date split into day / month / year) works the same way. Laying out whole forms is [Form Layout](form-layout.md)'s job.

## Orientation (author hint)

```html
<fieldset class="canon-fieldset" data-orientation="horizontal">
```

| `data-orientation` | Items |
|---|---|
| absent | the theme decides (Canon stacks them) |
| `horizontal` | in a row, wrapping when the row runs out |
| `vertical` | stacked |

A hint in the `canon.hints` layer, like `data-size`: only the author knows whether the labels are short enough to share a row.

In a container with `data-label="start"` ([Field](field.md#label-beside-the-box-author-hint)), the legend and hint take the label column and the items sit beside them, lined up with the fields' boxes.

## Theme obligations

- Keep items' top margins equal, so items in a horizontal row line up.
- Space stacked fields wider than choices (Canon: fields 16px apart, choices 8 / 8 / 12px).
- Space slots with margins (no gaps that apply between absent slots).
- Hide an empty message (`:empty`).

## Look

**Legend:** The label's type (12 / 14 / 16px medium), a red `*` when required

**Hint / message:** hint in the label description's type, 4 / 6 / 8px under the legend; items 12 / 16 / 16px under them and 8 / 8 / 12px apart; message (the field's, with its icon) 12 / 16 / 16px after them. Switches reach 2px past their box, so their steps grow by that (4px more between two) and the visible spaces are the same

**Error:** the danger message

## Deferred

- **Conditional reveal** (choosing an option reveals a nested field): done in [Form Layout](form-layout.md) (`.canon-form-reveal` after a choice).

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/form-layout.md

# Form Layout

Tier: **T0** (layout; a reveal's disabling is T2)

How a whole form is arranged: the space between what it holds, sections with a title, fields side by side, a settings layout with the sections' titles beside their fields, questions that appear after a choice, and the buttons at the end. Everything inside is ordinary [Fields](field.md), [Fieldsets](fieldset.md), [Form Repeaters](form-repeater.md) and choices.

## Elements

```html
<form class="canon-form" data-layout="aside">
  <section class="canon-form-section" aria-labelledby="profile-title">
    <header class="canon-form-section-header">
      <h2 class="canon-form-section-title" id="profile-title">Profile</h2>
      <p class="canon-form-section-description">Shown on your public page.</p>
    </header>
    <div class="canon-form-row">
      <div class="canon-field">… First name …</div>
      <div class="canon-field">… Last name …</div>
    </div>
    <div class="canon-field">… Bio …</div>
  </section>

  <section class="canon-form-section" aria-labelledby="contact-title">
    <header class="canon-form-section-header">
      <h2 class="canon-form-section-title" id="contact-title">Contact</h2>
    </header>
    <fieldset class="canon-fieldset">
      <legend class="canon-fieldset-legend">How should we contact you?</legend>
      <div class="canon-choice">… Email (radio) …</div>
      <fieldset class="canon-form-reveal">
        <div class="canon-field">… Email address …</div>
      </fieldset>
      <div class="canon-choice">… Phone (radio) …</div>
    </fieldset>
  </section>

  <div class="canon-form-actions" data-sticky>
    <button type="submit" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="high">…Save…</button>
    <button type="reset" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral">…Discard changes…</button>
  </div>
</form>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-form` | yes | On the `<form>` (or the element that holds a form's parts). Stacks what it holds a step apart. A size container (`canon-form`) for the rows and the aside layout. |
| `.canon-form-section` | no | A `<section>` named by its title (`aria-labelledby`). Starts with its header; then fields, fieldsets, rows, repeaters. |
| `.canon-form-section-header` | with a section | A `<header>`: the title and an optional description, nothing else. |
| `.canon-form-section-title` | with a header | A heading (`<h2>`, `<h3>`…) at the page's level. |
| `.canon-form-section-description` | no | A `<p>` under the title. |
| `.canon-form-row` | no | Fields side by side (only Fields). |
| `.canon-form-reveal` | no | A `<fieldset>` right after a `.canon-choice` (in a Fieldset, or alone): shown while that choice is checked. |
| `.canon-form-actions` | no | The buttons at the end: the main action first (DOM order is reading order; a theme may place it last). A form that edits something saved ends with a [Save Bar](save-bar.md) instead: it also says what changed and keeps it safe. |

- **Sections or not:** a short form is fields and actions; a long one is split into sections that each answer one thing ("Profile", "Notifications").
- **Rows** are for fields that belong on one line (City · Postcode, First · Last name, card number · expiry · CVC). Their boxes line up whatever their labels, descriptions and messages (the row's three grid rows, label / box / message, shared by its Fields), labels start together at the top. Columns share the width; `--canon-form-columns` sets them like `grid-template-columns` (`minmax(0, 2fr) minmax(0, 1fr)`), as layout. When the form is narrower than 24rem the row stacks.
- **A reveal** is the follow-up to a choice: a radio's question ("Email address" after "Email"), a checkbox's details. It shows while the choice before it is checked (CSS). canon.js disables it while hidden, so its fields are neither checked nor sent. Without canon.js the hidden fields are still sent and checked, so don't make them `required` unless the server checks which choice was made.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-layout` | `.canon-form` | `aside`: each section's header in a side column, its fields beside it (settings pages) | stacked | no |
| `data-sticky` | `.canon-form-actions` | (present): the actions stay at the bottom of the window while the form scrolls | in place | no |
| `data-size` | the form or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |
| `--canon-form-columns` (CSS) | a row | a `grid-template-columns` value | equal | yes (custom property) |
| `--canon-form-aside` (CSS) | the form | the header column's width | `33%` | yes |

- `data-layout` and `data-sticky` are author hints (the `canon.hints` layer): only the author knows a form is a settings page read section by section, or long enough to keep its buttons in view.
- **Aside** applies when the form is at least 40rem wide; narrower, sections stack.

## Core

- `.canon-form`: a block and an inline-size container named `canon-form`. Sections: `display: flow-root`. Rows: a grid of three rows (label / box / message) and a column per field (`--canon-form-columns`, or equal), each Field spanning the three rows as a subgrid; below 24rem a column. Actions: a wrapping flex row. A reveal: a reset fieldset, `display: none` while the choice before it isn't checked.
- Aside (hint): the header floats to the inline start at `--canon-form-aside`; everything else in the section, and the actions, start `--canon-form-aside` + `--canon-form-aside-gap` in, and are at most the width left (so a full-width part, a Description List, doesn't run past the form).
- Sticky (hint): `position: sticky` at the block end.

## Accessibility

- Sections are landmarks of the form named by their titles; titles are headings at the page's level, so the form reads as an outline.
- A reveal follows its choice in the DOM, so it is read and tabbed in order; hidden, it is out of the tab order (and, with canon.js, disabled).
- Sticky actions must not cover the focused field: themes keep them short (one row of buttons).
- Rows keep each field's own label; on narrow screens they stack in reading order.

## Theme obligations

- Space fields a step apart and sections a larger one; show where a section ends.
- Section titles clearly above field labels in the type hierarchy.
- A reveal visibly attached to its choice.
- Sticky actions on the page's background, set off from the scrolling content.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Labels beside their boxes (horizontal fields) | `data-label="start"` on the form ([Field](field.md#label-beside-the-box-author-hint)) |
| A reveal driven by a select | If it comes up |
| Multi-step forms | Wizard (pattern) |
| An error summary at the top | With validation, if it comes up |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Steps 12 / 16 / 20px (between fields, rows' columns, header to fields); sections 24 / 32 / 40px apart with the line halfway; titles 14 / 16 / 18px on 20 / 24 / 28px lines; actions a section's step under the content.

Built from the system's spacing (Fieldset's step between fields). Titles semibold zinc-900 (dark white), descriptions in the label description's type and zinc-500 (dark zinc-400); section lines hairline rules (black at 10%, dark white at 10%). Actions 8px apart; sticky ones on white (dark zinc-950) with a hairline rule above, 12px above and below. Aside: the header in the first third, 32px from the fields. A reveal: a 2px zinc-200 line (dark zinc-700) under the choice control's middle, its fields where the choice's label starts.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/form-repeater.md

# Form Repeater

Tier: **T2** (without canon.js the items the page starts with are an ordinary form)

A list of items people add to and remove, each a row of fields: team members, line items, links. Items are ordinary [Fields](field.md) in a `.canon-repeater`, written once: Add copies the first item, empty, with the next number in its ids and names. The Add and Remove buttons are [Buttons](button.md) with Canon commands; canon.js copies, numbers, removes and moves focus.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-repeater" id="members" data-max="5">
  <div class="canon-repeater-item">
    <div class="canon-field">
      <div class="canon-label"><label class="canon-label-text" for="members-0-team">Team</label></div>
      <div class="canon-select">
        <select id="members-0-team" name="members[0][team]">
          <option value="" hidden>Select team</option>
          <option selected>HR</option>
          <option>Finance</option>
        </select>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="canon-field">
      <div class="canon-label"><label class="canon-label-text" for="members-0-name">Name</label></div>
      <div class="canon-text-input">
        <input type="text" id="members-0-name" name="members[0][name]" placeholder="Enter name" value="John Doe">
      </div>
    </div>
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="danger" data-display="icon"
            commandfor="members" command="--canon-remove">
      <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="trash" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="canon-button-label">Remove</span>
    </button>
  </div>
  <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-intent="neutral" commandfor="members" command="--canon-add">
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="plus" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="canon-button-label">Add member</span>
  </button>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-repeater` | yes | The list, with an `id` the buttons name. |
| `.canon-repeater-item` | — | One item: its Fields (or boxes, below) in DOM order, then its Remove button. The page starts with any number (from the server, the values people saved). |
| `<template>` | when the list can start empty | One `.canon-repeater-item`, empty, with `{index}` where the number goes (`id="members-{index}-team"`, `name="members[{index}][team]"`). Used instead of the first item when present. |
| `command="--canon-remove"` | no | The item's last child: a `<button type="button" class="canon-button">`, `commandfor` the repeater. Recommended: danger, low emphasis, icon only. Its label is the author's ("Remove", "Remove member"). |
| `command="--canon-add"` | no | After the items: a `<button type="button" class="canon-button" data-intent="neutral">`, `commandfor` the repeater. Its label is the author's ("Add", "Add member"). |

- **Labels are optional.** With Fields, their labels show over the first item only, as column headers; later items keep theirs for screen readers (visually hidden), so each control is still named by its own label. Without labels, an item holds the boxes themselves (`canon-select`, `canon-text-input`, …), each control named by `aria-label`, and there are no headers.
- **The new item** is the first item as the page wrote it, empty: values, choices (a select goes back to its placeholder option, `value=""`, or its first), checks, `aria-invalid` and messages cleared. canon.js takes the copy before it enhances anything, so drawn parts (date segments, combobox lists) are made fresh. Hidden inputs are cleared too (a row's record id belongs to that row).
- **Numbers:** the first item's number is the first `[n]` in its names (`members[0][name]`). In the copy, that whole number is replaced in ids, names and the attributes that point at ids (`for`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-controls`, `list`, `commandfor`, `popovertarget`, `data-match`): `members-0-name` becomes `members-3-name`, but `q10-name` keeps its 10. The new number is one past the highest item's, skipping numbers whose ids are taken; numbers aren't reused or closed up after a removal (most servers read `members[0]`, `members[3]` as a list). Names without a number (`team`, repeated) stay as they are, and the copy's ids get `-<number>` added.
- **A list that can start empty** has no item to copy: give a `<template>` instead.
- **Field actions** and messages work in items as in any Field. A message shows under its box; boxes and Remove buttons stay in line.
- To give the list a name ("Members") and say the limit ("Up to 5 members."), put it in a [Fieldset](fieldset.md): the legend and hint describe the list.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-max` | `.canon-repeater` | the most items | no limit | no |
| `data-min` | `.canon-repeater` | the fewest items | `1` | no |
| `data-size` | the repeater or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` (xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes |
| `--canon-repeater-columns` (CSS) | `.canon-repeater` | a `grid-template-columns` value, one track per Field or box: `minmax(0, 2fr) minmax(0, 3fr)`, `10rem minmax(0, 1fr)` | equal columns | yes (custom property) |

- `--canon-repeater-columns` is layout: only the author knows the team names are short and the names long. Set it wherever the page sets its layout (a stylesheet, or `style`).

## Behavior (canon.js)

- **Add** puts the new item after the last one, opening its room (`data-state="opening"` while the theme's animations run), and moves focus to its first control. At `data-max` items, Add is hidden (`hidden`); it comes back when an item goes. With nothing to copy (no items and no template) it stays hidden.
- **Remove** takes its item out, announces "Item removed", closes its room (`data-state="closing"`, its fields disabled and left out of the form meanwhile, then it goes), and moves focus to the next item's first control (the previous item's, for the last; Add's when no items are left). At `data-min` items every Remove is hidden: with the default 1, a single item has none (people clear its fields instead).
- **Item names:** each item is `role="group"`, named "Item 2 of 3" (the `repeater-item` string), kept current as items come and go. An item the author named (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`) keeps its name.
- **Events:** the repeater fires `canon-add` and `canon-remove` (bubbling; `detail.item` is the item) after the change.
- **Apps** that add or remove items themselves (or change `data-min` / `data-max`) are followed: the buttons and names update. New items' components (selects, dates, …) are set up as anywhere else.
- **Form reset** restores values, not items: items added since stay.
- **Disabled:** a disabled fieldset around the repeater disables every control in it, the buttons too.
- Without canon.js (`scripting: none`) the buttons are hidden, like every Canon command, and the items the page starts with are an ordinary form.

## Core

- `.canon-repeater` is a column; items are `--canon-repeater-gap` apart (0.5rem by default; themes set it).
- An item is a grid of three rows, label, box and message, that its Fields share (`grid-template-rows: subgrid`), so boxes line up whatever their labels and messages. Boxes without a Field go in the box row. Columns are `--canon-repeater-columns`, or equal; the same gap apart.
- The Remove button sits at the end of the box row, in padding kept for it (`--canon-repeater-remove-size`, by default the control height, plus the gap) while it shows. Hidden Remove buttons give their space back.
- Labels of items after the first are visually hidden (clipped, never `display: none`).

## Accessibility

- Every control keeps its own label (or `aria-label`), so later items are named although their labels don't show.
- Items are groups named by position ("Item 2 of 3"); a Remove button is heard inside its item.
- Focus never gets lost: it moves into a new item, and to a neighbour when one goes. Removal is announced.
- Say the limit in the description (or the fieldset's hint): Add disappears at the limit without a message.

## Strings

`repeater-item` ("Item {index} of {count}"), `repeater-removed` ("Item removed"), translated in `i18n/`.

## Theme obligations

- Space items like rows of a form, closer than separate fields; Add a clear step under the last item.
- Line boxes and Remove buttons up; keep the header labels over their columns.
- Use logical properties (in right-to-left, the columns mirror and Remove moves to the left).

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Reordering (drag, move up / down) | An addition if it comes up (`--canon-move-up`, `--canon-move-down`, then drag) |
| Undo after removing | The app (`canon-remove` gives it the item) |
| A count ("3 of 5") | The author's text, or Count, if it comes up |
| Nested repeaters | Allowed (each button names its own repeater); not designed further |
| Items as cards (fields stacked) | Form Layout, with the repeater's behavior |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Items and columns 8 / 8 / 12 apart, Add 12 / 16 / 16 under the last item. Remove as tall as the box (32 / 40 / 48, square).

Fields (label 6px over the box), Remove the danger icon button with low emphasis, Add the medium button with a plus. Labels over the first item only.

**Motion:** a new item's room opens (0.2s), then it fades in (0.15s), the Add button moving down with it; a removed item fades out (0.15s), then its room closes (0.2s) and the items under it move up. With reduced motion it only fades.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/input-otp.md

# Input OTP

Tier: **T2** (without canon.js it is one text field)

A one-time code: one native text input in a `.canon-otp` box, its `maxlength` the code's length. canon.js draws a cell per character, in groups, and keeps the input over them, invisible: typing, pasting, the browser filling a code it received (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`), the label and the form value all stay the input's.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-field">
  <div class="canon-label"><label class="canon-label-text" for="code">Verification code</label></div>
  <div class="canon-otp" data-groups="3 3">
    <input type="text" id="code" name="code" inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="one-time-code" maxlength="6">
  </div>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-otp` | yes | The box. In a [Field](field.md) it takes the control's place; it is as wide as its cells. |
| `<input>` | yes | Its only child: `type="text"` (or `password`), `maxlength` (the length), `autocomplete="one-time-code"`. Named by a `<label for>` (in a Field) or `aria-label`. |

- **One input, not one per cell:** the browser fills a received code into it, a pasted code lands in one place, screen readers hear one field with its value, and the form submits one value.
- **The value is the characters alone**: groups are only drawn (`279279`, not `279-279`).

### What canon.js adds

Themes style these; authors don't write them.

```html
<div class="canon-otp" data-groups="3 3">
  <input …>                                         <!-- over the cells, invisible -->
  <div class="canon-otp-cells" aria-hidden="true">
    <span class="canon-otp-group">
      <span class="canon-otp-cell">2</span>          <!-- data-active: the caret's cell -->
      <span class="canon-otp-cell" data-placeholder="0"></span>   <!-- empty: its placeholder character -->
      …
    </span>
    <span class="canon-otp-separator"></span>       <!-- between groups -->
    <span class="canon-otp-group">…</span>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `maxlength` (native) | input | the code's length | — (required) | — |
| `data-groups` | `.canon-otp` | group sizes, space-separated, adding up to `maxlength` (`"3 3"`, `"2 2 2"`) | one group | no |
| `inputmode` (native) | input | `numeric`: digits only (and a number pad on phones) | letters and digits | — |
| `type` (native) | input | `password`: each filled cell shows a dot | `text` | — |
| `placeholder` (native) | input | one character per cell (`000000`) | none | — |
| `data-size` | the field, the box or a container | `xs` · `sm` · `md` · `lg` · `xl` · `2xl` (three-size themes: xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes |

Everything else is native: `pattern` (the browser's check on submit), `required`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, `autocapitalize`.

## Behavior (canon.js)

- **Characters:** only letters and digits are kept (digits only with `inputmode="numeric"`); anything else typed is ignored.
- **The caret's cell** shows focus. A filled one is selected, so typing replaces it and moves on; past the value the caret waits in the next empty cell (with a full code, the last cell).
- **Pointer:** a press picks the cell under it, or the first empty one past the value. Focus from Tab or the label starts after the value.
- **Keys:** Left and Right move a cell; Home or Up go to the first, End or Down past the value. Backspace and Delete work as in any field (later characters move up).
- **Paste:** the code is cleaned (`123-456` becomes `123456`). A whole code replaces the value; a part is inserted at the caret. The input gets `input` (`insertFromPaste`).
- **Autofill:** a code the browser fills in (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`) is cleaned and drawn.
- **Apps** that set the value in code fire `input` on the input; canon.js redraws. Form resets are followed.
- Codes read left to right in every language: the cells keep their order in right-to-left.

Without canon.js the input is one text field, about as wide as the code (typed `attr()`; elsewhere 8 characters wide).

## States

| State | Hook | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Focus | `.canon-otp-cell[data-active]` | The caret's cell, while the input has focus. |
| Hover | the box's `:hover` | On every cell but the active one. |
| Error | `aria-invalid="true"` on the input (or `:user-invalid`) | With a danger message, in a Field. |
| Disabled | `disabled` | |

## Core

- Without canon.js the input is sized by its `maxlength` (`1.5ch` a character). With canon.js it covers the box, `opacity: 0`, over `.canon-otp-cells`: a flex row of groups `--canon-otp-gap` apart (default 0.75rem), `direction: ltr`.
- Cells are square at the control height (`--canon-control-block-size`), the control's font size, tabular figures. An empty cell's `::before` shows its `data-placeholder`.

## Accessibility

- One labelled text input: its name, value, description and state are the native ones. The cells are `aria-hidden`.
- `autocomplete="one-time-code"` lets browsers and phones offer a code from a message; `inputmode="numeric"` brings up a number pad.
- Focus is shown on the cell where typing will go; themes show it by more than color (the ring).

## Theme obligations

- Cells visibly separate, the groups apart; the active cell clearly marked; an empty active cell shows where typing goes (a caret).
- Text Input's states on the cells: hover, focus, error, disabled.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Submitting the form when the code is complete | An option if it comes up (`data-autosubmit`); apps can listen for `input` with a full value |
| Success and warning (data-intent) | With the rest of Text Input's intents, if needed |
| A resend link and countdown | The app, next to the field |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Cells 32 / 40 / 48 square, text 12 / 14 / 16 (Text Input's). Groups 12 / 14 / 16 apart, the separator 8 / 12 / 16 long. Corners 4 / 8 / 12 at a group's ends.

Cells are Text Input's frame (white, a zinc-200 line; dark zinc-900, zinc-700), joined in a group by one line between neighbours; a group of three is 96 / 120 / 144 wide. The separator is a 1px zinc-300 line (dark zinc-700). The states, Text Input's: hover zinc-400 on every cell; the active cell blue-600 with a 3px blue-100 ring (dark blue-400, blue-900) and, empty, a blinking caret (steady with reduced motion); error red; disabled zinc-50 cells with zinc-400 text; the placeholder in zinc-400 (dark zinc-500).

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/label.md

# Label

Tier: **T0** (the info tooltip is T0 where interest invokers exist, polyfilled by canon.js)

What a control is called, with everything that goes with the name: a required marker, "(optional)", an info button with a tooltip, and a description. The first part split out of Field; Field, Slider and Range Slider use it, and Fieldset and checkbox groups can later.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-label">
  <label class="canon-label-text" for="phone">Phone <span class="canon-label-optional">(optional)</span></label>
  <button type="button" class="canon-label-info" interestfor="phone-info" aria-describedby="phone-info">
    <span class="canon-visually-hidden">About phone</span>
  </button>
  <div class="canon-tooltip" id="phone-info" popover="hint" role="tooltip" data-placement="block-end inline-end">We only call about deliveries.</div>
  <p class="canon-label-description" id="phone-description">Include the country code.</p>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-label` | yes | The block. In a field, its first child (the field's label area). |
| `.canon-label-text` | yes | The name. `<label for>` when it names a control; an element with an `id` when it names a group (`role="group"` + `aria-labelledby`, as Range Slider does). One per block. |
| `.canon-label-optional` | no | Inside the label text, so it is read with the name ("Phone (optional)"). **Author text**, in the page's language. |
| `.canon-label-info` | no | `<button type="button">` with `interestfor` and `aria-describedby` pointing at a [Tooltip](tooltip.md) (it says more than the button's name), and a name (visually hidden text or `aria-label`) that says what it is about. The theme draws the icon. A sibling of the label text: buttons can't go inside a `<label>`. |
| `.canon-tooltip` | with info | The info button's tooltip, right after it. `data-placement` is the author's (`block-end inline-end` is a good fit). Text only: anything interactive belongs in a Popover. |
| `.canon-label-description` | no | Helper text, with an `id`. The control (or the group) lists it in `aria-describedby`. |

- **Required** is the control's native `required`; the theme draws the marker (it is not read: the control already says it). Themes find it beside the label: a required sibling, or one inside a sibling (a field's box). A control is required or optional, never both.
- **Size** follows `data-size` like the field it labels (inherited from the field or a container).
- Without the info button and description it is just `<div class="canon-label"><label class="canon-label-text" for="x">Name</label></div>`.

## Accessibility

- The label text is the control's name. "(optional)" is part of it; the required marker is not.
- The description is read after the name, through `aria-describedby`.
- The info button is reachable by keyboard; its tooltip shows on hover and focus, and `aria-describedby` reads it as the button's description. Don't put information there that people need to fill the field: that belongs in the description.

## Core

- A wrapping row: the label text takes the room left, the info button sits at the end of the first line, the description gets a line of its own.
- Long labels wrap; the info button stays on the first line.
- "(optional)" floats to the end of the label's last line.
- The info button: user-agent styles reset, the size of an icon (`--canon-icon-size`).

## Theme obligations

- Draw the required marker when the label's parent holds a required control (`:has(> .canon-label):has(> :required, > * > :required)`), and hide it from assistive tech (`content: "*" / ""`).
- Draw the info icon, with hover and focus states; the focus ring like buttons'.
- Themes that put the description elsewhere (under the box, say) use `.canon-label { display: contents }` and place the parts in the field's grid.

## Not in the contract

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Generated "(optional)" or "(required)" words | Not offered: words are the author's |
| Rich content in the tooltip (links, buttons) | Popover |
| Character counter | Field (`canon-field-counter`, reserved) |
| Label action ("Forgot password?") | Field (`canon-field-action`) |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Label 12 / 14 / 16px medium on 16 / 20 / 24px lines; description 10 / 12 / 14px on 12 / 16 / 20px, 4 / 6 / 8px below; info icon 16 / 20 / 24px. md by default, like the controls.

Label zinc-900 (dark white); red-700 `*` (dark red-300), semibold, 4px after the label; "(optional)" zinc-500, regular; info Lucide `info`, zinc-400 (dark zinc-500), darker on hover and focus; description zinc-500 (dark zinc-400). The tooltip stays sm at every size and, end-aligned, reaches past the icon so its arrow sits under the icon (15px in from the edge).

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/number-input.md

# Number Input

Tier: **T2** (without canon.js it is a native number field: typing and the arrow keys)

A count people nudge up and down: guests, seats, retries. A native `<input type="number">` in a `.canon-number` box, between two [Buttons](button.md) that step it; or, for a number typed as often as nudged, with both buttons stacked at its end.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-field">
  <div class="canon-label"><label class="canon-label-text" for="guests">Guests</label></div>
  <div class="canon-number">
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-display="icon" commandfor="guests" command="--canon-step-down">
      <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="minus" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="canon-button-label">Fewer guests</span>
    </button>
    <input type="number" id="guests" name="guests" value="2" min="1" max="8">
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-display="icon" commandfor="guests" command="--canon-step-up">
      <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="plus" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="canon-button-label">More guests</span>
    </button>
  </div>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-number` | yes | The box. In a [Field](field.md) it takes the control's place; it is as wide as its parts. |
| `<input type="number">` | yes | The value, `min`, `max`, `step` and the form value. Named by a `<label for>` (in a Field) or `aria-label`. |
| The step buttons | yes | Around the input: first `command="--canon-step-down"`, last `command="--canon-step-up"` (icons `minus` and `plus`). At the end: after the input, step-up then step-down (icons `chevron-up` and `chevron-down`). Both `commandfor` the input, icon only (`data-display="icon"`), their labels the author's ("Fewer guests"). |

### Buttons at the end

```html
<div class="canon-number">
  <input type="number" id="port" name="port" value="8080" min="1024" max="65535">
  <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-display="icon" commandfor="port" command="--canon-step-up">
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="chevron-up" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="canon-button-label">Higher port</span>
  </button>
  <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-display="icon" commandfor="port" command="--canon-step-down">
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="chevron-down" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="canon-button-label">Lower port</span>
  </button>
</div>
```

- **The order says which:** the input first, then step-up, then step-down (icons `chevron-up` and `chevron-down`): the box fills its place like a [Text Input](text-input.md), the value starts where a text field's does, and the two buttons stack at its end, up over down. For a number typed as often as nudged that lines up with the fields around it: a port, a year, a quantity in a long form. Everything else (the keys, holding, the limits, the roll) is the same.
- **For counts:** whole numbers in a small range, nudged more than typed: the buttons around the value. A free number (a price, a weight with its unit, a percentage) is a [Text Input](text-input.md) with `type="number"` and a suffix.
- The value is the input's: typing, the arrow keys (the browser steps by `step`), `required`, `min` / `max` / `step` validation and the form value are all native.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `min`, `max`, `step` (native) | input | numbers | none, none, 1 | — |
| `data-size` | the field, the box or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |

Everything else is native: `required`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`.

## Behavior (canon.js)

- **The buttons** step with the browser's `stepDown()` / `stepUp()` (so `min`, `max` and `step` apply) and fire `input` and `change`.
- They are out of the tab order (the input is one stop; its arrow keys step), and a press doesn't take focus from the input.
- **At a limit** its button is disabled (− at `min`, + at `max`); both are while the input is `disabled` or `readonly`. Values typed or set in code are followed.
- **Holding a button down** repeats the step (after 0.4 s, every 60 ms) until released or at the limit.
