- **A step rolls the value** (a button or the arrow keys; not typing): the box is `data-rolling="up"` or `"down"` while the theme's animations run, restarted by the next step. For whole numbers canon.js puts an `aria-hidden` `.canon-number-ticker` over the input's text holding the old value and the new one (the theme moves them and hides the input's text meanwhile); for other values (which each browser writes its own way, `3.5` or `3,5`) the theme rolls the input's own text.
- Without canon.js (`scripting: none`) the buttons are hidden, like every Canon command, and the field is a plain number input.

## States

| State | Hook |
|---|---|
| Focus | the input's `:focus` (the box shows it) |
| Error | `aria-invalid="true"` on the input, or `:user-invalid` |
| Disabled | `disabled` on the input |
| Read-only | `readonly` on the input |
| A button at its limit | `disabled` on the button (canon.js) |
| Rolling after a step | `data-rolling="up"` / `"down"` on the box (canon.js) |

## Core

- The box: an inline flex row. The input: centered tabular figures, growing with its value (`field-sizing: content`), the browser's spin buttons hidden (`appearance: textfield`).
- Buttons at the end: the box is a grid as wide as its place (in a Field, the control's full width), the input start-aligned across both rows, the two buttons a column at the end, one row each.

## Accessibility

- One stop for Tab: the input, a spinbutton to screen readers, with its value, min and max. The arrow keys step it.
- The buttons have names ("Fewer guests"), for pointer and switch users; they are not Tab stops.
- A disabled button at a limit tells sighted users the limit is reached; the input's own `min` / `max` tell screen readers.

## Theme obligations

- The box reads as one control: Text Input's states (hover, focus, error, disabled, read-only) over the whole of it.
- A button at its limit visibly unavailable.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Bigger steps (Shift, Page Up / Down) | canon.js, if it comes up |
| A unit inside the box ("kg") | Text Input's suffix (a free number) |
| Formatting while typing (thousands separators) | If it comes up |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** 32 / 40 / 48 tall: the buttons square, the value at least 48 / 64 / 80px wide (112 / 144 / 176 in all), Text Input's type; corners 4 / 8 / 12 at the ends.

The value in Text Input's frame (white, zinc-200; dark zinc-900, zinc-700), centered; Text Input's faint lift under the whole box; the buttons zinc-100 with zinc-200 lines on their outer sides (dark zinc-700, no line), icons zinc-500 (dark white). From Text Input and Button: hover a darker frame (zinc-400), focus blue-600 with Text Input's 3px halo around the whole box, error red, read-only dashed, disabled zinc-50 with zinc-400 text; the buttons zinc-200 on hover and zinc-300 pressed (dark zinc-600, zinc-500); a button at its limit fades its icon (zinc-300, dark zinc-500).

**Motion:** a step rolls the value (0.2s): stepping up, the old value slides up and out as the new one comes up from below, both fading; stepping down, the other way. A value with decimals rolls in alone, from as far as the box leaves room. With reduced motion it only fades.

**Buttons at the end:** Text Input's frame, states and lift on the whole box, the value where a text input's sits (start-aligned, 12 / 16 / 20 in). The buttons a column 4px in from the end, top and bottom, 20 / 24 / 28 wide: zinc-100 (dark zinc-800), split by a 1px line of the box's color, its corners the box's less 4px; chevrons 10 / 14 / 18, zinc-500 (dark zinc-400); hover zinc-200 (dark zinc-700), pressed zinc-300 (dark zinc-600), at a limit the chevron fades (zinc-300, dark zinc-500). Read-only, the box's line dashed; disabled, zinc-50 (dark zinc-800). The value rolls from where it starts.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/password.md

# Password

Tier: **T0** (show / hide, generate, rule checks, Caps Lock and confirmation are T2, via canon.js; real strength scoring is the app's)

A password box with show / hide, and, when people choose a new password, a strength meter and the rules it must meet. Three parts, each usable alone; with a [Label](label.md) they make a [Field](field.md).

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-password">
  <input id="pw" type="password" name="password" autocomplete="new-password" placeholder
         aria-label="Password" aria-describedby="pw-strength pw-rules">
  <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-display="icon"
          aria-pressed="false" commandfor="pw" command="--canon-toggle-password">
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="eye" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="canon-button-label">Show password</span>
  </button>
</div>

<meter class="canon-password-strength" id="pw-strength" min="0" max="4" value="2"
       aria-label="Password strength" aria-valuetext="Weak"></meter>

<div class="canon-password-rules" id="pw-rules">
  <p class="canon-password-rules-title">Password must contain:</p>
  <ul>
    <li class="canon-password-rule" data-state="met">at least 8 characters</li>
    <li class="canon-password-rule">at least 1 number</li>
  </ul>
</div>
```

### The box: `.canon-password`

[Text Input](text-input.md)'s box, frame, sizes and states, around `<input type="password">`.

- **Show / hide:** a trailing button with `command="--canon-toggle-password"` (canon.js) switches `type` to `text` and back, and sets `aria-pressed`; its label stays "Show password". Hidden without scripting.
- **Generate** (optional): a button with `command="--canon-generate-password"` (icon `sparkles`, label "Generate password") fills in a random password from the browser's secure source: at least 16 characters, or the longest `min-length` rule, with every kind of character. It shows it (show / hide pressed), fills any confirmation (`data-match`) too, and announces "Password generated". Before show / hide.
- These two are the only buttons the box takes.
- **Caps Lock** (canon.js): while it is on as people type, the input gets `data-state="caps-lock"`, announced once ("Caps Lock is on"); themes show it in the box. Cleared on leaving.
- Optional leading `.canon-icon`. No prefix or suffix.
- `autocomplete="new-password"` when choosing one (password managers offer to generate it), `"current-password"` when signing in.
- Status: `aria-invalid="true"` for an error; `data-intent="warning"` or `"success"` on the box, as for Text Input.

### Strength: `meter.canon-password-strength`

A native `<meter>`, `min="0" max="4"`: 0 empty, 1 weakest, 2 weak, 3 medium, 4 strong. The fill is the meter's own value.

- **The app scores the password** (e.g. zxcvbn) and sets `value` and `aria-valuetext` (the word: "Weak"). Color never says it alone.
- **Or `data-score="rules"`:** canon.js scores it from the rules met (none 0 → all 4) and sets the word from the strings. A simple stand-in: it measures the rules, not how guessable the password is.
- Named with `aria-label` (or a visible label).
- **The word, visible** (optional): `<p class="canon-password-strength-label" aria-hidden="true">Weak</p>` right after the meter. Hidden from assistive tech (the meter says it); canon.js keeps it in step when it scores.

### Rules: `.canon-password-rules`

A title (`.canon-password-rules-title`) and a `<ul>` of `.canon-password-rule` items, in the author's words.

| `data-state` | Means |
|---|---|
| (none) | Not met yet |
| `met` | Met |
| `error` | Not met, after the person tried to submit |

- **Screen readers hear the state:** core gives each item's icon the alternative text "Met: " or "Not met: " (strings `--canon-text-rule-met` and `--canon-text-rule-not-met`, translated in `i18n/<lang>.css`). The theme draws the icon.
- **Who sets the states:** the app, or canon.js when a rule carries its check in `data-rule`:

  | `data-rule` | Met when the value has |
  |---|---|
  | `min-length:N` | at least N characters |
  | `digit` | a digit |
  | `lowercase` / `uppercase` | a lowercase / uppercase letter |
  | `symbol` | a character that is neither a letter, a digit nor a space |
  | `pattern:<regex>` | a match for the regular expression |

  canon.js marks rules met or pending as people type; while any is unmet, the input is invalid (`setCustomValidity`, "The password doesn't meet every rule."), so the form won't submit; a failed submit marks the unmet ones `error` until they are met.
- **Showing them while they matter** (optional): `data-reveal="focus"` on the rules. canon.js collapses them (`data-state="collapsed"`) until the input has focus or a value, and again once every rule is met; themes animate the rows in one by one. Collapsed rules are still read (through `aria-describedby`). Without canon.js they always show.
- Not a live region: announcing every keystroke is noise. The box lists the rules in `aria-describedby`, so they are read on focus.

### Confirmation (optional)

A second Password box whose input has `data-match="<id of the first input>"`. canon.js keeps it invalid while it differs ("The passwords don't match.") and gives its box `data-state="match"` when it matches; themes show that as success.

In a [Field](field.md), the strength (with its word at its end) and the rules go under the box and over the message, across the field. With an empty message, these problems (rules unmet, passwords differ, required and empty) show as the field's error message, not the browser's bubble.

## Accessibility

- The box is named by its label (in a Field) or `aria-label`; the strength and the rules describe it (`aria-describedby`).
- Show / hide is a toggle button (`aria-pressed`), never a checkbox labelled "Show".
- Don't block paste.

## Theme obligations

- The box: Text Input's.
- Strength: a fill per step that doesn't rely on color alone where the system allows (Canon: its length).
- Rules: pending, met and error distinct in icon and text, not by color alone.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Scoring the password | App |
| Server-side rules (breached passwords, history) | App: set the rule's state yourself |

## Look

Box: Text Input's, the eye (Lucide `eye`) in the icon color. Strength: a 4px bar, zinc-200 (dark zinc-700), a quarter per step: red-500, yellow-500, lime-500, green-600 (dark: the 600s, green-700). Rules: title in the sm label's type; rows 8px apart, a 16px dot 4px before 12px text. Pending zinc-300 dot, zinc-600 text (dark zinc-600, zinc-400); met green-600 dot with a white check, zinc-900 text (dark white); error red-700 dot with a white "!", red-700 text (dark red-300). Strength and rules have one size. Also: the strength's word (12px medium, in the fill's color, dark the 400s); Caps Lock as Lucide `arrow-big-up-dash` before the buttons; a confirmation that matches in the success colors; revealed rules open to their height in 0.3s and fade in from 4px above, 50ms apart (none with reduced motion).

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/range-slider.md

# Range Slider

Tier: **T0** (fill, no-crossing and values are T2, via canon.js)

Pick a from–to range on one track: a price range, working hours, a severity band. Single values use Slider (`slider.md`), whose anatomy, marks, vertical hint, tokens and theme obligations this component shares.

```html
<div class="canon-field" role="group" aria-labelledby="price-label">
  <div class="canon-label">
    <span class="canon-label-text" id="price-label">Price</span>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-control">
    <output class="canon-control-value" for="price-min" aria-hidden="true">200</output>
    <input type="range" id="price-min" name="price-min" min="0" max="1000" step="10" value="200" aria-label="Minimum">
    <input type="range" id="price-max" name="price-max" min="0" max="1000" step="10" value="800" aria-label="Maximum">
    <output class="canon-control-value" for="price-max" aria-hidden="true">800</output>
  </div>
</div>
```

- **Two native range inputs on one track**, each with its own `name`, so the form submits both and each thumb has native keyboard and accessibility support. Tab reaches the first, then the second.
- **The label names the pair, not an input:** the label text is a `<span id>` (see `label.md`), with `role="group"` and `aria-labelledby` on the field. A description goes in `aria-describedby` on the field. Each input names its thumb with `aria-label` ("Minimum", "Maximum", "From", "To"): the author's words.
- Both inputs share `min`, `max`, `step` and `list`.
- **Without JS it still works** (T0): only the thumbs take the pointer, so each can be dragged. The thumbs can cross; the server validates.
- **canon.js (T2):**
  - stops the moving thumb at the other one,
  - sets `--canon-slider-start` and `--canon-slider-end` on the box, and core fills between the thumbs,
  - keeps both `<output>`s in sync (named marks included),
  - when the thumbs meet, raises the one that can still move (`data-state="front"` on the first input, past the middle).
- The values: an `<output>` before the inputs belongs to the first thumb, one after them to the second. A theme may put them at both ends or as a bubble over each thumb (Canon: bubbles). For bubbles, canon.js reports each value's width as `--canon-slider-start-value-size` and `--canon-slider-end-value-size` on the box, so a theme can push the two apart where they would meet.
- The first input draws the track; the second draws only its thumb.

## Look

As Slider, plus:

**Range:** Slider's track and thumbs, zinc-900 (dark white) between them; a value bubble over a thumb only while that thumb is hovered, focused or dragged (each input takes the pointer only over its thumb, so its `:hover` is the thumb's); when both show, they sit side by side (4px apart) around their middle where they would meet, each arrow kept inside its bubble

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/rich-text.md

# Rich Text

Tier: **T2** (without canon.js the textarea shows the HTML as text)

A [Textarea](textarea.md) for formatted text: headings, emphasis, links, lists. `data-rich` on the box; canon.js draws a [Toolbar](toolbar.md) and an area to write in. The `<textarea>` keeps the value, clean HTML, which is what the form sends.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-field">
  <div class="canon-label">
    <label class="canon-label-text" for="notes">Release notes</label>
    <p class="canon-label-description" id="notes-description">Shown to everyone on the changelog.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-textarea" data-rich data-tools="history block marks link lists">
    <textarea id="notes" name="notes" rows="6" placeholder="Write something…"
              aria-describedby="notes-description">&lt;p&gt;Hello&lt;/p&gt;</textarea>
  </div>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-textarea[data-rich]` | yes | A Textarea box. |
| `<textarea>` | yes | The value: HTML (escaped in the markup, as any textarea text). Its label, description, `placeholder`, `rows`, `data-max-lines`, `required`, `disabled` and `readonly` are the editor's. |

### What canon.js adds

Themes style these; authors don't write them.

```html
<div class="canon-textarea" data-rich>
  <div class="canon-toolbar canon-rich-toolbar" role="toolbar" aria-label="Formatting" data-size="sm">…</div>
  <textarea …></textarea>                                    <!-- hidden: the value -->
  <div class="canon-rich-area" role="textbox" aria-multiline="true" contenteditable="true"
       aria-labelledby="…" aria-describedby="…">…</div>      <!-- data-empty while empty -->
</div>
```

- The toolbar is made of Canon components: [Button Groups](button-group.md) (toggles with `aria-pressed`, the alignment `data-select="one"`), a [Select](select.md) for the block style, single [Buttons](button.md), [Popovers](popover.md) (link, text color, image) and a [Menu](menu.md) (Insert). It is small (`sm`; `md` in a large box).
- The textarea stays in the box, hidden (`aria-hidden`, out of the tab order): still the form value, the label's target and what the browser checks. Its focus (the label, a failed check) goes to the area.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-rich` | `.canon-textarea` | (present) | — | no |
| `data-tools` | `.canon-textarea` | groups, space-separated, or `all` (below) | `history block marks link lists` | no |
| `rows`, `data-max-lines` | textarea | as [Textarea](textarea.md): the height, growing up to N lines (`none`: no limit) | 2, fixed | — |
| `data-size` | the box or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |

**Tools**, shown in this order whatever order they are written in:

| Group | Controls |
|---|---|
| `history` | Undo, Redo |
| `block` | Paragraph, Heading 1, 2, 3 (written `h2`, `h3`, `h4`: content sits under the page's own `h1`), Quote, Code |
| `align` | Align left, Center, Align right, Justify (one at a time; written as logical `start` / `end`) |
| `marks` | Bold, Italic, Underline, Strikethrough |
| `link` | Link: a popover with the address, "Open in a new tab", Apply and Remove link |
| `color` | Text color: a popover of Swatches (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, gray) and Default color |
| `clear` | Clear formatting |
| `script` | Subscript, Superscript |
| `lists` | Numbered list, Bulleted list |
| `indent` | Decrease, Increase indent (in lists) |
| `insert` | A Menu: Horizontal line, Image… (a popover: address and description) |

## The value

Only this HTML is kept. Whatever is typed, pasted or set is cleaned to it, both when it is shown and when it is written back:

| Kind | Kept |
|---|---|
| Blocks | `p`, `h2`, `h3`, `h4` (`h1` becomes `h2`, `h5` and `h6` `h4`), `blockquote`, `pre` (its text only), `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `hr`, `img` (`src`, `alt`) |
| Inline | `strong` (from `b`), `em` (from `i`), `u`, `s` (from `strike`, `del`), `sub`, `sup`, `br`, `a` (`href`; `target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener"`), `span` with a palette color (`style="color: #2563eb"`) |
| Alignment | `style="text-align: center \| end \| justify"` on blocks (left and right are turned into start and end for the text's direction; start, the default, isn't written) |

- Links and images take `http:`, `https:`, relative addresses, `mailto:` and `tel:` (links only); anything else (`javascript:`, `data:`) is dropped.
- Dropped with their content: scripts, styles, embeds, forms. Unwrapped (their text kept): every other element, classes, ids, event attributes and other styles. A `div` of text becomes a paragraph; loose words between blocks go into paragraphs.
- **Empty is empty:** an editor with no text (and no image or line) has the value `""`, so `required` works.
- The value is written on each change (`input` on the textarea), and `change` when the editor loses focus. An app that sets the textarea's value and fires `input` sees the editor follow; form resets are followed.

## Behavior (canon.js)

- **The toolbar follows the selection:** toggles show what is applied (Bold pressed in bold text), the block style shows the paragraph's (Heading 2), the alignment its side; Indent and Outdent are available in lists only.
- **Buttons keep the selection:** pressing one doesn't take focus from the text (from the keyboard, focus stays on the button).
- **Keys:** the toolbar is one Tab stop (Toolbar's arrows); in the text the browser's own ⌘B / Ctrl+B, ⌘I, ⌘U, ⌘Z work, and ⌘K / Ctrl+K opens the link popover.
- **Paste** is cleaned (HTML), or inserted as text.
- **Popovers:** the link popover opens on the selection's link if there is one (with Remove link); without a selection, the address becomes the link's text. Color and image popovers close once applied; focus goes back to the text.
- **States:** `disabled` and `readonly` on the textarea make the area uneditable (`aria-disabled`, `aria-readonly`) and the toolbar unavailable; `required`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` are copied to the area. A failed check shows in the field's message (Field's validation), the box turns red, and focus goes into the text.
- Without canon.js the textarea is an ordinary one showing the HTML as text.

## States

The Textarea box's: focus in the text rings the whole editor; error, disabled, read-only and the intents as on any box.

## Accessibility

- The area is a multi-line textbox named by the field's label, described by its description and messages, with `aria-required` / `aria-invalid` from the textarea.
- The toolbar is a named toolbar, its buttons named, toggles pressed or not, shortcuts in `aria-keyshortcuts`.
- Headings in the content start at `h2`, under the page's `h1`.
- An image's description is asked for in its popover (its `alt`).

## Theme obligations

- The toolbar visibly part of the editor; the text styled readably (headings, lists, quotes, code, links).
- The placeholder shown while the editor is empty.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Tables, mentions, emoji, file uploads | If they come up (Insert's menu is where they'd go) |
| Markdown shortcuts while typing (`# `, `- `) | If it comes up |
| A character counter | Counter counts the value's HTML today; a text count if it comes up |
| Collaborative editing, comments | Out of scope |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** The toolbar sm (md in a lg box), 8px inside the box; the text where a textarea's sits.

The Toolbar inside the Textarea's box, a hairline rule under it; focus in the text rings the whole box. The text: paragraphs 0.75em apart, headings semibold (1.375 / 1.2 / 1em), lists 1.5em in, quotes after a 2px zinc-300 line (dark zinc-600) in zinc-600 (dark zinc-400), code blocks on zinc-100 (dark zinc-800) in JetBrains Mono, code in the text a chip (zinc-100 behind zinc-700, dark zinc-700 behind zinc-100; 4px either side, 2px corners; 0.8em and larger corners in a heading; Link's blue on blue-50, dark blue-950, in a link), links blue-600 (dark blue-400) underlined, lines hairline rules (black at 10%, dark white at 10%); the placeholder Textarea's.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/save-bar.md

# Save Bar

Tier: **T0** (Save and Discard are a form's own buttons) · tracking changes, saving states, the shortcut and asking before leaving are **T2** (canon.js)

Save and Discard in reach while someone edits, and whether there's anything to save: the last thing in an edit form, sticking to the bottom of the window while the form goes on below.

## Elements

```html
<form class="canon-card" action="/invoices/2041" method="post">
  …fields…
  <footer class="canon-save-bar">
    <p class="canon-save-bar-status"></p>
    <button type="reset" class="canon-button" data-intent="neutral">…Discard…</button>
    <button type="submit" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="high" aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+S Control+S">
      <span class="canon-button-label">Save</span><kbd class="canon-kbd" aria-hidden="true">⌘S</kbd>
    </button>
  </footer>
</form>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-save-bar` | yes | Inside its `<form>`, last. In a [Card](card.md) that is the form, the card's footer. |
| `p.canon-save-bar-status` | — | First. canon.js keeps it (and adds it when it's missing): a [Status Indicator](status.md) saying where the form stands. |
| Discard | no | `<button type="reset">`, neutral: the browser's reset, bringing back what's saved. |
| Save | yes | `<button type="submit">`, high emphasis, last. `aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+S Control+S"` and a [Kbd](kbd.md) for its shortcut. |

- **What's saved is the form's defaults.** The values a control starts with (`value`, `checked`, `selected` in the markup) are the saved ones. A control that differs from its default is a change; Discard (reset) brings the defaults back. After a save, the values shown become the new defaults.
- **Unavailable, not disabled:** with nothing to save, and while saving, canon.js makes Save and Discard `aria-disabled="true"`. They stay in place and in the Tab order, heard as unavailable, the status beside them saying why ("No changes", "Saving…"); a click, Enter in a field or the shortcut does nothing. Never `disabled` (out of reach, unexplained) and never hidden (the buttons would move).
- **One per form.** A page with several forms has a bar in each; the shortcut saves the one focus is in.
- **Save Bar or [Form Layout](form-layout.md)'s actions?** A form that edits something saved (a record, settings) ends with a Save Bar: there is a saved state to compare with and to lose. A form that creates (a new invoice, a sign-up) ends with actions, sticky (`data-sticky`) if it's long.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-state` | the bar (canon.js) | `changed` · `saving` · `saved` · `failed` | none: no changes | — |
| `--canon-sticky-offset-end` | a container (a style) | a length: how far from the window's bottom it sticks | `0` | yes (CSS) |
| `--canon-page-inset` | a container (a style) | the page's side padding, which the bar reaches across on a page | `0` | yes (CSS) |

## Core

- A row: the status at the start, the buttons at the end; it wraps when narrow.
- Sticky at the bottom (`--canon-sticky-offset-end`) while the form continues below; at the form's end, it sits there.
- On a page (not in a Card), it reaches across the page's side padding.

## Behavior (T2, canon.js)

- **A new status:** when the state changes (changed, saving, saved, failed, none), the status is marked `data-updated` while the theme's animations run; a count changing within a state isn't.
- **Tracking:** on every `input` and `change`, canon.js compares the form's named controls with their defaults and counts the changes, once per name ("2 unsaved changes"). The bar is `data-state="changed"`.
- **Discard:** the browser's reset; the count goes back to "No changes".
- **Availability:** Save and Discard are `aria-disabled` while there are no changes or while saving; an unavailable button's click (and Enter in a field, which clicks Save) is cancelled.
- **Saving:** on `submit` the bar is `saving` ("Saving…").
  - A form that submits the browser's way leaves the page: nothing more to do.
  - An app saving on its own (`preventDefault()` on `submit`, then `fetch`) answers on the form:
    - `canon-saved`: the values become the new defaults, the bar `saved` ("Changes saved").
    - `canon-save-failed` (`detail.message` optional): the bar `failed` ("Couldn't save", or the message), the changes kept.
- **Leaving:** with unsaved changes, closing or reloading the page asks first (the browser's own question). Leaving within an app's own navigation is the app's to check: `form:has(.canon-save-bar[data-state="changed"])`.
- **Shortcut:** the Save button's `aria-keyshortcuts` (⌘S, Ctrl+S) submit its form: the one focus is in, or the only one on the page. The browser's own "save page" is kept from opening.
- Values the app changes in code fire no events: dispatch `input` on the control so the bar sees them.

## Accessibility

- The status is a `role="status"` region: "2 unsaved changes", "Saving…", "Changes saved", "Couldn't save" are heard as they come, without moving focus.
- The state is in the words, not only the dot.
- A submit with invalid fields doesn't save: the browser (and [Field](field.md)'s messages) points to the first one.
- The shortcut is declared (`aria-keyshortcuts`); its Kbd is hidden from screen readers.

## Theme obligations

- The bar set apart from the form scrolling under it once stuck (a line, a fill).
- Save the most prominent thing in it.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the status is on the right.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Asking before leaving inside an app | The app, reading `data-state` |
| Saving by itself as people type (autosave) | If it comes up: the same states, without Save |
| Showing which fields changed | If it comes up: `data-changed` on the field |

## Look

**Sizes:** The shell's inset above and below (8 / 12 / 16); 8px between things. In a card, the card's padding.

A Card's footer that stays. The status a Status Indicator: no changes neutral, changed warning (amber), saving info (pulsing), saved success, failed danger. In a card: the card's white and its line above. On a page: the page's color, the shell's line above once it's stuck (a scroll-state query).

**Motion:** a new status rises 4px into place and fades in (0.2s); a count changing within one doesn't move. With reduced motion it only fades.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/select.md

# Select

Tier: **T0** (the styled list is T1: browsers that support it, fine pointers; its steady width is T2)

Pick one option from a list. A native `<select>` in a box: keyboard, form value, validation and the mobile picker are the browser's. Where the browser supports customizable selects (`appearance: base-select`), the list is styled too; elsewhere, and on touch devices, it is the native list.

Searching, or picking several values, is a [Combobox](combobox.md): the same markup in `.canon-combobox`.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-select">
  <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="globe" aria-hidden="true"></span>      <!-- optional -->
  <select id="region" name="region" required>
    <button><selectedcontent></selectedcontent></button>                      <!-- optional -->
    <option value="" hidden>Please select</option>                            <!-- placeholder, optional -->
    <optgroup label="Europe">
      <option value="eu-west-1">Ireland</option>
      <option value="eu-central-1">Frankfurt</option>
    </optgroup>
    <hr class="canon-separator">
    <optgroup label="Asia">
      <option value="ap-northeast-1" disabled>Tokyo</option>
    </optgroup>
  </select>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-select` | yes | The box: [Text Input](text-input.md)'s frame, sizes and states. The theme draws the arrow. The select reaches under the whole box, so clicking anywhere opens it. |
| `<select>` | yes | Single choice: no `multiple`, no `size`. Named by a `<label for>` (in a Field) or `aria-label`. |
| `.canon-icon` | no | Leading, `aria-hidden="true"`. |
| `<option value="">` | no | **Placeholder:** first, with an empty value; `hidden` keeps it out of the list. With `required`, the select can't be submitted while it is chosen. Themes show it muted. |
| `<optgroup label>` | no | A group with a caption. |
| `<hr class="canon-separator">` | no | A [Separator](separator.md) between options or groups. |
| Clear button | no | After the select: a [Button](button.md) with `command="--canon-clear"` and `commandfor` the select. Goes back to the placeholder (or to nothing chosen); hidden while nothing is chosen. |
| `<button><selectedcontent></selectedcontent></button>` | no | First child. The closed box shows the chosen option's markup (icon, avatar, label); descriptions are left to the list. Without it, the closed box shows the option's text. |

### Options

Plain text, or markup inside the option, in this order:

| Part | Notes |
|---|---|
| `.canon-icon` or `.canon-avatar` | First. Decorative (`aria-hidden`); the theme sizes it. |
| `.canon-option-label` | The name. |
| `.canon-option-description` | After the label, muted. Shown in the list only. |

- **In a text input:** a `.canon-select` box can be the first or last child of a [Text Input](text-input.md) (a country code, a currency). It drops its own frame for a line beside the value, and keeps the width of its widest option.
- **Keep a space between the parts:** the native list shows the option's plain text ("t3.large 2 vCPU · 8 GiB").
- **Don't use the `label` attribute with rich options:** in a customizable list it replaces the option's markup.
- `disabled`: shown, not choosable.
- `data-intent="danger"`: an option that destroys something ("Delete the project"). Rare in a Select; mostly for menus.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-size` | box or a container | `xs` · `sm` · `md` · `lg` · `xl` · `2xl` (three-size themes: xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes (the list follows) |
| `data-intent` | box | `warning` · `success` | none | no |
| `data-intent` | option | `danger` | none | no |

## States

| State | Hook | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Open | `select:open` | Shown like focus; the arrow turns. |
| Focus | the select's `:focus` | |
| Placeholder | the empty option `:checked` | Muted text |
| Error | `aria-invalid="true"`, or `:user-invalid` (`required`, empty) | In a Field, canon.js shows the browser's message there. |
| Warning, success | `data-intent` on the box, or a field's message | |
| Disabled | `disabled` | Wins; a status still shows, softened |
| Option chosen | `option:checked` | The theme marks it (`::checkmark`) |
| Option highlighted | `option:hover`, `option:focus-visible` | Hover and the keyboard's place |

## Core

- The box: the shared box rules (like Text Input), with the select stretched under the box's padding, icon and arrow: themes set `--canon-select-start` and `--canon-select-end`, the distances from the border to the text.
- The list (customizable selects): anchored to the whole box, at least as wide, below it, flipping above when there's no room. The browser's arrow is hidden.
- After closing, core keeps the anchor for 400ms so a close transition fades out in place. **Themes keep close transitions under 400ms.**
- In the closed box, `selectedcontent` shows the label, not the description.

## Behavior (canon.js)

- **A steady width:** a Select that sizes to its content (outside a Field: in a Toolbar, a Pagination, a sentence) keeps the width of its longest choice, so what comes after it doesn't move as the choice changes. A plain select always did this; a styled one is only as wide as the choice it shows, so canon.js measures every choice once the select is shown (and again when the page's fonts have loaded) and sets that as its minimum width. A Field's own Select fills the field and is left alone. Without canon.js a styled select follows its choice.

## Accessibility

- Native: the select's role, keyboard (arrows, type to jump, Enter, Escape) and announcements are the browser's.
- Icons and avatars in options are decorative; the label is what is read.
- The placeholder is not a name: the select still needs a label.

## Theme obligations

- The list readable on every surface it opens over; options as tall as touch targets at their size.
- The chosen option marked by more than color (Canon: a check and medium weight).
- Touch devices keep the native picker.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Searching, filtering | [Combobox](combobox.md) with `data-search` |
| Several values (tags in the box) | [Combobox](combobox.md), `multiple` |
| A search field inside the list | [Combobox](combobox.md) with `data-search="list"` (a select's list can't hold one) |
| Typing a new value | [Combobox](combobox.md) with `data-creatable` |
| Menus of actions (context menu) | Menu |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Box: Text Input's (32 / 40 / 48, radius 4 / 8 / 12); the arrow (Lucide chevron-down, the icon color) 2 / 2 / 0px past the text, turning up while open. List: 4px under the box and 8px wider, so the options' text lines up with the box's; radius 8 / 12 / 16; 4px padding. Options 32 / 40 / 48, the box's text size and inset, radius 4 / 8 / 12. Captions: 10px semibold capitals, 32px rows. Separators: [Separator](separator.md)'s (12 / 16 / 20px rows).

List white (dark zinc-900), no frame: a hairline edge (black at 12%, dark white at 12%) and the floating shadow. Options zinc-900 (dark white); hover zinc-100 (dark zinc-800); chosen medium with a check; disabled zinc-400 (dark zinc-600); destructive red-700 on red-400 at 15% (dark red-300 on red-500 at 20%). Captions zinc-500 (dark zinc-400). Placeholder zinc-500 (dark zinc-400). Styled list for fine pointers only.

**Motion:** the styled list fades in from 97% (0.15s) and fades out where it is (0.1s); with reduced motion it only fades.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/slider.md

# Slider

Tier: **T0** (fill, value display and placed marks are T2, via canon.js)

Pick a value from a continuous or stepped range. For two values (a from–to range), use Range Slider (`range-slider.md`).

## Anatomy

A Slider is a **Field** (`field.md`) whose box holds a native range input:

```
canon-field
├── canon-label                   <label for> + optional description (label.md)
└── canon-control                 no frame around a slider
    ├── canon-control-prefix      optional · min label, author text, aria-hidden
    ├── <input type="range">      the native element, no class
    ├── canon-control-suffix      optional · max label, author text, aria-hidden
    ├── canon-control-value       optional · <output for aria-hidden>, kept in sync by canon.js
    └── <datalist>                optional · named marks, linked with list
└── canon-field-message
```

```html
<div class="canon-field">
  <div class="canon-label">
    <label class="canon-label-text" for="cpu">CPU limit</label>
    <p class="canon-label-description" id="cpu-description">Per instance.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-control">
    <span class="canon-control-prefix" aria-hidden="true">0</span>
    <input type="range" id="cpu" name="cpu" min="0" max="16" step="1" value="4"
           aria-describedby="cpu-description">
    <span class="canon-control-suffix" aria-hidden="true">16 vCPU</span>
    <output class="canon-control-value" for="cpu" aria-hidden="true">4</output>
  </div>
</div>
```

- **The native input does the work:** keyboard, `min` / `max` / `step`, the form value, accessibility. Without CSS or JS it is still a working slider.
- **Min and max labels** are the box's prefix and suffix: author text (the words are the author's, "16 vCPU"), `aria-hidden` like every affix. CSS can't read the input's `min` / `max` from a sibling.
- **The value** is an `<output>` that canon.js keeps in sync. It is `aria-hidden`: the input already exposes its value, and a live `<output>` would announce every change a second time. Without scripting it isn't shown (it would go stale). Themes place it beside the slider or as a bubble over the thumb (Canon: a bubble while the thumb is hovered, focused or dragged).
- Core lays the box out as a grid with named areas, so every slot has its place whatever is present.

## The fill (T2)

CSS can't read a range input's live value, so canon.js sets `--canon-slider-percent` (0–100, unitless) on the box as the value changes, and core draws the fill from it. Without canon.js the slider works, unfilled.

For a value floated over its thumb, canon.js also reports, on the box, the track's length as `--canon-slider-track-length` and the `<output>`'s width as `--canon-slider-value-size` (CSS can't measure either), so a theme can keep the bubble centered on the thumb yet inside the track, and aim its arrow at the thumb.

## Named marks

```html
<input type="range" id="priority" name="priority" min="0" max="2" value="1" list="priority-marks">
<output class="canon-control-value" for="priority" aria-hidden="true">Medium</output>
<datalist id="priority-marks">
  <option value="0">Low</option>
  <option value="1">Medium</option>
  <option value="2">High</option>
</datalist>
```

- The `<datalist>` goes **inside the box**, after the input; themes show it as a row of labels under the track. The labels are the option text (the author's words).
- **T0:** the labels are spread evenly, which is right when the values are evenly spaced.
- **T2:** canon.js places each label at its value (`--canon-mark-percent`, `data-state="placed"` on the list), so uneven values (1 month / 6 months / 1 year) line up. Labels are centered on their value but start-aligned at the minimum and end-aligned at the maximum, so they never overhang the track.
- When the value is on a mark, canon.js shows the mark's name in the `<output>` and sets **`aria-valuetext`** on the input, so screen readers say "Medium", not "1".
- Values are formatted in the element's language (`Intl.NumberFormat`).

## Vertical (author hint)

```html
<div class="canon-field" data-orientation="vertical">
```

- Same hint as on Fieldset, in the `canon.hints` layer. Core stands the input up with native `writing-mode` (minimum at the bottom), so keyboard and accessibility follow.
- The length is `--canon-slider-length` (theme default; the app may override it). Height is layout, not markup.
- The suffix and value sit above the track, the prefix below; named marks beside it, spread evenly (not placed by value).

## States

| State | Hook |
|---|---|
| Focus | `:focus-visible` on the input (themes draw it on the thumb) |
| Disabled | `disabled` |
| Invalid | `aria-invalid="true"` + danger message, or `:user-invalid` |

## Theme contract

Core maps custom properties onto both engines' pseudo-elements (`::-webkit-slider-*`, `::-moz-range-*`), so a theme writes its slider once. **Set them on the box**, where marks and values see them too:

| Property | Draws |
|---|---|
| `--canon-slider-track-size`, `--canon-slider-track-radius` | track thickness and corners |
| `--canon-slider-track`, `--canon-slider-fill` | inactive and active colors |
| `--canon-slider-thumb-inline-size`, `-block-size`, `-radius` | thumb shape |
| `--canon-slider-thumb`, `--canon-slider-thumb-border`, `--canon-slider-thumb-shadow` | thumb paint, halo, focus ring |
| `--canon-slider-thumb-scale` | grow on hover / press without reflow |
| `--canon-slider-track-image` | replaces the fill gradient (on the input) |
| `--canon-slider-length` | vertical length |

Read-only, from canon.js (on the box): `--canon-slider-percent` (the value, 0–100), `--canon-slider-track-length` (the track's length in px, along it, vertical too) and `--canon-slider-value-size` (the `<output>`'s width, for a bubble). A value floated over the thumb can be placed in the track's cell: an absolutely positioned grid item with `grid-area: track` (the box positioned) has that cell as its containing block. Draw a bubble's arrow on the `<output>` itself, not on the input: browsers don't reliably paint (Chromium while it fades) or draw at all (Firefox) pseudo-elements on a range input.

For a custom track (gaps around the thumb, say), themes read `--canon-slider-pos-start`, `--canon-slider-pos-end` (positions on the track, accounting for the thumb's travel) and `--canon-slider-direction` in a `--canon-slider-track-image` declared on the input.

## Theme obligations

- No frame around a slider's box (no border, background, padding or focus ring on the box; focus is on the thumb).
- **No `gap` on a slider's box:** absent slots leave empty grid columns, and gaps would still apply. Core spaces slots with margins.
- Use the slider tokens; style vendor pseudo-elements only for what the tokens can't express.

## Size

**sm:** 4px track, 16px control (14.4px thumb), 12px value

**md / lg:** 5 / 6px, 20 / 24px (18 / 21.6px), 14 / 16px value

## Look

**Track and thumb:** A track a quarter of the control (4 / 5 / 6px), zinc-200 (dark zinc-700), filled zinc-900 (dark white); the thumb the checked radio's look, 90% of the control, white with a zinc-900 ring a quarter of it thick (dark zinc-900 with a white ring). Focus is the choices' ring (2px out, 1px blue-600, dark blue-300); disabled zinc-300 with a zinc-100 middle (dark zinc-600, zinc-400); invalid red-600 (dark red-500)

**Value:** the Tooltip inverted (zinc-900 with white text, in dark mode white with zinc-900 text) at the slider's size, 4px over the control (6px beside it on the left when vertical), only while hovered, focused or dragged; centered on the thumb, sliding in at the ends, its arrow on the thumb

**Min / max labels:** the label description's look

## Deferred

- **Editable value** (a number box you can type into): with Number input.
- **Tick marks on the track** at each named mark.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/swatches.md

# Swatches

Tier: **T0** (expanding is T2, via canon.js)

Pick one color from a few: a radio group drawn as colored circles. Each radio's value is its color and is what the form submits. For any color, use [Color Picker](color-picker.md), which shows these swatches in its popover too.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-field">
  <div class="canon-label"><span class="canon-label-text" id="color-label">Color</span></div>
  <div class="canon-swatches" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="color-label">
    <input type="radio" name="color" value="#3b82f6" aria-label="Blue" checked>
    <input type="radio" name="color" value="#22c55e" aria-label="Green">
    <input type="radio" name="color" value="#ef4444" aria-label="Red">
  </div>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-swatches` | yes | `role="radiogroup"`, named with `aria-labelledby` (the field's label, a `<span id>` as for a [Range Slider](range-slider.md)) or `aria-label`. In a [Field](field.md) it takes the control's place; it is as wide as its swatches. |
| `<input type="radio">` | yes | The only children, one `name`. Each is a swatch: `value` is the color (any CSS color) and the submitted value; `aria-label` names it ("Blue"), since a color has no visible text. |

- **Its color** is the value, read with typed `attr()`. When the value isn't a color (a token or an id: `value="ocean"`), set the color with `style="--canon-swatch: #0ea5e9"`. Browsers without typed `attr()` get it from canon.js, which copies a color value to `--canon-swatch` (an author's `--canon-swatch` always wins).
- **The keyboard is the radio group's:** Tab reaches the chosen swatch (or the first), the arrow keys choose the next one.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-collapse` | `.canon-swatches` | (present) only the chosen swatch shows until the group opens | every swatch shows | no |
| `data-size` | the group or a container | `xs` · `sm` · `md` · `lg` · `xl` · `2xl` (three-size themes: xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes |
| `disabled` (native) | a radio, or all | | | — |
| `checked`, `required` (native) | a radio | | | — |

## Expanding (`data-collapse`, T2)

canon.js adds a chevron button after the swatches (`.canon-swatches-toggle`, `aria-expanded`, named with the `more-colors` string, out of the tab order). While it is closed, only the chosen swatch shows (none chosen: the first, so Tab still reaches the group).

- **Opens** when focus enters the group (Tab) or on a click anywhere in it: closed, the chevron's target is the whole box.
- **Closes** when focus leaves, on Escape, after a click picks a swatch, or on a click after the last swatch: open, the chevron's target is everything from there to the box's end, its full height. With focus still inside, an arrow key, Enter or Space opens it again (the first key only opens).
- Without canon.js every swatch shows: a plain swatch row.

## States

| State | Hook |
|---|---|
| Chosen | `:checked` |
| Hover, focus | `:hover`, `:focus-visible` on the radio |
| Open (expanding) | `.canon-swatches-toggle[aria-expanded="true"]` |
| Disabled | `disabled` on a radio |

## Core

- The group is a wrapping flex row; swatches are `--canon-swatch-size` (default: the icon size), `--canon-swatches-gap` apart. Radios draw nothing themselves (`appearance: none`): themes paint `--canon-swatch-color` on their `::before` / `::after`.
- While an expanding group is closed, the swatches that aren't chosen are hidden.

## Accessibility

- A radio group: the group's name, each swatch's name, its state (checked) and the arrow keys come from the native radios.
- The chevron is for the pointer; keyboard users open the group by entering it. Its `aria-expanded` says whether the other colors show.
- Colors alone don't tell swatches apart for everyone: the names do. Themes mark the chosen swatch by more than color (a dot, a ring).

## Theme obligations

- The chosen swatch marked by more than its color; focus visible on the swatch, or on the box when the box shows the keyboard's place.
- Every swatch visible against the page, white and black included (an outline or a ring where needed).
- An expanding group looks like a control while closed (it opens), and its chevron shows which way it goes.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Several colors at once | Checkboxes drawn the same way, if it comes up |
| Any color, typed or picked | [Color Picker](color-picker.md) |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** The box is a text input's height (32 / 40 / 48), swatches the icon size (16 / 20 / 24), 8 / 10 / 12 apart and from the edges, Text Input's corners (4 / 8 / 12).

A swatch is the radio's circle (90% of the control) in its color; the chosen one has the radio's white dot (a quarter of the control). Hover: a 3px blue-100 halo (dark blue-900); focus: the choices' ring (2px out, 1px blue-600, dark blue-300). The box: white with a zinc-100 line (dark zinc-900, zinc-800). Expanding: Text Input's line and hover, a zinc-400 chevron (dark zinc-500) pointing right while closed and left while open; open, or closed with keyboard focus inside, the box shows Text Input's focus (blue-600 line, 3px blue-100 ring; dark blue-400, blue-900) and the swatches lose their own ring. A 1px edge inside every swatch (10% black, dark 15% white), so white and black swatches still show; disabled swatches at 45% opacity.

**Motion:** opening, the other swatches grow in from the chosen one and fade in (0.2s), the chevron turning; closing, they shrink back into it. Not while canon.js sets the group up (the toggle is `data-state="ready"` after the first paint); none with reduced motion.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/text-input.md

# Text Input

Tier: **T0** (box actions are T2, via canon.js)

A one-line text box around a text-like `<input>` (`text`, `email`, `search`, `url`, `tel`; passwords are [Password](password.md)). On its own it is named with `aria-label`; with a [Label](label.md) it is a [Field](field.md). Multi-line text is [Textarea](textarea.md); selects are [Select](select.md) and [Combobox](combobox.md); number gets a component of its own.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-text-input">
  <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="tag" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="canon-text-input-prefix" aria-hidden="true">$</span>
  <input type="text" inputmode="decimal" aria-label="Price in USD" placeholder>
  <span class="canon-text-input-suffix" aria-hidden="true">USD</span>
  <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-display="icon"
          commandfor="…" command="--canon-clear">…</button>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-text-input` | yes | The box. The frame, the focus ring and the states belong to it, not to the input. |
| `<input>` | yes | The main control: the box's direct child, no class. A text-like `type`. |
| `.canon-icon` | no | Leading and/or trailing, `aria-hidden="true"`. |
| `.canon-text-input-prefix` / `-suffix` | no | Text before / after the value ("https://", "kg"). `aria-hidden="true"`: the input's name carries the meaning ("Price in USD", not "Price" + "$"). Text only: a control goes in as a select box (next row). |
| `.canon-select` / `.canon-combobox` | no | A [Select](select.md) or one-value [Combobox](combobox.md) box as the **first or last child**: a country code before a phone number, a currency after an amount. One frame, with a line between them. The select needs its own name. |
| `.canon-button` | no | Trailing actions, last: clear, copy (below). |

- Order is icon, prefix, input, suffix, icon, buttons. Themes may reorder (Canon shows the prefix first and the suffix last, at the box's ends, the icons and buttons inside them; both are hidden from assistive technology, so nothing that is read moves).
- **Clicking anywhere in the box** (padding, icons, affix text) focuses the input; only buttons and a select box keep their own clicks.
- Affixes truncate before the input gets less than 4rem; they keep their own direction in right-to-left text.
- **A select box in the text input:**

```html
<div class="canon-text-input">
  <div class="canon-select">
    <select name="country-code" aria-label="Country code" autocomplete="tel-country-code">
      <button><selectedcontent></selectedcontent></button>
      <option value="+44"><span class="canon-option-label">+44</span> <span class="canon-option-description">United Kingdom</span></option>
      <option value="+90"><span class="canon-option-label">+90</span> <span class="canon-option-description">Türkiye</span></option>
    </select>
  </div>
  <input type="tel" aria-label="Phone number" placeholder autocomplete="tel-national">
</div>
```

  The select keeps its own list and keyboard; the text input draws the frame and shows focus for both. With `selectedcontent`, the box shows the code and the list also names the country. A [Combobox](combobox.md) with `data-search="list"` lets people search a long list. The select box is as wide as its widest option (canon.js measures it), so the value doesn't move when the choice changes.
- `type="search"` has no native clear button (it can't be themed): add the clear action. Escape still clears natively.
- **Expected length:** native `size` or `maxlength`; themes may size the box from them.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-size` | box or a container | `xs` · `sm` · `md` · `lg` · `xl` · `2xl` (three-size themes: xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes |
| `data-intent` | box | `warning` · `success` | none | no |

- **`data-intent`**: the value is accepted but questionable (warning), or checked and fine (success). ARIA has neither, so the meaning must also be in words (in a Field, the message). **Error is not an intent:** it is `aria-invalid="true"` on the input, which assistive tech reads.

Everything else is native on the input: `placeholder`, `required`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `aria-invalid`, `autocomplete`, `inputmode`.

## States

| State | Hook | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Hover | `:hover` on the box | |
| Focus | the input's `:focus` | Shown on the box. A focused trailing button shows its own ring instead. |
| Disabled | `disabled` | Wins over every other state. |
| Read-only | `readonly` | The value can be selected and copied. |
| Error | `aria-invalid="true"`, or `:user-invalid` | The browser's check only counts once the user has been there. In a field, a danger message says what is wrong. |
| Warning, success | `data-intent` on the box, or a field's message intent | In a field, the message sets it; no need to repeat it on the box. |
| Disabled with a status | `disabled` + any of the above | The status still shows, softened. |
| Empty | `:placeholder-shown` | Needs a `placeholder` attribute (bare is enough). Required inside a field. |
| Autofilled | `:autofill` | Themes override the browser's colors. |

## Box actions (T2, canon.js)

Trailing `canon-button`s with invoker commands, pointing at the input (`commandfor` + its `id`). Hidden without scripting.

| `command` | Does | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--canon-clear` | Empties the input, fires `input` and `change`, focuses it | Hidden while there is nothing to clear (`:placeholder-shown`) |
| `--canon-copy` | Copies the value, announces "Copied" | `data-state="copied"` for 2 seconds |

Details (polyfill, the translated "Copied" string): [field.md](field.md#box-actions-t2-canonjs).

## Accessibility

- The name: a `<label for>` (in a Field) or `aria-label`. Placeholders are not names.
- Affix text and icons are hidden; the name says what they would.
- Description and message (in a Field) are wired with `aria-describedby`.

## Theme obligations

- Show focus on the box, error, disabled and read-only distinctly, and not by color alone where the system allows (Canon: read-only is dashed).
- Keep the input owning the whole box (core does it: the input reaches past the box's edges and the box clips it).
- Style `:autofill`.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Label, description, messages | [Field](field.md) |
| Number steppers | Number (its own component) |
| Multi-line | [Textarea](textarea.md) |
| A status icon | The Field's message carries it (field.md), not the box |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** 32 / 40 / 48px tall (the button's); padding 8 / 10 / 12, text a further 4 / 6 / 8 in; prefix, value and suffix 2 / 4 / 6 apart; icons 16 / 20 / 24, 2 / 2 / 0 from the text; text 12 / 14 / 16; radius 4 / 8 / 12. md by default.

White box, zinc-200 border, a faint lift under it (0 1px 2px, black at 5%; dark 30%), gone while pressed and when disabled (the focus halo takes its place), zinc-900 text, zinc-400 placeholder, affixes and icons (dark: zinc-900, zinc-700, white, zinc-500). Hover zinc-400 (dark zinc-500). Focus blue-600 with a 3px blue-100 halo (dark blue-400, blue-900). Error red-400, red-600 on hover and focus with a red-100 halo (dark red-500, red-400, red-900). Disabled zinc-50 with zinc-400 text, zinc-300 affixes (dark zinc-800, zinc-500, zinc-600). Also: warning (amber) and success (green) on the error recipe; disabled with a status: its border softened (300s, dark 800s); read-only dashed; box buttons 24 / 28 / 32px, the icon's color, a zinc tint on hover. Prefix and suffix are segments at the box's ends (the prefix first and the suffix last, whatever the markup's order): its full height, reaching its edge, zinc-50 (dark zinc-800) behind zinc-500 text (dark zinc-400), a 1px line in the frame's resting color (zinc-200, dark zinc-700) on the inner side, their text the box's inset from each side and what follows the line as far from it as from the box's edge; disabled, zinc-100 with zinc-400 text (dark zinc-700, zinc-500). A select box in it: no frame of its own, a 1px line in the frame's resting color (zinc-200, dark zinc-700) between it and the value, its text and the value's each the box's inset from the frame or the line.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/textarea.md

# Textarea

Tier: **T0**

Text over several lines: a native `<textarea>` in a box that looks like a [Text Input](text-input.md). It can stay at a fixed height, grow as people type, and let them resize it. On its own it is named with `aria-label`; with a [Label](label.md) it is a [Field](field.md).

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-textarea">
  <textarea id="note" name="note" rows="2" data-max-lines="5" data-resize="vertical" placeholder></textarea>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-textarea` | yes | The box: Text Input's frame, sizes and states. The frame, the focus ring and the states belong to it, not to the textarea. |
| `<textarea>` | yes | The only child, no class. |

No icons, affixes or buttons: they belong to a one-line box.

**Rich text:** `data-rich` on the box makes it an editor for formatted text (a toolbar, HTML as the value). See [Rich Text](rich-text.md).

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rows` (native) | textarea | a number | 2 | — |
| `data-max-lines` | textarea | a number, or `none` | absent: fixed at `rows` | no |
| `data-resize` | textarea | `vertical` · `none` | theme decides | no |
| `data-size` | box or a container | `xs` · `sm` · `md` · `lg` · `xl` · `2xl` (three-size themes: xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes |
| `data-intent` | box | `warning` · `success` | none | no |

| Need | Contract |
|---|---|
| Starting / minimum height | native `rows` |
| Grow up to N lines, then scroll | `data-max-lines="N"`; `"none"` grows without limit. Absent: fixed at `rows`, scrolls (native) |
| Manual resize | `data-resize="vertical"` or `"none"`. Absent: theme decides. Horizontal resizing is not offered |

- Growth uses native `field-sizing: content`; heights are `rows × 1lh` and `data-max-lines × 1lh`, read with typed `attr()`. Browsers without typed `attr()` get the common values (rows 1–6; max lines 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12); browsers without `field-sizing` keep the height of `rows` and scroll.
- If someone drags the resize handle, their height wins and growing stops for that textarea (native behavior).

Native attributes to use instead of new ones:

| Need | Native |
|---|---|
| Character limit | `maxlength` (in a Field, add a counter, which also makes the limit soft: [field.md](field.md#counter-t2-canonjs)) |
| No line wrapping | `wrap="off"` |
| No spellcheck | `spellcheck="false"` |
| Enter key label on mobile | `enterkeyhint` |
| Auto-capitalization | `autocapitalize` |

Everything else is native too: `placeholder`, `required`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `aria-invalid`, `autocomplete`.

## States

Text Input's: hover, focus (on the box), disabled, read-only, error (`aria-invalid="true"` or `:user-invalid`), warning and success (`data-intent` on the box, or a field's message), disabled with a status, empty (`:placeholder-shown`, needs a `placeholder` attribute; required inside a field).

## Core

- The textarea owns the box: it reaches 20rem past the start (the box clips it) and takes over the box's padding exactly on the other three sides, so its scrollbar and resize handle sit at the box's inner edge. Themes set `--canon-textarea-inset-block` and `--canon-textarea-inset-end` to their padding.
- The textarea measures its content box, so `rows × 1lh` is exact.
- No resize handle unless `data-resize="vertical"`; never horizontal.
- Never less than one line tall (`min-block-size: 1lh`), so the handle can't drag the text out of sight; `rows` with `data-max-lines` raises that minimum.

## Accessibility

- The name: a `<label for>` (in a Field) or `aria-label`. Placeholders are not names.
- Description and message (in a Field) are wired with `aria-describedby`.
- A limit set with `maxlength` stops typing silently: say it in the description ("Up to 280 characters").

## Theme obligations

- Look like the theme's Text Input, with the same states.
- Show where the text is when it scrolls (the native scrollbar is enough).

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Animated growth | A canon.js enhancer (CSS can't animate a size the content decides) |
| Code input (monospace, tabs) | `data-content="code"` |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Text Input's: text 12 / 14 / 16 on 16 / 20 / 24px lines, radius 4 / 8 / 12, text 12 / 16 / 20px from the sides. The first line sits where a text input's does (8 / 10 / 12px from the top), so one row is 32 / 40 / 48px tall, a text input's height. md by default. No resize handle unless asked.

Text Input's colors and states.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/time.md

# Time

Tier: **T2** (without canon.js it is the browser's time field)

A time of day: when a meeting starts, a shift ends, a report runs. A native `<input type="time">` in a `.canon-time` box, a component of its own. canon.js draws the field itself: each part (hours, minutes, and AM/PM where the reader's language uses it) is a cell of its own, typed into, stepped with the arrow keys, or nudged with the up and down arrows the focused cell shows. The input stays underneath, hidden: the value (`14:30`), `min`, `max`, `step`, `required` and the form value are still the browser's.

A **range** is two time inputs in one box: a start and an end.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-field">
  <div class="canon-label"><label class="canon-label-text" for="starts">Starts at</label></div>
  <div class="canon-time">
    <input type="time" id="starts" name="starts" value="08:00" step="900">
  </div>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-time` | yes | The box. No frame of its own: each cell is framed. |
| `<input type="time">` | yes | The value (what the form submits, always 24-hour `HH:MM` or `HH:MM:SS`). Named by a `<label for>` (in a Field) or `aria-label`. |

### A range

```html
<div class="canon-field" role="group" aria-labelledby="shift-label">
  <div class="canon-label"><span class="canon-label-text" id="shift-label">Shift</span></div>
  <div class="canon-time">
    <input type="time" id="shift-from" name="from" aria-label="Start" value="08:00">
    <input type="time" id="shift-to" name="to" aria-label="End" value="16:30">
  </div>
</div>
```

- **Two native time inputs**, each with its own `name` and `aria-label`; the field's label is a `<span id>` naming the pair, with `role="group"` and `aria-labelledby` on the field, as for a [Date](date.md) range.
- **An end before the start** is invalid ("The end time is before the start time."), unless the range may run past midnight: `data-overnight` on the box (a night shift, 22:00 → 06:00).

### What canon.js adds

Themes style these; authors don't write them.

```html
<div class="canon-time">
  <input type="time" … tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true">              <!-- underneath, invisible -->
  <div class="canon-time-segments" role="group" aria-labelledby="…">   <!-- data-empty: no value; a range's: data-part="start" / "end" -->
    <span class="canon-time-cell" data-type="hour">                      <!-- the frame; data-active, data-empty -->
      <span class="canon-time-value" role="spinbutton" contenteditable aria-label="Hours"
            aria-valuemin="0" aria-valuemax="23" aria-valuenow="8" aria-valuetext="8">08</span>
      <button type="button" class="canon-time-step" data-direction="up" tabindex="-1" aria-label="Later hour"></button>
      <button type="button" class="canon-time-step" data-direction="down" tabindex="-1" aria-label="Earlier hour"></button>
    </span>
    <span class="canon-time-literal" aria-hidden="true">:</span>
    <span class="canon-time-cell" data-type="minute">…</span>
    <!-- with seconds (step under 60): a second cell; in 12-hour languages: a day-period cell (AM / PM) -->
  </div>
  <!-- a range: <span class="canon-icon canon-time-arrow" data-icon="arrow-forward" aria-hidden="true">, then the second input and its cells -->
</div>
```

- Each cell is a frame holding its spinbutton (the same as Date's parts) and two step buttons beside it, for the pointer (`tabindex="-1"`, named for switch and voice users).
- A cell is `[data-empty]` while it has no value, `[data-active]` while its spinbutton has focus (the theme grows it). A press anywhere in a cell focuses it; its buttons step only once it is active.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `value`, `min`, `max` (native) | input | `HH:MM` or `HH:MM:SS` | — | — |
| `step` (native) | input | seconds: `900` steps minutes by 15, `1` adds seconds | `60` (minutes by 1) | — |
| `aria-label` | each input of a range | its name ("Start", "End") | — (required) | — |
| `data-overnight` | `.canon-time` (a range) | (present) the end may be earlier: the next day | an end before the start is invalid | no |
| `data-size` | the field, the box or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` (xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes |

Everything else is native: `required`, `disabled`, `readonly`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, `name`, `form`.

- **12 or 24 hours** follows the reader's language (the nearest `lang`), as Date's order does: 12-hour languages get an AM/PM cell and hours 1–12. The value is always 24-hour.
- **`step` drives the arrows and the keys.** With `step="900"`, Up from 08:00 goes to 08:15, not 08:01; a typed 08:07 is invalid ("Enter a time in steps of 15 minutes.", the browser's own check).

## Behavior (canon.js)

- **Typing:** a cell takes digits and moves on when it can't take more (two digits; a first hour digit of 3–9 in 24-hour, 2–9 in 12-hour, is the whole hour: 3 → 03); `:` or a space moves on too; in the AM/PM cell, A or P chooses. Backspace clears the cell, then goes back. A pasted time (`14:30`, `2:30 pm`) fills every cell. Cells are editable (`contenteditable`), so phones show a number keyboard.
- **Keys:** Up and Down step the cell (from now when empty), wrapping (59 → 00, 23 → 00, PM ↔ AM); minutes and seconds step by `step` and carry nothing into the hour. Left and Right move between cells (reversed right-to-left); Tab goes through them like a native field's.
- **The arrows:** the up and down arrows of the focused cell step it as Up and Down do. Holding one repeats the step (after 0.4s, every 60ms), as Number Input's buttons do. A press doesn't take focus from the cell.
- **The value:** a complete time sets the input and fires `input` and `change`; clearing a cell empties it. Leaving an incomplete time fires `change`, and the input is invalid ("Enter a complete time."). A time outside `min`–`max` is invalid with the browser's own message; a range's end before its start, unless `data-overnight`.
- **A press on the box, or on the label,** goes to the first empty cell, else the hour.
- **Disabled and read-only:** disabled cells leave the tab order; read-only cells can be focused and read but not changed, and show no arrows.
- **The language** (the nearest `lang`) gives the cycle (12 or 24 hours), the day-period names (AM / PM, or the language's) and the digits.
- **Apps** that set the value in code fire `input` or `change` on the input; canon.js follows. Form resets are followed.

Without canon.js: the browser's own time field.

## States

| State | Hook | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Hover | a cell's `:hover` | That cell's frame darkens. |
| Active | `[data-active]` on the focused cell | It grows, showing its arrows. |
| Empty | `[data-empty]` on a cell | Its placeholder ("--"). |
| Error | `aria-invalid="true"` on the input, or `:user-invalid` | Every cell takes the error line; one message, in a Field. |
| Disabled, read-only | `disabled`, `readonly` | No arrows; read-only cells dashed. |

## Core

- Without canon.js the input is a Text Input-sized field. With it, the input covers the box, invisible and out of reach (`opacity: 0`, `pointer-events: none`), under `.canon-time-segments`: an inline row of cells, literals and (a range) the arrow, tabular figures, centered on each other.
- **The active cell grows over what's around it, never moving it:** its size in the row stays the cell's, and the growth is drawn outside that box, from the middle, equally up and down. It is raised above its neighbours (and the field's label and message) while it is active.
- The step buttons are inside the cell, at its top and bottom; they take no room while the cell is at rest.

## Accessibility

- The field is a group named like the input (its label, description, `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` copied) of spinbuttons named "Hours", "Minutes", "Seconds" and "AM/PM", each with its value or "Empty". The hidden input is out of the tab order; its label still works, and so does its validation.
- One Tab stop per cell, as a native time field. The arrows are not Tab stops: the keys do what they do.
- A range's fields are each named by their input ("Start"), inside the field's group ("Shift").
- Strings (`time-hour`, `time-minute`, `time-second`, `time-period`, `time-hour-placeholder`, `time-minute-placeholder`, `time-second-placeholder`, `time-period-placeholder`, `time-step-up-*`, `time-step-down-*`, `time-incomplete`, `time-range-order`) are translated in `i18n/` and follow `lang`.

## Theme obligations

- Each cell reads as part of one control: the same frame, the separators quiet, the error on every cell at once.
- The active cell unmistakable (its growth and the focus ring), its arrows clearly for that cell only.
- The arrows' targets bigger than the arrows (see Look).
- Growing calm, and none with reduced motion.
- Use logical properties: right to left, the cells and a range's arrow follow the direction; a time's own digits stay in their order.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A list of suggested times | If it comes up (a `<datalist>`, as Date's presets) |
| Date and time in one field | Not a field of its own: a [Date](date.md) and a Time side by side, two components with their own looks (a framed box, a row of framed cells) |
| Durations ("1 h 30 min") | Not a time of day: a Number Input or Text Input with a suffix |
| Time zones | The app (a Select beside the field) |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** A cell is a control's height square (32 / 40 / 48), Text Input's corners (4 / 8 / 12) and type; cells 4 / 4 / 6 apart, the `:` in between; a range's arrow (Lucide arrow-right) the icon size, 8 / 8 / 12 from the cells. Active, a cell is the icon size taller on each side, up and down (52 / 64 / 76 tall), the growth drawn over its neighbours; its arrows fill its top and bottom, the icon size tall (each about 24 × 12 at md), 4px in from the frame.

At rest a cell is Text Input's frame (white, a zinc-200 line; dark zinc-900, zinc-700) with its arrows' tabs peeking: a 4px zinc-100 bar (dark zinc-800) inside its top and bottom edges, the frame's inner corners. Hover: that cell's line zinc-400 (dark zinc-500), the tabs zinc-200 (dark zinc-700). Active: Text Input's focus (blue-600 line, its 3px blue-100 halo; dark blue-400, blue-900), the tabs open into the arrows: zinc-100 buttons (dark zinc-800) with Lucide chevron-up and chevron-down in zinc-500 (dark zinc-400), hover zinc-200 (dark zinc-700), pressed zinc-300 (dark zinc-600). Cells wrap (59 → 00), so no arrow is ever unavailable. The `:` and the arrow zinc-400 (dark zinc-500). Empty cells show "--" in the placeholder color. Error: every cell's line red-400 (dark red-500). Disabled: zinc-50 cells (dark zinc-800), zinc-400 text, no tabs; read-only: dashed lines, no tabs.

**Targets:** for every pointer, each arrow's target reaches 12px further out than the button it draws, past the cell's edge, invisible; the active cell is above everything around it, so the larger target takes nothing from its neighbours.

**Motion:** becoming active, the cell grows from its middle to its full height and the tabs open into the arrows (0.15s, fast then settling); leaving, it shrinks back (0.1s). With reduced motion it changes at once.

## Open questions

- **The resting tabs:** shown at rest for now (as designed); whether they show only while a cell is hovered is still to be decided.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/accordion.md

# Accordion

Tier: **T0** (the browser's `<details>`: no JavaScript)

Parts of a page that open one by one, under rows that name them: a settings page's advanced options, a record's less-used details, a help page's questions. Each item opens and closes by itself, or, with one `name`, one at a time.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-accordion">
  <details class="canon-accordion-item" open>
    <summary class="canon-accordion-summary">
      <span class="canon-accordion-title">Billing details</span>
      <span class="canon-accordion-description">Where invoices go, and when they're due</span>
    </summary>
    <div class="canon-accordion-content">…</div>
  </details>
  <details class="canon-accordion-item">
    <summary class="canon-accordion-summary">
      <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="mail" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="canon-accordion-title">Reminders</span>
      <span class="canon-count">3</span>
    </summary>
    <div class="canon-accordion-content">…</div>
  </details>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-accordion` | yes | A `<div>` around the items, even for one (an "Advanced options" disclosure). |
| `details.canon-accordion-item` | yes | One per part. `open` for one that starts open. |
| `summary.canon-accordion-summary` | yes | First in its item: the row people click. It is the button; the theme draws the chevron. |
| `.canon-accordion-title` | yes | A `<span>`: what the part is, a few words. |
| `.canon-accordion-description` | no | A `<span>` under the title: what's in it, or its state ("2 of 5 set"). |
| `.canon-icon` | no | First in the summary, `aria-hidden="true"`. Use them on every item or none. |
| A [Tag](tag.md), [Count](count.md) or [Status Indicator](status.md) | no | Last in the summary: a fact about the part ("3", "Overdue"), read with the title. |
| `.canon-accordion-content` | yes | After the summary: anything (text, a [Description List](description-list.md), fields, a nested accordion). |

- **One at a time:** the same `name` on every item of an accordion; opening one closes the one that was open. Use it for parts people compare one after the other (questions); leave it out where several are open together (settings).
- **Not a heading:** a summary is a button, and inside it a heading loses its role in screen readers. When the parts belong in the page's outline (people jump between them), use [Sections](section.md) instead, or a heading before the accordion.
- **Nothing interactive in the summary:** no links or buttons in the row; actions go in the content.
- **Accordion, Tabs or Sections?** [Tabs](tabs.md) show one part in place of another, for parts of the same weight; Sections show everything; an Accordion shows the names and opens what's needed, for parts people mostly skip.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `open` | an item | present: open | closed | — |
| `name` | every item | a name shared by the accordion's items: one open at a time | none: each on its own | — |
| `data-size` | the accordion or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |

## Core

- The summary is a row: the icon, the title with the description under it, the Tag (Count, Status) at the end, the chevron last. Columns only for what's there. The browser's marker is hidden.

## Behavior (T0, the browser)

- **Opening and closing:** a click on the row, Enter or Space on it. The `toggle` event fires on the item.
- **Finding:** the browser's find in page, and links to something inside a closed item (`#id`), open it.
- **One at a time:** items sharing a `name` close each other.
- No canon.js.

## Accessibility

- Each summary is a button that says whether it's expanded ("Billing details, collapsed"); its whole text is its name, the description and the Tag included, so keep them short.
- The icon is decoration; the chevron is the theme's.
- Content in a closed item is out of the way: not read, not reached with Tab, but found by find in page.

## Theme obligations

- Rows told apart (a line, a gap), the open state shown by more than the content appearing (the chevron).
- The row's focus ring visible, around the whole row.
- Opening calm, and none with reduced motion.
- In forced colors, the chevron still shows.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the icon is on the right, the chevron on the left.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Expand all, collapse all | If it comes up: a canon.js command on the accordion |
| An action in the row (Edit, Delete) | The content; or a Section with header actions |
| Remembering what's open across visits | The app (`toggle`, then `open` in its markup) |
| A tree of nested items with keys | Tree View |

## Look

**Sizes:** rows 8 / 12 / 16px inside (sm / md / lg); titles 13 / 14 / 16px, descriptions 12 / 13 / 14px; icons 16 / 16 / 20px; the chevron 16px; 12px between the row's parts; the content 12 / 16 / 20px over the next line.
