Rows divided by hairline rules (black at 10%, dark white at 10%), a line above the first and under the last (not under the last when it ends a Card's body, where the Card's edge closes it; neither for one nested in another's content, framed by the outer rows), no box, so it sits the same on a page and in a [Card](card.md). The title medium in the text's color, its description under it in zinc-500 (dark zinc-400); the icon zinc-500; the chevron zinc-500 (dark zinc-400), the text's color on hover, turning over when open. The content in zinc-600 (dark zinc-300), lined up with the title. Opening and closing slide (0.2s, where the browser can animate to the content's height; none with reduced motion). Focus: a 2px ring in the focus color around the row, 2px out, 6px corners. Forced colors: the chevron in the text's color.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/avatar.md

# Avatar

Tier: **T0** (photo fallback and the spotlight's tooltip are T2: canon.js)

A person, team or bot, shown as a photo, initials or an icon, optionally with a status dot, a badge and a count.

## Elements

```html
<span class="canon-avatar" data-seed="4821">
  <img class="canon-avatar-image" src="ada.jpg" alt="">
  <span class="canon-avatar-fallback" role="img" aria-label="Ada Lovelace">AL</span>
  <span class="canon-avatar-status" data-status="online"><span class="canon-visually-hidden">Online</span></span>
  <span class="canon-count">3<span class="canon-visually-hidden"> unread</span></span>
</span>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-avatar` | yes | `<span>`, or `<a href>` / `<button type="button">` when it does something (profile link, account menu) |
| `img.canon-avatar-image` | no | The photo. Always `alt=""`: the fallback carries the name. Comes before the fallback. |
| `.canon-avatar-fallback` | yes | Initials, or **empty** (no whitespace) for the theme's icon. Carries the name with `role="img"` and `aria-label`; `aria-hidden="true"` instead when the name is written beside the avatar. |
| `.canon-avatar-status` | no | `data-status` + visually hidden text |
| `.canon-avatar-badge` | no | A `canon-icon` + visually hidden text (what it means: "Verified") |
| `.canon-count` | no | See [count.md](count.md) |

- **Type comes from the content.** Photo when there is an `<img>`, initials when the fallback has text, the icon when it is empty. Nothing to declare.
- The fallback always sits under the photo, so its name is read whatever the photo does. While a photo loads, the fallback shows.
- **Many photos:** `loading="lazy"` on the `<img>` (a long list or a table of people) waits to fetch each photo until it nears the window; the initials show until it comes.
- **Broken photos:** canon.js sets `data-state="error"` on the avatar when its photo fails (or has no `src`); the fallback shows instead of the browser's broken-image icon. It clears if a new `src` loads. A photo still loading when canon.js starts marks the avatar `data-state="loading"` until it comes.
- canon.js also sets, on the avatar, for themes to use (never written by authors):
  - `--canon-count-inline-size`: the count's width, so a cut-out can follow "12" or "99+".
  - `data-seed-slot`: the seed modulo the theme's `--canon-seed-colors`, for browsers that can't compute it in CSS (typed `attr()`, `if()`). Both paths give the same slot; a seed that isn't an integer gets none (neutral).
- Status and badge share the bottom-end corner: use one or the other. The count sits top-end. All three move to the other side in right-to-left text.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-seed` | avatar | an integer (a user id) | none: neutral | no |
| `data-kind` | avatar | `person` · `team` · `bot` | `person` | no |
| `data-spotlight` | avatar | (present) under the pointer or with focus it grows a little and shows its name (see [Avatar Group](avatar-group.md#spotlight-data-spotlight)) | — | no |
| `data-size` | avatar or a container | `xs` · `sm` · `md` · `lg` · `xl` · `2xl` | theme decides | yes |
| `data-status` | status | `online` · `away` · `busy` · `offline` | required | no |
| `data-intent` | badge | `info` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` | theme decides | no |

### `data-seed`: a color that stays the same

Avatar colors tell people apart; they don't mean anything. The app passes a stable number (a user id), and the theme picks one of its colors from it, the same one every time and on every page. Two themes may pick different colors for the same seed. Without a seed the avatar is neutral (also used for "+3" overflow avatars).

- Integers only (`data-seed="4821"`). Hash other ids (UUIDs, emails) to an integer in the app.
- Themes declare how many colors they have with `--canon-seed-colors` on `:root`.
- [Tags](tag.md) take the same seeds: a theme gives a seed the same hue on both, so a person's avatar and their tag match.

### `data-kind`

What the avatar stands for, not its shape. Themes typically draw people round and teams and bots as rounded squares (GitHub, Slack), and give an empty fallback a matching icon.

## States

| State | Hook | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Photo failed | `data-state="error"` | Set by canon.js |
| Photo loading | `data-state="loading"` | Set by canon.js |
| Focus (link, button; any avatar with `data-spotlight`) | `:focus-visible` | Same ring as buttons |
| Menu open | `aria-expanded` | On a `<button>` with `aria-haspopup` |

## Accessibility

- "AL" means nothing read aloud: the fallback's `aria-label` is the full name.
- The status and badge text is read after the name ("Ada Lovelace, Online, 3 unread").
- Decorative avatars (the name is printed right beside them): fallback `aria-hidden="true"`, no `role`, no `aria-label`.
- With `data-spotlight`, an avatar that isn't a link or button becomes a focusable image named by its person, its status, badge and count included ("Ada Lovelace, Online"); its tooltip shows the name, or the author's own Tooltip (`interestfor`), which also describes it.
- A clickable avatar's name is its content, so the link or button needs nothing more. Make the label say what it does when that differs ("Your account, Ada Lovelace").

## Theme obligations

- Keep status, badge and count readable on photos: Canon's own themes cut a gap around them into the avatar rather than drawing a ring in a background color, so it works on any surface.
- Draw the icon for an empty fallback, per `data-kind`.
- Map every seed to a color; with no seed, use a neutral one.

## Not in the contract

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A color chosen by the author | Not offered: use `data-seed` |
| Shape as an option | Theme, from `data-kind` |
| Stacks, "+3" | Avatar Group |
| Presence updates (live status) | App (change `data-status`) |

## Look

**Sizes:** 24 / 32 / 40 / 48 / 56 / 64; md by default. Initials 10 / 12 / 14 / 16 / 16 / 24px. Icon half the size (Lucide `user-round`, `users-round`, `bot`).

Seeds pick one of 17 hues (light: tone-400 at 15% with tone-700 text; dark: tone-500 at 20% with tone-300). No seed: zinc-100 / zinc-500 (dark zinc-700 / zinc-300). Status green / amber / red / hollow zinc; badge a green-tinted 16px circle; count rose-600. Each cut into the avatar with a 2px gap. Every face has a hairline inner rim (0.5px on sharp screens, else 1px), so a light face doesn't bleed into the page: on initials and icons their own color at 20% (a seeded avatar's rim in its hue), on a photo black at 15% (dark white at 15%); it follows the face's shape, and the holes cut it too. The pointer over an avatar that isn't a link or button is the arrow, not the text cursor. Teams and bots: radius 20% of the size.

**Motion:** a photo still loading waits unseen over the initials, then fades in (0.2s) when it comes; a fade, so also with reduced motion.

**Spotlight:** under the pointer or with focus it scales to 110% (0.15s; not with reduced motion) and shows its name in a [Tooltip](tooltip.md) above it; Button's focus ring.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/avatar-group.md

# Avatar Group

Tier: **T0** · the spotlight's tooltip and keyboard reach are **T2** (canon.js)

Several avatars in a row (members, reviewers, people online), usually ending with a count of the rest.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-avatar-group" role="group" aria-label="Project members" data-size="sm">
  <span class="canon-avatar" data-seed="1">
    <img class="canon-avatar-image" src="ada.jpg" alt="">
    <span class="canon-avatar-fallback" role="img" aria-label="Ada Lovelace">AL</span>
  </span>
  <span class="canon-avatar" data-seed="2">
    <span class="canon-avatar-fallback" role="img" aria-label="Grace Hopper">GH</span>
  </span>
  <span class="canon-avatar">
    <span class="canon-avatar-fallback" role="img" aria-label="5 more">5+</span>
  </span>
</div>
```

- `.canon-avatar-group` with `role="group"` and a label that says who they are.
- Direct children are [avatars](avatar.md), in order: the first is in front.
- **The rest:** a last avatar with no seed (neutral) whose fallback says how many ("5+") and whose label says it ("5 more"). It may be a `<button>` that opens the full list (`aria-haspopup="dialog"` or `"menu"`).
- How many to show before "the rest" is the app's call.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-size` | group or a container | `xs` · `sm` · `md` · `lg` · `xl` · `2xl` | theme decides | yes (reaches every avatar) |
| `data-density` | group or a container | `compact` · `comfortable` · `spacious` | theme decides | yes |
| `data-spotlight` | group | (present) the avatar under the pointer or with focus comes forward and shows its name | — | no |
| `interestfor` | an avatar in a spotlight group | the id of the author's own [Tooltip](tooltip.md) for it (more than the name) | a tooltip of its name | no |

### `data-density`: how tightly they sit

Independent of size: any size at any density. A hint, like `data-size`; the theme decides what each means for avatars and what to do without one.

| Value | Typically |
|---|---|
| `compact` | Overlapping |
| `comfortable` | Touching |
| `spacious` | Apart |

## Spotlight (`data-spotlight`)

For groups whose avatars people want to tell apart (who's on this project, who reviewed).

- **Coming forward** (the theme, CSS): the avatar under the pointer or with keyboard focus is drawn on top of the others, a little bigger, no longer cut by the one before it; the others step back.
- **Its name** (canon.js): a [Tooltip](tooltip.md) over it, after a short wait for the first, at once while moving along the group. The name comes from the avatar (its fallback's `aria-label`); `interestfor` on an avatar points at the author's own Tooltip instead (a role, a status, the names behind "5+").
- **Keyboards** (canon.js): avatars that aren't links or buttons become focusable images, named by their person (with their status, badge and count: "Ada Lovelace, Online"). The group is one Tab stop; the arrow keys, Home and End move between them. Links and buttons keep their own Tab stops. Escape hides the tooltip.
- **Touch:** no hover, so no tooltip; a tap on a link or button does what it does.

## Theme obligations

- Keep each avatar readable where they overlap. Canon cuts a gap into the avatar behind (and around the status, badge or count of the one in front) rather than drawing a ring in a background color, so groups work on any surface.
- The first avatar reads as in front, in both directions.
- Clickable avatars need room for their focus ring; without `data-density`, themes may spread them out.
- With `data-spotlight`, the avatar in front reads as in front wherever it sits (no cut of its own, its neighbours cut around it), and the others are still recognizable.

## Not in the contract

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Overlap amounts per density | Theme |
| Counting the rest, truncation | App |
| Spreading the avatars apart on hover | Out of scope (`data-spotlight` brings one forward) |

## Look

compact: overlapping by 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 / 12px (xs → 2xl); comfortable: touching; spacious: two rings apart. Each avatar is cut by the one before it plus a ring of 2 / 3 / 4 / 4 / 5 / 6px. Default compact; groups of links or buttons default to spacious. The rest: zinc.

**Spotlight:** the avatar under the pointer or with focus scales to 110% on top of the others, its own cut gone and the one before it cut around it by the same ring (the one after it, its cut grown to match); the others fade to 40%. 0.15s; with reduced motion only the fade. Avatars that aren't links or buttons get Button's focus ring. The name in a [Tooltip](tooltip.md) above it.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/card.md

# Card

Tier: **T0**

A framed box: one thing (a customer, a project) or one part of a page (billing details, a settings group), set apart. A [Section](section.md) is the same anatomy without the frame.

## Elements

```html
<section class="canon-card">
  <header class="canon-card-header">
    <h3 class="canon-card-title">Billing details</h3>
    <p class="canon-card-description">Where invoices go, and when they're due</p>
    <div class="canon-card-actions">
      <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-intent="neutral">…Edit…</button>
    </div>
  </header>
  <div class="canon-card-body">
    <dl class="canon-description-list">…</dl>
  </div>
  <footer class="canon-card-footer">
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-intent="neutral">…Cancel…</button>
    <button type="submit" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="high" data-align="end">…Save…</button>
  </footer>
</section>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-card` | yes | A `<section>` when it is a part of the page; an `<article>` when it stands on its own (one of many, in a list or a grid); a `<form>` when it is one; a `<div>` otherwise. |
| `.canon-card-header` | no | First. The title, then an optional description and actions. |
| `.canon-card-title` | with a header | A heading (`<h2>`–`<h6>`), at the level the page's outline needs. |
| `.canon-card-description` | no | A `<p>`: one line about the card. |
| `.canon-card-actions` | no | [Buttons](button.md) about the card (Edit, View all, a "…" menu). |
| `.canon-card-body` | no | The padded content, its things one under another. At most one. |
| `.canon-card-footer` | no | Last, under a line: actions about the whole card. `data-align="end"` on an item sends it and what follows to the far end. |
| Anything else directly in the card | — | Runs edge to edge: a [Table](table.md) (dropping its own frame for the card's), an image. |
| [Section](section.md)s directly in the card | — | Its parts: padded like a body, a line between them (a settings card's groups). |
| `.canon-card-link` | no | An `<a href>` in the title: the whole card becomes its link. One per card. |

- **A link card:** a click anywhere on the card opens the title's link, and its other buttons and links stay themselves, above it. Screen readers hear one link, named by the title, not the whole card's text. Use it for cards that each open a record.
- **Landmarks:** a `<section>` card is not a landmark unless named (`aria-labelledby` its title). Name only the few that should be, or every card becomes one.
- **Not a Dialog or a Popover:** a card is part of the page, never on top of it.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-size` | the card or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |
| `data-align` | an item in the footer | `end` | — | — |

## Core

- A column: the header, the body, the footer at the bottom. What runs edge to edge is clipped to the card's corners.
- The header: the title and the actions in a row, the description under both; when the card is narrow (under 20rem, a container query), the actions go under it all.
- A link card: the link's `::after` covers the card; other controls in it are raised above it.

## Accessibility

- The title is a real heading, so the card shows up in the page's outline.
- A link card is one link named by its title; its other controls are separate tab stops.
- The footer's actions read after the content they act on.

## Theme obligations

- The card set apart from the page (a line, a fill).
- A link card shows hover and focus on the whole card.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the actions sit on the left.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A card you select (a checkbox, a radio) | If it comes up: a [Checkbox](checkbox.md) or [Radio](radio.md) card |
| A collapsible card | Accordion |
| A danger card ("Delete workspace") | If it comes up: `data-intent` |
| Dashboard numbers | [Stat](stat.md), in the card |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Padding 16 / 20 / 24 (the shell's inset and 8px); the header 12 / 16 / 20 above the body; titles 14 / 16 / 18px on 20 / 24 / 28px lines; text in the control's type (12 / 14 / 16px); Table's corners (8 / 12 / 16).

The shell's measures and Table's frame. White (dark zinc-900) with a hairline edge (black at 12%, dark white at 12%) and the raised shadow (0 1px 2px at 6%, 0 1px 3px at 4%); a link card's edge darkens to 22% under the pointer; titles semibold; descriptions zinc-500 (dark zinc-400). Hairline rules (black at 10%, dark white at 10%) between Sections and above the footer. A Table edge to edge, its edge cells lined up with the card's padding. A link card takes the focus ring when its link has focus.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/code-block.md

# Code Block

Tier: **T0** · copying, wrapping and the scrolling region are **T2** (canon.js)

Code people read or copy: an API request, a webhook's payload, a config file, a log excerpt, an embed snippet. A `<pre><code>` in a frame, with an optional title and a copy button. Not an editor: code people change is a [Textarea](textarea.md).

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-code-block">
  <div class="canon-code-block-header">
    <span class="canon-code-block-title">invoice.paid.json</span>
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-intent="neutral" data-display="icon" data-size="sm"
            commandfor="payload" command="--canon-copy">
      <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="copy" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="canon-button-label">Copy invoice.paid.json</span>
    </button>
  </div>
  <pre><code id="payload"><span class="tok punctuation">{</span>
  <span class="tok string">"id"</span><span class="tok punctuation">:</span> …</code></pre>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-code-block` | yes | The frame. Its children: an optional header, the `<pre>`, or a corner button. |
| `.canon-code-block-header` | no | First. A `.canon-code-block-title`, then [Buttons](button.md): the wrap toggle, then copy (others, such as download, between them). |
| `.canon-code-block-title` | with a header | What the code is: a file name ("deploy.yaml") or a description ("Request"). Names the code's scrolling region. |
| `<pre><code>` | yes | The code, as text or highlighted tokens (see Highlighting). The `<code>` gets an `id` for the copy button. |
| Corner button | no | Without a header: one copy button after the `<pre>`, icon only. |

- **Wrapping** is a Button with `command="--canon-wrap"` and `commandfor` naming the `<code>`, before the copy button, icon only and named "Wrap lines": a toggle whose `aria-pressed` is the state. Lines scroll while it's `false` and wrap while it's `true`; start it `true` where wrapped reads better (logs on a narrow screen). Only in a header: a short snippet without one doesn't need it.
- **Copying** is a Button with `command="--canon-copy"` and `commandfor` naming the `<code>`. It copies the code's text, without the highlighting. Name it for what it copies where a page has several ("Copy deploy.yaml", "Copy command").
- **Inline code** in a sentence is a plain `<code>`, not a Code Block.

## Highlighting

Canon doesn't highlight code. Do it before the page is sent (on the server, or at build time) and put the result in the `<code>`: token spans named as [twinkleplop](https://twinkleplop.pngwn.at/docs/themes-ref) names them, `<span class="tok keyword">`, `tok string`, `tok tag_name`, `tok attr_name` and so on. Themes color those names. Code without spans is plain text (logs, keys, output).

- Other highlighters' markup works too, but brings its own colors.
- Highlighting is never the only way something is told apart: it's a reading aid, and screen readers read the text.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-size` | the block or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg`: the code's type and spacing | theme decides | yes |
| `--canon-code-block-max-height` | the block (a style) | a length | none | yes (CSS) |

## Core

- The code is always left to right, in a left-to-right box (`direction: ltr`, isolated), also on right-to-left pages; the header follows the page.
- Lines keep their breaks and indentation, and scroll sideways in their own box; while the header's wrap toggle is pressed (`aria-pressed="true"`) they wrap instead. With `--canon-code-block-max-height`, it scrolls down too.
- A long title is cut (…).
- The corner button sits in the top right corner (physical right, where code lines end), over the code.

## Behavior (T2, canon.js)

- **Scrolling:** when the code doesn't fit its box, the `<pre>` gets `data-scrolls` and becomes a region (`role="region"`, `tabindex="0"`) named by the title, else "Code" (the `--canon-text-code` string), so keyboards can reach and scroll it. It stops being one when the code fits. Attributes the author wrote are left alone.
- **Wrapping:** `--canon-wrap` flips the toggle's `aria-pressed`; the block's CSS follows it. The scrolling region comes and goes with it.
- **Copying:** the button gets `data-state="copied"` for 2 seconds and screen readers hear "Copied" (see [Button](button.md#copy-t2-canonjs)).

## Accessibility

- Screen readers read the code as text; token spans are not announced.
- A scrolling block is a named region and a Tab stop; arrow keys scroll it.
- The copy button is named for what it copies.

## Theme obligations

- Code set apart from the page (a fill or a frame), in a monospace face, readable token colors on that fill in both schemes (4.5:1 for text).
- A scrolling block's focus is visible.
- The corner button never lets code show through it.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Line numbers, highlighted lines, diffs | A later version (they need the lines marked) |
| Tabs between languages or files | Tabs around several blocks |
| Highlighting in the browser | The app (Canon stays dependency-free) |
| Editing code | Textarea, or an editor |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Code 12 / 13 / 14px at 1.6 line height, 12 / 16 / 20px inside; the header 40 / 40 / 48px.

Table's frame (its hairline edge and corners), a hairline rule under the header; the header white (dark zinc-900) with the title in Table's header type (zinc-500 medium, dark zinc-400); the code on zinc-50 (dark halfway from zinc-900 to zinc-800, Table's stripe), zinc-800 (dark zinc-200), in JetBrains Mono (no ligatures). Tokens in palette colors, 700 on light and 400 (sky 300) on dark: tags, selectors and functions blue; attributes and variables violet; strings emerald; numbers amber; properties and keys sky; keywords rose; punctuation and comments zinc-500 (comments italic). The wrap and copy buttons minimal and neutral (wrap pressed: Button's filled pressed look; its icon a wrapping line); the corner one on the code's fill. Focus: Button's ring around the block.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/data-table.md

# Data Table

Tier: **T2**, narrowly: without canon.js it is a plain [Table](table.md), whose rows, row checkboxes and row actions work. Everything that makes it a data table needs canon.js: sorting, search, filters, paging, select-all, the columns panel, pinning, the bulk bar and export.

A Table people work with: search and filter it, sort it, select rows, act on a row, edit a value in its cell, choose and pin its columns, page through it, export it, and see where it stands while it loads or when there's nothing to show. Editing cells has its own page: [Data Table: editing cells](data-table-editing.md).

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-data-table" data-local>
  <div class="canon-data-table-toolbar">
    <div class="canon-text-input">
      <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="search" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <input type="search" aria-label="Search users" placeholder="Search">
    </div>
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral" data-panel="filters">…Filter…</button>
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral" data-panel="columns" data-align="end" aria-haspopup="dialog">…Columns…</button>
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral" popovertarget="users-export" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">…Export…</button>
    <div class="canon-menu" id="users-export" popover role="menu" aria-label="Export">
      <button type="button" class="canon-menu-item" role="menuitem" data-export="csv">…CSV…</button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-table">
    <table>
      <caption class="canon-visually-hidden">Users</caption>
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th scope="col" data-column="select">
            <div class="canon-choice">
              <input type="checkbox" id="users-all">
              <label class="canon-choice-label canon-visually-hidden" for="users-all">Select all rows</label>
            </div>
          </th>
          <th scope="col" aria-sort="none" data-type="text" data-pin>User</th>
          <th scope="col" aria-sort="none" data-type="date">Date</th>
          <th scope="col" aria-sort="none" data-type="number" data-align="end">Amount</th>
          <th scope="col" data-type="choice">Status</th>
          <td data-column="actions"></td>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <td>
            <div class="canon-choice">
              <input type="checkbox" id="users-1" name="users" value="1">
              <label class="canon-choice-label canon-visually-hidden" for="users-1">Select Edwin Mueller</label>
            </div>
          </td>
          <th scope="row">Edwin Mueller</th>
          <td><time datetime="2024-08-16">16.08.2024</time></td>
          <td data-value="495.90">$495.90</td>
          <td data-value="Waiting"><span class="canon-tag" data-intent="warning">…Waiting…</span></td>
          <td>…the row's actions…</td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
  <nav class="canon-pagination" aria-label="Pagination" data-per-page="10">
    <p class="canon-pagination-summary"></p>
  </nav>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-data-table` | yes | Around the toolbar, the Table and its [Pagination](pagination.md) (the toolbar and Pagination optional). As wide as its container: a wider table scrolls in its frame. |
| `.canon-data-table-toolbar` | no | Before the table: a search field (a [Text Input](text-input.md) with `type="search"`, named), a `data-panel="filters"` [Button](button.md), a `data-panel="columns"` Button, an Export menu button (low and neutral: `data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral"`), and anything else the app needs. `data-align="end"` on an item sends it and what follows to the far end. canon.js draws the panels these buttons open, and the filter chips under the toolbar. |
| `.canon-table` | yes | A [Table](table.md), named, with a header row (`<thead>`) whose cells line up one-to-one with the body's (no `colspan` in the header). |
| A sortable header | no | `<th aria-sort="none">` (or `ascending` / `descending` when the rows already come sorted). canon.js puts its content in a sort button. |
| A filterable header | no | `data-type` says what the column holds: `text`, `number`, `date` (cells with `<time datetime>` or an ISO `data-value`) or `choice` (a few values; `data-options="Ready, Waiting"` lists them, else canon.js collects them from the rows). |
| An Export item | no | A [Menu](menu.md) item with `data-export="csv"` (or another format the app handles). |
| `template.canon-data-table-no-results` | no | In the data table: the [Empty State](empty-state.md) shown when the search and filters leave no local rows (canon.js has a default). |
| The select column | no | Its header `data-column="select"` holds a select-all [Checkbox](checkbox.md); each row's cell in that column holds a row checkbox (`name` / `value` for a form), each with a visually hidden label ("Select Edwin Mueller"). |
| `.canon-data-table-bulk` | no | The actions for the selected rows: `role="region"`, named ("Selected users"), holding [Buttons](button.md) by meaning (the main action; `data-intent="danger"` for a destructive one), menu buttons or a [Toolbar](toolbar.md). Needs the select column. canon.js adds Clear selection, the count and Select all before them; without canon.js it is a row under the table (a form round trip). |
| The actions column | no | Its header cell `data-column="actions"`: an empty `<td>`, or a `<th>` with a title. Each row's cell holds either a menu button (a minimal icon [Button](button.md), "Actions for Edwin Mueller", opening a [Menu](menu.md)) or a few buttons in a [Toolbar](toolbar.md) named for the row. |
| A message row | no | One row, one cell, holding an [Empty State](empty-state.md): nothing yet, no results, or an error. canon.js spans it across the columns. |

- **Statuses** are status [Tags](tag.md) (`data-intent`).
- **Cells stay on one line**, so rows keep one height; `data-wrap="normal"` on a cell lets it wrap, `data-wrap="truncate"` cuts it with "…" (at `--canon-truncate`, 16rem), and `data-wrap="middle"` cuts plain text in its middle, keeping its end (its last third: at least 8 characters, and a file name's extension with the 5 before it), for file names, paths and ids that differ at the end. Don't cut numbers, amounts or dates: people compare them. `data-align` and `data-wrap` on a header apply to its whole column.
- **One select column, one actions column**, at the start and the end of the row.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-local` | the data table | (present) all the rows are in the page: canon.js sorts them and shows them a page at a time | — (the app sorts and pages) | no |
| `aria-sort` | a header `th` | `none` · `ascending` · `descending` | not sortable | — |
| `data-column` | a header cell | `select` · `actions` | — | — |
| `data-pin` | a header `th` | (present) keep the column in view while the others scroll | — | — |
| `data-value` | a body cell | the value to sort and filter by | the `<time datetime>` inside, else the text | — |
| `data-type` | a header `th` | `text` · `number` · `date` · `choice` | not filterable | — |
| `data-options` | a `choice` header | the values, comma-separated | the values in the rows | — |
| `data-panel` | a toolbar button | `filters` · `columns` | — | — |
| `data-export` | a menu item | `csv`, or a format the app handles | — | — |
| `data-export-name` | the data table | the CSV's file name | the caption, else "table" | no |
| `data-wrap` | a cell or a header | `none` · `normal` · `truncate` · `middle` | one line | — |
| `aria-busy` | the data table | `true` while the rows load | — | — |
| `data-loading-rows` | the data table | how many skeleton rows | a page (the Pagination's `data-per-page`), else the rows shown, else 5 | no |
| `data-size` | the data table or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |
| `data-density` | the data table or a container | as [Table](table.md) | theme decides | yes |
| `data-lines`, `data-striped`, `data-hover`, `data-frame` | the Table's frame (`.canon-table`) | as [Table](table.md) | — | no |

## Behavior (canon.js)

- **Sorting:** a press cycles none → ascending → descending → none and fires **`canon-sort`** on the data table (`detail: { column, index, key, direction }`, bubbling, cancelable; `key` is the header's `data-key`, else its text). Unless cancelled, the header's `aria-sort` changes (the others go to `none`) and, with `data-local`, the rows are sorted: by `data-value`, else a `<time datetime>`, else the text; numbers as numbers, text in the page's language with numbers inside it in order ("Item 2" before "Item 10"). `none` restores the order they came in. One column sorts at a time.
- **Selecting:** the select-all checkbox checks or clears the rows shown; it is checked when they all are and mixed when some are. Shift+click on a row checkbox sets every row between it and the one clicked before. Each change fires **`canon-select`** (`detail: { rows, values, allMatching, count }`: the selected rows and their checkboxes' values; `allMatching` when every row matching the search and filters is selected, all pages included, and `count` how many that is).
- **The bulk bar** (`.canon-data-table-bulk`): canon.js makes it a manual popover, shown while rows are selected, floating at the bottom of the window, centered, over the page; it fades in and out without moving anything, and its width holds steady while the count changes (the theme gives it a minimum). Before the app's actions: Clear selection (an icon Button; it clears every row, and focus goes back to the select-all checkbox), the count ("3 selected", a status: screen readers hear it change) and a vertical [Separator](separator.md). When every row shown is selected and more match (`data-local`: the matching rows; else Pagination's `data-total`), the count reads "All 5 on this page selected" and a [Link](link.md) button offers "Select all 12": with `data-local` canon.js checks them all; otherwise `canon-select` says `allMatching`, rows the app adds come checked, and any change to the selection or the filters ends it. If the bar hides with focus in it, focus goes to the select-all checkbox.
- **Pinning:** the select column (at the start), `data-pin` columns and the actions column (at the end) stay in view while the others scroll under them. canon.js writes `data-pinned="start" | "end"`, `--canon-pin-offset` and `data-pin-edge` (the innermost pinned column of each side) on their cells, and on the frame `data-scroll-start` / `data-scroll-end` while rows are hidden under that side.
- **Paging** (`data-local` and a Pagination): the Pagination counts the rows (`data-total`), and its pages show those rows; sorting keeps the page. Without `data-local` the Pagination works as on its own: the app listens for `canon-page` and loads the page.
- **Loading:** while `aria-busy="true"`, skeleton rows stand in for the body (the body is hidden, not removed), and "Loading" is announced. When it goes, the rows return, and the data table is `data-loaded` while the theme shows them in.
- **Search:** typing in the toolbar's search field narrows local rows to those containing every word (in any data column, ignoring case and accents); without `data-local` the app hears it a quarter second after typing stops.
- **Filters:** one per column, each a column, a condition and a value: text (contains, doesn't contain, is, is not, starts with, ends with), number (=, ≠, <, ≤, >, ≥), date (is, is before, is after), choice (is, is not, any of several values). The Filter button opens the builder: a row per filter (Column, Condition, Value), Add filter, Apply filter; nothing changes until Apply. Applied filters show as chips under the toolbar (a choice's values as their Tags, two and "+N"): a chip opens that column's filter alone (Condition, Value, Apply), its × removes it, Clear all removes them all. A filtered column also shows a filter button in its header, which opens the same filter; unfiltered columns have none. Search and filter changes fire **`canon-filter`** (`detail: { query, filters: [{ column, key, operator, values }] }`); with `data-local` canon.js hides the rows that don't match, pages what's left and, when nothing is left, shows the no-results Empty State with Clear filters.
- **Columns** (the `data-panel="columns"` button): a panel listing the data columns, pinned ones first: a checkbox shows or hides each (the last one shown can't be hidden), a pin button pins it (moving it to the end of the pinned ones) or unpins it, and the grip reorders it within its group: drag it, or focus it and press Up / Down (the new position is announced). Changes fire **`canon-columns`** (`detail: { columns: [{ column, key, hidden, pinned }] }`) for the app to remember.
- **Export:** an item with `data-export` fires **`canon-export`** (`detail: { format, rows, columns }`, cancelable). For `csv`, unless cancelled, canon.js downloads the rows that match the search and filters (all pages) in the columns shown, as text.
- **A header that stays:** give the frame a `max-block-size` and it scrolls down as well; the header stays at its top.
- **Truncated cells** show their full text as a tooltip (`title`) while cut; the full text is in the page, so screen readers read it all.
- **Rows the app adds or replaces** are marked, pinned, and (with `data-local`) sorted, filtered and paged again.
- **Editing cells** (`data-edit` on a header): see [Data Table: editing cells](data-table-editing.md).
- **Without canon.js** it is a Table: row checkboxes submit with a form, row buttons and menus work, the bulk actions are a row under the table, headers don't sort and, with `data-local`, every row shows. What only canon.js can do isn't shown (`@media (scripting: none)`), so there are no dead controls: the search field (unless it is in a `<form>` that sends it), the Filter and Columns buttons, the Export items (and a menu holding only them), and the select-all checkbox.

## States

| State | Hook |
|---|---|
| Sorted column | `aria-sort="ascending" | "descending"` on its header |
| Selected row | its checkbox `:checked` (`tr:has(:checked)`) |
| Pinned cell | `data-pinned`, `data-pin-edge` (canon.js) |
| Rows under the pinned columns | `data-scroll-start`, `data-scroll-end` on the frame (canon.js) |
| Loading | `aria-busy="true"` on the data table |
| A filtered column | its header's filter button shown (canon.js) |
| A hidden column | `hidden` on its cells (canon.js) |
| Empty, no results, error | a message row with an [Empty State](empty-state.md) |

## Core

- The data table: a column, as wide as its container and never wider (`contain: inline-size`), so the frame scrolls. Cells `nowrap` (unless `data-wrap="normal"`). Select and actions columns as narrow as their content. Pinned cells `position: sticky` at `--canon-pin-offset`; header cells sticky at the top (above pinned body cells). While busy, the real body is hidden and the skeleton body shown. The toolbar and chips are wrapping rows; a truncated cell's text is a block cut with an ellipsis.

## Accessibility

- Sorting is a button in the header; the header's `aria-sort` tells screen readers the order. Only one column has a direction at a time.
- Every checkbox has a name ("Select all rows", "Select Edwin Mueller"); the select-all's mixed state is the native `indeterminate`.
- Row actions are named for their row; a set of buttons is a Toolbar (one Tab stop per row).
- While loading, the data table is `aria-busy` and "Loading" is announced; skeletons are hidden from screen readers.
- A message row keeps the table and its headers: screen readers hear the table, then the message.
- The search field is named; the panels are dialogs (Popovers) named "Filters", "Filter User", "Columns", with labelled fields; chips are a group named "Filters" whose buttons say what they do ("Edit filter: Status is Ready", "Remove filter: …").
- Reordering columns works from the keyboard (the grip and Up / Down), and each move is announced.

## Theme obligations

- Sort state visible in the header; a selected row distinguishable; pinned columns separated from what scrolls under them; a skeleton that reads as "loading".

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A bulk bar for lists that aren't tables | Bulk Action Bar (pattern), from this one |
| Keeping the bar off the page's last lines | The app's bottom padding (the bar floats over them) |
| A header that stays in view while the page (not the frame) scrolls | If it comes up |
| Sorting by several columns | If it comes up |
| Row click (opening a row) | If it comes up |
| Several filters on one column, or "or" between filters | If it comes up |
| Remembering columns and filters between visits | The app (from `canon-columns`, `canon-filter`) |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Table's sizes; the select column as wide as a row is tall (48 / 56 / 64); the actions cell 8px in; the pagination 16px under the table.

Sort arrows (Lucide arrow-down-up; sorted, arrow-up, turning over to point down for descending, 0.2s) 8px after the label in the header's color; a selected row zinc-50 (dark zinc-800), its fill (and the hover's) fading in 0.12s; on a striped table zinc-100, a step darker than a stripe. Fill order: the row under the pointer, then selected, then striped; pinned cells paint the same fill. Pinned columns: a data column keeps a line at its end and a pin icon at the end of its header; the innermost pinned column casts a 4px band (black at 5%, dark white at 5%) while rows scroll under it; the actions column always has the line at its start, and the band before it while rows hide under it. Row action buttons: a Toolbar's buttons (zinc frame, zinc icons). Loading: ghost rows (lines of varying length, a square for the checkbox, a circle for the actions). Toolbar: items 12px apart, search 200px wide; filter chips 16px apart, joined segments on zinc-50 with zinc-200 lines (dark zinc-800, zinc-700), 2px end corners, choice values as their Tags; a filtered column's header shows its filter button (Lucide list-filter); the filter builder's rows 8px apart inside, 16px between, Add filter and Apply filter under a line; Columns: a grip (Lucide grip-vertical, zinc-400), the checkbox, a pin button shown while pinned, or with the row under the pointer or keyboard focus, a line after the pinned columns. The select column pinned on its own shows the line and band only while rows scroll under it; sort hover zinc-900 (dark white), focus Button's ring; Clear all a minimal Button; panels with Popover's corners and padding; the toolbar's Filter, Columns and Export are low neutral Buttons (`data-intent="neutral"`), as are row action Toolbars' buttons. The bulk bar: Canon's panel look, floating 1.5rem above the window's bottom, at least 48rem wide and at most 64rem (the window less 1rem each side when smaller), so the count changing moves nothing (the actions keep to the end; under 40rem they take their own row under a line); white (dark zinc-900), no frame: a hairline edge and the floating shadow, Popover's corners, 8px inside, items 8px apart; the count medium; it rises 8px and fades in 0.15s (still with reduced motion).

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/description-list.md

# Description List

Tier: **T0**

Facts about one thing, as terms and their values: a record's details, a profile, an invoice's totals, a settings overview. The read-only side of a form: with the same `data-label` it lines up the same way, so a page can switch between showing and editing without moving. To compare many records, a [Table](table.md).

## Elements

```html
<dl class="canon-description-list" data-label="start">
  <div><dt>Invoice</dt><dd>INV-2041</dd></div>
  <div><dt>Status</dt><dd><span class="canon-tag" data-intent="success">…Paid…</span></dd></div>
  <div><dt>Participants</dt><dd>Ada Lovelace</dd><dd>Grace Hopper</dd></div>
  <div>
    <dt>Email</dt><dd>ada@example.com</dd>
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-intent="neutral">…Change<span class="canon-visually-hidden"> email</span>…</button>
  </div>
</dl>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `dl.canon-description-list` | yes | The list. Its only children are `<div>` items. |
| `<div>` | yes | An item: one term, then its values, then an optional action. |
| `<dt>` | yes | The term. Text; or an icon (`canon-icon`, `aria-hidden="true"`) with its words in a `canon-visually-hidden` span, for a panel where the icons say enough at a glance (an event, a contact card). |
| `<dd>` | yes | A value, one or more per term. Any inline content: text, a [Tag](tag.md), a [Link](link.md), a `<time>`, an [Avatar](avatar.md) and a name, a copy button. Empty (`<dd></dd>`): a dash, heard as "Not set" (the `--canon-text-not-set` string). |
| Action | no | A [Button](button.md) (minimal and neutral, or low for something weightier: Export, Delete) or [Link](link.md) after the values, at the item's end ("Change"); named for its item where several are alike ("Change email"). |

- **Not for** a list of things (a list, Nav List, Timeline) or headline numbers ([Stat](stat.md)).

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-label` | the list or a container | `start`: terms beside their values, in Field's label column (`--canon-label-width`, a third), while the list has 32rem; above below that · `above` | terms above | yes ([Field](field.md#label-beside-the-box-author-hint)'s hint) |
| `data-columns` | the list | `2` · `3`: items side by side, as many columns as fit at 16rem each, up to that number | one | no |
| `data-lines` | the list | `none`: no lines between items | lines | no |
| `data-size` | the list or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg`: Table's type and row heights | theme decides | yes |

## Core

- The list is a grid of items (`--canon-description-list-gap` between columns, 2rem); it is a size container for `data-label`. Each item is a grid: term and values in a column, an action at the end; an icon term sits beside its values, as every term does with `data-label="start"`.
- Values wrap, even unbroken ones (an address, a key).

## Accessibility

- A description list: screen readers announce the list and its number of items, each term with its values. An icon term's words are hidden visually only, so the pair still reads ("Date, 10 October 2026").
- An empty value is announced as "Not set" rather than skipped.

## Theme obligations

- Terms read as labels (quieter than values); items read as separate (lines or space).
- An empty value is visible as empty (a dash), not a blank.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left, terms are on the right.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Groups of items under a heading | Headings between lists, or a Section / Panel |
| Editing a value in place | A form with `data-label="start"` in its place |
| Headline numbers | [Stat](stat.md) |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Items a Table row's height (48 / 56 / 64), 8px inside; stacked, the value 4px under its term; beside, 16px apart; an icon term a control-sized square (32 / 40 / 48), 8px from its values; columns 32px apart.

Table's look and the event sheet's details: a hairline rule between items (black at 10%, dark white at 10%); terms in Table's header type (zinc-500 medium, dark zinc-400), values zinc-900 (dark white) in Text Input's type; icons zinc-500 (dark zinc-400), the value's first line level with the icon; an action centered on the item when its term is stacked over its value, and on the item's line when they sit beside each other (`data-label="start"`); empty values zinc-400 (dark zinc-500).

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/empty-state.md

# Empty State

Tier: **T0**

What a view shows when it has no content: nothing yet, nothing matching a search or filters, or an error, and what to do next.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-empty-state">
  <span class="canon-empty-state-icon" aria-hidden="true"><span class="canon-icon" data-icon="table" aria-hidden="true"></span></span>
  <h3 class="canon-empty-state-title">No users yet</h3>
  <p class="canon-empty-state-description">People you invite will show up here.</p>
  <div class="canon-empty-state-actions">
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="high">…Invite people…</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-empty-state` | yes | Where the content would be: a page's body, a panel, a [Data Table](data-table.md)'s message row. |
| `.canon-empty-state-icon` | no | `aria-hidden="true"`, holding one `canon-icon`: decoration; the title says it. |
| `.canon-empty-state-title` | yes | A heading at the page's level when it stands for a section's content, else a `<p>`. |
| `.canon-empty-state-description` | no | A sentence: why it's empty, what will appear, what to try. |
| `.canon-empty-state-actions` | no | [Buttons](button.md) or links: the way forward (create, clear filters, try again). One main action at most. |

- **Nothing yet:** say what will appear and how to start ("No users yet" · "People you invite will show up here." · Invite people).
- **No results:** say nothing matches and offer the way back ("No matching users" · "Try other words, or clear the filters to see everyone." · Clear filters).
- **Error:** `data-intent="danger"`; say what happened in plain words and offer to retry ("Couldn't load users" · "Something went wrong on our side. Try again in a moment." · Try again).

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-intent` | the empty state | `danger`: an error | — | no |
| `data-size` | the empty state or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |

## Core

- A centered column; title and description without margins; actions a centered, wrapping row.

## Accessibility

- The title is real text (a heading where the page needs one); the icon is hidden from screen readers.
- When it replaces content after an action (a search with no results), the app announces it or moves focus as it would for any new content.

## Theme obligations

- The title stands out; the description reads as secondary; an error is recognizable as one beyond its color (its icon, its words).

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Illustrations instead of an icon | The author's image in place of the icon, if it comes up |
| Full-page states (403, 404, 500, maintenance) | Status Pages |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** The icon in a hexagon 5 / 6 / 7rem, icons 2 / 2.5 / 3rem; Text Input's type (12 / 14 / 16px); the actions a field step (12 / 16 / 20) under the text.

The icon in a soft hexagon (zinc-100 fading to the surface; dark zinc-800), icon zinc-400 (dark zinc-500); the title medium zinc-900 (dark white), the description zinc-500 (dark zinc-400). The hexagon's sizes; an error tints the hexagon red-50 and the icon red-500 (dark red-400); the description at most 32rem wide.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/filter-bar.md

# Filter Bar

Tier: **T2** (without canon.js it is a search form: the popovers open, Apply submits)

Narrows a list (cards, search results, a feed): a search field, facets (a button opening the choices for one thing: Team, Date posted, Salary), quick [Toggle Chips](toggle-chip.md), Clear all and the number of results. For a table with columns, the [Data Table](data-table.md)'s own filters (column, condition, value) fit better.

## Elements

```html
<form class="canon-filter-bar" id="jobs-filters" role="search" aria-label="Filter jobs" method="get">
  <div class="canon-text-input">
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="search" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <input type="search" name="q" aria-label="Search jobs" placeholder="Search jobs">
  </div>

  <div class="canon-filter-bar-facet">
    <button type="button" class="canon-filter-bar-button" popovertarget="jobs-team" aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-expanded="false">
      <span class="canon-filter-bar-label">Team</span>
    </button>
    <div class="canon-popover" id="jobs-team" popover role="dialog" aria-label="Team">
      <fieldset class="canon-fieldset">
        <legend class="canon-fieldset-legend canon-visually-hidden">Team</legend>
        <div class="canon-choice">…Design (checkbox, name="team")…</div>
        <div class="canon-choice">…Research…</div>
      </fieldset>
    </div>
  </div>

  <label class="canon-toggle-chip">
    <input type="checkbox" name="remote" value="1">
    <span class="canon-toggle-chip-label">Remote</span>
  </label>

  <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-intent="neutral" commandfor="jobs-filters" command="--canon-clear">…Clear all…</button>
  <button type="submit" class="canon-button canon-filter-bar-apply" data-emphasis="high">…Apply…</button>
  <output class="canon-filter-bar-count" data-align="end">128 jobs</output>
</form>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `form.canon-filter-bar` | yes | `role="search"`, named (`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`). A wrapping row. Its children: the items below, [Buttons](button.md), a [Select](select.md) or [Segmented Control](segmented-control.md) (a sort, a view), hidden inputs. |
| Search field | no | A [Text Input](text-input.md) with `<input type="search">`, named. |
| `.canon-filter-bar-facet` | no | One thing to filter by: a `button.canon-filter-bar-button` (`type="button"`, `popovertarget`, `aria-haspopup="dialog"`) and, right after it, the [Popover](popover.md) it opens (`role="dialog"`, named like the button). |
| `.canon-filter-bar-label` | in a facet's button | The facet's name ("Team"). An icon (`aria-hidden="true"`) may come before it. canon.js adds `.canon-filter-bar-value` after it. |
| Facet content | yes | The choices: Checkboxes or Radios in a [Fieldset](fieldset.md) (its legend can be visually hidden: the button names it), or fields (two numbers for a range; dates are a [Date](date.md), a range in one box, never a bare date input). Every control has a `name`. |
| `.canon-toggle-chip` | no | A quick filter of its own ("Remote"), or a set of them. |
| Clear all | no | A minimal neutral Button with `command="--canon-clear"` and `commandfor` the bar's `id`. Shown while something is chosen. |
| `.canon-filter-bar-apply` | no | `button[type="submit"]`: for pages without JavaScript; hidden while scripting runs. |
| `output.canon-filter-bar-count` | no | The number of results, kept up to date by the app (an `<output>` is announced as it changes). |

- **`data-align="end"`** on an item sends it and what follows to the far end (the count, a sort).
- **A radio whose value is empty** ("Any time") means nothing is chosen in that facet; Clear all goes back to it.
- **Choices apply as they're made:** no Apply inside the facets.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-submit` | the bar | (present): canon.js submits the form after each choice (and on Enter in the search field), for pages the server renders | canon.js fires `canon-filter` | no |
| `data-align` | an item | `end` | — | no |
| `data-size` | the bar or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |

## Behavior (canon.js)

- **Each facet's button shows what is chosen** in its popover: the first choice's label and how many more ("Team: Design +1"), a pair of values as a range ("Salary: 80,000 – 120,000"), dates in the reader's format ("Due: Oct 1 – Oct 31"), numbers with the reader's separators. Its name for screen readers lists everything ("Team: Design, Research"). The facet gets `data-active`; the bar gets `data-active` while anything in a facet, a chip or the search field is chosen.
- **Every change fires `canon-filter`** on the bar (`detail: { values }`, the form's values by name, each an array: `{ q: ["engineer"], team: ["design", "research"] }`): choices at once, typing a quarter second after it stops, Enter in the search field at once. The form doesn't submit. With `data-submit` the form submits instead.
- **Clear all** (`--canon-clear` on the bar): checkboxes off, each radio group back to its empty-valued radio, fields emptied, sliders to their full range, then one `canon-filter`; focus moves to the search field (else the first control). A sort or other control outside the facets, chips and search is left as it is.
- **The popovers** are Popovers: focus moves in, closing returns it, the button's `aria-expanded` follows.
- A form reset updates the buttons and fires `canon-filter`. After changing values in code, dispatch `change` on the control.

## States

| State | Hook |
|---|---|
| A facet with a choice | `.canon-filter-bar-facet[data-active]` (canon.js) |
| Something chosen | `.canon-filter-bar[data-active]` (canon.js) |
| A facet open | `.canon-filter-bar-button[aria-expanded="true"]` |
| Hover, focus | `:hover`, `:focus-visible` on the button |

## Core

- The bar is a wrapping flex row, items centered; `data-align="end"` takes the rest of the row before an item. A facet's button is an inline row that doesn't wrap; its value cuts with … where it must.
- Clear all hides while nothing is chosen; Apply hides while scripting runs.

## Accessibility

- A search landmark, named for what it filters. Each facet's button says what is chosen (its name lists every choice); its panel is a named dialog with a group of choices.
- The count is an `<output>`, so its changes are announced. Say what changed in it ("12 jobs"), not only a number.
- Focus stays where the person is: choosing in a facet doesn't close it; Escape or a click outside does, returning focus to its button.

## Theme obligations

- Facet buttons and chips read as one row with the search field (the same height).
- A facet with a choice stands out from one without, beyond color where the system allows (its value shows in the button).
- The facet's open state and focus visible; the chevron shows it opens.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A long facet with its own search (50 owners) | A [Combobox](combobox.md) in the panel, if it comes up |
| Collapsing to "Filters (3)" in a drawer on small screens | With Drawer |
| Removable chips for each choice under the bar | As Data Table's chips, if it comes up |
| A single Slider in a facet (only pairs are summarized) | If it comes up |
| Sort | The app's Select at the end (`data-align="end"`) |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Items 8px apart; the search field 16rem (at most the row); facet buttons and chips a control's height (32 / 40 / 48) so the row lines up.

A facet button is a Toggle Chip with a chevron (zinc-500, dark zinc-400, turning while open): a zinc-200 line (dark zinc-700), labels zinc-700 (dark zinc-200); hover zinc-50, a zinc-300 line (dark zinc-800, zinc-600); open zinc-100 (dark zinc-700). With a choice, a chosen [Toggle Chip](toggle-chip.md)'s look: zinc-900 with a white label and chevron (dark: white with zinc-900), hover zinc-800 (dark zinc-200), open or pressing zinc-700 (dark zinc-300); forced colors, Highlight. Panels at least 12rem, choices in a column 8px apart. The count zinc-500 (dark zinc-400), tabular figures. Clear all a minimal Button.

**Motion:** Clear all fades in (0.15s) when something is chosen; it goes at once.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/kbd.md

# Kbd

Tier: **T0**

A keyboard key or shortcut, shown as a small key cap: in running text, in a tooltip, or as a button's or tag's accessory.

## Element

```html
<kbd class="canon-kbd">⌘K</kbd>
```

- Always `<kbd>`.
- Text only: the keys as the platform writes them. Which platform's keys to show (⌘ or Ctrl) is the author's call.
- One `canon-kbd` per shortcut (`⌘K`, `Ctrl Shift P`). A sequence is several, with words between: `<kbd class="canon-kbd">G</kbd> then <kbd class="canon-kbd">I</kbd>`.
- Symbols (⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ↵) are read differently by each screen reader. Where it matters, write the word (`Ctrl`, `Enter`) or an `<abbr title="Command">⌘</abbr>`.

## Where it goes

| Place | Markup | Accessibility |
|---|---|---|
| Running text | `Press <kbd class="canon-kbd">⌘K</kbd> to search` | Read as part of the sentence |
| Tooltip | After the text: `<div class="canon-tooltip" …>Bold <kbd class="canon-kbd">⌘B</kbd></div>` | Read with the tooltip |
| Button accessory | Last child, `aria-hidden="true"`; the button gets `aria-keyshortcuts` | Announced once, from `aria-keyshortcuts`, and only where the shortcut works |
| [Tag](tag.md) accessory | Last child | Read with the tag |

```html
<button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral" aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K">
  <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="search" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="canon-button-label">Search</span>
  <kbd class="canon-kbd" aria-hidden="true">⌘K</kbd>
</button>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data-size` | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |

- In a button, the key follows the button's size (so it is md in a default button). A `data-size` on the key still wins.
- In a tag, it follows the tag's size the same way.

## Core

- Resets the browser's monospace font to the surrounding text.
- Never wraps inside: lines break between keys.
- Always left to right (`direction: ltr; unicode-bidi: isolate`): shortcuts are written that way in every language, and in right-to-left text `⌘K` would otherwise render as `K⌘`.
- As a button, tooltip or tag accessory, centered on the line.

## Theme obligations

- Readable on every surface it can sit on: the page, tooltips, and the buttons it accessorizes in all 16 emphasis × intent variants.
- Never change case or symbols in a way that changes the key (uppercase is fine; `Esc` and `ESC` are the same key).

## Not in the contract

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Platform detection (⌘ vs Ctrl) | App |
| Key press animation | Out of scope |
| Clickable keys | Button |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** 16 / 20 / 24px tall, 2 / 4 / 6 radius, text 10px semibold uppercase at every size; sm by default, the button's size inside a button

Derived from the surrounding text color (text 55%, chip 4.4%; dark 80% and 23%), so it reads on any surface; a hairline along its bottom in the text color at 25% (the key's edge). On the page: zinc-100 with zinc-500 text (dark: zinc-700, zinc-300) within a few RGB units. Solid high-emphasis buttons and tags use the dark recipe.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/stat.md

# Stat

Tier: **T0**

One number that matters, with what it measures and how it moved: revenue this month, open invoices, average response time. The headline numbers of a dashboard, the top of a list page ("142 orders"), a record's overview. Plain content: a [Card](card.md), a row of stats or the page around it frames it. Also called a KPI.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-stat">
  <p class="canon-stat-label">Revenue this month</p>
  <p class="canon-stat-value">$48,210</p>
  <p class="canon-stat-change" data-direction="up" data-intent="success">Up 12% from last month</p>
  <p class="canon-stat-description">Goal: $50,000</p>
  <div class="canon-stat-chart"><svg viewBox="0 0 120 32" preserveAspectRatio="none" aria-hidden="true">…</svg></div>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-stat` | yes | A `<div>`. Its children in this order; only the label and the value are required. |
| `.canon-stat-label` | yes | What is measured, with its period where it matters ("Revenue this month"). A `<p>`; holds a `.canon-stat-link` when the stat leads somewhere (see Linking). |
| `.canon-stat-value` | yes | The number, formatted by the app: units, currency, abbreviations ("$48,210", "1.2 s", "48.2K"). A `<p>`. Empty: a dash, heard as "Not set" (`--canon-text-not-set`, as Description List's). |
| `.canon-stat-change` | no | How it moved, in the app's words: the whole phrase, direction and comparison included ("Up 12% from last month", "+3 since yesterday", "No change"). A `<p>`. The theme draws an arrow before it from `data-direction`. |
| `.canon-stat-description` | no | More context: a target, a breakdown, when it was updated ("Goal: $50,000", "8 overdue", "Updated 5 minutes ago"). A `<p>`. |
| `.canon-stat-chart` | no | A sparkline the app draws: an inline `<svg>` that strokes or fills with `currentColor`, so the theme colors it. `aria-hidden="true"` when the change already says the trend; `role="img"` and a name when it says more. Canon doesn't draw charts. |

- **The app writes the change.** Canon never formats numbers or composes "12%" into a sentence: the phrase is the app's, in the reader's language. It must say the direction in words ("Up", "+", "more"), because the arrow is decoration.
- **Direction and meaning are separate.** `data-direction` says which way it moved; `data-intent` says whether that's good. Revenue up is good, an error rate up is bad, a headcount up is neither: the author says each, the theme never guesses from the direction.
- **Stat or [Description List](description-list.md)?** A Description List gives facts about one thing at equal weight; a Stat puts one number first, to be compared with others and over time.
- **Stat or [Count](count.md)?** A Count is a small badge on something else ("3 unread"); a Stat is a number that stands on its own.

### A row of stats

```html
<div class="canon-stats" role="group" aria-label="This month" data-lines>
  <div class="canon-stat">…</div>
  <div class="canon-stat">…</div>
  <div class="canon-stat">…</div>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-stats` | no | Stats side by side, as many columns as fit (each at least 12rem), wrapping onto more rows. Named (`role="group"` and `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`) when the stats share a context the page doesn't already give ("This month"). Its only children are stats. |

### Linking

```html
<div class="canon-stat">
  <p class="canon-stat-label"><a class="canon-stat-link" href="/invoices?status=overdue">Overdue invoices</a></p>
  <p class="canon-stat-value">8</p>
</div>
```

- A stat that leads to the list behind it ("8 overdue" → the overdue invoices): its label holds an `<a href class="canon-stat-link">`, whose target covers the whole stat, as `.canon-card-link` does a [Card](card.md). The link's name is the label; the value and change are read after it, as the stat's text.
- One link per stat. A stat with other actions keeps them out of it (in the Card's header, say).

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-direction` | the change | `up` · `down` · `flat` | none: no arrow | no |
| `data-intent` | the change | `success` (good) · `danger` (bad) · `warning` · `info` | none: neutral | no |
| `data-size` | the stat, the row or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` (xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg): the value's size, and the rest to match | theme decides | yes |
| `data-lines` | the row | present: a line between the stats of a row | no lines | no |
| `aria-busy` | the stat or the row | `true` while the value loads | — | — |

- **`data-size` is the only way to make a stat bigger.** A headline stat over smaller ones is `lg` beside `sm`, not a different kind of stat.
- **`data-intent` on the change, not the stat.** The number itself is neutral; only how it moved is good or bad.
- **`warning`** for a move toward a limit (storage 90% full, "Up 40%: near your plan's limit"); **`info`** for a change worth noticing that is neither good nor bad.

## States

| State | Hook | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Loading | `aria-busy="true"` on the stat or the row | The app puts a [Skeleton](skeleton.md) (`data-shape="block"`) in the value, and leaves the change empty or out. |
| No value | an empty `.canon-stat-value` | A dash, heard as "Not set". |
| Out of date | the app's words in the description ("Updated 3 hours ago"), `data-intent="warning"` on the change where it matters | Canon doesn't track time. |

## Core

- A stat is a column: label, value, change, description, chart, each on its own line, in that order whatever the theme does with spacing.
- The value never breaks inside a number: it wraps only at spaces ("$48,210 per month"), and its figures are tabular, so values in a row line up as they change.
- A row is a grid of columns at least 12rem wide (`--canon-stats-min`), as many as fit. With `data-lines`, each stat draws a line before it at the gap's middle; the row cuts off the one before its first column, so lines only fall between stats. Wrapped rows are apart by the gap, without a line.
- The chart fills the stat's width at a height the theme sets; its SVG is stretched to it (`preserveAspectRatio="none"` is the app's), and core keeps its strokes their drawn width (`vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`).
- A linked stat: the label's link reaches over the whole stat (its `::after`, as a link card's), so all of it is the target.

## Accessibility

- Read in order: "Revenue this month, $48,210, Up 12% from last month, Goal: $50,000". No role, nothing announced around it; a row is a named group when it has a name.
- The arrow is decoration: the change's words say the direction. Its intent is shown by color, so where good or bad isn't plain from the label and the direction, the app says it ("Error rate up 3%: above target").
- An abbreviated value ("48.2K") reads as written; where the exact number matters, the app adds it as visually hidden text ("48.2K<span class="canon-visually-hidden"> (48,210)</span>") or links to it.
- A loading stat says so with `aria-busy`; its Skeleton is hidden from assistive technology, so only the label is read until the value comes.
- Values that update while the page is open are not announced: a dashboard that speaks every refresh can't be used. An app that must announce one (a threshold crossed) uses an [Alert](alert.md) or a [Toast](toast.md).
- A linked stat is one link, named by its label; its focus ring goes around the whole stat.

## Theme obligations

- The value is the first thing read on the stat; the label quieter, the change and description quieter still.
- Each intent told apart by more than its hue alone: the direction's arrow is always drawn, and the change keeps its words.
- A chart in a quiet color by default, so it supports the number instead of competing with it.
- A row's stats start level with each other, so short labels put their values on one line. (A label that wraps pushes its value down: keep labels short.)
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the arrow and the text start on the right, and the sideways part of the arrows mirrors (time runs the other way).

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Drawing charts (sparklines included) | The app, as an `<svg>` in `.canon-stat-chart`; charts are planned later |
| Formatting numbers, units and currency | The app (`Intl.NumberFormat`) |
| Progress toward a target as a bar | Meter / Progress, in the description's place |
| Counting up to a value as it loads | Out of scope: motion that doesn't explain a change |
| Choosing the period ("This month ▾") | The app: a [Select](select.md) or [Segmented Control](segmented-control.md) over the row |
| Layout of mixed content in columns | [Grid](stack.md) |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** The value 24 / 30 / 36px on 32 / 36 / 44px lines, semibold; the label 12 / 14 / 16px on 16 / 20 / 24px lines, medium, the value 4 / 4 / 8 under it; the change and the description in the control's type (12 / 14 / 16px), 4 / 6 / 8 under what's above; the arrow 16 / 16 / 20, 4px before the change's text; the chart 32 / 40 / 48 tall, 8 / 12 / 16 under what's above. A row: stats 24 / 32 / 40 apart, rows the same; with `data-lines`, the line halfway between the stats of a row.

No frame, no fill, no padding: it takes its container's. The label zinc-500 (dark zinc-400); the value zinc-900 (dark white), tabular figures; the change in its intent's color, the 600 (dark the 400; warning amber-600, dark amber-400), neutral zinc-500 (dark zinc-400), medium, with Lucide's `trending-up`, `trending-down` or `move-right` before it; the description zinc-500 (dark zinc-400). The chart zinc-400 (dark zinc-500), or the change's intent color at 60% when the change has one. A row's lines hairline rules (black at 10%, dark white at 10%). Loading: a Skeleton block 6rem wide at the value's size, Button's corners. A linked stat: its label in the text's color, underlined on hover with Link's line; focus a 1px ring in the focus color 4px out from the stat, at Button's corners. Forced colors: the arrow and the chart in the text's color.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/status.md

# Status Indicator

Tier: **T0**

Where something stands, in a word and a dot: Draft, Sent, Paid, Overdue. A status in text, light enough for a column of a [Table](table.md) where every row has one.

## Element

```html
<span class="canon-status" data-intent="danger">
  <span class="canon-status-label">Overdue</span>
</span>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-status` | yes | A `<span>`; its only child is the label. The theme draws the dot. |
| `.canon-status-label` | yes | The status, a word or two. Also when only the dot shows (it stays as the status's text for screen readers). |

- **The label says it; the dot repeats it.** A status is never the color alone.
- **Status or [Tag](tag.md)?** The same words (`data-intent`), two weights. A Status in text and lists, many to a screen; a Tag where the status is the point, one or two to a screen (beside a record's title in its [Page Header](page-header.md)).
- **Not a [Count](count.md):** no numbers. Not an [Avatar](avatar.md)'s status: a person's presence is the avatar's dot.
- **Changing by itself** (a deploy finishing): the app puts the status in a live region (`role="status"`) if people should hear the change.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-intent` | the status | `info` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` | none: neutral | no |
| `data-pulse` | the status | present: in progress right now | absent | no |
| `data-size` | the status or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |
| `data-display` | the status or a container | `icon`: the dot only, the label visually hidden | label shown | yes |

- **`data-intent`:** `info` (sent, scheduled), `success` (paid, live), `warning` (due soon, needs attention), `danger` (overdue, failed). None: neutral (draft, inactive, queued).
- **`data-pulse`:** for the few states that change by themselves while you look (syncing, deploying), not for "pending". Reduced motion stops it.
- **The dot only:** where something else says what the colors mean (a legend, a column header, a tooltip on what it sits beside). On its own, a dot is just a color.

## Core

- An inline row, one line: the dot (`::before`), then the label, cut (…) where there is no room.

## Accessibility

- Read as its text: "Overdue". No role and nothing announced around it. In a table cell, the column header gives it its context ("Status, Overdue").
- The dot is decoration; with the dot only, the label is visually hidden and still read.
- In forced colors the dot keeps its shape (filled, or a ring for neutral), in the text's color.

## Theme obligations

- Each intent's dot distinguishable from the others; neutral clearly "nothing happening".
- The pulse calm, and off with reduced motion.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the dot comes first on the right.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A status with a time ("Paid 3 days ago") | The app's text after it |
| Steps of a process | Steps |
| A progress amount | Meter / Progress |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Dots 6 / 8 / 10px, 6 / 6 / 8px before the label; the label in the control's type (12 / 14 / 16px).

Labels zinc-700 (dark zinc-300). Dots: info blue-500, success green-600, warning amber-500, danger red-600 (dark: the 400s); neutral a hollow zinc-400 ring (dark zinc-500), as an avatar's offline. `data-pulse`: a ring grows from the dot and fades every 1.6s. Forced colors: the dot in the text's color.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/table.md

# Table

Tier: **T0** (the frame becoming a keyboard-scrollable region when the table is wider than it is **T2**, canon.js)

Rows and columns of data, read across and down: a native `<table>` in a frame. [Data Table](data-table.md) builds on it (sorting, selecting, filtering); a Table on its own shows data as it is.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-table">
  <table>
    <caption>Orders</caption>
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th scope="col">User</th>
        <th scope="col">Date</th>
        <th scope="col" data-align="end">Amount</th>
      </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <th scope="row">Edwin Mueller</th>
        <td><time datetime="2024-08-16">16.08.2024</time></td>
        <td data-align="end">$495.90</td>
      </tr>
    </tbody>
    <tfoot>
      <tr><th scope="row">Total</th><td></td><td data-align="end">$495.90</td></tr>
    </tfoot>
  </table>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-table` | yes | The frame. Its only child is the table. It scrolls sideways when the table is wider. |
| `<table>` | yes | Named: by a `<caption>`, or `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`. Never a layout table (`role="presentation"`). |
| `<caption>` | no | The table's title, shown as its first row. Visually hidden (`canon-visually-hidden`) when a heading nearby already says it; it still names the table. |
| `<thead>` | no | Column headers: `<th scope="col">`. A column whose header has nothing to say has an empty `<td>` there. |
| `<tbody>` | yes | The rows. A row's first cell can be its header (`<th scope="row">`): screen readers read it with every cell of the row. Several bodies are groups of rows. |
| `<tfoot>` | no | Totals and summaries. |
| Cell content | — | Text, numbers, `<time>`, links, and content components: a status [Tag](tag.md), an [Avatar](avatar.md) before a name (its fallback `aria-hidden`, the name written beside it). Selecting rows and a row's actions are [Data Table](data-table.md)'s. |

- **For data, not layout:** columns of the same kind of thing. A form's label and field pairs are [Form Layout](form-layout.md); term and description pairs are a Description List.
- **Figures** are tabular (all digits the same width), so numbers line up down a column; amounts still read better aligned to the end.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-align` | a cell (`th`, `td`) | `start` · `center` · `end` | `start` | no (write it on each cell of the column, its header too) |
| `data-wrap` | a cell (`th`, `td`) | `none`: the cell's text on one line · `normal`: it wraps | wraps (in a Data Table: one line) | no (write it on each cell of the column) |
| `data-lines` | the frame | `rows`: lines between rows · `grid`: between columns too · `none`: no lines between rows (the header keeps its line) | `rows` | no |
| `data-striped` | the frame | (present) every other body row filled | — | no |
| `data-hover` | the frame | (present) the body row under the pointer filled (devices with a pointer) | — | no |
| `data-frame` | the frame | `none`: no border, corners or fill; the table sits on the page | framed | no |
