| `data-density` | the frame or a container | `compact` · `comfortable` · `spacious`: how much taller than the header a row is | theme decides | yes |
| `data-size` | the frame or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |

## Behavior

**T0:** the browser's table. Cells wrap their text (not with `data-wrap="none"`); header cells stay on one line. The frame scrolls sideways when the table can't fit.

**canon.js (T2):** while the table is wider than its frame, the frame gets `data-scrolls`, `role="region"`, `tabindex="0"` and the table's name (its caption, through `aria-labelledby`), so keyboard users can reach it and scroll with the arrow keys. When it fits again they are removed. A role, tab stop or name the author wrote is kept.

## States

| State | Hook |
|---|---|
| Scrolls sideways | `data-scrolls` on the frame (canon.js) |
| Frame focused (when it scrolls) | `.canon-table:focus-visible` |

## Core

- The frame: `overflow-x: auto`, at most as wide as its container. The table: full width, `border-collapse: separate` (so the theme can round the frame and draw row lines), tabular figures. Cells: start-aligned (`data-align` changes it), vertically centered, sized including their padding; header cells and `data-wrap="none"` cells `nowrap`.

## Accessibility

- A native table: screen readers announce rows and columns, read headers with each cell, and move by cell. `scope` says which way a header reads.
- Named by its caption, so a list of tables on the page tells them apart; a visually hidden caption keeps the name without repeating a heading.
- A scrolling frame is a named region and a Tab stop, so its hidden columns can be reached without a mouse.

## Theme obligations

- `data-lines`, `data-striped`, `data-hover` and `data-frame` honored; a striped or hovered row still reads as one row (fills, not lines).

- Rows visibly separated (lines or fills); header cells distinguishable from data.
- A focus ring on the frame when it is focusable.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Sorting, selecting rows (checkboxes, a bulk bar), a row's actions, filtering, column menus, pagination, loading and empty states | [Data Table](data-table.md) |
| A header that stays in view while scrolling down | Data Table (`data-sticky`, with a height) |
| Column widths | The author's `<col>` / `<colgroup>` and CSS |
| Truncating a cell with "…" (`data-wrap="truncate"`), a column's setting written once on its header | Data Table |
| Stacking rows as cards on narrow screens | If it comes up |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Header rows 32 / 40 / 48 (the button's height); body rows 16px taller (48 / 56 / 64), the same as the header with `compact`, 32px taller with `spacious`; an avatar 8px before a name; cells 12 / 16 / 20px in (where a text field's text sits); Text Input's type (12 / 14 / 16px); corners 8 / 12 / 16.

A hairline edge (black at 12%, dark white at 12%) for its frame, white (dark zinc-900); lines between rows hairline rules (black at 10%, dark white at 10%); header text medium zinc-500 (dark zinc-400), body regular zinc-900 (dark white). `data-lines="grid"` the same rules between columns; stripes zinc-50 (dark halfway from zinc-900 to zinc-800); hover zinc-100 (dark zinc-800), on devices with a pointer; `data-frame="none"` drops border, corners and fill; densities other than comfortable; the caption a title row (semibold, a line under it); the footer medium over a line; a focusable frame gets Button's ring.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/tag.md

# Tag

Tier: **T0**

A short label in a chip: a category ("Design"), a status ("Active"), a person ("Ada Lovelace"). It shows something; the one thing it can do is be removed (a remove button). Other libraries often call it a badge.

## Elements

```html
<span class="canon-tag" data-emphasis="high" data-intent="success">
  <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="circle-check" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="canon-tag-label">Approved</span>
</span>
```

In order, all optional but the label:

| Element | Notes |
|---|---|
| `.canon-avatar` | First. A face for a person tag: photo or initials, no status, badge or count. The label already says the name, so its fallback is `aria-hidden="true"` (see [avatar.md](avatar.md)). The theme sizes it. |
| `.canon-icon` | Leading and/or trailing, `aria-hidden="true"` |
| `.canon-tag-dot` | Empty, right before the label. Decoration in the text color: the label carries the meaning. |
| `.canon-tag-label` | **Required.** The text. One line; it truncates with an ellipsis when the tag runs out of room. |
| `.canon-kbd` | Last. Read with the tag. See [kbd.md](kbd.md). |
| `.canon-tag-remove` | Last (instead of a key). `<button type="button">` with a name that says what goes: `aria-label="Remove Design"`. Empty: the theme draws the icon. The app (or [Combobox](combobox.md), which makes its own) removes the tag on click. |

```html
<span class="canon-tag" data-seed="4821">
  <span class="canon-avatar">
    <img class="canon-avatar-image" src="ada.jpg" alt="">
    <span class="canon-avatar-fallback" aria-hidden="true">AL</span>
  </span>
  <span class="canon-tag-label">Ada Lovelace</span>
</span>
```

- **Several tags** are a list: `<ul>` with one tag per `<li>`, so screen readers say how many.
- **Icon only:** `data-display="icon"` on the tag (or a container) hides the label visually; it is still read.
- **Removable:**

```html
<span class="canon-tag" data-seed="15">
  <span class="canon-tag-label">Design</span>
  <button type="button" class="canon-tag-remove" aria-label="Remove Design"></button>
</span>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-emphasis` | tag | `high` · `medium` · `low` | theme decides | no |
| `data-intent` | tag | `info` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` | none: neutral | no |
| `data-seed` | tag | an integer (a label id, a user id) | none: neutral | no |
| `data-size` | tag or a container | `xs` · `sm` · `md` · `lg` · `xl` · `2xl` (three-size themes: xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes |
| `data-display` | tag or a container | `icon` | label shown | yes |

### Color: meaning or identity, never both

- **`data-intent`** when the color means something: a status ("Approved", "Overdue"). Many statuses in a list (a column of a table) are lighter as a [Status Indicator](status.md): the same words, a dot instead of a chip. The same words as buttons and messages. Themes may give statuses their own look (shape, case), so a status never reads as a category. A status has no avatar and no key.
- **`data-seed`** when it only tells tags apart: categories, labels, people. The app passes a stable number and the theme picks one of its colors, always the same one, and the **same hue an avatar with that seed gets**. Integers only; hash other ids in the app. canon.js writes `data-seed-slot` for browsers that can't compute it in CSS (as for avatars).
- **Neither:** neutral.

### `data-emphasis`

| Value | Typically |
|---|---|
| `high` | Solid |
| `medium` | Tinted |
| `low` | Outlined |

The same words as buttons, so a theme's emphasis reads the same across components.

## Accessibility

- A tag is text: the label is read in place, with nothing announced around it. Don't rely on color alone; the label (or an icon's hidden text) says what the color means.
- Icons and the dot are decorative. An icon-only tag keeps its label, visually hidden.
- The remove button's name says which tag it removes ("Remove Design", not "Remove"). After a removal, move focus somewhere that makes sense (the next tag's button, or the control that added it): the button it was on is gone.

## Theme obligations

- Every emphasis readable in every color, on the page and on gray, tinted and dark surfaces.
- Keep the box the same across emphases (an outline doesn't make a tag bigger).
- A status may look different from a category, but never only by color.
- A key inside a solid tag stays readable.
- The remove button is the size of an icon, in reach of the tag's edge, with a visible focus ring; its icon contrasts with the tag on every emphasis and color.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Clickable tags (links, filters) | Not decided yet |
| A color chosen by the author | Not offered: `data-seed` or `data-intent` |
| Choosing the pill or uppercase look | Theme, from `data-intent` |
| Counts ("12") | [Count](count.md) |
| Tag input (typing to add tags) | [Combobox](combobox.md) with free values |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** 24 / 32 / 40px tall; padding 4 / 6 / 8, gap 2 / 4 / 6, radius 2 / 4 / 8; text 12 / 14 / 16 medium; icons and avatar 16 / 20 / 24; dot 6 / 8 / 10. sm by default.

Medium by default. Hues (17 seeds; intents info blue, success green, warning amber, danger red): high tone-600 with white; medium tone-400 at 15% with tone-700 (dark: tone-500 at 20%, tone-300); low a tone-700 border (dark: tone-300 at 50%) with the medium text. Neutral is derived from the surrounding text, like Kbd, so it reads on any surface; on the plain page it lands on zinc within a few RGB units: high zinc-600 / zinc-100 (dark zinc-500 / white), medium zinc-100 / zinc-900 (dark zinc-700 / white), low zinc-300 border / zinc-900 (dark zinc-600 / white). Only a solid tag's text is fixed (zinc-100, dark white): it contrasts with the fill. **Remove** (the badge's x): Lucide x at the icon size, the text color at 65% (dark 50%: zinc-500 / zinc-400 on the plain page), full on hover; on a hued tag (a status too) it is a segment of its own in zinc-100 with a zinc-500 x (dark zinc-700, zinc-400), the tag's padding around it and the tag's end corners (round on a status). **Statuses** (`data-intent`) are pills with uppercase 10 / 11 / 12px semibold text, tracking 0.03em, label 8 / 12 / 16px from the edge; same heights.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/breadcrumb.md

# Breadcrumb

Tier: **T0** (the collapsed pages' menu is [Menu](menu.md)'s: T1, its keyboard T2)

The trail of pages above the current one, each a link back up.

## Elements

```html
<nav class="canon-breadcrumb" aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol>
    <li><a href="/"><span class="canon-icon" data-icon="house" aria-hidden="true"></span><span class="canon-visually-hidden">Home</span></a></li>
    <li>
      <button type="button" class="canon-breadcrumb-more" popovertarget="trail-more" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">
        <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="more" aria-hidden="true"></span>
        <span class="canon-visually-hidden">More pages</span>
      </button>
      <div class="canon-menu" id="trail-more" popover role="menu" aria-label="More pages">
        <a class="canon-menu-item" role="menuitem" href="/docs"><span class="canon-menu-label">Docs</span></a>
      </div>
    </li>
    <li><a href="/docs/components">Components</a></li>
    <li><a href="/docs/components/breadcrumb" aria-current="page">Breadcrumb</a></li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `nav.canon-breadcrumb` | yes | Named "Breadcrumb" (`aria-label`, in the page's language): a navigation landmark. |
| `<ol>` | yes | Its only child: the pages in order, top first. |
| `<li>` | yes | One per page: a link (`<a href>`), or the "more" button with its menu. |
| `aria-current="page"` | — | On the last item, the current page (a link to itself, or a `<span>`). A trail may also end at the parent page and leave the current one out. |
| An icon link | no | A `canon-icon` (`house` for home) with its name in a `canon-visually-hidden` span. |
| `.canon-breadcrumb-more` | no | A `<button type="button">` standing for the pages left out: `popovertarget` a [Menu](menu.md) of them (links, `<a class="canon-menu-item" role="menuitem">`), `aria-haspopup="menu"`, its name in a visually hidden span ("More pages"). |

- **Drawn by the theme, never written:** the separators between items (they point the reading direction, so they mirror in right-to-left).
- **Collapsing** is the author's (or the app's): which pages to leave out is a choice about the page, not the space. A long trail otherwise wraps onto more lines. The exception is a [Page Header](page-header.md#behavior-t2-canonjs) whose trail doesn't fit its row: there canon.js keeps the last page after a generated "more" button listing the rest (the author's own "more" menu's pages among them), until there is room again.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-current` | the current page | `page` | — | — |
| `data-size` | the breadcrumb or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |

## Core

- The `<nav>`: a flex row; the `<ol>`: a wrapping flex row, no list markers or indent; items: inline flex rows, the separator a `::before` on each item but the first. Links: inherited color, no underline. The "more" button: a button reset.

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` named "Breadcrumb", an ordered list, `aria-current="page"` on the current page: screen readers hear the landmark, how many pages, and which is this one.
- Separators are drawn, not text, so they aren't read.
- An icon link and the "more" button keep a name in visually hidden text; the menu of left-out pages is a Menu (keys, focus, closing).

## Theme obligations

- Links distinguishable from the current page, and a visible focus ring.
- Separators pointing the reading direction.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Collapsing automatically when the trail doesn't fit, outside a Page Header | canon.js, if it comes up (as in a Page Header) |
| A dropdown on each item (siblings of that page) | If it comes up |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** A row the button's height (32 / 40 / 48), no padding at the sides (the trail starts where the page's text does); text 12 / 14 / 16px on 16 / 20 / 24px lines; icons and separators 16 / 20 / 24px, 6 / 8 / 8px from the words.

Links and the "more" button zinc-500 (dark zinc-400); the current page, the separators (Lucide chevron-right) and a home icon (house) quieter, zinc-400 (dark zinc-500). Hover zinc-900 (dark white), focus the button's ring (2px, then 1px blue-600; dark blue-400).

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/command-palette.md

# Command Palette

Tier: **T3** (filtering, the keyboard and the shortcut are canon.js's; without it, offer a link to a search page)

A search box for the whole app: press ⌘K (Ctrl+K), type a few letters, and go to a page or run an action without looking through menus. A shortcut, not the only door: every command must also be reachable another way.

## Elements

```html
<button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral" commandfor="palette" command="show-modal" aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K Control+K">
  <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="search" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="canon-button-label">Search</span>
  <kbd class="canon-kbd" aria-hidden="true">⌘K</kbd>
</button>

<dialog class="canon-command-palette" id="palette" aria-label="Command palette">
  <div class="canon-command-search">
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="search" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <input type="search" aria-label="Search commands and pages" placeholder="Search commands and pages">
  </div>
  <div class="canon-command-list">
    <div class="canon-command-group" aria-labelledby="palette-pages">
      <p class="canon-command-heading" id="palette-pages">Pages</p>
      <a class="canon-command-item" href="/invoices">
        <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="receipt" aria-hidden="true"></span>
        <span class="canon-command-label">Invoices</span>
        <span class="canon-command-hint">Billing</span>
      </a>
    </div>
    <div class="canon-command-group" aria-labelledby="palette-actions">
      <p class="canon-command-heading" id="palette-actions">Actions</p>
      <button type="button" class="canon-command-item">
        <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="plus" aria-hidden="true"></span>
        <span class="canon-command-label">Create invoice</span>
        <kbd class="canon-kbd" aria-hidden="true">N</kbd>
      </button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <footer class="canon-command-footer">…↑ ↓ to move · Enter to run · Esc to close…</footer>
</dialog>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | yes | A Button with `command="show-modal"` naming the palette; its `aria-keyshortcuts` (`Meta+K Control+K`) opens it from anywhere on the page and is heard with the button. A Kbd accessory shows it. |
| `dialog.canon-command-palette` | yes | A modal `<dialog>` with an `id`, named (`aria-label`). |
| `.canon-command-search` | yes | First: an optional icon and the `<input type="search">`, named. canon.js makes it the combobox. |
| `.canon-command-list` | yes | The commands (canon.js gives it `role="listbox"`): items, or groups of them. |
| `.canon-command-group` | no | A group (`role="group"`), named by its `.canon-command-heading`. `data-remote` for the app's own results (below). |
| `.canon-command-item` | yes | A link (it goes) or a `<button type="button">` (it does): an optional icon or Avatar, a `.canon-command-label`, an optional `.canon-command-hint` (where it is: "Billing"), an optional Kbd for its own shortcut (`aria-hidden="true"`). `data-keywords` adds words it matches ("preferences account"); `data-value` is what it returns; `data-keep-open` keeps the palette open after it runs. |
| `.canon-command-empty` | no | What shows when nothing matches; canon.js writes one ("No results for “xyz”") if there is none. |
| `.canon-command-footer` | no | Hints about the keys, after the list. |

- **Not a Menu** (actions from one button, a short fixed list) nor a **Combobox** (a value for a form field): the palette runs commands and goes places.

## Behavior (canon.js)

- **Opening** (the trigger, its shortcut, or `showModal()`): the field is emptied, every item shows, the first is active, focus is in the field. The shortcut pressed again closes it.
- **Typing** narrows the items to those holding every word typed, in any order (in the label, the hint and `data-keywords`; case and accents ignored); the words are marked in the labels (`mark.canon-command-match`). Groups with nothing left hide; with nothing at all, the empty message shows. Screen readers hear how many results there are once typing pauses.
- **Keys:** ↑ ↓ move the active item (`aria-selected`, `aria-activedescendant`, scrolled into view), wrapping at the ends; Enter runs it; Escape closes the palette, and so does a click beside it (canon.js sets `closedby="any"` unless the palette has another `closedby`). The pointer makes an item active as it moves over it, and a click runs it. Focus never leaves the field.
- **Running** an item is a click: a link goes, a button fires its listeners. Then the palette closes (its `returnValue` the item's `data-value`, else its text), unless a listener cancels the click or the item has `data-keep-open`.
- **The app's results:** every change fires **`canon-search`** on the palette (`detail: { query }`, a quarter second after typing stops). Items the app puts in a `data-remote` group show as they are (the app has matched them); canon.js marks their words and keeps the keyboard working as they come and go.

## Accessibility

- A modal dialog holding a combobox (the field) and its listbox (the list) of options in named groups; the active option is the field's `aria-activedescendant`. The shortcut is on the trigger (`aria-keyshortcuts`).
- An item's name is its label and hint; icons and Kbds are hidden.
- The result count is announced after a pause, not on every key.

## Theme obligations

- The active item unmistakable (and in forced colors), the matched words visible in the labels.
- The palette doesn't move as the list narrows (anchored near the top, not centered).
- No motion: opened from the keyboard many times a day, it opens and closes at once.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Steps ("Change theme…" opening a second list, Backspace back) | If it comes up |
| Recent items remembered between visits | The app (it writes them first) |
| Fuzzy matching by letters ("crinv") | If it comes up; words match in any order now |
| A loading line while the app looks up results | With Progress |

## Look

**Sizes:** 640px wide, at most 480px tall, 12% of the window from the top; the search row a control's height + 16px; items a control's height, the list 8px inside.

Dialog's panel (its hairline edge, overlay shadow and backdrop color, unblurred) with 16px corners, opening and closing at once; the search row unframed, 16px type, a hairline rule under it, the icon zinc-500; Menu's items (the active one zinc-100, dark zinc-800; icons zinc-500) and headings (10px semibold capitals); hints zinc-500 after the label; matched words semibold; the empty message centered in zinc-500; the footer's hints 12px zinc-500 under a line. Forced colors: the active item outlined in Highlight.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/menubar.md

# Menubar

Tier: **T1** (each item opens its menu with the browser's popover) · keyboard and moving between menus are **T2** (canon.js)

A row of menus, as at the top of a desktop app: File, Edit, View. For apps whose commands are too many for a toolbar. Each item opens a [Menu](menu.md).

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-menubar" role="menubar" aria-label="Main">
  <button type="button" class="canon-menubar-item" id="file-item" role="menuitem"
          popovertarget="file-menu" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">File</button>
  <button type="button" class="canon-menubar-item" id="edit-item" role="menuitem"
          popovertarget="edit-menu" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">Edit</button>
</div>

<div class="canon-menu" id="file-menu" popover role="menu" aria-labelledby="file-item">…</div>
<div class="canon-menu" id="edit-menu" popover role="menu" aria-labelledby="edit-item">…</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-menubar` | yes | `role="menubar"`, named by `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Only items inside. |
| `.canon-menubar-item` | yes | `<button type="button">` with `role="menuitem"`, its text the name. Opening a menu: `popovertarget` and `aria-haspopup="menu"`; an item without them is an action of its own. |
| Menus | — | [Menu](menu.md)s, outside the bar, each named by its item (`aria-labelledby`). Submenus as in Menu. |

- **Size:** `data-size` on a container around the bar and its menus (the menus aren't inside the bar).
- **Disabled item:** `aria-disabled="true"`; the keyboard skips it.

## Behavior

**The browser (T1):** an item opens and closes its menu; opening one closes the other; clicking outside or Escape closes it.

**canon.js (T2):**

- **One tab stop:** the last item focused (the first, to start). Right and Left move along the bar (wrapping, mirrored in right-to-left), Home and End to its ends.
- **Down, Enter or Space** open an item's menu at its first item; **Up** at its last ([Menu](menu.md)'s keys from there).
- **Across menus:** in an open menu, Right and Left (where they don't open or close a submenu) close it and open the next or previous item's menu, at its first item.
- **Pointer:** while one of the bar's menus is open, pointing at another item opens its menu.
- Escape closes the menu and returns to its item; Tab closes it and leaves the bar.
- The bar's menus get `data-menubar` (themes may open them clear of the bar).

## States

| State | Hook |
|---|---|
| Menu open | `aria-expanded="true"` on the item |
| Keyboard focus | `:focus-visible` on the item |
| Disabled | `aria-disabled="true"` (or `disabled`) |

## Core

- The bar: an inline flex row. Items: a button reset, their own width.

## Accessibility

- `role="menubar"` with `menuitem`s: screen readers announce the bar, the items and their menus (`aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded`). One Tab stop; arrows move inside.
- Use a menubar for app commands. Navigation is a Nav List (links), not a menubar.

## Theme obligations

- The open item held (as pressed), and keyboard focus visible on the bar.
- Menus clear of the bar.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Typing an item's first letter on the bar | If it comes up |
| Shortcuts that open a menu (Alt+F) | The app (`aria-keyshortcuts` on the item) |
| Collapsing into one menu when narrow | Layout: the app shows a Menu button instead |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Items 32 / 40 / 48 tall, padding 8 / 10 / 12, label 4 / 6 / 8 further in, corners 4 / 8 / 12; the bar 4px inside, corners 8 / 12 / 16.

A hairline edge (black at 12%, dark white at 12%) around white (dark zinc-900); items medium zinc-500, the open one zinc-100 (dark zinc-800) with zinc-900 text (dark white). Menus 4px under the bar. Hover and keyboard focus look like the open item; disabled zinc-300 (dark zinc-700).

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/nav-list.md

# Nav List

Tier: **T0** (links and native `<details>`) · opening the current page's section is **T2** (canon.js)

The links of a sidebar: the main way around an app (Inbox, Projects, Settings), or a settings page's sections (Profile, Account, Billing). Navigation: links in lists, with the keyboard of any page.

## Elements

```html
<nav class="canon-nav-list" aria-label="Workspace">
  <ul>
    <li>
      <a class="canon-nav-list-item" href="/inbox" aria-current="page">
        <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="mail" aria-hidden="true"></span>
        <span class="canon-nav-list-label">Inbox</span>
        <span class="canon-count">12</span>
      </a>
    </li>
    <li>
      <details class="canon-nav-list-section">
        <summary class="canon-nav-list-item">…icon… <span class="canon-nav-list-label">Projects</span></summary>
        <ul>
          <li><a class="canon-nav-list-item" href="/projects/website"><span class="canon-nav-list-label">Website</span></a></li>
        </ul>
      </details>
    </li>
  </ul>
  <p class="canon-nav-list-heading">Teams</p>
  <ul>
    <li>
      <a class="canon-nav-list-item" href="/teams/design">…Design…</a>
      <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-intent="neutral" data-display="icon" data-size="sm">…New project in Design…</button>
    </li>
  </ul>
</nav>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `nav.canon-nav-list` | yes | Named (`aria-label`: "Workspace", "Settings"): a navigation landmark. Its children: lists, each optionally after a heading. |
| `.canon-nav-list-heading` | no | Names the group (the list) after it ("Teams"). |
| `<ul>` / `<li>` | yes | Each item an `<li>`: a link, or a section. |
| `a.canon-nav-list-item` | yes | An optional icon (`aria-hidden="true"`) or Avatar, a `.canon-nav-list-label`, an optional [Tag](tag.md) right after it, an optional [Count](count.md) at the end. `aria-current="page"` on the page people are on. |
| `details.canon-nav-list-section` | no | An item with sub-pages: a `summary.canon-nav-list-item` (icon, label) opening the `<ul>` of sub-pages after it. One level deep. |
| Row action | no | A [Button](button.md) after a link, in the same `<li>`: minimal, neutral, icon only, small, named for its row ("New project in Design"). |

- **A tag** ("New", "Beta"): one per item, one word, for a page that is new or changing; its meaning from Tag's `data-intent` (`info` for New). Its text joins the link's name ("Reports, New"). Remove it once it no longer applies; numbers are a Count.
- **Not a Tree View** (files and folders, deep nesting, arrow keys, choosing items), **not a Menu** (actions), **not Tabs** (panels in one page). Never menu or tree roles.
- **[Sidebar](sidebar.md)** is the layout column around it (a brand or workspace switcher above, a footer below); the Nav List is its links.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-current` | an item | `page` | — | — |
| `open` (native) | a section | | closed (canon.js opens the one holding the current page) | — |
| `data-display` | the list or a container | `icon`: a rail; labels, headings, tags and counts hidden visually, kept as names | labels | yes |
| `data-size` | the list or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg`: rows a control's height (a sidebar uses the default; `sm` for a dense one) | theme decides | yes |

- **A rail** (a collapsed sidebar) needs a [Tooltip](tooltip.md) per link (`interestfor` on the link, the tooltip after it in the `<li>`, `data-placement="inline-end"`), so sighted people can read the names. Beside the icon, toward the page: above or below, it would cover the next link, and a rail sits at the window's edge. Tooltips in a Nav List show only in a rail, so a sidebar that collapses keeps them in both states.

## Rail

`data-display="icon"` on the list or a container. There is no room for a section's sub-pages in a rail, so they open beside its icon, over the page, with their labels: a click (or Enter, Space) on the section opens them. One at a time. They close when a page is chosen, on Escape (focus back on the section), and when focus or a click goes elsewhere. No section opens by itself in a rail; the one holding the current page is marked (filled) instead. Becoming a rail closes open sections; leaving it opens the current page's again.

## Behavior

- **The browser (T0):** links go; a section's summary opens and closes it (Enter, Space, a click), announced as expanded or collapsed.
- **canon.js (T2):** the section holding `aria-current="page"` opens, and its summary gets `data-current` (shown while it's closed); again whenever the app moves `aria-current`. In a rail, sections open beside it instead (see Rail), and canon.js follows `data-display` changing (a [Sidebar](sidebar.md) collapsing).
- A row's action shows while the pointer is on its row or focus is in it (always where there is no hover), and is a Tab stop of its own.

## Accessibility

- A named navigation landmark of lists of links; headings name their groups. The current page is `aria-current="page"`, heard as "current page".
- Tab and Shift+Tab move through it like the rest of the page; no arrow keys to learn.
- In a rail, the labels stay as the links' names; tooltips show them on hover and focus.

## Theme obligations

- The current page unmistakable (a filled row); hover clearly lighter.
- A section reads as opening (a chevron that turns); its sub-pages line up under its label.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left, icons are on the right and a closed section's chevron points left.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| The sidebar around it (brand, footer, collapsing to a rail) | [Sidebar](sidebar.md) |
| Reordering items by dragging, favorites | The app |
| Deeper nesting | Tree View |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Rows a control's height (32 / 40 / 48), the icon as far from the edge as from the top (10px at md), Button's corners, a quarter of their height apart (10px at md); icons Button's icon-to-label space before the label (6 / 8 / 8); sub-pages start where the labels do, half a row less 8px apart and from the rows around them (8 / 12 / 16); groups 16px apart; a rail's items square.

Labels regular zinc-900 (dark white), icons zinc-500 (dark white); hover zinc-50 (dark zinc-800 at 50%); the current page zinc-100 (dark zinc-700) with a medium label. A tag after the label at Tag's small size (20px tall at every size). Counts a quiet zinc-500 number (not Count's pill). Headings Menu's. A section's chevron zinc-500 at its end, pointing to the end while closed and down while open (the common sidebar convention). In a rail, a section's sub-pages in Menu's panel, 16px out. A row's action a minimal neutral Button. Focus: the button's ring.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/pagination.md

# Pagination

Tier: **T0** (written links) · drawn from a page count, fitting, rows per page and jump in place are **T2** (canon.js)

Moving through a long list a page at a time: numbered pages, a compact "Page 2 of 30", or a table footer with rows per page. For feeds, [Load more](#load-more) is in this spec too.

## Elements

```html
<nav class="canon-pagination" aria-label="Pagination">
  <ol>
    <li><a class="canon-pagination-prev" href="?page=1" rel="prev">
      <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="chevron-left" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="canon-pagination-label">Previous</span>
    </a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=1" aria-label="Page 1">1</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=2" aria-label="Page 2" aria-current="page">2</a></li>
    <li><a href="?page=3" aria-label="Page 3">3</a></li>
    <li class="canon-pagination-gap">…</li>
    <li><a href="?page=30" aria-label="Page 30">30</a></li>
    <li><a class="canon-pagination-next" href="?page=3" rel="next">
      <span class="canon-pagination-label">Next</span>
      <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="chevron-right" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    </a></li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `nav.canon-pagination` | yes | Named "Pagination" (`aria-label`, in the page's language): a navigation landmark. |
| `<ol>` | yes | The controls in order, each in an `<li>`. Drawn by canon.js with `data-pages` (below). |
| A page | yes | `<a href>` (or a `<button type="button">` in an app), its number as text, `aria-label` "Page 3" recommended. The current page `aria-current="page"`. |
| `.canon-pagination-prev`, `.canon-pagination-next` | yes | A link (`rel="prev"` / `rel="next"`) with an icon (`chevron-left`, `chevron-right`) and its words in `.canon-pagination-label`. The icon goes on the outer side: before "Previous", after "Next". |
| `.canon-pagination-first`, `.canon-pagination-last` | no | The same, to the ends of the list (`chevrons-left`, `chevrons-right`), outside Previous and Next. |
| `.canon-pagination-gap` | no | An `<li>` where pages are left out ("…"). Not a control. |
| `.canon-pagination-current` | no | "Page 2 of 30" between the arrows, in place of the pages (compact). |
| `.canon-pagination-summary` | no | Before the list: "1–10 of 300". |
| `.canon-pagination-size` | no | Before the list: a `<label>` and a [Select](select.md) of rows per page. |
| `.canon-pagination-jump` | no | After the list: a `<form>` with a `<label>` ("Go to page") and a [Text Input](text-input.md) `type="number"` named `page`. |

- **Nowhere to go:** on the first page, Previous (and First) is a link without `href`, `aria-disabled="true"` (a disabled `<button>` in an app); on the last page, Next and Last. They stay, so the row doesn't move.
- **Which pages to show** is the author's when writing them: the first and last, a few around the current one, gaps between. canon.js draws the same with `data-pages`.
- **Table footer:** a summary or rows-per-page select before the list sends the list to the far end of the row; the row wraps when narrow.
- **Not tabs, not steps:** pages are the same list cut in parts. Views of different content are Tabs; a sequence to complete is Steps.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-pages` | the pagination | the page count: canon.js draws the list | — | no |
| `data-total`, `data-per-page` | the pagination | rows in all, rows per page: canon.js counts the pages and writes the summary | —, 10 | no |
| `data-page` | the pagination | the current page | 1 | no |
| `data-siblings` | the pagination | pages shown on each side of the current one | 1 | no |
| `data-ends` | the pagination | (present) First and Last | — | no |
| `data-href` | the pagination | a link pattern, `{page}` and `{per-page}` filled in (`?page={page}`) | absent: buttons | no |
| `data-layout` | the pagination | `compact`: "Page 2 of 30" always | — | no |
| `data-display` | the pagination, an arrow or a container | `icon`: arrows only · `label`: their words too | theme decides | yes |
| `data-size` | the pagination or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |

## Behavior

**T0:** links. The jump form is a plain `GET` form: Enter sends `?page=12` to the page's address (the browser checks `min` and `max`).

**canon.js (T2), with `data-pages` or `data-total`:**

- **Draws the list:** First (with `data-ends`), Previous, the first and last pages, `data-siblings` pages around the current one, gaps, Next, Last. Always `siblings × 2 + 5` pages and gaps (or all the pages when there are fewer), so the arrows don't move from page to page. Numbers in the page's language: page numbers without thousands separators (page 12480, a name), counts of rows with them ("9,871–9,880 of 124,800"); arrows named "Previous", "Next", "First page", "Last page", pages "Page 3" (strings `pagination-*`).
- **Fits:** when the list doesn't fit on one row, fewer pages around the current one, then "Page 2 of 30". Again on each resize.
- **Links or buttons:** with `data-href` the pages are links to the pattern. Without it they are buttons: a press fires **`canon-page`** on the pagination (`detail: { page, perPage }`, bubbling, cancelable); unless cancelled, `data-page` changes and the list is drawn again. The app shows that page's rows. Focus stays on the control pressed (on the current page when it can go no further), and the new page is announced ("Page 3 of 30", or the summary).
- **The app moves it** by setting `data-page` (or `data-pages`, `data-total`, `data-per-page`); the list follows.
- **Summary:** with `data-total`, canon.js writes "1–10 of 300" into `.canon-pagination-summary`.
- **Rows per page:** a change to the select sets `data-per-page` (through `canon-page`, or the link pattern's `{per-page}`), keeping the first row shown in view (from page 3 of 10 rows, rows 21–30, to page 1 of 25).
- **Jump:** the form goes to the page (through `canon-page` or the link pattern); canon.js sets the field's `min` and `max`, so a page out of range gets the browser's message.

## Load more

```html
<ul>…the first 20 results…</ul>
<div class="canon-load-more" data-shown="20" data-total="300">
  <p class="canon-load-more-status">Showing 20 of 300</p>
  <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral"><span class="canon-button-label">Load more</span></button>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-load-more` | yes | Under the list it adds to. |
| `.canon-load-more-status` | no | How many are shown. With `data-shown` and `data-total`, canon.js writes it ("Showing 20 of 300", string `load-more-status`) and makes it a polite status. |
| A [Button](button.md) | yes | `<button type="button">`; or, without canon.js, a link to the next page (`<a class="canon-button" href="?page=2">`). |

| Attribute | On | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data-shown`, `data-total` | the box | numbers | — |
| `data-auto` | the box | (present) load on scrolling near the button | — |

**canon.js (T2):**

- A press fires **`canon-load-more`** on the box (bubbling) and makes the button busy (`aria-busy`, `aria-disabled`: Button's loading state).
- The app adds the rows, then sets `data-shown`: the button is ready again, the status updates. At `data-total` the button goes (focus on it moves to the status). On failure the app removes `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` itself.
- **`data-auto`** (infinite scroll): the button loads by itself as it comes within 400px of view, and again while the list is still too short to push it away. The button stays: the way in for keyboards, and what a screen reader finds.
- A link is left to the browser.

## States

| State | Hook |
|---|---|
| Current page | `aria-current="page"` |
| Nowhere to go | `a:not([href])` (`aria-disabled="true"`), `button:disabled` |
| Focus | `:focus-visible` |
| Loading more | `aria-busy="true"` on the Button |

## Core

- The nav: a wrapping flex row. The list: a wrapping flex row, no markers or indent; after a summary or select it takes `margin-inline-start: auto`. Pages and arrows: inline flex, at least the control's height square, tabular figures, link and button styles reset. The arrows' icons mirror in right-to-left.
- Load more: a centered column.

## Accessibility

- A `<nav>` named "Pagination" around a list: screen readers hear the landmark and how many items.
- The current page is `aria-current="page"`; pages named "Page 3", arrows by their words (visually hidden with `data-display="icon"`).
- Arrows with nowhere to go stay, unavailable, so the layout and the reading order don't change; gaps are text, not controls.
- Buttons keep focus where it was and announce the new page; content changes are the app's to manage.
- Load more keeps a button even with `data-auto`, and announces the new count.

## Theme obligations

- The current page distinguishable from the other pages without color alone; a visible focus ring; unavailable arrows visibly so.
- Arrows pointing the reading direction.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A gap that opens a jump field or the pages it hides | If it comes up (Breadcrumb's "more" menu is the model) |
| Cursor paging (no total: Previous and Next only) | Written today (two arrows); a drawn variant if it comes up |
| Updating the address in a button app (`history.pushState`) | The app's (on `canon-page`) |
| Dots for a carousel | Carousel |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Squares 32 / 40 / 48 (wider for long numbers), 8px apart; Button's type (12 / 14 / 16px medium) and corners (4 / 8 / 12); icons 16 / 20 / 24. The summary, select and jump field 16px from the list. Load more: the status a field step (12 / 16 / 20) above the Button.

Numbers zinc-900 (dark white), arrows zinc-500 (dark zinc-300), the gap Lucide ellipsis in zinc-400; the current page framed zinc-200 (dark zinc-700), no fill. Arrows icons only by default. Hover zinc-100 (dark zinc-800), pressed zinc-200 (dark zinc-700), focus Button's ring; unavailable arrows zinc-300 (dark zinc-600); "Page 2 of 30" Text Input's type in zinc-900; the summary and the labels zinc-500 (dark zinc-400); First and Last Lucide chevrons-left / chevrons-right; the jump field as wide as its number, centered, without spin buttons.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/tabs.md

# Tabs

Tier: **T0** (links) · in-page tabs and folding are **T2** (canon.js)

The parts of one page or record, one shown at a time: a record's Overview, Payments and Activity; a settings page's General, Billing and Members. Under a [Page Header](page-header.md), in the page.

## Elements

In-page, a tablist and its panels:

```html
<div class="canon-tabs">
  <div class="canon-tabs-list" role="tablist" aria-label="Invoice INV-2041">
    <button type="button" class="canon-tab" role="tab" id="tab-overview" aria-controls="overview" aria-selected="true">
      <span class="canon-tab-label">Overview</span>
    </button>
    <button type="button" class="canon-tab" role="tab" id="tab-activity" aria-controls="activity" aria-selected="false" tabindex="-1">
      <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="list" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="canon-tab-label">Activity</span>
      <span class="canon-count">14<span class="canon-visually-hidden"> new</span></span>
    </button>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-tabs-panel" role="tabpanel" id="overview" aria-labelledby="tab-overview" tabindex="0">…</div>
  <div class="canon-tabs-panel" role="tabpanel" id="activity" aria-labelledby="tab-activity" tabindex="0" hidden>…</div>
</div>
```

Links, each part its own page:

```html
<nav class="canon-tabs-list" aria-label="Invoice INV-2041">
  <a class="canon-tab" href="/invoices/2041"><span class="canon-tab-label">Overview</span></a>
  <a class="canon-tab" href="/invoices/2041/activity" aria-current="page"><span class="canon-tab-label">Activity</span></a>
</nav>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-tabs` | in-page | Around the strip (first) and its panels. |
| `.canon-tabs-list` | yes | The strip, named (`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`): `role="tablist"` in-page, a `<nav>` for links. Two or more tabs, its only children. |
| `.canon-tab` | yes | In-page: a `<button type="button" role="tab">` with an `id`, `aria-controls` its panel and `aria-selected`; the chosen one `aria-selected="true"`, the others `tabindex="-1"`. Links: an `<a href>`, the current one `aria-current="page"`, no tab roles. |
| `.canon-icon` | no | Before the text, `aria-hidden="true"`. |
| `.canon-tab-label` | yes | The tab's text, also when only the icon shows (it stays as the tab's name). |
| [Count](count.md) | no | After the text: how many in that part, with what it counts visually hidden ("14 new"). |
| `.canon-tabs-panel` | in-page | One per tab: `role="tabpanel"`, its `id`, `aria-labelledby` its tab, `tabindex="0"`; all but the chosen one `hidden`. |

- **In-page or links?** Links when each part has its own address (it can be bookmarked, shared, reloaded) or loads separately. In-page when the parts are already on the page and switching is instant.
- **Not a Segmented Control:** both are "one of these", but a Segmented Control sets a value (a form value, the same content seen differently), while Tabs show a different part. In Canon they share the raised card on a track; Tabs are told apart by what they carry (icons, counts) and where they sit (heading a page's parts).
- **Not a Nav List:** Tabs are the parts of one thing; the app's places are its [Sidebar](sidebar.md).

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-fill` | the strip | present: the tabs share its width equally | absent: each as wide as its text, from the start | no |
| `data-size` | the strip or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |
| `data-display` | the strip or a container | `icon`: the text hidden, square tabs | theme decides | yes |
| `aria-disabled` | an in-page tab | `true`: not available yet, still announced | — | — |

## Core

- The strip is one row that never wraps, at most its place's width (a theme may draw it as wide as its tabs); the tabs are as wide as their text (`data-fill`: the strip's full width, the tabs equal, cutting their text with … when narrow).
- Without JavaScript, in-page tabs can't switch: the strip doesn't show and every panel does, one after the other. Links work as links.

## Behavior (T2, canon.js)

- **Choosing (in-page):** a click, or the arrow keys moving and choosing at once (Left and Right, mirrored in right-to-left; Home and End to the ends; wrapping; skipping `aria-disabled` tabs). The chosen tab is the strip's one Tab stop; Tab goes on to its panel. Its panel shows, the others are `hidden`; canon.js makes them `hidden="until-found"` where the browser has it, so find in page reaches their text and chooses the tab it's in. `canon-tab` fires on `.canon-tabs` (`detail.tab`, `detail.panel`), for an app that loads a part when it's first shown.
- **Folding:** tabs that don't fit go into a **More** menu at the strip's end, from the last, one at a time; the current tab never folds. Choosing one from the menu shows it (it takes a place in the strip, another folding instead) and focuses it; for links, the menu's items are the links. One at a time rather than all at once, so as many parts as fit stay one click away. The More button is in the `<nav>` for links; beside the tablist for in-page tabs (a tablist may only hold tabs), over the strip's end, which keeps room for it (`--canon-tabs-more-size`).
- Folded tabs get `data-folded`, the strip `data-fold`.

## Accessibility

- In-page: heard as "Activity, tab, 3 of 5, selected", then the panel, named by its tab. The arrows move between tabs; Tab goes to the panel.
- Links: a named navigation landmark; the current part heard as "current page".
- A Count reads with its tab ("Activity, 14 new").
- Folded, every tab keeps its name, as an item of the More menu ("More", `--canon-text-more`).
- A disabled tab stays in the strip and is announced as unavailable; it is skipped by the arrows.

## Theme obligations

- The current tab unmistakable, by more than color; hover clearly weaker.
- Focus visible on the tab, over its neighbours; on a panel too.
- In forced colors, the current tab still shows.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the tabs run from the right.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| The chosen tab in the address (`#activity`) | The app, on `canon-tab`; or links |
| Vertical tabs | If it comes up (a Nav List may fit better) |
| Closing or reordering tabs | Not for parts of one thing |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** The strip 32 / 40 / 48 tall with 3px inside and 2px between tabs, its corners Button's plus 2px (6 / 10 / 14); tabs 26 / 34 / 42, corners 3px tighter, padded 8 / 10 / 12, set as a button (12 / 14 / 16px medium); icon, text and count 6px apart; icon only, square. The panel 12 / 16 / 20 under the strip.

A raised card on a track: a zinc-100 strip (dark zinc-800) as wide as its tabs (the full width with `data-fill`, and while tabs fold into More, so More sits at its end). Tabs zinc-500 (dark zinc-400); hover darkens the text to zinc-950 (dark white), pressing adds zinc-200 at 60% (dark zinc-700 at 60%). The current tab a white card (dark zinc-700) lifted by a ring of black at 6% (dark white at 6%) and a soft shadow, zinc-950 (dark white). A Count in a tab is neutral: zinc-200 with zinc-600 text (dark zinc-700, zinc-300), on the current tab zinc-900 with white (dark the reverse). Disabled zinc-400 (dark zinc-600). The More button one more tab at the end, with a chevron. The current card is drawn once by the strip and anchored to the current tab, so it glides to the tab chosen (0.3s, fast then settling; none with reduced motion); without anchor positioning, and in forced colors, each tab draws its own. Focus: the button's ring. Forced colors: the current tab in Highlight.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/dialog.md

# Dialog

Tier: **T1** (a native modal `<dialog>` opened by an invoker command: it traps focus, closes on Escape and returns focus without JavaScript) · polyfills and initial focus are **T2** (canon.js)

A task over the page that has to be finished or dismissed before going on: editing an event, confirming a deletion. Modal: the page behind can't be used. For a short task beside a button that leaves the page usable, a [Popover](popover.md).

## Elements

```html
<button type="button" class="canon-button" commandfor="edit-event" command="show-modal">…Edit event…</button>

<dialog class="canon-dialog" id="edit-event" aria-labelledby="edit-event-title">
  <form method="dialog">
    <header class="canon-dialog-header">
      <h2 class="canon-dialog-title" id="edit-event-title">Edit event</h2>
      <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-intent="neutral" data-display="icon" commandfor="edit-event" command="close">
        <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="close" aria-hidden="true"></span>
        <span class="canon-button-label">Close</span>
      </button>
    </header>
    <div class="canon-dialog-body">
      <div class="canon-dialog-section">…fields…</div>
      <div class="canon-dialog-section">…fields…</div>
    </div>
    <footer class="canon-dialog-footer">
      <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral" commandfor="edit-event" command="close">…Cancel…</button>
      <button type="submit" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="high" data-align="end" value="save">…Save…</button>
    </footer>
  </form>
</dialog>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | yes | A `<button>` with `commandfor` (the dialog's id) and `command="show-modal"`. |
| `dialog.canon-dialog` | yes | An `id`, named by its title (`aria-labelledby`) or `aria-label`. Never written `open`: it opens modal. Anywhere in the page (it is shown over everything). |
| `form` | no | Around the parts, taking no place: `method="dialog"` closes the dialog on submit (its `returnValue` is the submit button's `value`); the app's own form submits as usual. |
| `.canon-dialog-header` | yes | The title and an optional close button (an icon-only minimal neutral [Button](button.md) with `command="close"`, named "Close") at the end. Only these: what the dialog says goes in the body. |
| `.canon-dialog-title` | yes | A heading at the page's level (usually `<h2>`). |
| `.canon-dialog-body` | no | The content: a message, fields. It scrolls when the dialog is taller than the window; header and footer stay. |
| `.canon-dialog-section` | no | In the body: parts of the content, edge to edge, with a line between. |
| `.canon-dialog-footer` | no | Buttons (a Split Button, a Link, a Checkbox, a short text also fit). `data-align="end"` on an item sends it and what follows to the far end: Cancel at the start, Save at the end. |

- **Closing:** a button with `command="close"` (or `request-close`, which lets the app cancel it), a `method="dialog"` form's submit, Escape. Focus goes back to the button that opened it.
- **Alert dialog:** `role="alertdialog"` for a decision that interrupts ("Delete Hackweek?"): the question in the title, its consequence in the body (a paragraph the dialog points at with `aria-describedby`), no close button; the footer's buttons are the answers, a destructive one saying what it does with `data-intent="danger"`. Put `autofocus` on the safe answer.
- **Not for** messages that don't need an answer (a Toast), short tasks beside a button (a Popover), or long flows (a page).

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `role` | the dialog | `alertdialog` | dialog | — |
| `closedby` (native) | the dialog | `any`: also a click beside it closes it (never an alert dialog) · `closerequest`: Escape · `none`: only its buttons | `closerequest` | — |
| `data-width` | the dialog | `sm` (a question) · `lg` (a table, a preview) | the theme's (a form) | no |
| `autofocus` (native) | a control inside | where focus starts | the body's first control | — |
| `data-size` | the dialog or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg`: the controls inside | theme decides | yes |

## Behavior

**The browser (T1):** `show-modal` opens it in the top layer over a backdrop; the page behind is inert; focus moves in and stays; Escape (and, with `closedby="any"`, a click beside it) closes it; focus returns to the opener.

**canon.js (T2):**

- **Focus starts in the content:** to the `[autofocus]` element, else the body's first control, else the dialog itself, not the header's close button.
- **Polyfills** where the browser lacks them: the dialog commands (`show-modal`, `close`, `request-close`) and `closedby` (`any`: a click on the backdrop closes it; `none`: Escape doesn't).

## Core

- Centered, as wide as `--canon-dialog-width` (`sm` 25rem, the default 40rem, `lg` 56rem) and at most the window less 1rem each side, as tall as its content and at most the window less 1rem each side: a column of header, body and footer where only the body scrolls.
- While a dialog is open the page doesn't scroll (`html:has(.canon-dialog:modal)`).

## Accessibility

- A modal dialog (or alert dialog), named by its title; an alert dialog also described by its message. Screen readers announce it on opening.
- The close button is named ("Close"); Escape always works unless `closedby="none"`, in which case the footer must offer a way out.
- Focus starts in the content (a field to fill, or the safe answer), stays inside, and returns to the opener.

## Theme obligations

- The dialog stands apart from the page (the backdrop) and from what's behind it (its edge).
- Header and footer stay put while the body scrolls, and read as parts of the dialog (lines or space).
- Opening and closing motion stops with reduced motion.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the close button is on the left and the footer runs from the right.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A panel from the side or the bottom | [Drawer](drawer.md): this Dialog with `data-side` |
| Steps inside a dialog | Wizard (pattern) |
| A non-modal dialog | [Popover](popover.md) |
| Full-screen dialogs on phones | If it comes up (`data-width="full"`) |
| Asking before closing a dialog with unsaved changes | The app, from `cancel` / `request-close` |

## Look

**Sizes:** Widths 400 / 640 / 896 (`sm`, default, `lg`); 24px corners; header 72px (16 / 16 / 16 / 24 inside), footer 88px (24 inside), body and sections 24 inside, their content 24 apart.

White (dark zinc-900), no frame: a hairline edge (black at 12%, dark white at 12%) and the overlay shadow (0 24px 48px −12px at 18%, 0 4px 12px at 6%; dark 60% and 30%); the page behind white at 85% (dark zinc-950 at 75%) blurred 4px. The title 16px semibold zinc-900 (dark white); the close button a minimal neutral Button (zinc-500 icon); hairline rules (black at 10%, dark white at 10%) under the header, between sections and over the footer, that take no height; footer buttons 12px apart; Cancel a low neutral Button. The widths `sm` and `lg`; opening, it fades in from 98% and the backdrop fades (0.15s); with reduced motion they only fade.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/drawer.md

# Drawer

Tier: **T1** (a [Dialog](dialog.md): a native modal `<dialog>`) · polyfills and initial focus are **T2** (canon.js, as for Dialog)

A Dialog that slides in from the side of the window: filters or a record's details, the app's navigation on a phone. Other systems split it into a drawer (navigation) and a side sheet (content); in Canon both are a Drawer. Modal, like a dialog: the page behind waits.

## Elements

```html
<button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral" commandfor="filters" command="show-modal">…Filters…</button>

<dialog class="canon-dialog" id="filters" data-side="end" aria-labelledby="filters-title">
  <form method="dialog">
    <header class="canon-dialog-header">
      <h2 class="canon-dialog-title" id="filters-title">Filters</h2>
      <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="minimal" data-intent="neutral" data-display="icon" commandfor="filters" command="close">…Close…</button>
    </header>
    <div class="canon-dialog-body">…</div>
    <footer class="canon-dialog-footer">
      <button type="reset" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral">…Reset…</button>
      <button type="submit" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="high" data-align="end">…Show 24 jobs…</button>
    </footer>
  </form>
</dialog>
```

A Drawer is a [Dialog](dialog.md) with `data-side`: the same element, parts, opening, closing (Escape, `command="close"`, `closedby`), focus and naming. Everything in Dialog's spec applies; this page lists what differs.

- **`end`** (the default choice): content about what's on the page (filters, details, an edit form).
- **`start`**: the app's navigation on a small screen, opened by a menu button; the body can be a `<nav>` (`class="canon-dialog-body"`, named).
- **Not a Drawer:** a panel that stays beside the content while people keep working (Sidebar, Split Pane); a decision (an alert dialog is centered: `role="alertdialog"` doesn't take `data-side`).
- `closedby="any"` suits drawers that only show or filter (a click beside them closes them); a form with unsaved input keeps the default.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-side` | the dialog | `start` · `end` (logical: `end` is the right in left-to-right text, the left in right-to-left) | — (a centered Dialog) | no |
| `data-width` | a drawer | `sm` (navigation) · `lg` (details) | the theme's (filters, a form) | no |

Dialog's other attributes (`closedby`, `autofocus`, `data-size`) apply as they are.

## Core

- At its edge, `--canon-drawer-inset` (the theme's) away from the window's top, side and bottom; the window's height less that; `--canon-drawer-width` wide (`sm` 20rem, the default 30rem, `lg` 40rem), at most the window less 3rem so the page shows beside it.
- Header, body and footer as in a Dialog: only the body scrolls; with a footer, it stays at the bottom of the drawer.

## Accessibility

As a Dialog: a modal dialog named by its title, focus inside from the content's first control, Escape to close, focus back to the opener. A navigation drawer's links are in a named `<nav>`.

## Theme obligations

- The drawer reads as belonging to its edge, and slides from it (none with reduced motion).
- Use logical properties: `start` and `end` follow the text's direction, the slide too.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A panel from the bottom (a bottom sheet, for phones) | If it comes up (`data-side="bottom"`, with dragging to dismiss) |
| A non-modal panel beside the content | Sidebar, Split Pane |

## Look

**Sizes:** 320 / 480 / 640 wide (`sm`, default, `lg`), 8px from the window's top, side and bottom; Dialog's header (72px), body and footer (88px).

Dialog's panel as it is (white, dark zinc-900; the hairline edge and the overlay shadow; 24px corners all round) floating 8px in from its edge; Dialog's backdrop. It slides in from its edge in 0.25s (ease-out) and back out; none with reduced motion.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/menu.md

# Menu

Tier: **T1** (a native popover: it opens, closes and anchors without JavaScript) · keyboard, submenu hover, checks and context menus are **T2** (canon.js)

A list of actions that opens from a button, or where people right-click: commands, settings to turn on and off, a choice among a few. The menu is a `popover` with `role="menu"`; its items are buttons (or links) with menu item roles.

## Elements

```html
<button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral" id="options-trigger"
        popovertarget="options" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="false">
  <span class="canon-button-label">Options</span>
</button>

<div class="canon-menu" id="options" popover role="menu" aria-labelledby="options-trigger">
  <button type="button" class="canon-menu-item" role="menuitem" aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+R">
    <span class="canon-menu-label">Reload</span>
    <kbd class="canon-kbd" aria-hidden="true">⌘R</kbd>
  </button>
  <button type="button" class="canon-menu-item" role="menuitem" popovertarget="tools" aria-haspopup="menu">
    <span class="canon-menu-label">More tools</span>
  </button>
  <hr class="canon-separator">
  <button type="button" class="canon-menu-item" role="menuitemcheckbox" aria-checked="true">
    <span class="canon-menu-label">Show bookmarks</span>
  </button>
  <hr class="canon-separator">
  <div class="canon-menu-group" role="group" aria-labelledby="options-people">
    <div class="canon-menu-heading" id="options-people">People</div>
    <button type="button" class="canon-menu-item" role="menuitem">
      <span class="canon-avatar">…</span>
      <span class="canon-menu-label">Pedro Duarte</span>
    </button>
  </div>
  <hr class="canon-separator">
  <button type="button" class="canon-menu-item" role="menuitem" data-intent="danger">
    <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="trash" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="canon-menu-label">Delete</span>
  </button>
</div>

<div class="canon-menu" id="tools" popover role="menu" aria-label="More tools">…</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | yes (or a context menu region) | A [Button](button.md) with `popovertarget` (the menu's id) and `aria-haspopup="menu"`. Its menu arrow is the theme's (Button's indicator rule). |
| `.canon-menu` | yes | `popover` (auto), `role="menu"`, an `id`, named by `aria-labelledby` (its button) or `aria-label`. Anywhere in the page; the browser lays it over everything (top layer). |
| `.canon-menu-item` | yes | `<button type="button">` (or `<a href>` for a link) with `role="menuitem"`, `"menuitemcheckbox"` or `"menuitemradio"`. Holds a `.canon-menu-label`; before it an optional `canon-icon` or `canon-avatar`; after it an optional `canon-kbd` (`aria-hidden="true"`, with `aria-keyshortcuts` on the item). |
| `.canon-menu-label` | yes | The item's words. |
| `<hr class="canon-separator">` | no | A [Separator](separator.md). |
| `.canon-menu-group` | no | `role="group"` named by a `.canon-menu-heading` (`aria-labelledby`): a set of items under a heading. Radio items are one choice per group. |
| A submenu | no | Its own `.canon-menu`, outside the menu (after it), opened by an item with `popovertarget` and `aria-haspopup="menu"`, named by `aria-label`. |

- **Drawn by the theme, never written:** the check of a checked item (from `aria-checked`), the arrow of an item that opens a submenu (from `aria-haspopup`), the trigger's menu arrow.
- **Disabled:** `aria-disabled="true"`. The item stays in the menu for screen readers but is skipped by the keyboard and does nothing.
- **Destructive:** `data-intent="danger"`.
- **Size:** `data-size` on the menu, or on a container around the trigger and the menu (the menu isn't inside its trigger, so the button's own `data-size` doesn't reach it).

### A context menu

```html
<div data-contextmenu="edit-menu">…</div>
<div class="canon-menu" id="edit-menu" popover role="menu" aria-label="Edit">…</div>
```

`data-contextmenu` on any element names a menu that opens where it is right-clicked (or long-pressed, where touch screens send a context menu event), or from the keyboard (the context menu key, Shift+F10) under the focused element. Without canon.js the browser's own menu shows.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-checked` | menuitemcheckbox, menuitemradio | `true` · `false` | — (required) | — |
| `aria-disabled` | an item | `true` | — | — |
| `data-intent` | an item | `danger` | neutral | no |
| `data-contextmenu` | any element | a menu's id | — | no |
| `data-size` | the menu or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` (xs is sm, xl and 2xl are lg) | theme decides | yes |

## Behavior

**The browser (T1):** the button opens and closes the menu; it opens under the button, from its start, and flips to fit; clicking outside or Escape closes it (Escape closes a submenu first); opening another menu closes the first. A submenu item opens its submenu.

**canon.js (T2):**

- **Focus:** opened from the keyboard (Enter, Space, Down), the first item; Up, the last; opened with a pointer, the menu itself (the keyboard then starts from there). Closing returns focus to the trigger.
- **Keys:** Down and Up move through the items (wrapping, skipping disabled ones); Home and End to the ends; typing jumps to the next item whose label starts with what was typed; Right opens a submenu at its first item and Left closes it (mirrored in right-to-left); Tab closes the menu and moves on from the trigger.
- **Pointer:** the item under the pointer is where the keyboard is; resting on an item with a submenu opens it after a moment, resting on another item closes it. Moving into an open submenu keeps it open.
- **Choosing an item closes the whole menu**, after the click's listeners ran; a listener that calls `preventDefault()` keeps it open. Clicking an item with a submenu only opens it.
- **Checks:** a `menuitemcheckbox` flips `aria-checked`, a `menuitemradio` becomes the checked one of its group (or of the menu), before the click's listeners run, so they read the new state.
- **Submenus** get `data-submenu` and open beside their item; a [Menubar](menubar.md)'s menus get `data-menubar`, a [Split Button](split-button.md)'s `data-split-button`.
- **Long menus** scroll in the room they have; one cut short opens towards the side with more room, and the keyboard keeps its item in view.
- **Context menus** open at the pointer (once the button is released), kept inside the window.
- Triggers get `aria-expanded`. Several triggers can share one menu (a row's actions in every row): the one that opened it is its trigger (marked expanded, anchoring it, getting focus back); closing marks them all collapsed.
- A `popover="manual"` menu (one always shown, as in documentation) is left alone.

## States

| State | Hook |
|---|---|
| The keyboard's place / hover | `:focus` on the item |
| Submenu open | `aria-expanded="true"` on its item |
| Checked | `aria-checked="true"` |
| Disabled | `aria-disabled="true"` (or `disabled`) |
| Open | `:popover-open` on the menu, `aria-expanded="true"` on the trigger |

## Core

- The menu: anchored to its trigger (`position-area: self-block-end span-self-inline-end`, flipping), a scrolling column at most as tall as its room. A submenu (`data-submenu`): `self-inline-end span-self-block-end`.
- Items: a flex row, full width, the label taking the room, everything else its own size.

## Accessibility

- `role="menu"` with menu items: screen readers announce the menu, the item count and position, checked states and submenus. The trigger's `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded` say what it opens and whether it is open.
- One tab stop: Tab leaves the menu (and closes it); arrows move inside.
- A shortcut is said once, from the item's `aria-keyshortcuts`; the Kbd is hidden.
- A disabled item is still announced (`aria-disabled`), so people know it exists.
- Use menus for actions. Navigation between pages is a nav list or links; a form value is a Select or Combobox.

## Theme obligations

- The keyboard's place clearly marked, and the same as hover.
- Checks and submenu arrows drawn from `aria-checked` and `aria-haspopup`, mirrored in right-to-left where they point.
- Destructive items and disabled items distinguishable by more than color where the system allows.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Items with a second line (description) | If it comes up |
| Search inside a menu | Command Palette |
| Opening and closing animation | The theme |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Items 32 / 40 / 48 tall, padding 8 / 10 / 12, label 4 / 6 / 8 further in, corners 4 / 8 / 12; the panel's corners 8 / 12 / 16, 4px inside; separators [Separator](separator.md)'s (12 / 16 / 20px rows); avatars 24 / 32 / 40.

Select's list (white, dark zinc-900; no frame: a hairline edge (black at 12%, dark white at 12%) and the floating shadow), 4px under the trigger and 4px before it (the items' text lines up with the trigger's), at least the trigger's width + 8 and 8rem. Text zinc-900 (dark white), icons and submenu arrows zinc-500 (dark zinc-400); checked items medium with a check in the text color; the heading 10px semibold capitals in zinc-500 (dark zinc-400); shortcuts are Kbd at its smallest, tinted from the item's text; destructive red-700 (dark red-300), icon too; disabled zinc-400 (dark zinc-600). A submenu sits 4px over the menu's edge, its first item level with its item. Hover and the keyboard's place zinc-100 (dark zinc-800, the open item's fill), destructive on a red tint (Select's); long menus scroll.

**Motion:** opening, it fades in from 97% (0.15s); closing, it fades out where it is (0.1s). With reduced motion it only fades.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/popover.md

# Popover

Tier: **T1** (a native popover: it opens, anchors and dismisses without JavaScript) · focus handling is **T2** (canon.js)

A panel a button opens over the page, for a short task beside it: editing a link, picking a color, a few words of help. Non-modal: the page stays usable around it.

## Elements

```html
<button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral" popovertarget="link-editor" aria-expanded="false">
  <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="link" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="canon-button-label">Link</span>
</button>

<div class="canon-popover" id="link-editor" popover role="dialog" aria-labelledby="link-editor-title">
  <h3 class="canon-popover-title" id="link-editor-title">Edit link</h3>
  <form class="canon-form">
    <div class="canon-field">… Link (type="url") …</div>
    <div class="canon-form-actions">
      <button type="submit" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="high">…Apply…</button>
      <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="low" data-intent="neutral" popovertarget="link-editor" popovertargetaction="hide">…Cancel…</button>
    </div>
  </form>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | yes | A [Button](button.md) with `popovertarget` (the popover's id). |
| `.canon-popover` | yes | `popover` (auto), `role="dialog"`, an `id`, named by its title (`aria-labelledby`) or `aria-label`. Anywhere in the page (it is laid over everything); right after its button keeps the reading and tab order natural. |
| `.canon-popover-title` | no | A heading at the page's level. |
| Content | yes | Anything: a [form](form-layout.md) with its actions, [Swatches](swatches.md) or other choices, a few words and a link. |

- **A button inside** with `popovertargetaction="hide"` closes it (Cancel); a form's submit is the app's (it closes the popover when done).
- **Not a tooltip:** a tooltip names or explains a control on hover and can't hold controls; a popover is opened on purpose and can.
- **Not a dialog:** a task that must be finished before going on is a modal [Dialog](dialog.md).
- **Not a menu:** a list of actions is a [Menu](menu.md).

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-size` | the popover or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |

## Behavior

**The browser (T1):** the button opens and closes it; it opens under the button, from its start, and flips to fit; clicking outside or Escape closes it; another auto popover opening closes it (unless it opened from inside).

**canon.js (T2):**

- **Focus moves in** when it opens: to its `[autofocus]` element, else its first field or control, else the panel itself. Closing returns focus to the button.
- **Focus moving out** (Tab past its end, or to anywhere else in the page but its button) closes it.
- The button gets `aria-expanded`.
- A `popover="manual"` popover (always shown, as in documentation) is left alone.

## Core

- Anchored to its button (`position-area: self-block-end span-self-inline-end`, flipping), at most as tall as its room, then it scrolls.
- A form inside is not a size container, so it widens the popover; its rows stay rows.

## Accessibility

- `role="dialog"` with a name: screen readers announce the panel and its title when focus moves in; the button's `aria-expanded` says it is open.
- Non-modal: the rest of the page stays reachable; leaving the popover closes it, so it never lingers behind focus.

## Theme obligations

- The panel set off from the page (frame, background), its content spaced like a form.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| An arrow pointing at the button | The theme, if it wants one |
| Opening on hover (hover cards) | Later (`interestfor`, as Tooltip) |
| Placement hints | If it comes up (Tooltip's `data-placement`) |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** Padding 12 / 16 / 20px, the same between what it holds; corners 8 / 12 / 16; as wide as its content, at most 24rem.

The Menu panel (white, dark zinc-900; no frame: a hairline edge (black at 12%, dark white at 12%) and the floating shadow), 4px under its button, Form Layout's spacing inside (a form's actions a field step under its fields), the title Form Layout's section title (14 / 16 / 18px semibold).

**Motion:** opening, it fades in from 97% (0.15s); closing, it fades out where it is (0.1s). With reduced motion it only fades.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/tooltip.md

# Tooltip

Tier: **T1** (interest invokers, `popover="hint"`, anchor positioning; canon.js polyfills interest invokers)

A short text that appears next to a button or link while the pointer rests on it or it has keyboard focus. It names or briefly explains the trigger. Nothing in it can be clicked.

## Elements

| Element | Role |
|---|---|
| Trigger: `<button>` or `<a href>` | Points at the tooltip with `interestfor="<id>"` |
| Tooltip: any element (`<div>`, or `<span>` inside phrasing content) | `class="canon-tooltip"`, an `id`, `popover="hint"`, `role="tooltip"` |

```html
<button type="button" class="canon-button" data-display="icon" interestfor="tip-delete">
  <span class="canon-icon" data-icon="trash" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="canon-button-label">Delete</span>
</button>
<div class="canon-tooltip" id="tip-delete" popover="hint" role="tooltip">Delete</div>
```

- The browser shows the hint popover when interest starts (hover or focus, after a delay), hides it when interest ends, and makes the trigger its implicit anchor. Escape dismisses it. Opening one hint closes the others.
- Put the tooltip right after its trigger. It renders in the top layer, so it never affects layout and is never clipped by `overflow`.
- `popover="manual"` is allowed for tooltips that are always open (documentation, onboarding). Never `popover="auto"`: it would close on the first click elsewhere and close other popovers.
- Not allowed: `title` as a tooltip, tooltips on elements that can't receive focus (`<span>`, `<div>`, icons), tooltips on `disabled` buttons.

## Anatomy

```
canon-tooltip
├── text          required, phrasing content
└── accessory     optional · canon-kbd (keyboard shortcut, after the text)
```

- Text only. No links, buttons or inputs: nobody can reach them. That is a Popover.
- Keep it short: a name, or one sentence. Information people need to finish a task belongs on the page, not in a tooltip.
- Indicators (an arrow pointing at the trigger) are drawn by the theme.

## Two uses

| The tooltip says | Example | `aria-describedby` on the trigger |
|---|---|---|
| **The trigger's label** | Icon-only buttons: "Bold", "Settings" | No. The label is already the accessible name; a description would read it twice. |
| **More than the label** | "Archive" → "Hidden from the list, kept for 30 days" | Yes, pointing at the tooltip's id. |

Explaining why an action is unavailable is a description: use `aria-disabled="true"` (the button stays focusable and hoverable) and `aria-describedby`.

```html
<button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="high" aria-disabled="true"
        interestfor="tip-publish" aria-describedby="tip-publish">
  <span class="canon-button-label">Publish</span>
</button>
<div class="canon-tooltip" id="tip-publish" popover="hint" role="tooltip">Add a title before publishing</div>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-placement` | tooltip | `block-start` · `block-end` · `inline-start` · `inline-end`; `block-start` or `block-end` followed by `inline-start` or `inline-end` | theme decides | no |
| `data-size` | tooltip or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |

### `data-placement`: where it prefers to go

A hint, like `data-size`: only the author knows what a tooltip must not cover (a vertical rail wants `inline-end`, a toolbar at the bottom of the screen wants `block-start`). The first word is the side; a second one aligns it to an edge of the trigger.

| Value | Side | Aligned |
|---|---|---|
| `block-start` · `block-end` | above · below the trigger | centered |
| `block-start inline-start` · `block-end inline-start` | above · below | to the trigger's start edge |
| `block-start inline-end` · `block-end inline-end` | above · below | to the trigger's end edge |
