| `inline-start` · `inline-end` | before · after the trigger in the reading direction | centered vertically |

- Logical: `inline-start` is on the left in left-to-right text and on the right in right-to-left text; `block-start` is above in horizontal text.
- It is a preference. When the tooltip doesn't fit, it flips to the other side (and alignment), then to both.

## Behavior

| Moment | What happens | Who |
|---|---|---|
| Pointer rests on the trigger, or the trigger gets focus | Shows after a delay | Browser (`interestfor`); canon.js where missing |
| Pointer moves onto the tooltip | Stays (WCAG 1.4.13: hoverable) | Browser; canon.js |
| Pointer and focus leave both | Hides after a short delay | Browser; canon.js |
| Escape | Hides | Browser; canon.js |
| Another tooltip shows | This one hides | Browser (`hint`); canon.js |
| Touch | Nothing (long-press where the browser supports it) | Browser |

- Delays belong to the theme: `interest-delay-start` and `interest-delay-end` on triggers. The canon.js polyfill uses 500 ms and 250 ms.
- canon.js's polyfill anchors the tooltip to its trigger by name (`anchor-name` / `position-anchor`) for browsers without implicit popover anchors.

## Positioning (core)

- Anchor positioning: `position-area` from `data-placement` (above and centered without it), in `self-` keywords so it follows the tooltip's own direction (the containing block is the viewport), `position-try-fallbacks: flip-block, flip-inline, flip-block flip-inline`.
- The tooltip is an anchored container (`container-type: anchored`), so themes can follow a flip: `@container anchored(fallback: flip-block) { … }` turns an arrow around.
- **Aiming at the trigger.** The implicit anchor has no name, so a theme's arrow (a pseudo-element) can't reach the trigger on its own. Just before a tooltip opens, canon.js gives its trigger a unique `anchor-name` and sets `--canon-tooltip-anchor` on the tooltip to that name. A `position: fixed` arrow with `position-anchor: auto` (the tooltip itself) can then aim with `anchor(var(--canon-tooltip-anchor, --canon-none) center, anchor(center))` and clamp against the tooltip's own `anchor(left)` / `anchor(right)`. Without canon.js the fallback keeps it on the tooltip's center.
- A `filter` (or `transform`) on the tooltip would become the arrow's containing block and cut it off from the trigger: use `box-shadow` on the tooltip and filters on the arrow.
- Anchor positioning keeps the last placement that fit while it still fits. A tooltip that flipped near an edge stays flipped until it closes.

## Theme obligations

- Draw the gap between trigger and tooltip on the side facing the trigger (margins flip with the fallbacks).
- If the theme draws an arrow, it points at the trigger (`--canon-tooltip-anchor`), and follows the placement, the direction and the fallbacks.
- Set a maximum width; long text wraps. If the theme draws an arrow, set a minimum width too, so a one-word tooltip ("OK", "5") is never narrower than the arrow and the room it keeps from the corners.
- Show the same tooltip for hover and focus. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for any entry animation.
- `pointer-events` stay on: people must be able to move the pointer onto the tooltip.

## Not in the contract

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Interactive content, rich previews, hover cards | Popover component |
| Inverse colors ("dark tooltip on a light page") | Theme |
| Show and hide delays | Theme (`interest-delay`) |
| Animation | Theme |
| Validation errors | Field message |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** 12 / 14 / 16px text, 4 / 6 / 8 radius; sm by default

**Arrow:** 14 × 10 rounded tab aimed at the trigger's center, at least 8px in from the tooltip's edges; so the tooltip is at least 30px wide, and text shorter than that is centered

**Gap:** 4px

white with a zinc-200 border (dark: zinc-900, zinc-700 border), the raised shadow (0 1px 2px at 6%, 0 1px 3px at 4%)

**Motion:** it fades in (0.12s) and goes at once. Opacity only, so its arrow keeps aiming at the trigger.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/alert.md

# Alert

Tier: **T0** · dismissing is **T2** (canon.js)

A message in the page that stays while it's true: "This invoice is overdue", "2 fields need attention", "Changes apply to new invoices only". It sits with what it's about, in the flow of the page, and goes when the thing it reports is fixed, or when someone dismisses it.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-alert" data-intent="warning">
  <p class="canon-alert-title">This invoice is overdue</p>
  <p class="canon-alert-description">It was due on 3 October. Globex hasn't paid yet.</p>
  <div class="canon-alert-actions">
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="high" data-intent="neutral" data-size="sm">…Send reminder…</button>
  </div>
  <button type="button" class="canon-alert-close"></button>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-alert` | yes | A `<div>`. The theme draws its icon from `data-intent`. |
| `.canon-alert-title` | one of the two | What's true, a short sentence. A `<p>`, or a heading (`h2`–`h6`) when the alert heads a part of the page (an error summary). |
| `.canon-alert-description` | one of the two | More: why, what next. A `<p>`, or a `<div>` holding paragraphs or a list (an error summary's links to its fields). An alert can be only a description: one sentence, no title. |
| `.canon-alert-actions` | no | [Buttons](button.md) or [Links](link.md) that deal with it: Send reminder, Retry, Review. |
| `.canon-alert-close` | no | Last, an empty `<button type="button">`: the theme draws the X, canon.js names it ("Dismiss", `--canon-text-dismiss`). Only for alerts that can be put away without fixing anything (a tip, news); one that reports a problem stays until the problem goes. |

- **Alert, Toast or Banner?** An Alert is about a part of this page and stays while it's true. A [Toast](toast.md) is news about what just happened, and goes by itself. A Banner is about the whole app (maintenance tonight, a trial ending) and sits above every page.
- **A callout** (a note in a settings page: "Changes apply to new invoices only") is an Alert with `data-intent="info"`, or none.
- **Placement:** right before what it's about: above the form it summarizes, at the top of the record it describes, inside the Card or Section it belongs to.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-intent` | the alert | `info` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` | none: a plain note, no icon | no |
| `data-emphasis` | the alert | `medium` · `high` (solid: it must not be missed) | medium | no |
| `role` | the alert | `alert` · `status`, only for one shown while the page is open (see Accessibility) | none | no |
| `hidden` | the alert | present once dismissed (canon.js), or before the app shows it | absent | no |
| `data-state` | the alert | `opening` (shown while the page is open) · `closing` (dismissed): while its animations run (canon.js) | absent | no |

## Core

- The icon, then the title with the description under it, the actions after them (centered on the text), the close button at the end. Under 20rem the actions go under the text, so long labels don't squeeze it. A part that isn't there leaves its column empty: no intent, no icon; no close button, nothing at the end.
- **Actions are small high neutral Buttons** (`data-emphasis="high" data-intent="neutral" data-size="sm"`), or Links. One is best; two at most.
- The icon is named for screen readers with the intent's word: "Information:", "Success:", "Warning:", "Error:" (`--canon-text-intent-*`, translated in `i18n/`), so the intent isn't told by color and shape alone.
- `hidden` hides it.
- Without scripting the close button isn't shown (it couldn't work).

## Behavior (T2, canon.js)

- **Dismissing:** the close button fires `canon-dismiss` on the alert (`detail.reason: "close"`), then closes its room (`data-state="closing"` while the theme's animations run) and hides it (`hidden`). The event is cancelable: an app that removes the alert itself, or remembers it was dismissed, calls `preventDefault()`.
- **Focus:** if focus was in the alert, it moves to the next thing in the page (or the one before), never lost.
- **Showing one later** is the app's: insert the alert with a `role` (see Accessibility), or remove its `hidden`. canon.js opens its room (`data-state="opening"` while the theme's animations run); one there from the start (no `role`) just appears with the page.

## Accessibility

- **There from the start** (part of the page as it loads): no `role`. It's read in its place, with its intent's word first.
- **Shown while the page is open** (after a submit, when a save fails): `role="alert"` when it needs attention now (warning, danger), `role="status"` otherwise. Insert it with its text, or unhide it; screen readers announce it once.
- **An error summary** after a submit that failed: a `danger` alert with a heading as its title and links to each field in its description; move focus to it (`tabindex="-1"` on the alert) so people start there. Each field still has its own message ([Field](field.md)).
- The intent is in words as well as color and icon. The title should still say what's wrong, not just "Error".
- The close button is named ("Dismiss").

## Theme obligations

- Set apart from the page around it, without looking like something over it (no shadow).
- Each intent told apart at a glance, and by shape as well as color (the icon).
- In forced colors, the intent still shows by shape.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the icon and the intent's mark are on the right.
- Coming and going without a jump: what's under it moves to make or give back room, not all at once. Calmer with reduced motion.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Remembering a dismissal across visits | The app (`canon-dismiss`, then `hidden` in its markup) |
| Alerts about the whole app | Banner |
| News that goes by itself | [Toast](toast.md) |

## Look

**Sizes:** 12px inside (the close button 8px in); icons 20px; text 14px on 20px lines; actions 12px after the text, centered on it, 8px apart (under 20rem, 8px under the text).

A [Toast](toast.md)'s look, in the page. The Card's surface (white, dark zinc-900) and a hairline edge (black at 12%, dark white at 12%), 12px corners, no shadow: it's part of the page. With an intent, a shadow 4px out at its start in the intent's 500 (dark 400), its own edge untouched, and the intent's icon: info blue-600 (a circle with i), success green-600 (a check), warning amber-500 (a triangle), danger red-600 (a circle with !); the 400s in dark. Title medium zinc-900 (dark white); description zinc-500 (dark zinc-400). `data-emphasis="high"`: Toast's solid fill, in the intent's 600 (warning amber-400 with amber-950 text), white text and icon, the description at 80%; no intent, inverted. Forced colors: the line 4px thick at the start, the icon in the text's color.

**Motion:** dismissed, it fades out (0.15s), then its room closes (0.2s) and what's under it moves up; shown while the page is open, its room opens (0.2s), then it fades in (0.15s). In a column of them, the gap goes and comes with it. With reduced motion it only fades.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/banner.md

# Banner

Tier: **T0** (a strip at the top) · staying in view over an App Shell and dismissing are **T2** (canon.js)

A message about the whole app, not one page: "Maintenance tonight, 22:00–23:00", "Viewing as Ana Duarte", "The last payment failed". It sits across the top, above the [App Shell](app-shell.md), the same on every page, while it's true.

## Elements

```html
<body>
  <div class="canon-banner" data-intent="warning">
    <p class="canon-banner-title">Maintenance tonight, 22:00–23:00</p>
    <p class="canon-banner-description">Invoices can't be sent during that hour.</p>
    <div class="canon-banner-actions">
      <a class="canon-link" href="/status">Details</a>
    </div>
    <button type="button" class="canon-banner-close"></button>
  </div>
  <div class="canon-app-shell">…</div>
</body>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-banner` | yes | A `<div>`, first in what holds the app (the `<body>`, before the App Shell): it runs across the top and is read first. The theme draws its icon from `data-intent`. |
| `p.canon-banner-title` | one of the two | What's true, a few words. |
| `p.canon-banner-description` | one of the two | One more sentence, beside the title (under it when narrow). |
| `.canon-banner-actions` | no | One or two small [Buttons](button.md) or [Links](link.md), at the end: Details, Update the card, Stop viewing. |
| `.canon-banner-close` | no | Last, an empty `<button type="button">`: the theme draws the X, canon.js names it ("Dismiss"). Only for news that can be put away; a banner about a state (read-only, viewing as someone) stays while the state does. |

- **Banner, Alert or Toast?** A Banner is about the whole app and is on every page. An [Alert](alert.md) is about a part of this page. A [Toast](toast.md) is news about what just happened, and goes by itself. If it would make sense on only one page, it's an Alert.
- **Several:** they stack, the most important first. Two at most: three banners say something else is wrong.
- **Short:** a banner takes room from every page. One line where it fits; the details behind a Link.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-intent` | the banner | `info` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` | none: plain news, no icon | no |
| `data-emphasis` | the banner | `medium` · `high` (solid: it must not be missed) | medium | no |
| `role` | the banner | `alert` · `status`, only for one shown while the page is open | none | no |
| `hidden` | the banner | present once dismissed (canon.js) | absent | no |
| `data-state` | the banner | `opening` (shown while the page is open) · `closing` (dismissed): while its animations run (canon.js) | absent | no |
| `--canon-banners-height` | their parent (canon.js) | the banners' height, which the App Shell's sticky parts start under | `0px` | yes (CSS) |

## Core

- One line that wraps: the icon, the title, the description beside it, the actions and the close button at the end.
- The icon is named for screen readers with the intent's word ("Warning:"), as Alert's is.
- `hidden` hides it. Without scripting the close button isn't shown.

## Behavior (T2, canon.js)

- **Staying in view:** canon.js marks the banners' parent `data-canon-banners` and measures them. Each sticks to the top of the window under the ones before it; their height (`--canon-banners-height` on the parent) moves the App Shell's sidebar, Top Bar and sticky parts (a sticky [Page Header](page-header.md)) under them, the sidebar as tall as the room left. Measured again when a banner changes size, is dismissed, comes or goes.
- **Dismissing:** as [Alert](alert.md)'s: the close button fires `canon-dismiss` (cancelable), then hides the banner after its closing animations (`data-state="closing"`); focus moves on; the shell moves back up with it. Remembering it across pages is the app's (`canon-dismiss`, then no banner in its markup). One shown while the page is open (unhidden, or put in with a `role`) opens its room first (`data-state="opening"`).
- **Without canon.js** banners scroll away with the page, and the App Shell sticks at the top as it does without them.

## Accessibility

- **There from the start** (almost always: the app puts it in every page): no `role`. First in the page, it's read first, with its intent's word.
- **Shown while the page is open** (the session is about to expire): `role="alert"` when it needs attention now, `role="status"` otherwise.
- The intent is in words as well as color and icon; the close button is named ("Dismiss").

## Theme obligations

- Across the top, set apart from the app under it (a fill, a line).
- Each intent told apart by shape as well as color (the icon).
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the icon is on the right, the actions and the close button on the left.
- Coming and going without a jump: the app under it moves with it. Calmer with reduced motion.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Remembering a dismissal | The app (`canon-dismiss`, then no banner in its markup) |
| A banner at the bottom of the window | If it comes up |
| Several messages behind one banner ("1 of 3") | If it comes up |
| Messages about one page | [Alert](alert.md) |

## Look

**Sizes:** at least 40px tall, 8px above and below; the shell's side inset (+4px) at the sides, the close button 8px from the end; 12px between the parts; icons 20px; text 14px on 20px lines.

A strip across the top, no corners, a line under it. No intent: zinc-100 (dark zinc-900) with a hairline rule (black at 10%, dark white at 10%). With an intent, tinted: the intent's 50 (dark its 950, 70% over the page) with its 200 line (dark 900), and its icon as Alert's (info blue-600, success green-600, warning amber-500, danger red-600; the 400s in dark). Title medium in the text's color; description zinc-600 (dark zinc-300); actions small high neutral Buttons (`data-emphasis="high" data-intent="neutral"`) or Links; on a solid banner an action is the inverse, filled in its text color. `data-emphasis="high"`: Alert's solid fill (the intent's 600, warning amber-400 with amber-950 text; no intent, inverted), white text and icon, the description at 80%. Forced colors: the icon and the X in the text's color.

**Motion:** as Alert's: dismissed, it fades out (0.15s), then closes (0.2s); shown while the page is open, it opens (0.2s), then fades in (0.15s); the shell follows it. With reduced motion it only fades.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/skeleton.md

# Skeleton

Tier: **T0**

Shapes that stand in for content while it loads, in its layout, so the page doesn't jump when it arrives.

## Elements

```html
<div aria-busy="true" aria-label="Profile, loading">
  <span class="canon-skeleton" data-shape="circle" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span class="canon-skeleton" aria-hidden="true" style="inline-size: 60%"></span>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-skeleton` | yes | Always `aria-hidden="true"`. Inside the region that is loading, which says so (`aria-busy="true"`, a name). |

- **Shaped like what comes:** a line per line of text, a circle for an avatar, a block for a control or a tag, a square for a checkbox. Vary the lines' lengths (`inline-size`) so they read as text.
- **Not for short waits** (under about half a second) or for an action's progress: that is a Button's loading state or a Spinner.
- A [Data Table](data-table.md) draws its own skeleton rows while it is `aria-busy`.

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-shape` | the skeleton | `block` · `circle` · `square` | a line of text | no |
| `data-size` | the skeleton or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | theme decides | yes |
| `data-motion` | the skeleton or a container | `sweep` | still | yes |

## Core

- A block, at most as wide as its container. The theme gives each shape its size.

## Accessibility

- Skeletons are decoration: hidden from screen readers. The loading region's `aria-busy="true"` (and its name) tells them the content is on its way; when it arrives, `aria-busy` goes, and canon.js marks the region `data-loaded` while the theme shows the content in.

## Theme obligations

- Reads as "loading", not as content; any motion stops with reduced motion.
- Shown only after a short wait, its room kept meanwhile, so a quick load never flashes it.

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** A line 8px tall, as long as its container; a block the control's height × 0.625 (20 / 25 / 30) and 4rem wide at Button's corners; a circle the control's height × 0.8 (26 / 32 / 38); a square the icon's size (16 / 20 / 24), 4px corners.

Flat rounded zinc-100 shapes (dark zinc-800). `data-motion="sweep"` adds a lighter sweep (zinc-200, dark zinc-700) passing every 1.5s; still with reduced motion.

**Motion:** a skeleton shows 0.3s after it comes, fading in (0.15s). Loaded, what came fades in (0.2s) where the skeletons were (a Data Table's rows only); a fade, so also with reduced motion.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/spinner.md

# Spinner

Tier: **T0** (the browser's `<progress>`: no JavaScript)

Something is working, and how long it will take isn't known: a panel waiting for an answer, a "Loading more…" row, "Checking availability…" beside a field. Shown only if the wait lasts: it appears after 0.4s.

## Elements

```html
<!-- Alone: named by aria-label -->
<progress class="canon-spinner" aria-label="Loading invoices"></progress>

<!-- With words: a label around it names it -->
<label class="canon-spinner-label">
  <progress class="canon-spinner"></progress>
  Loading invoices…
</label>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `progress.canon-spinner` | yes | No `value`, no `max`: a progress whose amount is unknown, which screen readers announce as busy. Named by what's loading: `aria-label`, or the words of the label around it. |
| `label.canon-spinner-label` | no | Around the spinner, the spinner first, then the words ("Loading invoices…"): they show and name it. Use words where the spinner stands alone in a space (a panel); inline, beside text that says it already, the spinner alone does. |

- **Which loading signal?** A Button running its action: the Button's own `aria-busy="true"`. The shape of what's coming is known (a list, a profile): [Skeleton](skeleton.md). How much is done is known ("3 of 8 uploaded"): Progress. Nothing known but that it's working: a Spinner.
- **The region that's loading** says so: `aria-busy="true"` on it while it loads (as with Skeleton), and the spinner goes when the content comes.
- **Not for waits that end at once:** it appears only after 0.4s, so a quick answer never flashes it. `data-delay="none"` shows it at once (a wait known to be long).

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-label` | the spinner | what's loading ("Loading invoices") | — (required without words) | no |
| `data-delay` | the spinner, its label or a container | `none`: shown at once | absent: after 0.4s | yes |
| `data-size` | the spinner, its label or a container | `sm` · `md` · `lg` | the text's size | yes |

## Core

- The browser's bar is cleared; the theme draws on the element. It's the text's size (1em), on its line.
- The label lines the spinner and its words up, half the text's size apart.
- It appears 0.4s after it's put in the page or shown (`@starting-style`); `data-delay="none"` shows it at once.

## Behavior (T0, the browser)

- No JavaScript: the spinner turns while it's in the page; the app puts it in, or takes it out (or `hidden`), as loading starts and ends.

## Accessibility

- A `<progress>` without a value is announced as busy, with its name: "Loading invoices, busy".
- The region that's loading carries `aria-busy="true"`; when the content arrives, it goes, with the spinner.
- With reduced motion it turns three times slower: it still says it's working.

## Theme obligations

- Visibly moving (it says "still working"), and calmer with reduced motion, never still.
- In forced colors, it still shows.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A known amount done | Progress |
| A full-page loading screen | If it comes up: a large spinner with words, centered in the page |
| A spinner over content (a dimmed overlay) | If it comes up |

## Look

**Sizes:** the text's size (1em) unless a `data-size` sets it: 16 / 20 / 32px (sm / md / lg), its words 13 / 14 / 16px on 20 / 20 / 24px lines; half the words' size between them.

Button's loading ring: Lucide's loader-circle (a 300° arc) over the same circle at 20%, turning once every 0.8s (2.4s with reduced motion), in zinc-500 (dark zinc-400). Its words beside it in the same color. A Button's `aria-busy` indicator is the same ring. Forced colors: the ring in the text's color.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/toast.md

# Toast

Tier: **T2** (canon.js shows, times and dismisses toasts)

Short news about what just happened ("Invoice saved", "Link copied"), in a corner of the window for a few seconds, sometimes with one thing to do about it ("Undo"). It never asks for anything: what needs an answer is a [Dialog](dialog.md); what must stay until fixed is an Alert in the page.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-toast" data-intent="success">
  <p class="canon-toast-title">Invoice deleted</p>
  <p class="canon-toast-description">INV-2037 is in the bin for 30 days.</p>
  <div class="canon-toast-actions">
    <button type="button" class="canon-button" data-emphasis="high" data-intent="neutral" data-size="sm">…Undo…</button>
  </div>
  <button type="button" class="canon-toast-close" aria-label="Dismiss"></button>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.canon-toast` | yes | A `<div>`. The theme draws its icon from `data-intent`. |
| `p.canon-toast-title` | yes | What happened, a short sentence. |
| `p.canon-toast-description` | no | One more line: which, where, what next. |
| `.canon-toast-actions` | no | One (at most two) Buttons or links: Undo, View, Retry. Choosing one dismisses the toast. |
| `.canon-toast-close` | — | Last, an empty `<button type="button">` named "Dismiss" (`aria-label`). canon.js adds one when it's missing (`--canon-text-dismiss`). |
| `section.canon-toaster` | — | Where toasts show. canon.js makes one at the end of the `<body>` when the page has none, named "Notifications" (`--canon-text-notifications`): a region people can jump to. Write one to place or name it yourself. |

### Showing one

- **From markup:** a Button with `command="--canon-toast"` and `commandfor` a `<template>` holding a `.canon-toast` shows a copy (so it can show again).
- **From app code** (most toasts: after the server answered):

```js
const detail = {
  intent: "success",
  title: "Invoice deleted",
  description: "INV-2037 is in the bin for 30 days.",
  emphasis: "", // or "high"
  timer: true, // show the time running out
  action: { label: "Undo", onClick: undo },
  duration: 10000, // milliseconds, or "none"
};
document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("canon-toast", { detail }));
detail.toast; // the toast shown
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-intent` | the toast | `info` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` | none: plain news, no icon | no |
| `data-emphasis` | the toast | `medium` · `high` (solid: the rare toast that must be noticed) | medium | no |
| `data-timer` | the toast | present: show the time running out | absent | no |
| `data-duration` | the toast | milliseconds, or `none` (stays until closed) | 5000; 10000 with an action | no |
| `--canon-toaster-inset` | the toaster (a style) | a length from the window's edges | theme decides | — |

## Core

- The toaster is a `popover="manual"`, pinned to the window's bottom-end corner, toasts stacked with the newest last. It lets clicks through except on its toasts.
- A toast: the icon, the title with the description under it, the action after them (centered on the text), the close button at the end. Under 20rem the actions go under the text.

## Behavior (T2, canon.js)

- **Showing:** the toast joins the toaster, which shows over the page (again on top of a modal dialog opened since). At most three at once: a fourth sends the oldest away.
- **Timing:** it goes after its duration, timed only while it can be read. The time stops while the pointer or focus is on the toaster, and while the page is hidden; the toast is `data-paused` meanwhile, and gets its duration as `--canon-toast-duration`. Let go, it has at least a second more, unless it shows its timer (`data-timer`): then it ends exactly when the timer does.
- **Dismissing:** the close button, Escape with focus in the toast, or one of its actions. `canon-dismiss` fires on the toast first (`detail.reason`: `timeout`, `close`, `action`, `escape`, `overflow`).
- **Focus:** a toast never takes focus. If it had focus when it went, focus moves to the toast beside it, or back to the page.
- **Stacking (for themes):** canon.js gives each toast its place from the front, `--canon-toast-index` (0 the newest), and how far above the toaster's bottom it sits when the toasts are spread out, the newest highest, `--canon-toast-offset` (the heights of the older ones and the toaster's gaps); and the toaster how many there are, `--canon-toaster-count`, the front toast's height, `--canon-toaster-front-height`, and all of theirs, `--canon-toaster-height`. A theme can lay the toasts over each other with these and spread them while the pointer or focus is on the toaster. A toast's own height is measured when it comes (its place is set before it joins, so it comes in from there) and again when the window's size changes.

## Accessibility

- Each toast is announced politely as it shows: its title, then its description. A toast never interrupts.
- The toaster is a named region ("Notifications"), so keyboard and screen reader users can reach a toast while it's there. Reaching it stops the time.
- Toasts with an action stay longer (10 seconds). Never put something only in a toast that people must do or can't find elsewhere: Undo is also in the bin, a link also in the page.
- The close button is named ("Dismiss"); the icon is decoration (the title says what happened).

## Theme obligations

- A toast set apart from the page under it (a shadow, a line).
- Each intent told apart at a glance, and by shape as well as color (the icon).
- Its coming and going calm, and still with reduced motion.
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left the toaster sits at the bottom-left.
- Stacked, every toast still reachable: spread out on hover and while focus is in the toaster, so keyboard users get the whole list.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A key to jump to the newest toast | If it comes up (the region is reachable already) |
| Progress in a toast ("Uploading 3 of 8") | Meter / Progress, if it comes up |
| Toasts at another corner | A theme's `.canon-toaster` position |
| Messages that must stay until something is fixed | Alert, Banner |

## Look

**Sizes:** The toaster 16px from the corner, at most 384px wide; toasts 8px apart when spread, 12px inside (the close button 8px in; with `data-timer`, 24px at the bottom, so an action's button stays 12px clear of the timer's line); icons 20px; text 14px on 20px lines.

**Stacked:** the newest in front, lifted so up to two older ones peek out under it, each 12px lower, 5% smaller and 25% fainter (75%, then 50%), cut to the front one's height with their content and intent bar hidden. While the pointer or focus is on the toaster they spread out into a column, the newest at the top, 8px apart, the toaster taking their height so moving between them keeps them open. Moving 0.35s, fast then settling; a new toast rises 8px into its place (0.2s); a toast going fades and shrinks to 96% (0.2s) while the others take its place. With reduced motion nothing moves: a toast just appears, and going it only fades (0.15s).

A Menu's panel. White (dark zinc-800), 12px corners, no frame: a hairline edge (black at 12%, dark white at 12%) and the floating shadow. With an intent, a shadow 4px out at its start in the intent's 500 (dark 400), its own edge untouched, so toasts tell apart at a glance. Icons in the intent's color: info blue-600 (a circle with i), success green-600 (a check), warning amber-500 (a triangle), danger red-600 (a circle with !); the 400s in dark. Title medium zinc-900 (dark white); description zinc-500 (dark zinc-400); actions small high neutral Buttons (`data-emphasis="high" data-intent="neutral"`), 12px after the text. `data-emphasis="high"`: solid in the intent's 600 (warning amber-400 with amber-950 text), white text and icon, the description at 80%, the close button in its colors, actions the inverse (filled in its text color); no intent, inverted (zinc-900 with white text; dark the reverse). `data-timer`: a 2px line 4px above the bottom and 12px in from the sides, on a zinc-200 track (dark zinc-700) like the password strength meter's, running out with the time, in the intent's color (no intent zinc-400; high emphasis its text, on a 25% track), stopping while held; it tells the time, so it stays with reduced motion.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/count.md

# Count

Tier: **T0** · marking a changing number is **T2** (canon.js)

A number that says how many: unread messages, notifications, items waiting. A leaf: it never contains other components, so anything can hold it (avatars, icon buttons and tabs; nav items show a quiet number), and a Tag can hold an Avatar without a loop.

## Element

```html
<span class="canon-count">3<span class="canon-visually-hidden"> unread messages</span></span>
```

- Text only: the number as the app formats it (`3`, `12`, `99+`).
- Add what it counts as visually hidden text: "3" alone means nothing read aloud.
- Never wraps; numbers keep their width (tabular figures).

## Where it goes

| Host | Position |
|---|---|
| Avatar | Top-end corner, cut into the avatar (see [avatar.md](avatar.md)) |
| [Tab](tabs.md) | After its text, in the row ("Activity 14") |
| Icon-only [Button](button.md) | Top-end corner, over the button (Canon: 4px past it): notifications in a [Top Bar](top-bar.md). The button's name and the count read together ("Notifications, 3 unread"). |

## Behavior (T2, canon.js)

- **A changing number:** when the app changes the count's text, canon.js marks it `data-updated` while the theme's animations run (Canon: a short pop). Without canon.js the number just changes.

## Not in the contract

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Labels ("New", "Beta") | [Tag](tag.md) with `data-intent` |
| A dot without a number | Avatar status, or a tag's dot |
| Capping (`99+`) | App |

## Look

rose-600 pill, white 10px semibold, 16px tall, at least round (16px wide), 4px side padding. In a [Tab](tabs.md) it is neutral: zinc-200 with zinc-600 text (dark zinc-700, zinc-300), zinc-900 with white on the current tab (dark the reverse).

**Motion:** its number changing, it pops to 120% and back (0.25s). None with reduced motion.

---

Source: https://recepkutuk.github.io/canon/docs/components/data-table-editing.md

# Data Table: editing cells

Tier: **T2** (without canon.js the cells show their values, and fields in a form submit them unchanged)

Changing a value where it's shown, without opening the record: a target, an owner, a status, a date. Part of the [Data Table](data-table.md). One cell at a time, each change saved on its own or, in a form with a [Save Bar](save-bar.md), all together.

## Elements

```html
<div class="canon-data-table">
  <div class="canon-table">
    <table>
      <caption class="canon-visually-hidden">Hiring KPIs</caption>
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th scope="col">KPI</th>
          <th scope="col" data-type="number" data-align="end" data-edit>Target</th>
          <th scope="col" data-type="text" data-edit>
            Owner
            <template class="canon-data-table-editor">
              <div class="canon-combobox" data-search="list">
                <select>
                  <option value="ada" data-seed="3">Ada Lovelace</option>
                  <option value="grace" data-seed="5">Grace Hopper</option>
                </select>
              </div>
            </template>
          </th>
          <th scope="col" data-type="choice" data-options="On track, At risk, Off track" data-edit>Status</th>
          <th scope="col" data-type="date" data-edit>Review</th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <th scope="row">Time to hire</th>
          <td data-value="40">40 days</td>
          <td data-value="ada">…Ada Lovelace's avatar and name…</td>
          <td data-value="On track"><span class="canon-tag" data-intent="success">…On track…</span></td>
          <td data-edit="none"><time datetime="2026-11-30">30 Nov 2026</time></td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</div>
```

| Element | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| An editable column | yes | Its header `th` has `data-edit`. Its cells are editable, except those marked `data-edit="none"`. |
| The editor | no | What a cell is edited with. By default it follows the column's `data-type`: `text` a [Text Input](text-input.md), `number` a Text Input with `type="number"`, `date` a [Date](date.md), `choice` a [Select](select.md) of its `data-options`. Without a `data-type` it is a Text Input. A `template.canon-data-table-editor` in the header gives another: one box (`.canon-text-input`, `.canon-number`, `.canon-select`, `.canon-combobox`, `.canon-date`) holding its control without a name or id. The control's own `min`, `max`, `step`, `pattern`, `maxlength` and `required` apply. |
| The value | yes | As for sorting: the cell's `data-value`, else a `<time datetime>` in it, else its text. In a form, a field in the cell holds it instead (below). |
| A field | in a form | `<input hidden name="kpi[3][target]" value="40">` in the cell: its value is the cell's, and it submits with the form. A text input with `hidden`, not `type="hidden"`, whose value can't be told from its default. |
| A checkbox or switch | no | A [Checkbox](checkbox.md) or [Switch](switch.md) in an editable column's cell is changed where it is: no editing, the same saving. The select column is never editable. |

- **Which columns:** the few that people change often. Each editable cell is a stop for Tab; a table where most cells are edited is a spreadsheet, which this is not (see Not in the contract).
- **Cells the person can't change** (a computed total, a locked record) are `data-edit="none"`: on a cell, a row, or the whole data table (a view-only mode).

## Attributes

| Attribute | On | Values | Default | Inherited from containers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-edit` | a header `th` | (present) its cells can be edited | not editable | — |
| `data-edit` | a cell, a row or the data table | `none`: not editable here | editable where the column is | yes (row and data table to their cells) |
| `data-type`, `data-options` | a header `th` | as [Data Table](data-table.md): they also pick the editor | text | — |
| `data-key` | a header `th` | the column's name in events | its text | — |
| `data-state` | a cell | `editing` · `saving` · `saved` · `failed` · `changed` (canon.js) | — | — |

## Behavior (canon.js)

- **Ready:** canon.js puts each editable cell's content in a button (`.canon-data-table-edit`) that fills the cell. Nothing else changes: the content looks and reads as before.
- **Starting:** a click, Enter, Space or F2 on the cell opens its editor in the cell, holding the value, all of it selected. Starting to type a letter or number (text and number cells) opens it with what was typed in place of the value. Pasting on the cell (not while editing) puts the pasted text in as the new value and saves it.
- **While editing:** the cell is `data-state="editing"`; its width and the row's height hold, so the table doesn't move. The editor's own keys work (a Select's or Combobox's list, a Date's calendar). A Select's or Combobox's list opens with it. An editor wider than the cell (a date, a list) reaches over the next cells, or the other way when the frame's edge is near.
- **Finishing:**
  - Enter, or leaving the cell (a click elsewhere, Tab), saves it. Tab then moves on as usual, to the next cell's button.
  - Picking from a Select, a Combobox (one value) or a Date's calendar saves at once.
  - Escape puts the value back and returns focus to the cell.
  - A value the control finds invalid (`min`, `required`, `pattern`, …) keeps the editor open, its message in a [Tooltip](tooltip.md) under it, until it's fixed or Escape.
  - A value that didn't change ends the editing quietly.
- **The new value shows:** canon.js writes it in `data-value` (and the field), and draws it in the cell:
  - a choice the way another cell of the column with that value shows it (its Tag, say), else as its option shows it (an avatar or icon and the label; avatars sized as the column's);
  - a number in the reader's format, kept in its words when the old number shows in them ("40 days" becomes "45 days", "$495.90" keeps its decimals);
  - a date as a `<time>` in the reader's medium format ("Nov 18, 2026");
  - text as it is.

  An app that shows values its own way draws them in its `canon-edit` listener (`detail.content`).
- **Saving on its own** (not in a form with a Save Bar): **`canon-edit`** fires on the cell (bubbling, cancelable; `detail: { value, previous, row, column, key, name, content }`, `content` the element showing the value).
  - Not cancelled: the edit stands; the app saves it as it likes.
  - Cancelled (`preventDefault()`): the app saves it and answers on the cell (the event needn't bubble), as with a Save Bar: the cell is `data-state="saving"` until **`canon-saved`** (then `saved` for a second), or **`canon-save-failed`** (`detail.message` optional), which puts the old value back, marks the cell `failed` with the message, and announces it. An app refusing a value at once (a rule across cells, a permission) answers `canon-save-failed` straight away.
- **In a form with a Save Bar:** an edit changes the cell's field (firing `input` and `change`), so the Save Bar counts it; the cell is `data-state="changed"`. Discard (the form's reset) puts every cell's value back; `canon-saved` on the form makes the values the new defaults and clears the marks. `canon-edit` fires too, not cancelable.
- **Checkboxes and switches** in an editable column save on change, with the same events and states (disabled while saving); a failure unchecks or checks them back and describes them with the message.
- **Rows stay put:** with `data-local`, an edited value doesn't move its row or hide it; the next sort, filter or page change puts it where it belongs.
- **Not while loading:** while the data table is `aria-busy`, cells can't be edited, and an open editor puts its value back.
- **Rows the app adds** are set up like the others.

## States

| State | Hook |
|---|---|
| Editable cell | in a `data-edit` column, not `data-edit="none"` |
| Editing | `data-state="editing"` on the cell |
| Saving | `data-state="saving"` on the cell |
| Saved | `data-state="saved"` on the cell, for a second |
| Saving failed | `data-state="failed"` on the cell, until it's edited again |
| Changed, not yet saved (in a form) | `data-state="changed"` on the cell |

## Core

- The edit button fills the cell and lays its content out as the cell would (alignment, wrapping, truncation); it adds no frame, padding or fill of its own.
- The editor takes the cell's place without changing its size: over the cell (the button stays, unseen, holding its size), as wide as it (a date or a list at least that), centered in the row; at the cell's end in end-aligned columns, keeping their alignment, and without a number field's arrows.

## Accessibility

- The cell's button is named by its content (the value), so moving through the table reads as before: "Target, 40 days, button". It is described as editable ("Edit", the `data-table-edit` string); an empty cell's button reads "Empty".
- The editor is labelled with the column and the row: "Target for Time to hire".
- Saving is silent; a failure is announced with its message ("Couldn't save", or the app's), and stays as the cell's description until it's edited again.
- Escape always gets back to the value as it was; focus returns to the cell after every edit.
- In a form, the Save Bar announces the changes as for any field.

## Strings

`data-table-edit` ("Edit"), `data-table-empty` ("Empty"), `data-table-edit-cell` ("{column} for {row}"), `save-failed` ("Couldn't save", shared with the Save Bar), translated in `i18n/`.

## Theme obligations

- Starting to edit moves nothing: the editor sits where the value was, its text where the value's text was.
- An editable cell is told from the others under the pointer and with focus, never only at rest.
- Saving, failed and changed show by more than color (a spinner, an icon or a mark).
- Use logical properties: in right-to-left a cell's marks are on its other side.

## Not in the contract (yet)

| Thing | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| A spreadsheet: arrow keys between cells, selecting ranges, pasting several cells, filling down, formulas | A grid of its own, if it comes up |
| Enter moving to the cell below | The spreadsheet |
| Undo and redo across edits | The app (`canon-edit` gives the previous value; a [Toast](toast.md) with an Undo action) |
| Values computed from others (totals, scores) | The app, from `canon-edit` |
| Editing several rows at once | A bulk bar action |
| Adding and removing rows in the table | The app, or a [Form Repeater](form-repeater.md) for a short list |
| Colors from thresholds ("below target") | `data-intent` on a cell, if it comes up |

## Look

**Sizes (sm / md / lg):** The edit frame and the editor the control's height (32 / 40 / 48), as wide as the cell, centered in the row (8px above and below; the whole row when `compact`), the text where the cell's text was (12 / 16 / 20px in); the spinner and the marks 16px, 8px from the value (before it in end-aligned columns); the changed mark 6px.

At rest an editable cell looks like any other. Under the pointer, Text Input's frame shows around it (a zinc-200 line, dark zinc-700, Text Input's corners) and the pointer is a text cursor. With focus, Button's ring around that frame. Editing: the editor at the table's size, in Text Input's focus look (blue-600 line and its halo), shown at once (no animation, for typing speed). Saving: the value in zinc-400 (dark zinc-500) and a Spinner at the frame's end, shown at once. Saved: a green-600 check (dark green-400) at the frame's end for a second, then it fades (0.2s). Failed: Text Input's error line around the frame and a danger icon (Lucide circle-alert, red-600, dark red-400) at the end; the message in a [Tooltip](tooltip.md) while the cell is under the pointer or focused. A checkbox or switch saving fades to 60%; failed, the danger icon at the cell's end. Changed (in a form): an amber-500 dot (dark amber-400) at the cell's top end corner, the Save Bar's changed color. Number cells keep their end alignment while editing. Forced colors: the frame and marks in the text's color, the failed frame in Mark.
